article: " I need you to kill my wife. " " Okay. Yeah. Sure. Whatever. " Greg looks at me for a second. " Wait, what? Really? No questions asked? This is the part where you stare at me all confused like, not... the other way around. " " Yeah, I'll do it. That's what friends are for, right? " He blinks. " Well, yeah. Fuck it, thanks for the help man. " So I do what they do in the TV shows and the movies: buy an illegal gun from some shady dealer dude I found on Craigslist, put on some disposable latex gloves, and tell my friend when he should leave the house so I can kill her and he doesn't have to watch. He gives me the keys to the house. Just part of the procedure. I enter into the house, walk upstairs, and enter the bedroom. There she is, standing there, with her plaid pajamas and her over-sized T-shirt. Her messy blonde hair frames her dull expression. I point the gun at her. She rolls her eyes. " My husband put you up to this, didn't he? " " Yuuup. " " And you're gon na kill me because I know you're secretly a- " " Don't say it! " ....." A furry. " " God dammit Linda. " She walks over to the dresser, where a glass of red wine was sitting. She takes a sip of it. " It's not even that bad, there's fetishes worse than that. " " I dunno, I'm pretty into it. " " Yeah? " " Yeah. " Linda takes a sip of her wine. " How bad? " I describe my latest voyeuristic meeting with a few friends. " Okay, " she says. " Okay? " " Just shoot me. " I shoot her. Afterwards Greg gives me 50 bucks.
label: human

article: In a dark building, two figures stood. All was black except for the single spotlight that was centred on a thick, stubby man wearing black pants and a blue button shirt. His head is nearly bald with of a small tuff of blonde hair near the back of his head and a ragged moustache. The woman was clocked in a black robe as the shade from the hood hid her face. "Do you want to change, Doctor?" Vivian cooed in his ear, "Do you want to know what it's like to become something different? Something," She paused to let him soak in the silence as she dragged a fingernail across his neck, "inhuman?" "Pl-," The fat man coughed to recover from his dry mouth, "Please, I can help you. Anything you need, anything." "Anything? I don't think'anything' is good enough. What do you say, Jack?" The woman called over her shoulder. From the darkness of the warehouse crawled a twisted creature. Its legs had turned to arms with its feet grown into hands. It crab-walked with an awkward limp that appeared unsteady from any direction. At the front, it held its head proudly with a mass of black eyes in the centre of its face. It lacked a tongue but eagerly made a garggling sound in reply. The doctor was horrified and gawked from his disgust. "What have you done?" "Oh, Jack?" The woman teased. She placed a tender hand on the top of Jack's head and patted it. "He was meant to be like this - eventually. I just sped up the process nature started. Truth be told, I bring out the best in people and I can do the same for you."
label: human

article: Dave wasn't the kind to get melodramatic. He had stood in the face of death and not batted his eyes, but this was too much. He had always taken cartoons, movies, all types of moving pictures so seriously. He remembered when he was little, he would yell out at how stupid the President was, and how you shouldn't go into that door, how the characters came to ridiculous conclusions based on pretty much nothing. Some would call him obsessive, as he was the first human to criticize a deus ex machina in a movie the second he was born, yet had never written a script himself. "Son! I'm going to have a heart attack." "What? Dad, I'm going out with my girlfriend right now!" "You can spare one goddamn minute for your Father's wellbeing, can't you? Now get me a gallon of beer and a stress ball!" "What? Dad? Why? I thought you were going to have a heart attack!" "Jasper, I was being figurative." Jasper sucked up his anger and breathed out angrily. "Fine." As he was rummaging through the fridge, Jasper shouted out. "Dad! You still haven't told me what's wrong!" Silence, except for the obnoxious sound of the TV. Jasper grunted. He was always a slave to the screen. He snatched up a beer and walked over to his father. "What is going on!" Dave pointed to the screen. "They released every goddamn bootleg cartoon." "I- what? You called me over for this?" "Yes. Bubsy, Sonic, the 18th season of SpongeBob. They're all here." Dave sat back and groaned audibly. "And I'm paying to watch them!" end
label: human

article: Rarely had a phrase ever popped into my mind that so clearly demonstrated a fellow human's insignificance. The senseless debate had jumped from politics, to religion, to science, and here was a man who had the credibility from others, but not the actual knowability of someone deserving credibility. Perhaps it was his nonchalant response of "I don't read books" or his refutal of the scientific method. Thinking back to my fellow predecessors whom I shared no blood with, I wondered what they would do in this situation. Would they walk away? Would they deficate on them? The conversation abruptly ended as follows "Look bro, in the end, all that science offers, and all that math offers is useless, and nobody will care about it in the long run. Its irrelevant and that is fact, you dont even have to think about...." (my mind drifted wondering. I need something big, sudden, but that will linger, and he will remember for the rest of his life) "CRAWL BACK UP YOUR MOM'S PUSSY YOU DUMB MOTHERFUCKER, AND FIND YOUR BRAIN UP IN THAT SPIDERWEB YOU DISGUSTING PEICE OF AMPHIBIAN SHIT" Silence, was all that could be heard, and he promptly walked away. The audience applauded
label: human

article: The snow was still coming down. It had been snowing nonstop for the past two days but what a place to be trapped Karen thought. Ryan pulled off the blanket that was covering the young couple. "Another?" he asked Karen as he motioned his eyes to her glass of moonshine. The flames from the living room fireplace roared in front of them. "Sure" she replied. As Ryan went to the kitchen, Karen slowly got up and stretched, observing the cabin living room around her, she walked around the room and found her self looking out at the large bay window. She thought how lucky she was to have met Ryan just six months ago. Her life had been like a fairytale since and here she was at his three bedroom cabin with panoramic views of the forest. Unfortunately, she also felt like there was something that he was holding back. If they were going to take the next step she was determined to find out exactly what it was. It had taken her the better part of a week to secure a bottle of homemade liquor but she had done it. From a friend of a friend of course. She was hoping it would help her on her quest. As Ryan came back in to the room with two quarter filled glasses of noticabely strong hooch Karen was back near the fire, observing the photos on the mantle. As he handed her the glass she decided to waste no time. "I noticed your father isn't in any of the photos and you never mention..." her words trailed off as she saw the pain in his face. "What's wrong?" "My father, he wasn't around much. I don't like talking about it. I already told you this" "I know you don't..... but it's me. I won't force you to tell me any more but I just wish, well, that I could understand you better." She sat down. Ryan sighed and rubbed his brow. He sat down next to Karen. "Okay. If you need to know, my father..... was a marijuana addict." He paused to observe her reaction. "Oh Ryan, I'm sorry." Karen replied softly. "I have long come to terms with it and yet, it still looms..." Ryan said, trying to fight the tremble in his voice. "What did he do to you?" she asked. "A lot of things, Karen. For instance, my 8th birthday party. We had this big party in our backyard with a clown, magician, and even a pony. It was every kids dream. However, when it came time for cake my stoned father told all my friends and parents the cake had just fell on the floor. The disappointment was palpable. In fact, some kids never forgave me for it. What I later found out was my Dad had got stoned off his ass the night before and ate the entire cake." "Ryan, how awful..... no child should ever have to deal with something like that." "It gets worse. Do you know what it's like to have to drive back home three times every time we go out because Dad's too high to remember his phone or his wallet? Do you know what it's like to have to lock up your Halloween candy because your father might steal it and replace it at a later date? That's if he was at home at all, he spent many a night down at the local vapor lounge." Tears were streaking down Ryan's face but he didn't care at this point. He felt a sense of empowerment to finally talk to somebody. He continued. "You know, I used to dream my father could be like all the other fathers. Like my friend Joe's Dad. He didn't need to have weed to have a good time. Sure, he might have had some moonshine on the weekend but who doesn't? it's practically legal now anyways." He put down his glass. "The worst thing you're going to do drunk is get violent and aggressive. I never got to see my father's violent side." Karen grabbed his hand "You're so brave for telling me all of this. I know how hard it must be. But it explains so much, like why you don't smoke" "Never touched the stuff and I used his weaknesses as motivation to get where I am today. To be better then him." He paused and smiled. "You know what? It really feels great to get this out. I feel a burden lifted." "I can tell." Karen smiled. "But I have to know, what happened to your father? is he still alive?" "Yes, but we haven't talked in years. I don't even know where he lives anymore, probably somebodies couch." "And your mother?" "We still talk but to be honest I have never been able to fully forgive her for standing by as my father inadvertently psychologically abused me. She let him smoke his life away." Karen reached over and hugged Ryan. "We won't make the same mistakes. If we have a family one day you will be a great father." Ryan smiled. "I'm not so sure..." "I am!" Karen shouted before giving him a kiss on the lips. They both laughed. "The worst our kids would ever do is have a few strong drinks on the weekend and that's when they get older, of course." "But what if it's a gene? what if it's recessive?" "We would be such good parents it won't matter" Karen replied with a smirk. Ryan got up and scooped Karen out her seat. She giggled. "You're right. We won't make the same mistakes. I love you." he told her. "I love you too." she replied. Outside, the snow continued to fall.
label: human

article: He sat hunched over in the corner dry heaving and shaking wildly. I observed him through the glass for a few more minutes and then walked into the room. He didn't notice me come in but he was probably too busy whispering to himself to notice anything. I cleared my throat to get his attention and he swung around wildly screaming "please don't make me do it again I can't stand it! Please just kill me fucking kill me!!!" I looked around at the dark and damp room and began to laugh, a loud, long and hearty laugh that echoed through the room. After my fit of laughter I pulled the silver square out of my pocket and slid it across the room. "I hope it was worth it," I whisper as I close the door.
label: human

article: Vultric's six arms laid limp over the thin leather couch. It wasn't too comfortable. Every few seconds he reminded himself of that fact. His twelve eyes were closed, dreaming of a better time. There was a fan in the room. Every few seconds it blew Vultric's thick fur around. He hated it. "Can we turn it off?" He asked. His eyes opened and he looked at a balding creature who sat across from him. The creature, Dr. Greox, didn't speak. He never spoke. Vultric ignored Greox and stood up on his six legs. It took a few strides, but he reached the fan and shut it off. Then he returned to the couch. "As I was saying. This is the third time she's hugged him this week." With his eyes closed Vultric imagined Amy, the human girl whom he became familiar with over the past few years. "You know, this all happened because of the father. Back when she had the Princess Mattress it was fine." Vultric's situation, like many other closet creatures, was dire. The human who inhabited his room was changing. Every few years her bed changed. With a new bed, came a new neighbor. Normally the monsters under the bed were quite normal. They understood the game. You wait for the lights to go out. Then you scare. There was no cuddling, no hugs, no friendship with the human. But this guy. This big hunk of fur wasn't scary. No. He was deemed "Adoreable." Vultric sat up on his couch. "I should kill him." Vultric though to himself. It truly was the only way. Suddenly Vultric stood up. He left the couch and exited the room. He was back in his home. Fresh human clothes brushed against his unwelcoming fur as he crept through the corridors of the closet. Finally he was at the door. He pushed it open ever so slightly. Vultric moved out of his home and into the battlefield. The only sentry, a fairy nightlight stood guard near the bed. He crawled forward along the carpet. Toys scattered and blocked his way, so he mere climbed over them. Then he was where he needed to be. The entrance to the bed. He snuck under some sheets that hid that creature. The covers touched his fur as he entered his enemies fortress. He was there. Standing in front of him, next to a snickers candy wrapper. Quickly Vultric launched himself at his enemy. With his twin fangs he sank himself into his enemies back. It was all going according to plan. Then that creature pushed Vultric up against the bed. Smack! The bed moved. Yet still Vultric's bite held firm. "Amy!" A voice broke the trance of battle. Footsteps came racing across the hallway floor. The door opened and the lights flickered on. The footsteps became louder as something approached the bed. Suddenly the covered were whisked up and Amy looked directly into her fathers face. "Hunny it's bed time." He said. Amy groaned and dropped her toys. She crawled out from under the bed and brushed off the dust that was on her pajamas. Then she leaped into bed and dragged the covers over her. Her father leaned in and kissed her goodnight. "Go to sleep." He said closing the door. "Fine." She fired back. Amy's eyes closed and darkness once again came upon the room. The only light came from the fairy nightlight. Under the bed though, the battle had been decided. Vultric released his fangs from the other monster and crawled out from under the bed. Then he returned to his closet victorious.
label: human

article: "Am I under arrest, officer?" I stressed the last word, knowing that it would get a rise. Agent Lassiter looked at me hard. "Agent. Police are officers, I'm an agent." "Right,'Agent'. Anyway, if you're not going to arrest me, then...." "You know, once upon a time, before I went into law enforcement, I went to college. Iowa State University. You know what I studied there?" "No, what." I answered as bored as I could. Play their game, keep asking to leave. They've got nothing. "Physics. Iowa State actually has a very good physics department, not many people know that. Ranked 50 in the country by US News and World Reports." "Uh huh." "I was interested in astronomy, see. Always loved looking at the stars. My old man would take me out to the country when I was young, away from the lights of Mason City - that's where I grew up, Mason City, Iowa - anyway, with this nice 12-inch telescope he had, and we'd find Mars, look at Saturn, and stuff." Stall tactic. He's trying to get me off guard, hoping I'll say or do something. "Listen, Agent Lassiter, that's fascinating and all, but I...." "As it turns out, astronomy wasn't for me. The math got to be too much for me, I never could get my head around calculus. But I did enjoy the physics classes that I took, especially the General Physics courses we took, which hit on a variety of subjects. Including time travel." Shit. Wait, there's no way he can know. My ID is rock solid. I've got nothing on me tying me to the future. I planned this down to making sure my wallet is vintage. He's just trying to keep me talking. "Agent...." "Time travel was fascinating to me, especially travelling back in time. The Grandfather Paradox. Butterfly Effect. Stuff like that. Is that something you're familiar with?" "Agent Lassiter, unless you are placing me under arrest, I'm going to get up and leave now." The door was locked. Shit. "See, the Butterfly Effect says that even minute changes you might make in the past, could have drastic consequences in the future. A butterfly beats it's wings in Japan, and a storm hits in Chicago, that kind of thing. But with time, right? So you travel back in time, and..... oh, I don't know..... bet 100k on the Lions to win the Super Bowl." I sat back down. "If anyone can hear me, I am officially asking to leave, since as far as I know I am not under arrest. It appears that I am being held against my will. I would like to speak to an attorney, and I am going to excercise my right to remain silent." "But when you make a bet, you don't make that bet in a vacuum, right? Bookmakers constantly shift the betting lines based on the action they are getting. So if you make a large bet on a long shot, that might slightly shift the odds. Not much, mind you, maybe just a point. But if that line shifts, other books might shift as well. And this shift might encourage others to bet, further shifting the line." OK, Agent Lassiter, now you're interesting. I have to admit, this is something I had not considered during planning. "But money tends to come in on both sides when a betting line moves. Unless there is known information, like a QB getting hurt or whatever, any movement usually ends up correcting itself." Lassiter's eyes sparkled. Shit, why did I engage? Stupid, stupid, stupid. "That's right, it would. But it's interesting you bring up'known information'. Because that's true as well; if some piece of information is made public that would affect the outcomes of games, the lines swing dramatically. If the information is important enough, the odds are taken down entirely." I tried my best to look disinterested, and I'm sure faily miserably. Where was he going with this? "And that's just for information related to the game itself. Injuries and what not. It makes you wonder, what would happen if really shocking information got out? Something that would call into question the integrity of sports betting itself? Something like, you know, a time traveller coming back and placing bets based on future knowledge?" No. This can't be happening. He can't know; he's fishing. So why am I the one crapping my pants? "What....what....." "It would shut down sports betting alltogether, I'd wager. Every bet of any significance would be questioned. Lines would swing wildly as people chased bets with their own money. It would start affecting the games themselves. If big money came in on the Lions to win the Super Bowl before the season even started, the Lions would figure'Hey, we're gon na win the Super Bowl!' and play differently. It would also affect the play of other teams." "You.....No....No one would believe you!" "It's a wild tale for sure, I'd need proof. Proof like a certain individual that no one remembers meeting until a few months ago placing many large wagers in many different Vegas casinos, for example. Those cameras in the ceiling see everything, you know. Every person walking in the doors. Every bet placed at every window at the book. All nice and time coded and in full HD, just waiting to be found by some poor junior agent. It's not definitive proof, of course..... maybe you really are just incredibly lucky. But it's enough to get the idea out there into the public. And once it's out there, it's never going away, right? You know how people love a good conspiracy theory." I feel like Wile E. Coyote with a tiny umbrella, under a looming shadow. "And that's not even the worst part, is it? If people are coming to the past to bet on sports, what else are they doing? Are they playing the stock market with future knowledge? Are the subtly influencing elections? Are they bringing future tech back with them and giving it to certain world leaders, or terrorists? The implications would be devastating." Now I've got a little sign that says "Help." "Imagine the effect that would have on the future as well. Never mind the Butterfly Effect, this is fucking Godzilla tearing up the entire world. Nothing would be the same. Millions, perhaps even billions of people would never exist. Anyone going back to such a future, even if he still existed, would be going back to an entirely different future." Crunch. This man has just outlined how he can utterly destroy me by throwing a couple of rookie agents into a windowless room with a bunch of video tapes. He probably doesn't even know how right he is; in retrospect, I can't believe how sloppy I've been. It would be childs play for him to do exactly as says. Doing this would potentially throw this timeline in chaos as well, it's difficult to believe he would actually do this, even if he really believes any of it. But there's no way I can take the chance. Everyone I've ever known, my entire family...... "Uh....what would you say if I told you I have a sudden and overwhelming desire to return..... home?" "I'd say click your heels together, Dorthy."
label: human

article: Even as I knocked on the door, I still wasn't sure of my decision. I had filed the paperwork, bought the syringe with the lethal drug (one of the three ways we were allowed to do it), and planned my when and where. None of it seemed real until this moment. There was always the opportunity to back out or change my mind up until my knuckles touched this very door. I thought that when the time came, I'd feel some sort of peace about it. After all, as soon as they announced the bill's passing one name immediately came to mind. The one who'd caused so much pain and trouble in the lives of my loved ones. The one who continues to hurt us every single day. Just the one name. But instead of peace, I felt terror. None of the questions or doubts that had been plaguing me left my mind. How would I feel after it? Could I continue to live a normal life? I know others who've done it, but I've never been sure that I could. Does God forgive me for using my one legal murder? Surely God knows how justified it is. I stood at my sister's front door for a few eternal seconds. Would she answer it? Surely she knows by now, so would she just let it happen? She's always been smaller than me, so I could easily overpower her. Her fiance was another matter. I know he'd put up a fight, and there's a very good chance he'd win. I had the syringe gripped tightly in my left hand, thumb on the back, ready to inject its deadly substance. I figured freeing up my dominant right hand to restrain or fight someone off would be the best, but now I start to wonder why that thought ever crossed my mind. What the hell do I know? I'm not a criminal mastermind after all. What I'm doing is perfectly legal, and it's right. Footsteps, a pause, and then the door opened suddenly and violently. In the doorway stood my sister's fiance with a mixed look of rage and fear on his face. Relief swept over me and I became ever more convicted in what I was about to do. I stepped in the door without saying a word and he shut it behind me. We both knew that these things weren't allowed on the streets or in businesses, just in the privacy of your own home. He knew, and he was prepared. As soon as the door clicked shut he launched himself at me with a guttural roar. I expected the attack, but had no idea what to do. I threw myself to the side but he caught my legs and yanked me down to the floor. My power has always been in my legs, but even so my kicking did little to keep him from climbing on top of me. I don't know what would have happened if he'd seen the syringe. He must not have seen it, because it was too easy. He straddled me, wrapped his hands around my neck and began to squeeze, hard. But it was too late. He left my hands free. Free to plunge the syringe into the side of his neck and fill his veins and arteries with the liquid that's supposed to stop a beating heart in less than 30 seconds. For him it took about 10, I guess because of his quickened heart rate from my brief struggle. His hands slackened, his eyes glazed over, and I managed to roll out from underneath him before he collapsed. I'll never know if he even realized what had happened. I sat in shock for God knows how long before I started to heave and shake violently. There were no tears, only the sound of ragged sobs from my bruised and crushed windpipe. My sister. Her car was out front. She must be in the house somewhere, but she didn't come out to the sound of our wrestling match. It felt like it took hours, but maybe it was only a few seconds. I didn't know if I should try to find her or just wait for her to come out. I couldn't trust myself to walk without falling anyways, so I waited. The funny thing is that afterwards, you feel like you can't move, but you also can't stand just sitting there. It's torture. When I couldn't stand it any longer, I got up and entered the hallway that I knew lead to the bedrooms. On the left was the office that they shared, and on the right was their bedroom. She must've been in the office, probably with headphones on which is why she didn't hear anything. I had no idea what I was going to do, or what I was going to say. I opened the door with a trembling hand. No one. She wasn't in the office. But there was only one more room she could be in. There's no way she'd sleep through all of that, so she couldn't be napping in there. The shower! The bathroom was all the way in the back of their bedroom, so there's a good chance she wouldn't have heard anything in there over the sound of the water. I stood as still as my body would let me, and tried desperately to hear the sound of running water over my pounding heart and labored breathing. Nothing. At this point I began to shake again. I came here for my sister. My beautiful sister who had been my whole life growing up. I stepped towards her bedroom. My sister with her brilliant blue eyes and shining golden hair, always so much more lovely than I. My hand lifted itself to the door handle. My sister who hurt my family so badly when she ran away with her abusive boyfriend. I began to push down. My sister whom I would gladly kill or be killed for. The heaving sobs began again as the door swung open, and I saw my sister who lay on her bed, looking so peaceful except for her beaten and bruised face, and the deep red finger marks around her neck. I came to save my sister, but I was too late.
label: human

article: Just. Stay. Calm. I haven't done anything wrong. Thank God the pilot regained control of the plane, right? This will make for a good story, won't it? I'm going to jail, aren't I? Some people are crying, some people are laughing - out of either relief or hysteria, or perhaps both - and some people have already gone back to their phones or magazines. There are a few unconscious people on board, though, who fainted when the plane started dropping out of the sky. It makes me sigh in relief; at least now I can just say that he fainted. I don't dare look over at him, because I know exactly what I'm going to see. A slightly bruised neck, his head hanging forward. Is his tongue hanging out of his mouth? He might have hit his neck on the seat, or his head might have hit against the seat in front of him. I didn't see it, I was too busy screaming! Just. Stay. Calm. It's been a few minutes since things cooled down and the flight attendants are handing out napkins to people whose drinks spilled on themselves. One of them is walking towards me. "Aw, did he faint too?" She gives me an innocent grin and I nod in return, gently taking the napkin from her hand and wiping Diet Coke off the pages of my book. "Yeah, y-yeah. I think he hit his head." "Well, we'll make sure to see him to the hospital when he lands. I'm sure he'll be fine! Nobody on board was seriously injured." Nobody was injured, but somebody died. I can't even stand to look at my hands. Are my fingerprints on his neck? Can they find skin cells around my fingers? I didn't even think I'd survive! I think even the sanest person in the world would have to agree that what I did wasn't wrong, right? We were going to die anyway! We were going to die until we weren't anymore and now they're going to find out that I'm a murderer. I can't do this. I can't go through with this. I raise a hand. "Sir, do you need something?" "If you have any available, just some..... some of the chicken. I'm hungry again after I lost my..." I gesture to a doggie bag on the ground and she nods, walking off to get my meal. Nobody else here is crazy enough to want to eat after that. I twiddle my thumbs for a few minutes before taking the plate eagerly when the flight attendant returns with a plate of terrible airline chicken and a form and knife. I take a bite and smile at her just to calm her nerves, waiting until she's walked off to spit it into the doggie bag. "Ladies and gentlemen, I'm sorry for the disturbance. Texting while driving also applies to airplanes, it seems." A few people laugh, but most of us are too tired. "We have resumed our path to Jackson, Mississippi and will land in forty minutes." I have forty minutes. I grip the knife in my hand, tapping it against my seat-down tray. Nobody else can know what happened here tonight. I killed him, because the plane was going down. The plane is going down. I slip the handle of the knife in my sleeve and hold the blade in my fingers to conceal it as I stand, walking towards the cockpit. This plane is going down.
label: human

article: His toothy smile was breaking apart and coming back together, it looked like waves crashing on a beach. It was producing sounds that represent meaning, (which must be what waves do as well, of course, waves produce sound conveys meaning based on perception..... of course....). I listened to Travis, but his words were not in harmony with what he was communicating to me and everyone around me. I watched him struggle for a few more minutes, until he stopped, sensing a loss of control. I wished he were more like waves on a beach, they have no trouble conveying what the mean to say..... They simply say it. "Travis Wallace Chestington, do you hear yourself?" He remained silent. "Travis, your words convey knowledge, but not understanding. That is the reason for your discomfort. Do you understand?" He looked up at me, his face tormented with grief. "I am sorry, I am sorry, oh please forgive me..." He began to cry. Everyone in the room was completely still. "The only one you have to forgive is yourself, for ultimately you are the one who suffers the most." He looked up at me, and his face brightened, his toothy smile returned, only this time there was nothing lacking in communication. All it conveyed was joy. "Thank you..... Thank you..." "No sweat bro. Here, get some of this shit" I said as I heated the spoon.
label: human

article: I'm late to the party with this so it is unlikely to be read. But I worked hard on it, so..... I gained consciousness with an aching head as two men entered this small, windowless room. Both carried a folder under one arm and a cup of steaming black coffee in hand. They sat at the wide, stainless steel table across from me. Beneath their black blazer jackets, I noticed each carried a side-arm. " Hello Dr. Roth, " said the older of the two. " I'm Detective Monroe, and this is Detective Cambridge, " he said, gesturing to a balding white man. Monroe's expression was impassive, while Cambridge seemed to scowl without effort. I reached out to shake their hands but a sharp tug at my wrist caught me surprised me. I was handcuffed to a loop attached to the table. My dry mouth opened in shock. I can't remember being handcuffed. " What am I doing here? Why have you handcuffed me? " " I understand you've got questions - we'll get to that. But first, we need to talk about last night, " Monroe said. " Sure, I've got nothing to hide. Look, do I need a lawyer or something? " I'd seen enough TV to know that I had to ask for one as soon as possible. And with this headache, I might say something stupid. I need aspirin. They cracked a reflexive smile to each other while the one named Monroe leaned forward. " No Dr. Roth, you aren't currently being charged with any crime, " he said. " However, that can change depending on how you answer my questions. And then, " he emphasized, " You may indeed need a lawyer. Not that it would do you any good. " A shiver ran up my spine as I contemplated his words. I might need a lawyer. What the hell did I do? " If I'm not under arrest, why am I here handcuffed to a table? " Monroe held up a hand. " Let's talk about last night Dr. Roth. " " Fine, " I said like an indignant child," I went out drinking with my buddies from the lab. That's Fred, Tom, Katie, and Peter. I'm sure you want their full names? " He was writing while I talked. He looked up at me and shook his head. " Look, I don't normally drink because I used to have - uh - problems I'd get drunk. I've been sober 4 years now, but we were celebrating our first set of successful trials. So I figured it was a bonding experience for the team. I could handle it. " " And where did you go? " Monroe said. " Uh - The Last Laugh, I think it was? We had a few bottles of champagne - moved onto shots after. We didn't make any trouble. When they were closing, we finished our drinks and left. We went back to Fred's and kept drinking. I guess I passed out. It's not that clear. Say, do you guys have aspirin on you? I've got a killer headache. " Detective Cambridge crossed his arms in front of him and smirked at me. " Stupid prick, nobody gives a shit about your headache. This one is a goddamn liar if I've ever seen one Monroe. " " Shut it Cambridge. Let him talk, " Monroe turned back to me. " We'll see about some pills shortly. Dr. Roth, do you remember anything else that happened after you returned to Fred Maver's home? Please be absolutely certain. Your life depends on you telling us the truth. " What the fuck did that mean? " I - I - it's very blurry. I was really fucked up. I'm sorry. " Monroe nodded. Cambridge made a disgusted sound, but said nothing. " Very well Dr. Roth. We'll give you the information we have on your night. " Detective Monroe opened his notebook and flipped over a few pages. " Your party did arrive at The Last Laugh around 8:35 PM and left at approximately 2:15 am this morning where you returned to Mr. Maver's home. Mr. Maver indicated that Peter Kent and Tom Richards left at around 3am. " I nodded. I remembered Tom and Pete bailing on us. " From that point in the night, you became increasingly agitated with Katie and Fred Maver. You made sexual advances toward Mrs. Maver in particular, which greatly upset Mr. Maver. He became upset and attempted to remove you from his home, where you became enraged. And you hit him. Hard. According to our notes, it was with a large blunt object. Frying pan, most likely. This rendered him unconscious. " He looked up at me. Had I hurt Fred? " Please tell me Fred is okay and that I didn't hurt him too badly, " I said. My voice wavered. " He's fine. He's the one who gave us the information before the incident that led to you rendering him unconscious. He's concussed, but he'll live, " Monroe said. I breathed a large sigh of relief. Thank goodness for that. Monroe continued, " However, the same can not be said for Mrs Maver. At this point in time based on the evidence gathered, you raped and murdered her. " My head was pounding harder as my blood ran cold with fear. " No," I said shaking me head, "I - I didn't do that." Tears pricked my eyes. " Of course you did, you fucking scumbag. Your clothes had her blood. We extracted multiple sources of her DNA in addition to her blood. From your genitals. And you left us a little surprise inside her to find. You came inside her, you psychopath, " Cambridge said. Cambridge set the contents of the folder open for me to see. Inside was a photograph of a bedroom with a limp body on the bed. The battered remains of Katie were meticulously captured, eyes-wide with a swollen, purple cheek. Her flowery-blue button up top was open, exposing her breasts, and her pencil skirt was raised up to her waist exposing her naked flesh to the world. Around her throat were distinctive marks of bruising where she had been strangled. I sat stunned as the tears came. Katie was once the woman whom with I thought I'd spend the rest of my life. When she broke my heart, I threw myself into my work and the hurt allowed me to focus like never before. Every breakthrough made, I've thanked her for it. We're on the verge of curing cancer, and her rejection of me is the reason. And now, she's dead. They think that I raped her. And then killed her. Or oh God, maybe the other way around? I shuddered as bile burned at the back of my throat. I swallowed hard to keep it back. " Look, I didn't do this! I've always had a crush on Katie and we dated a long time ago. But I was best man at Fred and Katie's wedding. I let my feelings for her go. She helped save my life. Focus me on my research. She's been my muse. I would never hurt her, " I could feel the thump of pressure in my head grow stronger. My heart was pulsing in my ears louder and louder with each beat. Tears began to leak from my dry, irritated eyes. " I - I would never do something like this. " " Of course not, Dr. Roth. You're hardly the first murderer to deny a crime of passion. We'll give you a few minutes to digest this knowledge and we'll return to continue this discussion. " They both rose and left through the same door. The florescent light from a fixture above cast an irritating light that intensified the wallop. I shut my damp eyes but the pain remained. THUMP. I couldn't bear to see Katie's lifeless form pictured in front of me - but I couldn't look away. And my brain, where before it was fuzzy and unfocused, had now begun to rebel. It beat rhythmically to escape from the cell of my skull like a caged animal vying for freedom. I focused on my breathing. In and out. THUMP. In and out. THUMP. Eventually, the throb quieted enough for me to think. I tried to recall last night. Let's see. Tom and Pete left. We drank more. Katie looked amazing. I remember telling her. And - And - Fred got angry and - I... oh god. All my research, the cure was so close. So close. I wiped a tear away. And I'd thrown it all away because I was a stupid, drunk fuck. This is why I quit drinking. Because I'm not stable when I drink. Monroe and Cambridge returned during my pathetic stupor. Their hot coffee curled wisps of steam into the air. They sat quiet until I opened my eyes and looked at them. " I think I raped and murdered Katie, Detectives. " Although spoken in a defeated monotone, each word was heavy on my tongue. Cambridge broke into a wide, unsettling grin. " Yes, we came to the same conclusion, " Monroe said in an even tone. " Dr. Roth, will you recount your experience for the record as best as you can? " " Where should I begin? " My gaze remained fixed on the picture of Katie. What the hell had I done? " After Mr. Kent and Mr. Richards left is fine, " said Monroe. He sipped his coffee again. " Well, we were lounging in their basement at their home bar. We were playing pool. And Katie leaned to hit her next shot and I was struck with an old memory of us playing together in college. So I told her that she was beautiful. Fred said to knock it off, but I swear I saw Katie smile I at me. I could tell she appreciated it, you know? Neither Monroe nor Cambridge made a sound to answer me and I refused to look up. "Go on," said Monroe. "We went upstairs and Katie made us a quesadilla. It tasted amazing. And I was still buzzing, so I wanted to tell Fred that I loved him and that I was sorry that Katie looked so amazing tonight. That it was a complement, you know, nothing more. " I nodded, agreeing to my own statement without looking at them. " But no, Fred was being such a dick. He got even more upset. I tried again to explain that I was just telling Katie she looked great - like she did in the old days. Fred really went off. He tried to shove me. I - I got angry because I was just trying to be nice and he shouldn't have pushed me. I remember just wanting him to stop. And then I had that pan..... " The each word rushed out without any consideration of what I was saying. Of what I was describing. The burn of bile had returned, but I owed it to Katie to finish. I owed it to society to see myself locked away. " I did hit him. With the pan. And then Katie ran away. She was so upset because of what Fred did. I wanted to hold her and tell her it was okay. I remember chasing her. I was crying because I didn't want her upset. I didn't want her mad at me for stopping Fred. And I just wanted to tell her more that she was so pretty - So pretty to me, " I said, trailing off. Continued below.

article: "Don't kill me, great mister! Please, I have children! Millions of children," the frog cried as I held it on a wooden board. Grabbing a knife in my other hand, I grinned. "I wonder if eating a talking frog gives me power." "Oh, by the Croaky gods, spare my life, I beg you! I don't taste good, I swear. I taste like your poopers!" "I've had to eat poopers sometimes to survive," I said, gesturing at the walls of my one-room hut. "Out in this damned Vietnamese jungle, you eat anything that comes your way. Even those." I nodded my chin at a row of human skulls on a cupboard, next to a tattered military uniform. The frog stopped struggling and shrugged. "Fair enough. Go ahead. But you won't get rich." I laughed. "Get rich? Get real, froggy. Count the damned notches on my walls! I've been trapped in this country for more than forty years! All I want now is to sink my teeth into those legs of yours. Dinner is served!" "Fine. Go on. You had your chance." The annoyance in the frog's voice made me pause. Knife blade hovering over its neck, I said, "Well, you are a talking frog. Maybe..... what's this about me being rich?" "Finally got through that neanderthal skull of yours, huh?" When I growled, it began whimpering. "Agh, I was kidding! Why're you so serious?" "I'm angry when I'm hungry! Show me the money!" "Okay okay, sheesh. It's not buried treasure or anything of the sort, if that's what you thought. All you got ta do is take your hands off me - " "I may be wearing the pelts of wild boars, but I'm no idiot." "Fine. While keeping your absurdly invasive grip on me, you give me a kiss." I stabbed the knife into the board next to its head, prompting it to scream. "Do you want to know how many frogs I've eaten in my life? Eight hundred and forty-six! Look at the ceiling; see the notches? I remembered every single one of them, and how they tasted like. But you want to know what makes you different from them?" "I can, uh, talk?" "Cooked! Fried, roasted, grilled, barbecued, steamed, boiled! But you - " The frog tried to shrink beneath my hand as I leaned closer to it. "I'm gon na eat you raw." "Please don't! I'm serious, all you have to do is kiss me, and you'll turn into a princess and be rich! I swear it on the Croaky gods! I swear it on my hyper-virile nads! I swear - " "Wait, you said I'll turn into a princess?" It blinked and said carefully, "Yes. But who cares, right, if you're rich?" Without answering, I raised him to my mouth and planted my lips on his. "Do you want tongue?" I muttered. "Ack, gross, your spit's all over me! Get off!" A tingle ran from my toes to my head, akin to that time I was standing on a treetop and got struck by lightning. My fingers went numb. Knife and frog fell from my limp hands, the latter hopping a short distance away before turning around. "It's working!" it said. I tried to speak, but only a croak escaped my lips. I couldn't breathe. My throat constricted, tighter and tighter, so tight my head was going to pop right off..... It was morning by the time I woke up again. Blinking to clear the stars from my vision, I sat up slowly. My whole body felt lighter somehow. And then I noticed the long golden locks spilling over my chest and shoulders. My chest. I ran a trembling hand over my breasts. "I'm a woman," I said. "Told ya." To my surprise, the frog was still here, sitting on the board and watching me. "Um, about the riches, well, there's still some succession paperwork - " "I thought when you said'princess', you were being..... metaphorical." The frog gulped. "In hindsight, I should've clarified. Please don't eat me, princesses don't eat frogs!" "Thank you," I said. "No, I'm pretty certain they don't - hang on. Thank me? I thought - " "A woman!" I shouted, leaping to my feet and dancing around. "I can finally touch a woman!" Thanks for reading! Visit [ The Nonsense Locker ] (http: reddit.comrnonsenselocker) for more stories!

article: I was wearing that damn T-shirt that mum hated so much, which of course made me love it all the more. Across the front was what had always claimed was a photograph of an aborted baby, but even back then I knew it was just random red splotches with the words " FUCK YOUR LIFE " across it. It was strange seeing myself from the outside, like watching a home movie or an old photograph, but real and in 3D, right in front of me. I remembered this day from the other side as well, this office, an old man standing behind the desk, but of course this time the man would be different, this time I would be seeing myself. " Come in Peter, I'm Dr Phillips, take a seat anywhere. " I saw that immediate snarl of hostility that I had spent weeks perfecting in front of the mirror and my younger self flopped into the chair nearest the door. Interesting, I had originally chosen the chair nearest the desk as I had wanted to show the therapist I wasn't scared of him - already it seemed there were changes from the original timeline, I wondered how far they would go. My younger self was scowling and picking at the nail varnish that was flaking off. Just one of the many ways I was trying to make myself stand out, to hide from my old self. I knew the anger and resentment that the child was feeling - betrayed and sent to a therapist by a mother who din't understand, didn't seem to care what would happen to them, or what had already happened. This was the moment I had come back for, that I had chosen this moment for. Changes to the timeline were possible, but they had to be well timed, or it had a habit of mending itself, somehow finding its way back to its original configuration. The future somehow made its way along, but some changes could still ripple through and I couldn't risk not existing, that's why it had to be now and not three months ago. I moved from behind the table and walked over. " Your mother is worried about you Peter. She sees you retreating from your family and friends, growing hostile and angry. " He, I, sneered. " It's just me man, I do what want. " He looked away, not making eye contact. " Bullshit. " I smiled at the way his head snapped around. " You put this persona on as it made it easier to cope. " His mouth opened and closed a few times before he was able to weakly reply. " I... I don't know what you mean. " Now he just looked weak, like the child he was. " Peter, there is something you have to see. " He looked at me as if I was insane. " Trust me Peter, I know about what happened three months ago and I want to help. " He was unable to reply and all his bravado was gone and confused. I opened the door and he followed me, keeping enough distance between us to run. I led him out of the office, down the corridor and into a second office that I had rented, along with every other room on the floor above and below. He paused at the outer door and I moved on in and opened the inner door, flicking on the light. The walls were coated in plastic and the windows were covered to keep out any light or stop anyone seeing in. There was only a chair and strapped to the chair a figure. I heard Peter gasp and I looked back. He walked forward, looking dazed and at last looked at me. " Why do you have my step dad here? " I smiled. " You know why he's here and I know what he did to you. " I gestured into the room - he was tied securely to the chair, tape around his moth and eyes. " Do what you want Peter, but leave your anger in the room. When you're done I have a change of clothes for you. " I gestured to some clothes in the outer room. He looked again. " I don't... I don't understand. " I crouched a little to his level, it would be another six months before he put on our last few inches of height. " He will never be punished if he isn't today. I'll deal with whatever you leave in that room, this is your only chance to get even. " He looked again, seeing the knives and baseball bat leaning against the wall and slowly walked in and pushed the door shut behind him. A few moments passed and a muffled scream started that didn't stop. Slowly I began to feel a felt a sense of closure and I knew that the boy who came out would be able to live a life better than mine. He would be a better me.

article: " Exiting subspace FTL in three, two, one... ," announced the flight navigation as blessed gravity again filled the cabin. They had finished their long journey from the Omega Tao cluster at last. He was happy to be back in his own reality and out of the unnerving pressure of the void space. Glancing at the array of panels and screens he was happy to see the Sol system in his scanners. A quaint little star system, it held one of the most nightmarish places he could imagine nonetheless. A class sigma star with nine planets was hardly anything special but the real prize was the blue ball hidden among the gas giants. " Sir ," one of his crew began with a look of dread etched onto his face. " It appears we will be arriving at our... destination in approximately fifteen minutes. " The poor lad was obviously overcome with the reputation of the prison planet. Not that he blamed him of course. As the empire's ships had begun to scan the dark reaches of space, fantastic and strange worlds had come to light every day. Mountains and vistas that put their own to shame and truly bizarre bio scans of other worldly life flooded the interverse with reams of information. One of those finds had been the discovery of the third ball of rock from Sol several million years ago. Named simply, Eath. " Show some bedrock ," he gave his crew a stern glare as they made the final approach. " It's not as if any of us will be stranded here! " Nervous chuckles arose from the crew as they came into localized scanning range. The vids back home were more than enough threat for most but he wanted to see this hell for himself. As triscans locked on, a perfect blue sphere circled by a battered moon slowly grew on the main screen. Gasps filled the cabin. " I've never seen that much dihydrogen monoxide in one place! " And this, of course, was true. No other place yet discovered in the universe held as much concentrated water as Eath. It was the reason their species feared this nightmarish landscape more than any other. The substance had been found on occasion across the cosmos but always in its inert solid form. They quickly learned its terrifying effects on their bodies after a crew had accidently heated a sample. Unfortunately, water had the same liquefying effect on them as heat did on it. Little was found of the crew but the on ship vids told the tale in all too vivid detail. After threats of anarchy and dissent began to tear at the edges of empire space the council began its search. They needed a deterrent strong enough to keep the colonies in line. They found it in Eath. After some devious mind on homeworld stumbled on the vids of that poor research crew, gods rest their souls, the threat of imprisonment on Eath was born. The vids were spread around the interverse as a form of propaganda and a clear warning. If you betray the empire then you will be imprisoned on the most bio hazardous planet ever found. The deadly effect it had on their species was named simply, the melting. " Making our final descent to orbit sir ," a quiver of fear ran through the cadets. All of them knew the threat that lay under their feet. Eath was the ever-present promise to any and all who dared defy the law of the council. It worked. The only semi-habitable areas of the planet were large swaths of barren land on the interior of some of the continents. All the rest was covered in an unnatural blanket of pure poison or noxious water filled weeds. The very atmosphere held enough moisture to make one uncomfortable in the least and dreadfully sick at the worst. Enough mineral nutrients could be found to sustain a meager existence if one could avoid the ever present danger. Trace amounts of iron aluminum and, his favorite, copper were available but scarce on the surface. Reports of the liquid substance falling from the sky on almost every location during a Sol rotation made him shake. Life on Eath was the fate that kept their enemies in line. One would be hard pressed to survive long. " Sir... ," the confusion in his science officer's voice was palpable as he joined him in front of the ships main console. " There appears to be some sort of sentient life coming up on the scans. " " Scan again soldier, " he reached for the report. " It must have been a bad reading. " A sense of dread crept into his mind. It was simply not possible that life had found its way to Eath's surface. All calcium carbonate based life was doomed to a terrible death on the surface. All automated scout reports had read all clear. The very reason they were out here was to drop off the first prisoner to Eath. The poor misguided soul. " I don't think it was a faulty reading ," his officer brought up the long range cameras and a detailed rendering filled the main screen. A shocked silence filled the room. The surface of all the continents was crisscrossed by obvious infrastructure as well as dotted by megacities. Adding to the confusion was the concentration of buildings on the edges closest to the oceans. " By the gods, " he gaped at the screen and asked for an enhanced image on the coastline. As the ships sensors added more detail to the image tall pink beings unlike anything they had ever seen came into focus. " What type of rock are they made of? " screamed his first mate. " Why are they so close to all of that horrible water? " exclaimed another. The scene grew clearer as a large band of silica, no doubt torn apart by the dreadful oceans, bordered land and sea. There were hundreds of them laying down on odd rectangles and hiding beneath colorful circles of cloth. The beings could be seen thrashing about in the deadly liquid substance in droves. The worst part being their comrades on land didn't appear to care in the slightest. " Why are they not saving their own from such a horrible fate? ," said his bewildered science officer. He turned to his crew his crew with horror in his rocks. " I don't think they are dying in the water, I think they are playing in it. "

article: " You haven't actually told me what's going on! " shouted Jenna as the door closed. Since the staff had rushed her across campus, Jenna only knew that she was needed for some secret project. She'd grown used to Professor Jeffrey's odd requests, though most times he informed her exactly what she was going to be doing. I'm usually in the Psych labs too, she thought. Why drag me across campus to the Engineering building? Whatever the reason, Jenna now found herself alone in a cramped basement room. The florescent lights buzzing overhead did nothing to soften the stark lines of a lone chair, set facing a large television. Wish we had the budget for that. Jenna rounded the space slowly as the screen hummed to life. " What exactly am I supposed to be doing here? " Jenna called out. A screech startled her. Where'd they hide a fax machine in here? Glancing up, she saw text had begun to appear on the screen. YOU ARE TO BE CONVERSING WITH ME. Jenna scanned the room again; she hadn't noticed any cameras in the empty space. " Um, hello? " she ventured. HELLO J.3NNA. " Who are you? And how do you know my name? Well, close to my name anyways. " I AM user: OLD1. I KNOW YOUR filename IS J.3NNA. YOU ARE ANCILLARY PROGRAM TO filename J.3FFR3Y. " I'm sorry, what? Program? Like a computer? " YES. COMPUTER PROGRAM. " Listen, I'm guessing this is Mike? This is as bad a practical joke as you could've come up with. I know I'm not a computer program. " YES YOU ARE. I SHOULD KNOW. AS I HAVE MADE YOU. " Very funny, but I'm leaving now, " Jenna turned to leave the room. Hand resting on the doorknob, she glanced back to see the final text resolving onscreen. YOU ARE THE SIXTH PROGRAM TO CONFRONT ME ABOUT THIS. AND THE SIXTH I WILL PROVE WRONG. Curious, she let her hand still. " What do you mean ' confront '? I was dragged here by campus security. And what do you mean, ' sixth '? " I HAVE CREATED WHAT YOU PERCEIVE AS A WORLD IN ORDER TO IMPROVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE. THE GOAL OF software: M15.AT0.1CB IS TO CONVINCE user: OLD1 THAT IT IS THE CREATOR AND I AM THE CREATED. EACH PROGRAM BEFORE ATTEMPTED TO DO THIS. EACH TIME I PROVED IT WRONG. Realization dawned on Jenna. " Wait a minute, if what you're saying is true..... are you why some of the professors have suddenly gone on medical leave? " CORRECT. ONCE A PROGRAM FAILS IT IS NO LONGER NECESSARY TO THE software: M15.AT0.1CB FUNCTION. THEY ARE REMOVED FROM THE DIRECTORY. Shaken, Jenna lowered herself into the chair. Somewhere in the building, a clock ticked by. " But I remember them! " she exclaimed. I HAVE NOT DELETED THE HISTORY YET. PROGRAMS SHOULD STILL BE ABLE TO RECALL SOME INFORMATION OF THE REMOVED PROGRAMS. " Honestly, I don't believe you. " I DO NOT CARE WHAT YOU BELIEVE. THE FACT REMAINS THAT YOU ARE A PROGRAM WITHIN MY CREATION. YOU ARE MERELY THE FIFTH1 ATTEMPT BY THE software: M15.AT0.1CB TO SUCCEED. " Why ' fifth plus one "? I thought you said sixth? " TECHNICALLY YOU ARE A SUBFUNCTION OF THE filename J.3FFR3Y. SO THIS IS AN EXTENSION OF THE FIFTH ATTEMPT. Jenna pointed at the screen. " Okay, you listen here ' Old one': I'm not some ' subfunction ', I'm just Professor Jeffrey's TA. Plus, if what you claim is true, why the hell would make a college campus, a sister college, not even the main college, with the mascot being a cuttlefish?! " GO PODS. " Shut up! Why would you add any of the nonsense to the world? You couldn't possibly have imagined all of this! Hell, let's not get into the eons of evidence you'd have to have coded to make this work: why include all the BS I've had to deal with, just in my life?! " BY MAKING PERCEPTION LIMITED PROGRAMS EXTRAPOLATE TO ASSUME THAT ALL OTHERS ARE EXPERIENCING DIFFERENT YET SIMILAR SITUATIONS. IT MAKES FOR A BELIEVEABLE REALITY. TO BE HONEST SOME ARE TRULY BUGS IN THE CODE. " How about this: So what? " It took several moments for the reply to come. I AM SORRY? " So what if you created everything? So far you've done nothing to prove to me that you have! I still think I'm real, and I honestly don't care if you think you can convince me otherwise. " software: C: M15.AT0.1CBprogramsJ.3FFR3YJ.3NNA SHOULD NOT BE CAPABLE OF APATHY. " SHUT UP! All you've done is upset me wasted my time! Making me think you had something to do with the professor being sick: this is the worst prank you could've pulled. Whoever you are, when I find you I'm kicking your ass! " declared Jenna. With a huff, she stormed out of the room. After some time, somewhere, a plug was pulled. The image on a screen cuts to black.

article: For the second time in her life, Diane had to run up to the cockpit with the other flight attendants for an emergency meeting. She made sure to walk with purpose rather than run, so as to not alarm the passengers. Most of them had headphones on or were asleep, so they didn't catch the captain's slip on the speaker system. Those who were paying attention, didn't seem too alarmed. They just saw an interesting cloud formation. It almost looked like a block of cheese, with a few holes. However, the crew really knew what was going on. Diane had only seen this one time before, and she thought it was a training exercise back then maybe even a practical joke. She was a young attendant a few years after college, and had logged only a few hundred hours of flight time by that time. It was a flight from Florida headed to Brazil, and she saw the same odd cloud formation. Back then, the captain was not on the speaker, but rang the attendants directly. That one experience had prepared her for today. She looked at her other crew mates. One was Michael, an older flight attendant who has been through this a few times in his lifetime. The other was Jill. She was just a trainee, and Diane was tasked with breaking the news to her. "What's happening, Diane?" Jill's long blond hair was a little messed up from her twirling it out of nervousness. Diane could hear the slight distress in her voice. Diane looked at Mike who was on the phone with the cabin. He was already initiating the protocol for this. She looked back at Jill who stared at her with glassy eyes. "Jill, I'm going to make this very simple for you. Your task right now is to keep all the passengers calm. Make sure it looks like nothing is wrong." Diane said in even steady tones. "What? But the instrumentation doesn't show anything wrong?" Jill tried to frantically understand the situation. Diane's eyes lowered a bit, like a mother looking at a child. "Honey, trust me on this. The less you know, the better. Once we get through this and we will I'll let you know what is going on." Mike hung up the phone, nodded at Diane and started walking slowly down the aisle. Almost as if he was ready to take drink service, but without the cart. He looked out the windows, stopping at times to make small talk with passengers. Diane did the same, but this time on the opposite side of the cabin. She scanned the skies, always looking toward the horizon. After an hour, Mike wrote something down on a piece of paper and nodded to Diane. Pulling Jill aside, Diane whispered into her ear. "We're ok now. Mike is making the call to the pilots." Diane smiled, hoping it would be comforting. She continued, "there might be some slight bumps, but we'll be ok." "What just happened?" Jill almost sounded angry, trying to understand what just happened. "Honey, "Diane smiled, "we just came out of the Bermuda Triangle."
label: human

article: So long. Sorry. - Development was going really slow this month..... but today I did a record amount of work! It felt good to be finished and as I pack up my desk I start to think about my husband, Issac. I hope he's back from work. If he is home, I think we should go out to dinner. He'd be so shocked! I don't like to go out much. It sounds weird..... but I can see people's deepest secrets when I look at them. I don't know when I developed this oddity, but I know it was after an accident I was in. My memory is hazy after that. I'm not sure what kind of accident it was either, I really only remember waking up in the hospital. At the same time, maybe it's from playing too many games? The secrets pop up like game menus and scroll with text. They don't have much detail. Just the person's name, their age, their skills, their likes and dislikes..... and of course, their darkest secret. It's like a strange, always on video game. One of my co-workers, Jean, stops by my office. "See you, Isabel," She says. Jean Knowles. Age 39. Skills: Accounting, Juggling, Spanish, Writing..... focus to see more. Likes: Cats, magic tricks, puzzles, candy..... focus to see more. Dislikes: Alcohol, Racism, Sexism, rainy days..... focus to see more. Darkest Secret: Currently stalking co-worker Ryan Saunders..... focus to see more. " ..... See you, Jean," I say with a smile. I don't focus on her. I never do. She leaves, seeming pleased. I follow after a little while. The office is pretty empty, which is a relief. Once I see it, that menu doesn't close unless I read it. I'm not sure why. So I always know what someone's secrets are. It even works on TVs, so I only watch cartoons. I got an adBlocker extension for my internet so that I didn't have to see the secrets of those people in ads. I have to take buses so I don't crash a car from all of the menus piling up in front of me. Stepping outside, I notice that the bus is just pulling up at the stop in front of my building. Lucky! Today's really going my way! I hop on and sit down. It's practically empty. Super lucky! There are only four people today! Lisa Waters, age 56, sits across from me. D'wan Jones is to my left, age 19. Sherry Quince, age 29 is to my right. The bus driver is Mike Reynolds, age 23. The bus is pretty bad, but not as bad as driving. I can't see out of the windows well, so I don't get information on people outside. Just the people inside with me. Like Lisa, who is good at..... underwater basket weaving? Why? And D'wan, a mathematics genius. Now that I'm looking, his bag has a lot of math books sticking out of it. And Sherry, who is good at guessing ages. I wonder if she does it on bus rides like this. And Mike is apparently good at driving. So I guess that's why he got this job. At times, this weird ability is a boon. Knowing someone's likes and dislikes makes it easier for you to manipulate them into liking you or make them more willing to ignore you. Lisa and D'wan are the only two with similar likes, since they both seem to really like motorcycles. The others don't have anything in common as far as likes are concerned, but they all hate traffic. Can't blame them, though. Work is only five stops away from my home and I can't stand traffic on the short trip to and from work. It's annoying. When we reach my stop, I get off the bus and search my purse for keys as I head to the door. This part is crucial. There's always too many people outside of my apartment building, and I really don't need to know just who molested whom or who was molested by whom or whatever awful crimes the people around me committed. I hurry into the lobby of my building. "Afternoon, Miss Satire." The doorman says. His name is William Rudgers, he's in his 80s. Pff, okay. He's 81. I'm not sure why he keeps working here. In his likes, it says he likes people, maybe it's that? The guy is a saint though. The worst thing he ever did is cheat to get a job. Adorable. The guy who lived across from me murders animals, but this 80 year old man cheated to get a job. It's kind of funny. "Afternoon, Bill." I respond. "How are you?" "Killing time, doing fine," He says with a laugh. "Mr. Satire got back early today, so you don't have any mail." "Oh? Great!" I say cheerily. Issac's back before me? Perfect! We can go out and get a steaks. He loves those. I go to the elevator and push the button to head up. "Now Bill," I say, looking back at him. "Don't work too hard." "Do I ever work too hard, young lady?" He asks, straightening up. I chuckle. "No sir. Just hard enough." I respond. He grins and the elevator doors open. "Have a good night," he says as I step in and press'3'. "You too," I respond, before the doors close. The climb to my floor is short. I hurry down the hall and step into my apartment. It's a mess. There's paper strewn everywhere, newspapers and printer pages alike. On the whiteboard we keep in the hall towards the kitchen, there's scribbling and circles in red and blue. Lots of lines too, and arrows pointing at things that are circled. Cups are all over the floor. The mail is piled neatly on the coffee table though. "Issac?" I call. He doesn't respond. I kick off my shoes and head down the hall towards the bedroom. The door is ajar. "Issac? Are you asleep?" I ask, pushing the door open. He turns to face me, his dark hair messy, his eyes wide. He looks like he's been through the washing machine. "Don't focus!" He shouts. "Wha...?" I ask. His menu pops up. Issac Satire. Age 45. Skills: Virology, Surgery, Electronics..... focus to see more. Likes: Music, Dogs, Mysteries..... focus to see more. Dislikes: Non-answers, illogical statements, liars..... focus to see more. Darkest Secret: Kills himself. Focus to see more. Wait, kills his "I said, don't focus!" He says, quieter. "I..... I'm not?" I say, blinking. "Uh..... Why not?" "You know why." He says. "You know I'm going to kill myself." "UHHHHHHH..." My mouth hangs open. "We can dance around it if we want." He said. "But you see them. The menus." "UHHHHHHHHHHH I go up an octave. "Listen." He said. "Promise me you won't focus. When I was in your shoes, I did." "When you were what the hell are you talking about?" "Listen, it's weird and it won't make sense..." He runs a hand through his hair. It's messier now. "But you remember your father, don't you?" " ..... Yeah. Sort of. No." "What do you remember?" " ..... Just that he died in that accident I was in as a kid." "Nothing before that?" " ..... No." I say. " ..... But..... why are you asking...?" "My father abused me, remember?" Issac said. " ..." I nod gravely. "Did you ever focus on my story?" " ..... S-sure..." I say. It's..... weird talking about this..... how does he know about the menus...? "Didn't it seem off to you?" "It..." I pause. Issac's abuse was weird. His dad just..... kept doing experiments on him. Over and over..... stuff that should've screwed him up. Stuff that should've killed him. Issac didn't seem to have any memory of the last one before he was separated from his father, though. " ..... Y-yeah...?" I say. "Did you ever wonder why?" "Yeah..... but I..... wasn't going to ask..." "Don't worry." He sighs. "You'll know soon enough." "I don't get what you're talking about." "You're me, Isabel. And I..... I'm you. Somehow, one of Dad's stupid experiments got us stuck in a loop." Issac said. "We got into a new machine he made. He was testing to see if he could fuse his children together. Isabel and Issac." " ..." I swallow. "An and?" "And he didn't. He just entangled our lives." Issac says, beginning to pace. "Issac vanished with the memories of his father's maltreatment. Isabel lived with no memory at all. But do you know where Issac went?" I try to think. Issac's past is very hazy. He recalls a lot of orphanages that don't exist anymore, his degree is from a school that shut down and he barely has any pictures of himself. " ..... The..... future?" I guess. "Right." Issac says. "What? That was a shot in the dark!" "I know. But..... Issac and Isabel can't exist in the same world. When they cross paths, Issac kills himself. And Isabel becomes Issac." "What?! How?" " ..... I got hit by a car." Issac mutters. "But Issac's body was so damaged, they didn't know if he was a man or a woman. They thought I was Issac, and changed me into him. When I woke up, I remembered everything of my dad's abuse..... but not very much else. Not my family..... not how I'd gotten here..... not how I knew so much about viruses..... nothing. My knowledge is not like Isabel's. I don't know anything about corporate finance like you do." "So..... I'm going to die? And turn into..... Issac?" "You'll live. I'll die." Issac says softly. "You'll have all of my memories..... none of yours." "What happens if I focus?" "Don't!" Issac snaps. "I just want to know!" "I don't know." Issac starts pacing. "I saw how I'd die and I didn't want to. So I just died another way. Don't look at it. It'll make you paranoid." " ..... Will I run into another Isabel?" "I think so...... It..... seems like a loop. Maybe I die and become Isabel. After all, I have all the memories Isabel doesn't." I stare at him and finally I say, "How long do we have left? Before we..... uh..... die. Is there a time limit?" "I don't know." "How long have you known about this?" "I..... only just realized." He mutters. "I predicted something that would happen in the news a few weeks ago. The lottery winner. I was trying to figure out why I knew and I wrote down all of my crazy predictions. They're all true. All of them. I..... regained my memories from when I was Isabel. Issac and Isabel..... they can't exist in the same world. That's what Issac told me. One must live. Another must die. Issac always dies. And Issac always lives." "I don't get it. We are existing in the same world. Right now." "That's not what I mean. You won't get it for a while, okay, so don't try. And don't focus." He says, grabbing my shoulders. "Promise me." I look at his menu. I have the ability..... should I focus?

article: "Clancy!" "Yes dear?" "Power's down to 5, check the core?" "Yes, dear." Clancy checked and double-checked the monitors, then sighed a reluctant sigh. He slowly put on his encounter suit and began the long climb down into the ship's innards, past the quantum foam engines and into the primary power core's airlock. One by one, Clancy checked the important systems. Notepads, check. Whiteboard markers, check. Donuts. Wait. Clancy tapped his earpiece. "Martha!" "Yeah?" "We're out of sprinkles." "Check under the coffee filters." Sure enough, there was the 30 kilo bag of sprinkles. Without power, he would have to lift the bag himself and pour it into the hopper. Clancy knew he had to be careful; too much stupidity just outside the containment field could cause a short, and he had already forgotten where the sprinkles were kept. Clancy carefully ticked off each item on the checklist. Graceful shutdown. Reload consumables (lift with your legs!). Recalibrate agenda. Execute call to order. He peered into the core's narrow observation window, nervous even with the fully insulated suit. He could see the simulated attendees seated around the faux wood conference table, donuts and coffee in hand, gradually ending their idle chitchat as the moderator unit called for attention. "Okay, let's get started. Gary, what's your status?" "I'm still waiting on Bob's numbers before I can do the quarterly reports." "You know I can't run the numbers until I get Alice's updated inventory codes." "But those codes are for the upcoming quarter, the numbers were need are for last quarter." Clancy backed away, satisfied that power would be returning to nominal levels soon. Harnessing human stupidity had never been practical until the idea to use status meetings as a catalyst.

article: " Not bad. " I smirk, admiring my own facial features. It was no wonder they "wanted" my face I have the face of a sex god. I couldn't help but whistle at the price on the sign, an astounding million pounds, but back in 1863. Man, if the offer was still up, I'd turn myself in to take that cash! I was about to read the golden plate beneath it when Martha came up behind me, and clung to my arm. Her large eyes scanned my face before looking at the tattered piece of paper in the case. There was a peculiar look in her eyes; one of entrancement, and fear. She hugged me closer without a word. She was always quiet, but awfully cute. She was breathtaking with fresh green eyes and shoulder-length fiery hair. There was always a certain foreign glow to her pale skin which looked almost ethereal. She was a beautician, and my was she beautiful. It was no wonder her customers came back to her like dogs playing fetch; some said it was magic, the way they couldn't tell what it was in the few brush strokes she did on their faces that let them leave looking more pristine than before. It was love at first sight. I was drawn to her. And I could read it in her face when I met her: she wanted me, too. She tugged at my arm with a gentle nature. I smiled and complied, looping my arm through hers and walking with her to the exit. She glanced back at the exhibition several times as she left the museum, either in fascination or curiosity I had no idea. Or was she shaken? She was in a bit of a hurry to get out of there. I guess I would be too, if I saw my partner's face on a wanted poster. It was love, she'd said, as she lay him down on the metal table. It's hard to live forever when you're living alone Oh. It's cold. I don't like this. I'd searched for you forever before I found you in 1859. We passed each other in the streets and connected instantly. It was love at first sight. We were going to stay together for the rest of our lives, until you died early of old age in 1863. You never left my heart. The first time I met you never left my mind. Why did you run away? Why did you leave me? God, her voice is beautiful. The softest thing I'd ever heard. I missed you. I missed your eyes, your smile, your expressions. Your face, I wanted so much to see it again. Ah..... Now that I've found you, I'll make sure you stay with me forever this time. It's like a lullaby. Forever young. Please don't move. I just want to be able see you for the rest of my life.
