article: Early on the morning of her twenty first birthday, the doorbell rang. Everyone in the apartment had been out late the previous night and was still in bed. Jessica was the only one to hear it, and she knew what it was. The package with her milestone genie bottle had arrived. She sat up, put on a pair of jeans, and went downstairs to the door. There it was, in iridescent silver packaging, containing a translucent, ruby colored crystalline bottle. Just like the ones she had received on her 5th, 13th, and eighteenth birthdays. As she held it in her hands, she thought of her prior milestone wishes. On her fifth birthday, she had wasted her wish on a new front tooth to replace the one that had just fallen out. She didn't realize that it would have grown back on its own. On her thirteenth birthday, she had wished for elf ears, which she still had and enjoyed enormously, always adorning them with the cutest earrings to make sure everyone noticed them. On her eighteenth birthday, she wished for usable wings, both because of their beauty and because she had many friends who could fly now, and wanted to have the power and enjoyment they derived from it. It had not disappointed her. It was especially wonderful on last year's trip to the Grand Canyon, where the aerial views were astonishingly breathtaking. She had thought a long time about what she would like to wish for this year, and had finally come to a decision. She wanted big breasts. Although her pixie-like figure matched well with her wings and elf ears, she felt as if she never really got the attention of men as much as she'd like and after having watched a number of infomercials about modern breast enhancement techniques, she concluded that it was because of her cup size. The medical solutions were too expensive on her student budget, so she would save her money and ask the milestone genie to grant her large breasts. She wanted to make the wish and undergo the change as soon as possible. She and her roommates planned on going out for brunch this morning, and she wanted to impress them all with her new buxom beauty. Following the instructions in the package, she rubbed the bottle and softly chanted the necessary incantations. The bottle lit up and a smooth male voice said " Congratulations! It's your twenty first birthday. Thanks to the generosity of our glorious leaders and corporate sponsors, today you have been granted the body enhancement of your choice. How may I be of assistance today? " " Dear genie, oh genie. Please grant me, on this my twenty first birthday, very large breasts. " The voice emanated from the bottle again " Your wish is my command. It shall be granted. This bottle contains a small tablet. Swallow this tablet with a full glass of water. The changes you requested will become effective within the next hour. Jessica didn't wait for the message to end. She pried open the bottle's pill compartment, put the pill in her mouth, and washed it down with diet cola. Then she went back to her room and turned on the television, anxiously awaiting the results. Within five minutes, her breasts were about one inch larger. By the first commercial break, they had doubled in size. That was about the amount of change she had hoped for, and she stood admiring her profile in the mirror. She would have to buy some new bras and shirts. A little expensive, but she would make it work, she decided. It would be fun to refresh her wardrobe a bit. By the twenty minute mark, they had doubled in size again, to about the size of basketballs. This was more than she had bargained for. She read over the genie bottle instruction brochure again to see if there was some way to halt the process. As she did so, her breasts had grown to the size of beach balls. Five minutes later, they were the size of pilates balance balls and were starting to block her view. She had to hold the instruction brochure at arm's length to find the customer service number. She found her phone and dialed it with one hand. A recording of soft music and a pleasant female voice was on the line " Your call is important to us. Please stay on the line and we will be with you shortly. Our glorious leaders and corporate sponsors are so pleased to provide you with the very best in milestone body enhancement technology. Your tax dollars and generous support makes it possible. Please consider a donation to Milestone Partners. We will be with you shortly... " Jessica's breasts were now equal in diameter to her height. She could no longer hold them up. Resting on them like two gigantic pillows, she struggled to keep the phone to her ear. Finally, a human voice was on the line. " Millenial Partners. Please hold... " Jessica pressed the mute button briefly and screamed out her frustration. Her roommate, Claire had heard and was standing outside the door " Jess, are you ok? " The customer service agent was back on the phone. With the phone still muted, Jessica shouted " Yeah, I'm good " and pushed the lock on the door. She unmuted the phone and half-whispered her situation to the agent. " Oh, honey! " said the agent with a sweet Southern drawl. " You did get yourself in a little fix there didn't ya? You know you're not supposed to take those pills out until the genie's done talking and the thing pops open. They just aren't ready yet. " She paused and Jessica though she could hear a faint chuckle in the background. Were they actually laughing at her? " OK, sweetheart. Here's what you got ta do. On the other side of the bottle, there's a little button. Press that and there's another pill. Take that and those boobs of yours will shrink back down to size in no time. Now that means you're not going to get an enhancement this year, but at least you'll get out of your predicament. " Jessica did as the woman suggested and as soon as she was able to, laid back on her bed waiting for the reversal process to complete. She was utterly humiliated, not only by the botched enhancement procedure, but by her own desire to have larger breasts in the first place. Why was everyone so hung up on enhancements anyway? Wasn't it already amazing enough to he human, to be alive, to live in a beautiful and complex world, and to be here with each other? Their glorious leaders and corporate sponsors could go enhance themselves to death as far as she was concerned. She was done with it. That morning at brunch, as she and Claire sat with their friends at the Sunnyside Cafe, Claire asked, " So Jessica, you're twenty one. What enhancement are you going for this year? " Jessica smirked and took a sip of her mimosa. " I already got it this morning. It's self esteem. "

article: Asmodeus was not the marrying kind. Not that he opposed marriage as a principle; if others chose to live in a hell of their own making, perhaps it would better prepare them for the realm he called home. And there were the wives He loved wives. Eating them. In front of their husbands and such. But to marry one of his own? To love and to cherish? It went against his principles. He would die first. And it was at the point of his own death that Asmodeus found, as so many do, that he was not overly attached to his principles after all. "May I have a moment of your attention, beautiful one?" She looked around, wondering if there were anyone else in this bleak cave he could be addressing. A perfect ingenue. The leathery winged creature to his right, her blazing eyes searching this penal cavern for another beautiful lady, suddenly became possesed of something no living creature ever had before. Asmodeus' pity. "Are you talking to me?" "Yes of course, my ... captivating captor." She giggled, shifting the gargantuan crossbow she held to rest on her shoulder. Its cruel quarrels, harpoon-sized, clinked loudly in her quiver as she turned to face him. "Well, what is it you wanted to say?" "It was more of a question I wanted to ask. Although it is somewhat hard to speak through this muzzle. Perhaps I'd better forget it." She looked around, her masters absent. It had been more than an hour of standing sentinel in the darkness. She loosed the muzzle. Asmodeus gasped and stretched his tongue, just for a moment, before resuming the conversation. For the first time, the young demoness heard the masculine plush that was his Voice. "I was just wondering where your gems are." "My... gems?" "Yes, a lady of your rare beauty deserves to be draped in stones similarly rare." "Aww," she blushed, "that's the nicest thing I've ever heard. It's a shame they're gon na pull your tongue out and kill you." "And have the Gibbering Malice feast eternally on my eyeballs, yes. But in all seriousness, your are the most breathtaking of the daughters of Lilith I have ever beheld. Would that my eyeballs could feast eternally on you." "You're not so bad yourself." Asmodeus fixed his gaze into hers. [ I ] Unchain me, dammit! [ i ] She stepped back, gripping her crossbow in both hands once more. "I mean, you are bad. Stealing treasure from the Tearing Yawn? That's that's really bad. " "Impressed?" She nodded. "Reach into my pocket. The best jewels are there." A succubus looking scandalized. That was new. "Trust me. And you can keep them. I want you to get something from this job. Infernis know they don't pay you what you're worth. What you deserve." She came close, thrusting her hand into his pocket, her pale, freckled neck close enough to bite. He did, once. Gently. Her hand felt for the jewels and eventually found them. Large, faceted, faintly blue. They fluoresced in the gloom, casting a glow on her open mouth as she stared deep into them. There was a commotion at the cave entrance. Torches cast harsh yellow light and trailed ugly black smoke. "Go take a shower, Lex!" an unpleasant voice called out. "You're not needed here anymore. And settle your supply fee with the purser." "But I already paid!" "You eat twice as much as any of the rest of us. And still so scrawny!" He scuttled closer, slapping her rear with one of his appendages. "Half breed." Lex's face twisted into a malicious smile as she lifted the bow and aimed. "Wait. Where the fuck's his muzzle?!" was the last thing he ever said.

article: Judge Gravizort peeked through a gap in the curtains to look at the audience. A vast landscape of tentacles, antennae, tails, and horns packed the audience chamber. Big crowd tonight. There was an enormous glass panel dividing the audience chamber from the Stage of Justice. A trapdoor opened in the middle of the stage, emitting an evanescent purple gas. Two figures arose from the mist. One was a six-foot-tall horned owl, with manacles binding its legs and customized handcuffs around its wings. Megalorp, Judge Gravizort thought, trying to get himself in character, What a waste of nitrogen. I'm gon na stick him with the death penalty. The other figure was humanoid from the waist up, arachnid from the waist down. Two sets of mouths, both with yellow fangs. " All rise, " the humarachnoid figure said, " The Court is now in session. " He pulled down hard on Megalorp's chains. The owl fell onto a hoverchair. Restraints sprang out of the chair and looped around him. The spectators rushed up towards the barrier to get a better look at Megalorp. They smeared their noses and snouts against the glass. " Defiler! " they shouted, " Blasphemer! " they roared, " You'll be the death of us all! " they cried. " The honorable Judge Gravizort, now presiding, " the humarachniod shouted at the crowd. He flipped a switch and a glowing ' APPLAUSE'sign flashed at the audience. They clapped wildly, jostling each other to get a better view of the stage. Gravizort clutched the curtain tightly in his little green pincer. No, not yet, he thought to himself. Make them wait a little. Build the tension. He took out a compact mirror from the pocket of his long black robe. " Stacy! " he hissed. " Come fix the make-up on my mandible. There's a smudge. " A pony-centaur with rainbow-colored hair trotted over on tiny legs. " I'm so sorry Mr. Gravizort, sir, " she said, her delicate hands massaging his mandible with a cotton pad and then dabbing him with a spot of rouge. " Is that better your Honor, sir? " she asked with concern, holding out a mirror. Gravizort inspected himself. He was such a handsome praying mantis. The black velvet robes hung from his austere shoulders. His lustrous silver wig fit snugly atop his smooth green head. They wig's long bouncy curls hung down to his waist. He winked at himself in the mirror, and then shooed Stacy away. The applause was rising now. " Gra-vi-ZORT, " the crowd chanted, " Gra-vi-ZORT, " Judge Gravizort took a deep breath and fixed an ingratiating smile to his face. He swept through the curtains and entered the stage. The crowd shouted jubilantly. Gravizort wheeled around the perimeter of the stage, waving at audience members behind the glass, feigning profound gratitude, bowing slightly to every corner of the room and blowing kisses at attractive females. Eventually he came to the Bench of Justice and sat down. The APPLAUSE sign turned off. " EVERYONE SIT! " the humarachnoid shouted at the crowd. He snatched two plasma pistols from his waist and held them akimbo towards the audience, daring them to disobey him. " Thank you Frank, " Gravizort said to the humarachnoid, " Let's get started. " Frank nodded, still eyeing the crowd distrustfully. He said, " We go LIVE in 3...2...1...go! " A long robotic arm extended down from the ceiling, pointing a camera at Gravizort. He smiled at the camera. " Welcome, " he said, " to the Stage of Justice! The crimes are all real, and everyone is guilty! We've got a great show for you tonight, folks. We'll start an infamous criminal - I'm sure you've seen him on the news already - the one, the only... Megalorp! " The camera twisted around to look at the giant owl, heavily restrained on its floating bench. Megalorp turned his head away from the camera, looking nauseous. The camera returned to Gravizort. " Later on in the docket, we have a case of criminal negligence. Juicy! And afterwards we'll hear a case about a fistfight in the Galactic Congress. What a day! " Gravizort smiled, " Stick around after the show folks, it's game-night right here on Channel 2240. See Antionio Rodriguez, hall-of-fame goalkeeper, playing in his first RocketBall match since getting his leg re-attached. " The show's theme song played. " It's time for our first case! " Judge Gravizort said, " Megalorp. You stand accused of falsifying the data in your BioChemistry lab report. How do you plead? " The owl shifted his eyes uncomfortably. " Not guilty, " he mumbled. " Not guilty? " Gravizort said in astonishment. " Well, I don't believe you! " He slammed the gavel down with a bang. " Guilty! " Gravizort said, " I recommend the death penalty. What say you, members of the jury? " He looked at the crowd behind the plate glass divider. They hollered with reckless abandon. " Kill him! " they shouted, " He's a menace to society! " they screamed, " If you let him go, he's just going to do it again, " a hoarse man yelled. " Very well, " Gravizort said, " The jury has spoken. I, the honorable Judge Gravizort, do hereby sentence Megalorp to death by decapitation. Any last words, Megalorp? " " This isn't fair, " Megalorp said, " I just falsified a lab report. It's not a big deal. " Gravizort's eyes widened. " Not a big deal? " he said, " To falsify a lab report? " He looked at Megalorp in shock. " The very foundation of our society is the scientific method. Without science, we are nothing. You are a deceiver, a misleader, a hoodwinker, and a betrayer! You would have us follow you to our collective doom! " Spittle was flying from Gravizort's mouth. Megalorp mumbled, " It was just an experiment about some crop fertilizer. " " SILENCE! " Judge Gravizort said, banging his gavel so hard that it cracked. " Frank, " Gravizort said, " Carry out the sentence. " The humarachnoid approached Megalorp menacingly. Backstage, Stacy patted a little green man on the shoulders. " That's your cue, " she said. The little green man ran out onto the stage, waving his arms. " Stop! " he squeaked, " Stop this at once! " " What's this? " Judge Gravizort said, feigning surprise. " I'm his lawyer, " the little green man squeaked defiantly. " Don't you know who he is? " he jerked his thumb at Megalorp. " He is a criminal in my courtroom, " Judge Gravizort declared, " Justice is blind. " " He's very highly connected, " the lawyer said, " He's a member of the Lorpadorp family. His uncle is in the Galactic Senate and his cousin is the CEO of AndromedaCorp. His father is the dean at - " " Enough, " Judge Gravizort held up his pincer admonishingly. " But you can't kill him, " the lawyer squeaked, " He's untouchable! " Gravizort's face was a mask of fury. " No one is untouchable in my courtroom, " he said, " I charge you with contempt in court. " " What? " the little green man said helplessly. " GUILTY! " Judgeg Gravizort shouted, " Death by lethal injection! " The little green man gave a little scream and tried to run away. Restrains sprang out of the stage and manacled him to the floor. " Kill them both, " Gravizort said. Frank scuttled towards the little green man. He pulled out a syringe and held it up to the light. He pressed the plunger a little, and a mysterious milky liquid oozed out the tip of the needle. He stabbed the little green man in the neck and threw down the plunger. " AAAAaaaah, " the little green man screamed, " My organs are burning! " He gurgled and went limp. Frank scuttled towards the Megalorp, who was shaking with terror. " Twist his head off! " someone in the crowd shouted. Frank nodded. He stood behind the owl, his hands gripping its head. " Any last words? " Frank asked. Megalorp screamed. Frank twisted his head 180 degrees. Nothing happened. Megalorp blinked confusedly. Frank scuttled around a little and twisted Megalorp's head another 180 degrees. Nothing happened. Frustrated, Frank ran in circles around Megalorp, holding the owl's head tightly in his hands. CRACK! Megalorp's chin fell down to his chest. " And there you have it folks! " Judge Gravizort said, " Justice has been served. Now let's take a quick commercial break and we'll be back with our next case! " The lights dimmed and an opaque partition suddenly dropped in front of the glass barrier, blocking the audience's view of the stage. The little green man straightened himself up. " Can I get these chains off? " he asked. Stage Manager Bongor rushed onstage and helped him out of the restraints. " Hey Frank, " the little green man said, " Do you still have my insulin injector? " Frank handed him the needle. " Excellent job, " Stage Manager Bongor said to the little green man, handing him a sugar-free candy bar. " How are we doing over here? " he asked Megalorp. The owl raised his head to meet Bongor's gaze. " I'm fine, " he said. Bongor undid his restraints. Megalorp stood up and did some stretches. " Okay, " Stage Manager Bongor said, " Everybody get offstage, it's almost time for the next case. " Frank swore. " I can't remember my lines for this one. What's it about again? " " No, " Bongor said, " This is our real case for tonight. " " What happened? " Judge Gravizort asked. " Some guy was renting a planet, " Bongor said, " There was an infestation of primitive humans, but he didn't clean it up. Things got unsustainable and now the property value is a lot lower. " " What kinds of punishments can I give? " Judge Gravizort asked eagerly. " Some community service, " Bongor said. Judge Gravizort frowned. " You can try for a few months on a prison planet, " Bongor said, " But he'll probably be able to get an appeal and they'll reduce the sentence. " " What's this guy's name? " Gravizort asked. " I dunno how to pronounce it, " Bongor said, " It's spelled Z-E-U-S. "

article: It was wet. Everything around her was wet; it wasn't just water it was denser, heavier. She was stuck in a giant sugar-free jello all because she wanted to flee her sorority. This was hour fifteen and her diabetes was starting to make her nauseus. They'd thrown all kinds of things at her- insulted every action she has ever taken. It would all be worth it though- Alpha Gamma Row girls always got their man and their job. Six of the last seven presidents went on to lead a hospital department, make millions and marry a man either running a city or a hedge fund. She would own a portion of the world, if she could just last a little longer. Massie, the president this year, came tumbling down the stairs, "what's up Sugar, how ya doing? Oh, sorry I probably shouldn't mention that word to a diabetic." "I'm good. Four more hours and I'll be good." "We've decided to extend that a bit actually..... and you need to recite a sonnet every hour- see the tv over there? It'll be flashing through a few for you to choose from." She managed it. Somehow she fought through the next six hours without passing out and memorizing the sonnets. She would never enjoy Shakespeare or Jello again but she was a queen in training now. Until the pinning. She still hadn't slept. Jello was unsurprisingly difficult to sleep in. Memorizing the sonnets had taken the last of her soul and when they pinned her, the pick pierced her skin, causing a droplet of blood to soak her dress and take the last bit of sugar with it. Her head smashed into Massie. The hospital room was bright white. Doctors were inspecting every inch of her and an iv was placed in her right arm. "uh..." she moaned. "Ma'am, you..... you're body is completely out of sugar. A normal person would have passed out hours ago but a diabetic..... they should have died. You can't ever dip below 50 on your blood sugar again. Ever. You need to hide away in the desert and simply drink apple juice and eat snickers bar until you recover." She frowned. This wasn't going as planned," the sorority is being sued- the entire sorority. The judge is probably going to rule in your favor," a nice pants suit wearing lady said to her. "You'll be a multi-millionaire if that's any consolation." Smirking, she realized she'd won faster than any other president, she was too good for their sonnets and jello anyway. [ end ]

article: Derrick was rather accustomed to the reliable way in which life played out every morning. This was not to say that life was boring, because boring and reliable aren't entirely the same thing. In this case though, it was, and they were. Derrick liked boring. He'd had a grilfriend once who had asked him to be more spontaneous. He had responded by sitting quietly in a room for hours, lacking the fundametal human capability for spontaneity. So it was with no amount of upset that Derrick opened his bathroom door to find something that he had not been expecting. Two suited dwarves stood awaiting him, they had their hands over their ears as if they had just heard some rather profane things, which they were no doubt about to share with Derrick. "Greetings, We began one before Derrick cut him off. It was much to early for this kind of shenanigans. "You, coffee." he said pointing to one of them. "You, clean." Without further ado Derrick dropped his shorts and stepped into the shower. As the water poured onto him some rather more primitive parts of Derrick's brain were kicking into motion, and chose this time to inform the rest of it that two suited midgets had just broken into Derrick's house. The rest of Derrick's brain laughed at these primitive parts, calling them all sorts of names and saying questionable things about their obviously lacking capability for rational thought. It was only when Derrick stepped out of the shower, to be confronted by a hot cup of coffee and the morning newspaper. Those same primitive parts of Derrick's mind were now rather unashamedly jumping around, and pointing out to the rest of Derrick's brain that it had indeed, it seemed, had a much more thorough education than its peers had assumed. This was because the coffee and newspaper found themselves attached to a small, suited elf. nbsp; Derrick took the coffee and the paper. The elf was kind enough to wrap a towel around his waist before escorting him out of the bathroom. The room was spotless, and Derrick would have been happy if his body had contained enough caffiene to facilitate the feeling of emotions. The one elf joined the other at the foot of the bed, and they stared at Derrick, clad only in a cotton towel, as if he were a small god. "We have completed the tasks Oh Great One. Now as per the contracts of the Snow and Beard you must accept our request." Derrick nodded absent-mindedly as he sipped his coffee, completing a magical contract that had three-thousand years of magic and tradition behind it. This would have caught Derrick completely off guard, if he had realised at all. The elves set about explaining that Santa Claus had vanished from the North Pole. Well, vanished may not be the correct word, one elf admitted, more like kidnapped. Derrick took another sip of coffee to help him digest this news. The other elf turned to Derrick, handing him a pamphlet and a set of keys. "Everything you need to know is in there," said the elf, his fingers twitching violently in an attempt to gift-wrap the pamphlet which he had just handed to Derrick. Luckily some other fingers were on call to restrain these, and the pamphlet remained unmolested. The rest of Derrick's brain had now started to realise the gravity of the situation, and were thinking rather hard about the implications of what he had just seen and heard. This quiet philosophical contemplation was in no way helped by the fact that his eyes, which were now readily sending information to the brain, took their time in capturing the spontaneous combustion of both elves in great detail before sending a.zip file of the footage to the optical nerve clusters. Derrick stooped down, his hands sifting the piles of confetti that marked the deaths of the elves. nbsp; END OF PART ONE

article: Growing up in a circus was spectacular. The lights, the colours, the animals, the people. It's like one gigantic family where everyone looks out for each other and each day is more fun than the last. My mom was a beautiful trapeze artist, but even with all the glitz and glamour and all her beautiful costumes, I wanted to be a clown. Just like my dad. The pies, the watches that squirt water, the shoes as big as my arms. It was just too much fun. Unfortunately, being a grown-up in a failing circus is not as much fun as being a kid in a successful one. We try and keep current. Try and get the kids'attention, but it's hard. Our world is different than theirs. Marcus, one of the new trapeze artists, he's smarter than the rest of us. He goes on the internet, finds out what the kids like, and we try to add it to our bits and routines. I peek out from behind the curtain. The circus is almost empty tonight. No surprise there. I'm a bit nervous today, I'm always nervous when we do a new bit. It's about a new dance Marcus heard of. " Chuckles! Chuckles! Where are you? Why is she always so late? " That's my cue. I honk my horn as I drive my little bicycle onto the floor, circling Clownzo as I pretend to squirt him with my watch. " Oh no! I wear a watch that will not work It makes me want to go berserk I'm always late, the stupid jerk This silly watch won't even squirt. This watch of mine just will not work, My stupid watch can't even twerk- " " But Chuckles, " Clownzo interupts " you can't twerk either. Har har " " Oh d'oh! Right you are Clownzo. Hardy har, silly me! Do you know how to twerk Clownzo? " " Gee Chuckles, is twerk a kind of jerky? " " No, you buffoon! It's a beautiful dance. I wonder if there's anyone who can teach me. " I give the little girl in the front row my goofiest smile, hoping that she will volunteer, but her eyes are glued to a phone. The boys with her are pinching each other. My heart sinks a little. " Hmmm, maybe someone in the audience knows how to twerk. " Clownzo tries again. Silence. Most of the kids at the back are on their phones as well. And there's no one else there. Improvising is a big part of being a clown; when you're throwing pies and hoping for volunteers, things don't always work out like planned. I look back at the sweet little girl with the phone in her lap and I just... I just give up. I look at my broken watch. Things were a lot different back when my dad was a clown. " Well Carl, I mean Clownzo. I guess... then, I guess, I guess- " My eyes are tearing up so I just drive off the stage with my silly little bike. It squeaked and honked the whole way to my trailer. When I entered the trailer I took off my nose and grabbed the flask from under my pillow. What's a clown to do when no-one loves clowns anymore? " I am a clown with many a quirk in a world where clowns don't work. It makes me feel like such a jerk It makes me want to go berserk. "

article: 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marines; quantity force: 2 It was only the Squad's Automatic Rifleman and the Designated Marksman that were left. They were huddled up in the rocks, and the enemy was combing everything over. Not a hair to be seen, except for that of the fallen Timberwolves. The Automatic Rifleman fixed the boonie hat - like the Designated Marksmans, though he had a shemagh over his mouth - before looking around for a few seconds. Nobody had passed. Dust blew over the sand, setting a better scene for the Designated Marksman. He looked over, placing a hand in the air. It closed into a fist - calling for attention from the Automatic Rifleman. Ranks didn't discern them, they were both Lance Corporals. The Marksman lifted his SAM-R slightly in one hand. He made a notion to set a strike - or suppressing fire - on the spread out force of forty that had taken down their friends. Fire spread amongst the air as the M240B's barrel began releasing howling rounds. Soon after, loud, although slow shots from the SAM-R began popping out. Recreating the punching outwards and gripping inwards signal, he then pointed towards a fragmentation grenade on his own vest. He had to return his focus, quickly, firing a few rounds. Men were dropped left and right, were they the Timberwolves who had fallen for these two Marines, now living to give it all against forty armed men. The SAM-R eventually unloaded, so by instinct the Lance Corporal withdrew his M9, firing a few rounds. Not very many hit, one egging a man in the arm. It wasn't going to be much, but the force that was trying to respond had only just then seen at least one of them - the Rifleman, who was reloading. The belt wasn't fitting right. The Designated Marksman pierced the air with one more round from the 9mm, and then threw it towards his ally and bashed his rifle to unjam a round. Each 5.56mm round that expelled itself from the SAM-R's chamber, was dwindling their resources. The Marksman rose slowly, entering a standing posture as he fired. The enemy force dwindled, next, to about ten men. However, once this milestone was achieved, seven rounds ripped into the Automatic Rifleman. Within this contact, it went up from the chest until, yes, he had fell. Left alone, the Designated Marksman pegged out four more rounds and then had to withdraw his knife. A round clipped his shin, and he drew the blade back and went into the neck of one of the standing hostile infantry. Once it was removed, he used them for stability, throwing the blade. Two more rounds pressed into his chest, leaving another force of two, amongst many more fallen bodies - however no more Timberwolves to run this troop down. The surviving Designated Marksman and Automatic Rifleman had failed, making way to a Afghan Rifleman duo. They had the drop, but they failed.

article: "You always were a coward." She said, as she held my hands, tears starting to well in her eyes. "When we were little, and I tried to fight older boys, you were the one who would grab my hand and run away with me. When we started elementary school, and the bullies tried to pick on you, you were the one to quietly walk away." The hands that were holding mine squeeze a little tighter. "When we got to highschool, and those girls started spreading nasty rumors, you stood up to them, and when their boyfriends threatened to beat us, you were the one who went to the principal and told." "When college came, and I wanted to drop out, you got so scared at my Dad finding out that you talked to me all night, and in the morning things didn't seem so bad." She looks up, into my eyes, and lifts her veil. "You always were a coward, except when it came to me. So that's why, today, I can say to you..... I do."

article: That dude gave me the chills..... How had he entered my bedroom? How come he looked like the spitting image of this story's narrator? Upon stepping into my world, he greeted me with the words: "Green. Your favorite color is'green'. It was the signal I had arranged with myself when I was a child and contemplated the problem of how I could possibly identify if I were to meet a time-travelling version of myself. He presented me his right forearm, it was bruised and hairless. The skin looked so pale, as though he hadn't been exposed to sunlight for a long time. The word engraved in it read:'Biscuit'. His pupils were wide as fuck, that's the only thing I remember from the dream I had in this particular night. Every other detail disappears into a hazy mishmash but it felt so REAL that time!! I never told anyone, especially not my wife.

article: After the initial shock wore off, Chad tried to make sense of what had just happened. He'd ordered a pizza. A ridiculous order. Something the 17 year old on the other end of the line should have scoffed at and hung up. Instead, 2 men had come to the door. "Thursday, we come back. Pay then, with the money or your life." Chad hadn't known what to say to that, thinking the kid on the phone had sent his pizza buddies to make a little prank of their own. Nope. Not that lucky. Inside the standard pizza box were dozens of baggies with a white, powdery substance inside. There were a lot of these baggies. Now, Chad hadn't gone to college for nothing, so he had an idea what these baggies might contain. After a moments hesitation, he knew what he had to do. He'd been out of college for a couple years, but it was always good to know a few people into darker things. He called Jenny - an old fuck-buddy whom had had quite the habit back-in-the-day, Thom - a ne'er-do-well who always had a scheme or a scam, and June - a stockbroker. He told them all that he needed them to come over as soon as possible. He knew they'd all stayed in or around the city, San Francisco had plenty of jobs for Stanford grads. They'd all kept in touch over the years, Chad had just seen Thom a few weeks past. One by one, they'd agreed to meet up the following afternoon for lunch. They went to Tacolicous. Yes, it's pretentious, but it's San Francisco..... What do you expect? Over margaritas and too-pricey tacos, Chad told them what had happened. June, always a little judgemental even on her best days, had a few choice words for Chad. "First of all, your 25. Why the fuck are prank calling pizza places? Second, you're an idiot. Third..... Why are we here? " Chad responded, not a little sheepishly, "I was bored and maybe more than a little stoned. Shit happens. And yes, I'm an idiot, I accept that. As far as why you're all here, well..... I was hoping you'd help me get rid of this shit. I don't really feel like dying. Hell, I don't really feel like getting kneecapped or shanked or whatever-the-fuck these dudes do with people who don't deliver. Before you ask why I don't call the cops, well..... Do you think they'd believe me?'Oh, yes, cops? I just happen to have about a thousand little bags of what I think is yayo, wan na come arrest me real quick? It'd take a huuuuuuuge weight, literally, off my shoulders.' No, no I don't think that'd work at all. So, I called you assholes. Thom, you're the schemer. If these other two lively, beautiful, flawless beauties can't come up with something, I'm sure you can. As for you, Jenny, you had quite the, uh, nose for this particular indulgence back when we were dating. Jenny interrupted "We weren't dating, asshole, we were fucking. And yeah, I liked a little party back then, of course, it was fucking college. I quit years ago. Shit, I quit while I was still blowing you in the dorm stairwell. So no, I don't know any fucking drug dealers. Except for my scumbag brother." "That's it! I knew there was a reason I called you!" Chad smacked the table. "Your scumbag brother is exactly the guy I need." Jenny looked at Chad like he'd lost his mind. "Andy is an idiot. A bigger idiot than you, Chud. He sells Molly to high-schoolers. He wouldn't know the first thing about moving a key of blow. Even if he did, I don't really want him in on this. He's a fucking idiot. I think I already mentioned that." Chad looked forlorn. "But Jen..... If he knows where to get E, he'll know who has coke. He'll know who sells it. I have 5 days to move more coke than I've ever seen in real life. If I had to move this on my own, I'd sell three bags and then run out of customers. Between you three and me, we can definitely sell all of it, but..." June held up a hand. "Why am I here, bud? I'm a fucking sto..... Oh. You just watched Wolf of Wall Street, didn't you?" "Actually, it was Boiler Room. Fuck Leo was good in Wolf of Wall Street! I didn't think of that, but yeah. It's because of that." June gave a way smile. "Well, you know I can't sell it personally. I can't lose my job like that. But, if I introduced Andy to a couple of guys, I'd have that shit moved in about 2 days." Chad beamed, and kissed June square in the lips. "June, you're a fucking champ. The best around. If you weren't married to your job, I'd ben..." Thom cleared his throat. "How much are we gon na make? Are we gon na cut it? How pure is it? Columbian? Russian? Afghani? How much did they say they wanted? We're lacking a bunch of info here, Chad. If we sell these lightweight stockjockeys, no offense June, some really pure shit and they start fucking dying, we're not really doing a great job. We need to know a lot of shit. And we need to know it fast. I've got a general idea of what a gram of decent shit goes for, about 50, but what do we cut it with? Aspirin usually works, but then we have to sell a whole bunch more. If we stomp it down to half, then we effectively have to move two fucking kilos in 5 days. Fuck that. We're not Scarface. So, we sell it as is. Do we plan on making money?" The conversation continued. They changed bars, went right up the street to Casanova, sat in a dark booth and schemed. They decided that Andy would make connections with June's co-workers. It was easy enough, those dudes loved to party. Andy had enough knowledge to undercut street prices a bit to entice the buyers, which helped move product quickly. It turned out Jenny still had some sorority sisters that liked a little party now and then, and she sold about 20 grams to them. As the deadline got closer, and with about 200 grams left, they pushed hard to sell as much as they could, vowing to have one last hurrah on Wednesday night, figuring if they got the math wrong, they might as well die stoned. The party was a success. They invited some of the frequent buyers, figuring they could move the last of it there. The night was a blur, but they sold or snorted the rest. They gathered the money, about 50k. And they waited for the knock. And that was how, in 5 days, Chad, June, Thom, Jenny and Jenny's scumbag brother Andy each made about 4k in a week, and didn't get killed by Russian Mobsters.

article: This is my first time commenting on a writing prompt. All opinions and criticism is welcome. I haven't written (in real life) in a while so bare with me as I am rusty. "Carey..... It's time" said Win as he opened the door to the dressing room where Carey had prepared his speech for his piece he was unveiling at the gala. Carey had become an overnight sensation in the realm of media for capturing seemingly unreal or perfect photos of wonders and relics long since passed. "Tonight in front of all of you, I am proud to show my new picture that encapsulates the times before modern technology. The times before we had cameras that had auto set He pauses for a moment mid sentence to realize the crowd fell completely still. He looked down at his watch, "Damn." he says realizing that the watch was the cause of time standing still. The watch needed to be wound back up every 9 hours or else time would freeze on it's own. This nifty worn down unsavory piece of metal was how he got his pictures in the first place, along with the help of a photo album he bought at a little shop of gilden street containing the images of ancient ruins and wonders of the world would change his life forever. He first found out about the power when he touched slid his hand across the picture of The House of Virgin Mary in present day Turkey. A flash of light and a few moments later he was standing in Ephesus just outside of the house where he saw Mary walk to the front door, then just as quick as she appeared in the flesh he was brought back to his time with only the memories of what happened. Carey thought of a plan to show the true essence of life before his time. This is where the watch makes it's appearance. A traveling man on day when Carey was taking pictures in Spain sold him the watch for a few coins, Carey felt the watch was strange as the minute hand would rotate counter clockwise. One day while collecting photos around the city he noticed a bird perfectly still on a fence. He quickly realized that somehow time was standing still. He looked at his watch and all hands stopped at 6:30:30. After winding for a few turns time gradually began flowing again. Carey starts to walk a few blocks and a woman with black hair walks up to him and says "Welcome to Unravel."

article: The line was never flat. It may have stuttered before, but for the first time, green against black, the line was flat. Pauline had heard of death, but there was something so archaic about it..... it never crossed her mind, the fact that an existence could be ephemeral. This world had never known of a life ending, only humans did, and for god's sake, we aren't humans. There was always a comfort in immortality. Being born without consequences. Pauline was still young, 86. A nurse. Sickness in this world was just discomfort. No one likes a stuffy nose or a broken arm. She had seen only a fraction of what this world had to offer, yet felt as though she had seen it all. In this world so similar to what Earth once was, her days began to melt into one. Rising with the Sun, sleeping only after her children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren were fed. She jumped from cliffs, planes. Tried drugs. Like everyone did. She had made mistakes. Loved. Lost. But she always found herself new friends..... new lovers. Like everyone had. She had traveled to the shells of old civilisations, great and powerful, reduced to only dust. Being at the hospital when the first one passed, she did not sleep that evening. She wondered only one thing. Without an end, is there a beginning?

article: "Hello" Frank chuckled under his breath. He knew this gag. Whenever one of them went alone into the test lab the other researchers would try and scare him using the intercom. "Your not fooling anybody" he said looking at the security camera. "Fooling anybody" a voice said behind him. Frank, admitedly surprised turned around. Nothing he thought as he eyes gazed over the cages. Dogs, cats, parrots and rats all stared at him blanky. "It was you wasn't it?" He said looking at the parrot. The African grey had always been a little mischievous. "Was me" the parrot whispered. "I know little guy, you scared old frank" As he thought about how uno had gotten his name (he was the first testee) Frank realized somthing. "I didn't say me" Frank whispers to himself. "I scared you. Let's write it down, let's write it down." Uno taunted "What the hell" Frank yelled "Enhanced intelligence, promoise I show promise, great promise. Let's write it down" Frank looked down at his papers.Uno had been on the drug for over a year, six months more than any other animal. So did it work? "Hey uno" "Frank, hi" said Uno disjointly "Do you?..... Have you?..... Uh" It seemed stupid, 7 years of his life and now he didn't know what to do, what to say. "Are you um smarter?" Frank asked feeling silly. "Enhanced intelligence was me, Uno shows promise, great promise" "I think, I think it worked" Frank said in disbelief. "Uno worked, Enhanced intelligence worked" Uno said clicking his beak. "I guess it makes sense it was you, parrots are naturally quite intelligent" "Was Uno, was me, was we" Uno whispered ominously. With that Frank heard a loud growel behind him. I guess Uno wasn't the only one. Edit: Made it pretty (spaces in between dialogue)

article: A static buzz gave way to fluorescent light and chatter as she awoke from her slumber. The oppressive light above seemed to force her eyes shut again. But the lights only grew brighter, and the bed sheets heavier. "We failed," she caught someone say as he left the room. The other attendants followed shortly after, leaving her alone. - "What do you remember before you woke up?" The old man's wide smile and round face projected kindness. But under that brown, old-fashioned suit, she could see he was stiff. She remembered remembered a few faces, a place here and there. "Nothing," she said. "There's no need to be nervous," he said with a plastic smile, eyes pointed not at her, she just realized, but at the loop of hair she was tugging at. She casually let go, then gathered another brown loop around her fingers. "I'm just glad my hair was kept in good shape," she said. "It's standard procedure, with a coma patient, for the nurses "I'm sorry, but I have to go," she said. - Slowly, more memories returned to the patient. She remembered her home address and where she grew up, her name and what she did for a living. She wasn't a celebrity or noteworthy person. So why, she wondered, did it feel like unseen eyes were upon her? When she found the hospital lobby, everyone staff and civilians alike noticed. She forced herself, one step at a time, to march through the awkward silence towards the exit. Just reach the exit, she thought, then I'm free. - "Is that her?" whispered another from behind. No matter. She knew she was close to home now. The streets changed minimally in the three years she was, supposedly, asleep. "It's the dreamer," whispered another. Just one more left turn, she thought, then my apartment is fifteen minutes straight ahead- The street was short. Very short. It was only two buildings deep before ending in a small parking lot, a far cry from the major road she remembered. She returned to the hospital defeated, but the doctor and the psychologist she spoke to earlier were already in the lobby. - "You were watching my dreams with a machine?" She asked. "Well, you see..." the old man paused to clear his throat generously, "we sort of..... we can't "Nobody," the doctor said, "in the entire world, knows anything about the world from more than three years ago. Not one person." "But this machine," the psychologist said, "showed us a world we couldn't imagine!" "It wasn't perfect." "A tad fuzzy, no color." "But we all saw ourselves. Past versions of ourselves. Your memories must be the only window we have into history. So our goal was to keep you in a coma, so the machine could collect as much data as possible." She sat in silence, for perhaps a whole minute, digesting this information. "You must be wrong," she finally said. The old man sighed. "Well, if you have a better idea, go ahead." "I don't think this world has a past" she said. "I think it's only three years old, and my memories came from somewhere else." "You think your memories of us coincidentally match the appearance and personality of people in real life?" asked the doctor. "Yes." She let that sink in. "I remember how I got into a coma now. "I was in an accident. But my boyfriend was also in the car. And he looked a lot like you, Doctor. Are you saying you survived with only minor cuts and bruises and somehow forgot to mention this so far? "On top of that," she added, curling her hair around my fingers, "are you sure nobody touched my hair?" she asked the psychologist. "Because my hair is naturally black. My hair was dyed this color on that day. "I'm still dreaming, and that machine only showed you your real-world counterparts."
label: human

article: "I'm going to live forever or die trying" "It's often an excuse used by most people to persevere and achieve the unachievable, beat the unbeatable or do the impossible. The path to establishing your own legacy is a treacherous one yet one that tastes sweet when overcome. I do believe you have made it through, sir. You are the very definition of a legacy. " , the doctor mumbled, trying so desperately hard to contain his sadness. "I sure hope so. Sir, if I may speak, I wish you to understand the true principles of government. I wish them carried out. I ask nothing more " , he blurted out with what little strength he has remaining "Yes sir. You shall live forever not in this earth but on our hearts and minds. " , the doctor spoke with utmost confidence "I am satisfied. " And with that, William Henry Harrison drew his last breath. He passed, knowing that he lives on until to this day.

article: " Mr. President, " General Kopanski said. " We're waiting on you. " Jim Graves never imagined he would be here, the destruction of a half-billion lives commencing with his command. Not lives, he reminded himself. Not really. Around him, a select handful of cabinet members and army officers stood, waiting for him to say anything. He had been silent for the last fifteen minutes. The general was the first one to break the silence in all that time. Jim had almost forgotten they were there. Just do it, he told himself. This order will be the most significant event in human history. He dwelled on that. Human history. It was a fictional history, but somehow solid. The struggles were real. The pain was real. Simulated, fake, illusory - yet real all the same. " Let me speak to the doctor, " Jim said. The staff filed out slowly. He could see the stress, fear, and excitement on their faces. This anticipation had reached a near unbearable climax for weeks, but now that the moment for his decision had come, he found invisible walls in his way. He was so close. He had only to say the word. But he wanted to speak to the doctor just one more time. Moments later the man entered. Dr. Volgi was in his late fifties, balding, and a bit too thin. The man always seemed unhealthy. His eyes were lit up with enthusiasm, but everything else about him looked faded. His pallor was grey, his posture crooked. This man, he reminded himself, had spent his life in libraries, lost in books, in deep basement labs, at the cost of his own health and body. " Yes, Mr. President, " Volgi said. " Doctor, you once calculated the percentage that you were wrong, " Jim said. " Run through the calculations for me. " Dr. Volgi looked surprised. After all their discussions and consultations, he had turned Jim into a disciple. A true believer. He still was, but he needed a fraction more certainty. It had all made sense during those meetings and discussions. It was only here, the moment upon him, that he saw the full spectrum of possibilities. " Well, " The doctor said. " There are endless assumptions built into this, but the basic theory about our universe is about as certain as the theory of gravity. " " But gravity is another piece of your theory, " Jim said. " Our theories about it were wrong. " " Our theories about its origins were wrong. Our calculations about its effects and mechanisms are accurate. The system invents the laws, and the programs abide by them. One of them being gravity. " " How sure are you that this will actually crash the system? " Jim said. He had asked this before, but he needed to ask again for his own sake. That was the worst part - the knowledge that, even if Volgi was right, the plan might not have the intended effect of summoning the virtual gods. Volgi shrugged. " I am confident about this as well. It's clear that people are the most complex programs in this world. Even the sun is simpler. With so many... deletions at one time, I am sure it will trip up the system. It may not crash it, but the system will recognize that something has happened. " And then we'll finally get their attention. The attention of the gods. Those who crafted this realm. At the cost of a half billion people. Jim clenched and unclenched his fists. His mind spun with questions, half-articulated fears. " Alright, " he said, his confidence returning in a sudden flare. This will make you the most important man who ever lived. " Send them in. " President Graves gave the orders, and the bombs flew. Many flew to Asia, devastating the coastline, others traveling far into the Russian interior. The detonations of the bombs had all been synchronized to explode as near to the same time as possible. Jim was standing in his office when they hit. As hundreds of millions died, a flash of pinkish hue shot across the world, colors distorting and flaring. It happened everywhere all at once. Lines became less defined, the earth vibrating around them. Dr. Volgi came staggering into the room, clutching his chest. His eyes were wild. He looked at the president. " Mr. President, " the doctor said. " Your head... " Jim looked at himself in the mirror. A flashing red dot hovered over his head. He studied himself, his pulse escalating wildly. He felt two small horns on the side of his skull. They hadn't been here before. They had simply appeared. Congratulations, Jim heard in his head, a thought silently transmitted. You have reached new levels of Evil. It wasn't this thought. It was foreign. Confusion overcame him. The words were alien. "What's happening?" he asked Volgi. "I don't know," the doctor said, voice cracking and low. Sudden anger rose to the surface, like oil from a well. His body felt different. You're new level is accompanied by new powers. You'll notice you have more control over your environment now. With a thought, he lifted the Volgi off the ground. The man gurgled, clutching at his throat. "You were supposed to be sure," Jim said. "You were supposed to bring the gods here." He didn't let Volgi answer. Instead he flung him across the room where he slammed into the wall. Volgi slumped to the ground broken. His anger began to subside. New powers. So his first attempt to summon the gods had failed, but it had gained him something. It had educated him. And he still had nine billion lives left to play with. He turned and began levitating down the hall to find Kopanski. He had a war to finish.

article: "Next chapter, coming soon." How soon is soon? , I wondered to myself. These damn web-novels keep twisting me up with their languid pace. Especially the translated ones. The idea that the story is already out there, just ready to be read hurts me in a very real way. I even tried learning new languages, but I have no talent when it comes to linguistics. What I do have is some proficiency in physics and electronics. Eventually, these stories will be written. Eventually, they will be translated. Well, all I want to do is take a peek at them. That shouldn't be so hard, right? I mean, it isn't like I'm going to be transferring any substantial objects through time. The theory was difficult. The construction harder. But that damned "Next chapter, coming soon" drove me. Eventually, I was ready for my test run. My first target was a half-completed Writing Prompt with a "To be continued" tacked to the end. I figured that a five hour scrape should net me the completed version. I held my breath and triggered the system. And time snapped like the delicate thread that it is.

article: So much has changed. The Dodgers were still in Brooklyn and the Braves were in Boston. Segregation was still a thing. It was 1948 in America. Germans, Irish and Italians dominated baseball. There was none of this corporate ownership of stadiums excluding Wrigley Field like there is now. I was 11 years old, sitting behind home plate in the old Municipal Stadium. My grandfather had gotten tickets for him and me. I watched the third, fourth and fifth games of the series from those seats. That was sixty eight years ago. Hard to believe. Now I'm a grandfather with my grandkid and my son. It's four to 1, in favor of the Cubs. Billy Sianis, where are you? I got life and death on this game. I know the Cubs have had a longer drought than we have, but I have to support the Tribe. If they don't win, it's a shame. 1.2.3. Right over the plate. YARD BABY YARD, I shout.

article: I spread my hands apart in a pleading gesture, "We tried to do good, didn't we?" He agrees in silence. I returned my arms to the negligible warmth of the blanket we huddled under. The darkness was like a blanket itself, tightening around us. Soon it would crush us. The air is so thick. I mumbled through numbing lips, "We were great. Humans, I mean. We did so many great things." Silent agreement. I continued, desperate for one last moving speech, one last legacy of our race. "We were great. We learned so much about our world. About space." A whispered, "Too much," gave me pause, but I battled on relentlessly, despite the darkness clutching at my throat. "We built great civilizations. We cured diseases. We were great." My companion rasped, "Too great," before breaking off to give a strangled cough. The air is so thick. I tried to continue. The human race deserved so much more than I could offer, in this last breath of humanity. I can not breath. We were so great.
label: human

article: In my last moments, as I lay here, waiting for the inevitable cold to finally take my suffering away, I can only think back on my actions, they were all so happy before, time traveling adventures with the children of St. Mary's Primary School, Class 7-C. I never realised it would be like this, all I ever thought was to go on grand adventures and teach the kids a little history. One of the kids suggested a year and we were off, piling into my magical time traveling boot, ready to ' Kick start our imagination!'as I used to say, back when I was me, back when I smiled. Back to the year 2066, they insisted it was a very important time period, only 50 years earlier than their current period, as they insisted. I didn't think anything of any real importance happened then, of course as any good 5th dimensional being, I have seen whole worlds crumble in a matter of moments, to me at least, so who knows, I may have missed some important event, or something of cultural import to the kids. Excuses. I should have asked more questions, should have realised. Little too late to wonder now I suppose. 15 year olds, still children, barely out of their eggs compared to my thousands of years. I suppose it's that kind of thinking that got me into this mess. That and not researching the local culture enough I suppose. After all, how was I to know the sci-fi channel had been playing constant time travel movies for weeks leading up to my arrival, or that the kids, at least the few I should really have been more worried about, had been getting all sorts of ideas, ideas that would make most people with a good healthy wariness to the time stream continuum cry. ' Out of the mouths of babes'it was a saying I had come across in my brief time in this world, something I have come to mean very differently than I believe was intended. Children, the pure, their minds untouched by greed, protected from pride, ignorant to most of the ' sins of man '. They were supposed to be GOOD. They were not. They had ideas. Wicked ideas. They wanted to be rich, famous, they wanted everything. Just, not yet. There are a few rules to be followed while time traveling, travel in the past, if you don't want to hurt yourself, or be very prepared. You know where you are, and what you will do. If it's your past and your future, there will be a way to interact with yourself, a way to change something. That is very painful. For me, and every 5th dimensional being in the area as time wrenches itself apart trying to change what's going on and all that excess energy has to go through some conduit. If you travel in the past, then that's fine, the ' You'being affected is separate from the ' you'you might see, and that means that time in the area you are traveling will only be affected centred on yourself from the ' now ', or the time period you were in originally, as the origin point that is the piece being affected, and will only be affected once. As soon as you interact with yourself in the future, the ' you'will be changed by your previous interaction, causing a ripple and recursively causing the ' you'you are interacting with to change and become something else, over and over again. The universe can heal itself, time is stretchy and flexible, but think of a piece of rubber, even putty, placed upon a grinding blade of a constant shifting presence, even the universe won't be able to mend the whole eventually. There are more specifics, but that is what you need to know for now. Well, that and they don't publish almanacs where I come from, oh and kids are dicks, I mean, who steals someone's boot? As I lie here, dying of internal time haemorrhaging, energy literally exploding my veins, watching as the older version of the kids take them away and teach them about themselves, all the while changing and telling them what did and didn't work, I realise there was something very important that I must have missed. Not that it matters now, I will die, never knowing Ms. Stacey decided to put up the 2116 calendar, rather than the 2016 one, thinking it would be a bit of fun, getting the kids excited about time travel week. I would never know that they would never know what happened to me, I would never know they attribute all of their work to a stranger who appeared like an angel and gave them this gift, only to disappear moments after they arrived, with an incredibly easy to use magic boot, I certainly would not realise the path I placed these humans on, galactic domination indeed, how do you fight against creatures who can advance their technology by millennia by giving it to themselves, how can you combat monsters who seem to know everything before it happens? Only I will know the truth, trapped in an endless paradox of my own stupid creation, 14 children, linking with their adult forms, creating a knowledge loop with my very blood as the channel. I awaited the final cold. It never came, just the burning sensation of never ending fires of time, burning my eternal energy, seeing all of creation crumble and rebuild itself in moments, only to crumble again an instant later. I lay here dying. I always lay here dying. Please, stop the humans.
label: human

article: An estate sale's a hell of a thing, cleaning out someone else's garbage and wondering, the whole time, whether any of it's worth a damn to them or to you. All a matter of preference, I guess, but this place, far as I could tell, didn't have a single thing worth preferring. Down in this fella's basement, ran into a stubborn old sheet of plywood stuck against the wall. "Nothing left behind," the client's worksheet had said, but this goddamned board wouldn't budge. Last bit of junk always ended up a pain in the ass. Why couldn't it have been a Rolex. Or a rare painting. Who am I kidding, though? God knows a dope like me wouldn't know good art if I painted the damned thing myself. Art curator could send me a letter, proclaiming perfection, and I'd still probably junk it. Had to go out to my truck and grab a crowbar to pry that wood board from the wall. Damn near bent the thing on my first tug, though. "Determined son-of-a-bitch," I said, my lips pursed as I pried at it again. "For the love of Christ," I yelled out, "get off the fucking wall!" I guess that final pull was a real good one, because just then, as I wailed out curses that would've made my daddy proud, the wood flung free and the lucky guy I am hit me smack dab in the forehead. I laid there, half-conscious, whispering angry little things to myself. Fucking estate sales. A Rolex. Just once, a Rolex, please, you sadistic gods of estate sales, just once give me that watch. Even if it's one of the cheaper ones, a used one, silver even, I'll never ask for another thing again. I noticed the crowbar next to me, lying there, bent right down the middle. Never seen wood do a thing like that. Matter of fact, I don't even remember pulling the board free. I guess a blow to the head'll do that to you. As I got up, right where the board used to be, I saw what looked like an elevator: two chrome doors, cut right down the middle, with a set of buttons on the side. Went up and tired the buttons. Nothing. No lights, no click, no ching. Weird. Looked like it might be some visual art, something you'd see at one of those contemporary art museums. You know, the ones with the upside down toilets and stuff. Maybe, I thought, this was like that. Thing is, behind those doors, through that little crack right down their center, I could see the slightest bit of light. Real feint. You could easily miss it. For a second, I thought that maybe it was coming from the outside, but then I remembered that I was in the basement. What a dope I was. Blow to the head'll do that to you. If that stupid crowbar hadn't bent so far, I'd use it to pry those doors open. Who knows, though. Maybe it would. I walked over and examined the thing. It looked like a crooked spoon at this point. There was no way I could get enough leverage with it to open the doors especially not these ones, heavy as they looked. "Ding!" The fucking shit? Behind me, just like that, with a ding, the doors opened. It was fully functional had lights and everything. At this point, I was thinking, "you know what, keep the damned Rolex." Too weird for me. But the thing is, it's a lot easier to say'no' to another roll at the craps table when you're back home sitting on the couch; when you're in Vegas, though, temptation, more often than not, says, "c'mon, lucky number seven!" That's why, God help me, I stayed the hell away from Vegas. I found myself in a remarkably similar situation, though. And while my gut said, "walk away," the gambler in me rolled the dice and walked inside. It was pretty nice in there swanky, even. Had these little designs, looked Greek, running along the edges of the mirrors. Red carpet, too. There were only two buttons: "UP and DOWN." And I figured since I'd already seen upstairs, why not take a look down below. "Oh..... well..... fuck it!" I said as I pressed the down button. I started smiling nervously. Almost a laugh, really the kind a meth head gets as he waits his turn, watching as his buddy lights up and gets off. A "hand-it-over" smile. Wait a minute..... What the fuck was I doing? The doors closed and I felt the elevator jerk. "Ohhh!" I screamed out, looking around for someone to share the fear with, but finding only my reflection in the mirror, terrified and smiling like a meth head. EDIT: Making some coffee. I'll work on it some more in a few.
label: human

article: "See, there are a thousand ways to be dead. Real dead, fake dead, undead." He chuckled mirthlessly at his own joke. Myra rolled her eyes. "In your scenario, though, thinking about fake dead, it's easier and harder than you think. Easier because all you need is a fat wad of cash and the right contacts which I am offering you and harder because," Mr Black paused to take a breath, lips pulled against his remaining teeth. "Because giving up everything from your old life is a real son of a bitch." "That'll be no problem for us," Josh replied. Myra loved his smooth voice. He could convince anyone of anything. He could sell the proverbial ice to eskimos. She nodded, hoping she didn't look too enthusiastic. Or desperate. Mr Black wasn't even looking at them, though. His gaze was fixed to the far wall of the KFC, at a cheap pastel print framed in brass. "Yep. Harder than you think." Myra glanced at Josh, feeling his impatience. "Look, Mr Black. We understand exactly what we're getting into here. We called you because we want to do this, not because we want to fuck around over shitty food. Can we dispense with the boring shit, and get on with the practicalities?" Mr Black's gaze returned to Josh's face, and he grinned suddenly. It didn't make him look any nicer. His eyes were set so deep in his head, Myra saw only a hard glint in shadowy sockets. Combined with the rotted stumps of the last three or four teeth in his mouth, she would have been happy to run out of there screaming. But Josh needed to do this, so she needed to, too. "This is what you need. You need to meet me tomorrow morning at the park bench on the Grove Street side of Fenster Park. There's a letterbox beside it, so you know which one. I'll pick you up in a Honda Odyssey. Bring nothing, except one hundred fifty thousand cash. When I say nothing, I mean nothing. Only the clothes you're walkin' in." Josh nodded as Mr Black spoke, taking it all in. He didn't flinch at the price. But he had expected it; his associate Kronfeld had warned him, had divvied up the proceeds in advance so Josh was prepared. Myra's breath hitched, but she kept as quiet and agreeable as she could. She didn't want to mess this up for them. "What will happen next?" Josh asked. "Passport, social security, drivers licenses all the ID you'll need to travel. My crew will take care of that. Then we take you south as far as we can. You'll end up in South America, but you won't know where until you get there. Once you're there, we're gone." Josh and Myra nodded. Myra felt butterflies flitting around in her stomach. It was a good thing she hadn't touched her chicken; she didn't think it would have stayed down. They needed this. Keep cool. They spent that evening at the movies, sitting near the back and whispering under the cover of the film's soundtrack. "What about my parents?" "What about them? Forget them! They'll figure you ran away. That's true." "I want to say goodbye." "No. No goodbyes." Myra slouched sulkily in her chair. She knew what would happen if she disobeyed Josh. She couldn't be left behind. She couldn't live without him. She'd already quit high school and spent every night out with Josh and his associates. They looked after her as well as her parents had. And school was pointless, anyway. Although maybe she should have taken Spanish classes. They stood together the next morning, Myra gripping Josh's arm tight enough to leave a red mark when she let go. He had a cheap suitcase in the other hand. It was full of neat piles of twenties, straight from the ATM. Kronfeld had set them aside from the last job, the one where Josh left his flashlight behind. A grey Odyssey pulled up down the street and Myra jerked on Josh's arm. "Is that it?" she hissed. He shook her off. "No. Shut up." They waited on the seat for another twenty minutes before a silver Odyssey came to a stop in front of them. The back door slid open and a hand waved impatiently. Josh pulled Myra in after him and closed the door. Mr Black sat in the passenger seat in front of them, stonefaced, and another man with a shaved head drove. Myra couldn't see his face, but his eyes in the rearview mirror were blank, staring straight ahead. "You ready?" Mr Black said to Josh. "Ready." He leaned back and fastened his seatbelt so Myra did too. Josh sat with one arm draped across the seat back, touching Myra's shoulder in what she figured was reassurance. Josh was so caring and protective. She loved him so much. "Let's do this, then." Mr Black gestured forward and the driver pulled away. Myra didn't pay attention to their surroundings she was imagining herself and Josh lying on beach towels somewhere in Brazil until she realised they were deep in the redwood forest. The road had gotten narrower, really only one lane wide. She guessed there was a cabin out here where they would get ready to go south. She was right. They pulled off the road when the woods were so thick there was no sun, only shadows. The van followed a bumpy dirt track for a mile or two, then stopped at last in front of a hunter's hut surrounded by the trunks of vast trees. They climbed out, Myra first, Josh close behind. The driver got out too and went to the trunk to get something. Myra was looking up at the treetops swaying, seeing the sun just hitting the tips of the conifers and slanting a little ways down, when she heard a popping sound. She hadn't even processed it when she felt the pain in her chest. She looked down and saw red on her t-shirt, and touched it. It was wet, and warm. She looked at Josh, standing beside her. He looked apologetic. "Josh?" "I'm sorry, babe. It wasn't going to work." She collapsed to the ground, feeling soft needles under her. Eyes open, she saw the driver standing over her with the gun pointed at her face. Before he shot her again, she heard Josh say, "You're right, Mr Black. It is harder than I thought."
label: human

article: I take a swig from my bottle of scotch, only to be greeted by air. Figures. Even my alcohol's abandoned me. I set the empty glass bottle on a nearby table and replace it with a 9mm pistol. I've already decided, this will be where and when I die. I've nothing else to live for. That was taken from me three months ago. My wife. My two daughters. Even the goddamned dog died in the accident. But somehow I lived. I was going to rectify that tonight. I chamber the lone round, then rest the gun in my mouth. Well, this is it. Goodbye cruel world. Before I pull the trigger, my eyes rest on a family photo. It was take the day of second daughter's birth, three years ago. Ah, what the hell. I'll give it one last look. Best to die with a happy memory than nothing. As I scan the picture, I notice little details that I'd never noticed before. My wife holds our newborn, a smile on her face. A smile of happiness. A smile of love. Our older daughter, four at the time, looks at her younger sister with curiosity. She has a goofy smile on her face. One that got her more than her fare share of spoiling. But, most of all, I see myself, a proud smile on my face. I look nothing like I do now. My hair is clean cut, I have practically no facial hair, and my eyes resonate a joy that I haven't had since that fateful day three months past. I then notice the cross on my neck. I haven't been to church since the accident. Before I was the most devout member of our congregation. Now I was the village drunkard. Seeing a reminder of my faith makes me reconsider my plans. Was it really cruelity that saved my life that day? Or was it a miracle, one that I had, up to this point, squandered? Would taking my own life bring my family back to me? I feel a tear roll down my cheek. Crying is something I've grown used to, but this wasn't a tear of sadness. It was a tear of happiness. I had been given a second chance. A chance to live again, and to make my girls up in the big house happy.
label: human

article: (First time writing here. Very slight variation on the prompt. Based loosely on real events.) The last year had been the hardest of her life. Only one person had managed to earn her trust, and he had spent most of the previous months using it against her. He always looked at her with disdain, but by now she felt this was more kindness than she deserved. At least he looked. No one else did. She now sat with him on a balcony, watching her frosted breath diffuse out into the cold night. Her focus, as usual, was on appearing outwardly to be okay, while on the inside she had finally reached the end of her rope and was hanging on by a thread. After a long silence, she looked at him, and asked a question, trying to sound not unhappy, but still serious. "Do you think there's anything in me worth trying to save?" He looked at her with a mixture of confusion and annoyance. He always seemed offended when she showed any sign of having emotional needs, or emotional pain. After a pause, but not too long of one as to require any real investment of energy to have been put into thought, he answered. "Meh. If I can't say anything nice, I shouldn't say anything at all." Silence hung noticeably in the air for a moment, until it slowly transitioned back into the usual, common, un-noteworthy silence. She said nothing, and he perceived no reaction from her. Quietly and unnoticed, her eyes slowly glazed over as she stared out into space at nothing in particular. The light that had struggled for so long to find a way or a reason to remain had finally left them. As the spark faded from her eyes, so faded the tattoo from her ankle. As it slowly appeared on his wrist, he didn't take notice. He didn't even notice it until the next day. He was sure there had been some kind of error, perhaps a drunken mistake made while blacked out. He had the tattoo removed. Her body caught up to her spirit a year or two later, heart failure at an oddly young age. The doctors failed to understand the death of her body, just as he had failed to understand the death of her soul. At least now it was over.
label: human

article: The strange man is sitting across the table, looking at me. I was always told to be a good boy and look people in the eye. So that's what I do. Until something better comes along. I'm sitting here in this big empty room, just waiting. They watch me, I watch them. I'm starting to get bored. My dad would often get mad. Or sad. Sometimes both. I never did understand it. After my mom died my dad sort of, drifted away. He was still there, physically. Did what he had to, but not much else. They say the last step of grief is acceptance. Well I think my dad might have tripped on that one. All he said during my stat ceremony was that he won't let me go through the same thing he did. " Do you want some crayons? " I don't know what these people want with me. " Tell me about your favourite toy. " I'm thinking about my dad. He really did his best. Not that it matters anymore. Sometimes I wonder how he saw this going. I guess even the best intentions can miss the goal. At least I won't miss him. " Do you have any friends at school? " My dad always told me that you shake a mans hand when you enter his house. To bad he started to decompose after only four days. It made shaking his hand hard, even more so than him hangning from the ceiling fan. " I do have some friends at school. They call me Apathetic Adam, I think it's because of my stats. "
