article: My power? It's ridiculously simple. I can amplify electrical energy. Something as simple as a AA battery could power a megawatt laser for a second or two with enough amplification. I'm still limited to the energy stored within the power source, be it a battery, a capacitor, or a simple generator. Fortunately, I continued on to college instead of trying to make a name for myself as a hero. Got a degree in computer engineering. Seems pointless, but its become very beneficial. You see, I can act like a powerful transistor as a bypart of the electrical amplification - something as simple as a small pulse from my power could create a massive electrical bolt between my palms. It hurts like hell to do - I didn't get rapid regeneration or electrically insensitive as powers or side effects - but it makes supplying massive amounts of power to one place a pinch. Weirdly, it also turns out that, by using my amplification on an extremely small scale, I can compute things as well. With enough transistor action going on, I can compute numerous things at once. It's become useful for field computing, where all we have as a power source is a battery and maybe some solar panels. And fortunately, there's been a few cases where I'm needed for field computing in remote areas. The last time I went into the field was in a case involving the equally unknown "Bendy McBendface" - he was once a famous gymnast and performer as he's incredibly flexible and can bend parts of his body in ways that it was not structured for - and once I recognized who we were dealing with I started computing. He's flexible, beyond human standards. Is he rubber-like? That makes any electrical attacks useless, yet if he was rubber-like he could compress easily as well and act like a spring. He doesn't spring around, nor does he compress. Must not be rubber then. What about silicone? No, too flexible. Silicone would bend out of shape at his weight. Hmm..... if he can bend so well, perhaps his bones are slightly more flexible than normal, designed like a living hinge. And when it comes to his joints, perhaps he's double or triple jointed, resulting in extreme flexibility. All of that computed in a couple of seconds, I set about setting up a passive computing system that would calculate his possible movements and how he moves. If my bone and joint theory is correct, he should be subdued quickly. I pull out my favorite weapon - a AAA battery electric pistol. Fires small bolts of electricity that are amped up to thousands of volts and normally around 32 amps per short. Holds six AAA batteries before I got ta reload too. I dash closer to Bendy McBendface. I need to keep my distance, if my theory is incorrect and he's more like silicone or rubber, it means he can stretch out and grip onto me. I prep my pistol. Batteries: loaded. Amplification system: ready. Target: within range. I pull the trigger and engage the entire amplification system to drain the AAA battery in a fraction of a second. A loud pop is heard, with an incredibly bright bolt of electricity as it grounds to Bendy's body. I run some final computations to analyze Bendy as his body responds to the electric shock. He certainly isn't rubber-like or silicone-like. Definitely mostly water, like a normal human. I see his bones shine dimly through his skin. The theory was correct. His bones are indeed living hinges. And if my brief foray into materials science is correct, his bones should shatter into individual pieces, leaving his bending ability useless. With Bendy McBendface subdued, I call the police to take him to jail. "You're going to want to wear some rubber gloves. He's still pretty electrified. Yeah, I can see the lighting bolts spread over his skin as it tries to ground. Better get here soon, if he grounds I can't guarantee what will happen." I walk away from the slowly convulsing body of Bendy McBendface. None of the other heroes were successful with him. Iron Man had tried, but Bendy would always flex away and avoid attacks, and any computations were simply too slow to provide good information. Captain America failed worse, with Bendy simply absorbing and deflecting most of the shield throws. Yet somehow, the guy with a simple power and a degree relating to the power managed to take down someone who escaped everyone else. I have a simple name. Quanta.

article: His name and face flickered up on the screen only after it had started buzzing. I looked over from my computer screen and dully, mild shock registered in my brain. Everything had been dull lately. In my mind, he wasn't dead; he was just calling to tell me some new breakthrough he'd had with whatever he was writing. I picked up my phone and held it for a moment, looking at his smugly smiling face from my screen. I should answer it. But who could be calling me from his number? Why? Why would they do that to me? I answered it. His boyfriend's face popped up. We stared at each other for a minute. He had been crying. I had not been. Finally, he swallowed and said, "You..... had texted him last. I plugged in his phone. It said come home, stay safe. You wanted him to come over to yours." I sighed. "He was out really late. I was closest." I looked away from the screen, I didn't want to cry, I never wanted to cry. "I'll always be his older sister, you know? I'll always want to keep him safe." "I know." I looked back at him, and when our eyes caught, his face began to crumple again, a small sob releasing itself from his chest like a ghost. The noises he made wore down the very last of my resolve. "I miss him." And then we were both crying, ugly tears that they don't show in the movies clutching our phones, mine and his, hoping that the answer laid somewhere in the circuitry.

article: I saw the old man push the swing, again. He had to be at least ninety, and as my aunt would say, "So close to death, he has the Grim Reaper on speed dial." He would sit for a while at the park where I worked as a ranger. Then, struggling to get up from the weathered, wooden bench with arthritic pain, he would rise, go over to the swing, and give it a few desultory pushes. At least, they seemed desultory to me. Each day since I started, for months: He'd sit with his cane, and stare off into nowhere. Then, get up, totter over to the swing set, and give an empty seat a few pushes. Often, that set was occupied by laughing children, challenging one another to swing higher than the rest, sure of their immortality and their ability to be just fast enough, or strong enough, to avoid mistakes the kind that, unfortunately, ended in a broken arm or twisted ankle for the ones who were not as quick, or as brave, as their peers. The old man would wait with the patience that only the elderly have, having known the passage of decades. When those children were done, he'd walk over to the chain-and-rubber child's playground toy, and give it one, two, three pushes. Sometimes four. Then, after a minute, he'd leave. ..... One day, I was overcome with curiosity. I approached him as he slowly made his way to the recently vacated swing set. "Hello?" I came up from behind him. Today he was wearing a yellow short sleeved shirt, the folds of his worn, aged skin moving shakily as he maneuvered his cane to support his frail body. He kept going. I don't think he heard me. "Hello!" I repeated, a little louder as he made it to the swing he traditionally pushed, lacking any child to enjoy it. He slowly turned and looked at me. "Pardon me?" He said with a thick accent. I would guess eastern European roots. "Hello!" "Hello, young man. How are you?" He extended a shaky hand, and I returned a soft handshake. I was approaching forty; I wouldn't say I was all that young. Compared to him, though, I was baby. I couldn't help but notice what looked like a bruise on his inner arm. Poor guy; they probably poked and prodded him for blood at his doctor's office. "Fine. How are you, sir?" I replied. "Oh, just getting along. I come here every day for wool-gathering, you know. Such a beautiful park, here." His voice sounded old, and tired. "It is, sir." "I think my brother and sister would have liked it, here." He said, eyes momentarily downcast behind his thick, Coke-bottle glasses. "Where are they?" "Dead." "I'm sorry to hear it." "Thank you, son." He looked up again, at me. "So, you have a question for me, Officer?" Heh. My uniform. Just under two years on the job, and I'm still not used to people addressing me as'Officer'. "My name is Dan." "Daniel?" "Just'Dan'." "Okay, Daniel. What's your question?" "Well, sir. I noticed you come and push the swing every day, with no children in it. May I ask why?" "You saw me do that, eh?" He smiled a little at this, like he was a child caught stealing from the cookie jar. "Yeah." "Then watch, and I'll explain." He turned to the swing, and gripped the chain with his right hand. "The soldiers took us my brother, my sister, my mother, and me when I was six years old. My father was probably at the factory; I do not know." He paused, his unsteady right hand shaking the chain, his left leaning on his cane. "The soldiers took us, and separated us. My sister and mother in one boxcar; my brother and me in another. I rode a night and a day, and when they let us out, we were herded into long houses. My brother and I stayed together. They put us children to work on machines where our little hands could get at smaller parts. Sometimes my friends' hands were crushed. My brother lost a finger..." He paused, again. "They gave me this to make sure I knew I was a number, not a person." He turned his arm, and showed me the bruise. Only, it wasn't a bruise; it was a series of numbers. Old, faded, but indelibly marked into his skin. "The Americans came and freed us, just a month too late. My mother and sister were dead from the gas chambers, and my brother died of pneumonia. I was ten when I left the camp. I was lucky, and got sent to live with my aunt here in America, where I got work in a bakery." He walked behind the swing, and steadied himself with his cane. "My brother, my sister, and me? We never had a childhood. We never played. We worked, starved, and did our best to avoid the guards' attention. So, I do this." And he pushed the swing. "One push, for my sister, Anna," The swing went out, and came back. "One push, for my brother Yosef," the swing went out, and came back again. "And one push for me, because no one ever did." And he pushed it again. ..... The silence was deafening, punctuated only by the creaking sounds of an un-greased playground swing, and a survivor's memorial to a childhood that was taken from him and his siblings.

article: "So there I was, right? Standing by the portcullis, you know? The one that leads to not a god damn thing but another gate? Anyway, I was talking to Ralph about this rye bread I got the other day. Had some mold on it, ate it anyway. Long story short, I tried to eat my daughter and race my stairs to the pumpkin that was riding our dog. Don't get rye bread from Karl's." adjusts in seat, favoring right leg "Anyway, Ralph is all'ahuuahaha', you know the way he laughs, right? Damn idiot could embarrass a seal. We're talkin and all of a sudden I see him. He's about one hundred-fifty paces out and walkin real funny. He'd stop, then walk, then stop, then jump, then stop, then run. Craziest thing I ever saw. I thought this guy had eaten some of Karl's bread at first then he just started crouching and walking real slow. Ralph had this "genius" idea to just keep doin what we were doing and pretend we didn't see him. Seemed like a troublesome fellow. Had a bow and some daggers and all that. At first he had his bow out. Then he shouldered his bow and took out both daggers. Nice fuckin daggers by the way! All black and shiny and jagged. Didn't look like they had been used though. But this guy, man. He just keeps slinkin toward us. He's maybe thirty or thirty-five paces out now when he just stops. Ralph and I are just standing there at attention like we're supposed to be, you know?, not really sure if this is a test of some sort. I mean, it's broad freakin daylight and this guy is now doing some type of roll thing move tumble over toward a bush and he stops again. Then the fucker shoots Ralph with his bow! I mean just twek! Right in Ralphs chest. Poor Ralph was too stunned to do anything. He just looked down at his chest and then over at me as if to say "Did he just shoot me?" and then again! klekt! He missed, I think, because Ralph was falling but damn! That next shot would have put some wood between his eyes!" sighs "So, Ralph's dead. I'm still trying to process what the flying pig shit is going on when all of a sudden this guy does his little tumbley roll thing over into another bush! I'm like, "HEY! WHAT THE FUCK IS WRONG WITH YOU, MAN?" I think he took this as a threat because next thing I know, I have an arrow flying in my direction. I yell back at him again, "HEY! CUT IT OUT MAN! WHAT THE HELL?" but I'm also no fool and start yelling for you lazy dicks but who's around in ear shot? Not a damned one of you. I swear it was like the time it takes a tree to grow before I managed just to make it inside the door and then all of a sudden, there it was." "That's when I took an arrow to the knee."

article: "Now, remember: you shouldn't be disappointed if none of these weapons attune to you yet." The boy nodded, clearly paying little attention. "These are our most powerful magic items. Many of them draw their power from ancient magic, with a kind of sentience of their own. They don't respond to anything except the touch of the most seasoned warriors - and if they aren't willing, you'll barely be able to lift them. Normally I wouldn't even show you this collection, but you were so excited..." The salesman trailed off, content to watch the bright, hungry look in the boy's eyes as he walked through rows of swords, axes, mauls and assorted polearms. He'd just set off from his little village, was still right at the beginning of his journey. The boy stopped now at a faintly glowing halberd, his eyes twinkling in the iridescent light. "Can I try taking this one off the rack?" "Go ahead." He tried; eventually he was gave up, hands sore. The weapon had not moved. "As I said, there's no need to be disappointed "I know. Can I keep looking at some more?" " ..... If you'd like to, though I really shouldn't let you stay back here for very long." The salesman couldn't help it; the boy reminded him far too much of his own ambitious youth. He was now closely considering a sword and shield hanging from the wall, likely lost in visions of dragonslaying. He tried to pull down the sword: it didn't budge. Neither did the golden trident-and-net combo further down the aisle. After trying his luck with a few brightly-colored longswords the boy started setting his sights on some of the less flashy targets, but the rusty, pockmarked mace lying forgotten in the corner proved too stubborn for his grip as well. "I'm sorry, but I need to get back to the front of the shop now. I'm sure once you've gotten a few adventures under your belt these items will be much more enthusiastic to see you." The boy nodded again weakly, glum and defeated. His mind was once again elsewhere, but this time the salesman felt no satisfaction watching him as he trudged to the exit. He felt fairly deflated as well. Perhaps he'd identified himself too closely with this overconfident young lad, and now felt a sharp pang of sympathy pain. They walked out of the back room towards the front of the store, where the non-magical weapons stood arrayed on simple wooden racks. The boy thanked the salesman and was about to walk out of the store when the man called him back, hesitating briefly. "There is..... one weapon you might want to try. You see that one over there?" He pointed at a sword. Steel, standard height and weight, leather grip. No magic whatsoever, but how would the child know that? "It's a sword of some note, actually. Been passed down for a few generations, and they say it's remarkably welcoming to newcomers - well, to some newcomers. It has greater powers that are locked away until the wielder gains experience, but it can sense potential, and will allow itself to be carried by any who it thinks can become powerful some day." The light shone in the boy's eyes again as he darted forward to try the sword. Sure enough, he yanked it off the display easily - so easily he fell backwards, catching himself just in time to avoid being skewered on a nearby glaive. "Can-I-buy-this-one?" the boy asked, his words rushing together. "Of course," replied the salesman. This was far from his most ethical business decision, but how could he disappoint his own eager young eyes staring out at him from this boy's face?

article: I wake up, battered and scarred from the beat I was given behind the burger joint. I think the name was Ronny's? My memory of yesterday, better yet the last week has been completely faded. It was looking into the fog of a familiar place. The throbbing sensation in my head turned into a throbbing pain, then I realized my entire body was sore and in pain. I look around trying to find any sign of light in the dark confined space I was thrown into. I rustle into a more comfortable position and I hear a rustle from the room beyond. Someone was here. My blood runs fast and my heart trembles. The door opens and behold stands a man that my mind had not expected at all. Here stands a well dressed man, in a black striped dress suit, blue tie, and a noticeable blue watch on his right hand. He extends his left hand to me. I stupidly I expected to be gently lifted up but instead he throws me upwards and pushes me towards a chair. I stumbled onto the chair, almost being thrown over the chair. I recover and took my respective seat. I was not in a very welcoming place. " Get up. " a very stern voice poked out from behind me. The room itself was very well illuminated and yet I didn't even seem him there nor heard him move. Am I still dazed? My thoughts ran wild as my anxiety flared up. I'm now on the ground and the entire room is ringing. My mind recovers and I stand up straight. The force of the unforeseen slap knocked me clear on the ground. I look into the eyes of the man that stood once behind me. This man was strange. Contrary to the well dressed man this man was very sloppily dressed. He had blue grey jeans that had grease stains all over, a black leather belt, and a light red shirt with a tear on the right shoulder. This was a man that did not give a fuck about his appearance. " Mr. Green. I've been very anxious to see you. " my blood rate pumped up at the mere sentence, " You've been noticed. I don't see what's so special about you, but apparently you are exactly that. Special. " I was confused. Have I done anything wrong? A horrifying thought appeared at the back of my mind. Could this be the Mafia that killed my family? I am the last living member of my family after my Father, God rest his soul, had a gambling addiction that went too far. My entire family was gunned down by them. I sputtered the only word my mind could think, " What? ." He seemed to be annoyed by this, but he continued. " I'll cut it short Green. My daughter has taken notice of you. She spoke to me about your skills in driving. You're quite the sport. " He took a deep breath, " I'll make it simple Green. I don't like you. I may look like I could be one of your buddies, but I hate you and everything you group of shitheads do. However I love my daughter, and I'm not going to let my opinions get in the way. I made an agreement with my daughter that she can have you if I first give you a taste of what will happen if you cross her. " I heard a doorknob turn and in walked an extremely attractive woman. Our eyes locked. I could feel the back of my eyes burn and water start to form in the front. I knew now that the situation wasn't a petty crush. I looked into the eyes of my Sister.
label: human

article: I was pacing all around my room. "I love that man" was all that I could think of over and over again for the last hour. My head was throbbing, it needed to get this thought out of its system. If only I wasn't a coward. If only I had the words to tell him, to tell him how insanely infatuated I was with him. His voice made me tremble and his gleaming smile infected me with pure joy. He was worse than nicotine. He was the type of drug that would kill me. I couldn't hold this any longer, I couldn't hide this anymore. I stared at the pill, it was taunting me. It laughed at me, pressuring me to ingest it. In that split second I said to myself, "fuck it," and I took it. I gulped. The moment of truth would come any minute, when the screeching doorbell would ring. What happened after this would determine everything. It was either a win or a fall. And it was then when I found myself standing in front of him. His physique impeccable. I opened my mouth to talk, but no words came out. It was as if something had obstructed my airway. I choked. He was waiting, waiting for my response. Last night I made a promise that earlier I had regretted, but now it was all my body wanted to do. "You said you would answer my question." He stated in a monotonous voice. "I did, didn't I?" I responded, stupidly. "Do you love me? "It was there, no running away from the truth anymore. My mouth spoke before my mind could analyze. Every word I poured out of my body was like I was spitting out water after being drowned. I was walking closer to him by the second. "I do, I have for the past three years and probably will fore the ones to come. I love you so much. I love your voice, and the way you say things with much confidence. I love the way you hold my hand gently and pet my hair. I love the way you kiss my nose and when you stare at my eyes as if we were the only two people in this universe. I love the way you tenderly grasp my head while kissing my lips. When I'm with you I can't even imagine anywhere I'd rather be. With you, I peak. You know every part of me and I know even the smallest freckle in your body. I can't imagine a world where I'm not with you, much worse, a world without you. It's nonsense. It's unreal, a nightmare. I love you, do you? Do you love me with the passion that I do?

article: It's been two years since I burned a world to save the people I love and cherish. Even then, I couldn't save everyone. Ever since the Empress rose to power in the Valadrian system, allied with Kovarth Federation and pocketed the Cabinet of Interstellar Security and Transit, our little corner of the universe has fallen apart. br br I watched it all unfold over the course of two decades while engineering the tech to bring me here. When the Jumpers were disabled, I knew it was time to reach into the past. Armed with ancient lore dismissed as faerie tales, I left the Arquaio cluster in search of our ruthless ancestors. br br Now, here I am. I didn't think the old Ki'Robil tech would work until I witnessed the fabric of space and time being ripped apart. Now as I stare out at this beautiful sphere suspended in the dead of space, I almost feel as though I am dreaming. br br I move my consciousness through the neural network of my ship's AI, checking the data scans returned from my probes and drones. The surface has much more oxygen than I am accustomed to, and the region I am going to has been reported as having high humidity. I frown as I pass over the thought of using my organic body. br br "It is most advisable, Cait" DREXEL, the AI, chimes. "If these creatures are, indeed, the ancestors to your organic species, then you need to take every measure you can to blend in. At least for their comfort. " br br "I still despise" I pause and imagine myself in a body, wrinkling my nose and crossing my arms stubbornly for DREXEL. "Such a delicate husk. What if they regard me as hostile? I'll be nearly defenseless!" I growl under my breath and navigate to the Organic Mass Cryostorage lab. br br "DREXEL, begin download" My tone is agitated, and I can almost feel myself grinding my teeth. br br "Consciousness transfer initiated. " br br Leaving the Collective is always strange. It's like free-falling thousands of feet only to get rubber banded into a bounce wall and then pitched into hot water. Or gelatin. br br When I open my eyes, I am initially startled at the intensity of my vision. Seeing everything with such detail is just..... Incredible every time. As a free form consciousness, the universe looks much more like a digitized heat map. br br After getting the cryo goo off and donning some clothing, I finally take up my seat in the bridge and give myself another look over. br br At "six foot one," I am considered small for my species, however I know from my research that the Terrans will be startled at it. I look at my child-like skin, strikingly pale blue eyes and thick white hair tied back in a strict bun, and realize that I may be downright intimidating. Especially with the brand by my right eye. I narrow my eyes as I continue to inspect a physique that would be described as too limby and scrappy. br br I laugh gently under my breath as I look down at the communication console to my right. "Let them be intimidated" I mutter as I attempt to establish a connection with what the Terrans called "The United Nations." The amount of time it takes is obnoxious, and a man answers in a very gruff and grumpy tone. br br Displeased, I terminate the call immediately and sigh. br br "Why?" br br "I have my reasons, DREXEL, now hush." I think for several moments before I hop up and grab my jump jack, plugging it into my neural socket interface and furiously pressing at buttons on the communications relay console. br br "Cait, I feel like this is a bad idea." DREXEL drones. I wave my hand flippantly through the air and after a few more keystrokes, I settle into my chair and my consciousness connects with my ship. It's an effortless transition, my skin becoming the shield, my bones and muscles becoming structure and armour. The many drones that help keep the ship up and assist with combat are now my eyes and ears. br br I go instantly for the orbital missiles, loading them into the launcher and descending into the atmosphere. At this point, I re-establish a comm link, but this time it's with something called "National Emergency Broadcast System" in the country The United States of America. "Should get someone's attention at least..." I mutter in the last seconds before my link goes live and dive further into the atmosphere, the heat making my skin tingle and bones vibrate. br br "My name is Cait Nathair. I am an operative of the Dalsic Collective in the Arquaio Cluster approximately one hundred-twenty..... Oh sod it..." I bite my lip for a moment and sigh heavily. "I need help..." br br For the first time in decades, I felt helpless. My people are enslaved under the tyrannical rule of a mad woman claiming to be chosen by God and waging international war in our cluster and here I am wanting to bring a somewhat innocent species into it. br br "I need them for their combat prowess..." I say out loud, unaware that DREXEL had connected a call with the "POTUS." br br "This is our reputation in the galaxy?" I signal for the visual feeds to activate and the face of a young man flickers to life before me. If the POTUS is a powerful person, then why do they have a mere child labeled as such? He couldn't be any older than thirty. br br "Uh, well..... More like the universe, Mister POTUS, sir" I manage a faint laugh. Ugh, this body and it's awkward feelings. "My name is..." br br "Cait Nathair. Yes, I got that." His drawling accenting is already irritating me. I just want to tell at him to speak faster, but instead opt for clenching at my arm rests as tight as possible. "What can I help you with, ma'am? Is everything okay? " br br "No." Sod it. Let's get down to business. "My people have been enslaved by a tyrannical empress and we have no means to fight back. Only a select few we designed with combat ability, and I am the only one left of that generation." I look away briefly as I am hit with an overwhelming sense of grief. I see Aaron's helmeted face, the jagged scar of a smile carved deeply into the faceplate. The emptiness I feel in my heart and mind at his absence starts to feel like a crushing pressure that will consume me. br br "Excuse me? We have not been made aware of any new established Governments or uprisings in our region. We haven't been contacted by the Intergalactic Militia or anything..." He looked deeply confused as he calls an aide over and starts giving him orders to seek information. br br This is it. The make it or break it moment. br br "Sir, you haven't heard about it because it is very far away, distance and time. Your people are a myth to my original species. I knew though, that I could find you. My research and developments are..... Were..... Illegal, but it got me here." I sigh and remove my jump jack. The look of shock on the young man's face could have been horror, but I wasn't certain. br br "I am a third generation Synth. Organically, I am a mixture of all my native races, but I was assimilated by an AI and am now a freeform consciousness able to take on an organic body or synth avatar. My people have done nothing but move for peace through pacifism and try to understand the Gaians, but because we are not actual Gaians and connected to a shared AI, we are seen as abominations, automatons who should do the bidding of those in the highest castes. " br br Mister POTUS looks skeptical, complete with a lonely cocked eyebrow. I manage a faint grin, my expression softening. "I will provide the technology to get your soldiers to and from home, and I will cover all your costs for ships, weapons and neural modifications. " br br "Whoa, hold on now. You're pretty much telling me that you are a..... What a robot? Hooked up to a hive network? And you want our help freeing your" he makes air quotes for the next part "people? " br br "You will be getting access to jump jack technology and a free trip across the universe. In other words, I will bring you to the big leagues as far as space travel goes, and you will have access to Research and Development labs to the create new weapons. Your soldiers will all be made jump jack compatible and be given cryostasis clone save states. This will prevent them from dying permanently. Except for tragic lab accidents..." The connection terminates and I sit there in silence, looking out the command bridge glass to peer down at the world below. "I'm sorry, Cait." DREXEL consoles. I smile wickedly and turn to a large insectoid drone that skitters around my feet. I reach out and touch it lovingly, like a mother would. "They'll say yes." I lean back into my seat and look at the man who has sat quietly at the command bridge cobsole, taking in everything. He nods in agreement, and folds his cybernetic arms across his chest. The lights on his ocular flare briefly as he looks at me. "And when they do?" "I will get him back." "Cait, Aaron's gone." Jackson stands and walks over to me, placing a gentle hand on my shoulder. "Your link has been dead for years now." I shake my head, feeling the wretched sting of sadness and regret against my eyes. "Then I will watch the Cluster burn for him..."

article: OFFICE OF THE GALACTIC EXECUTIVE FOR TOP LEVEL VISUAL APPENDAGES ONLY PRELIMINARY REPORT ON PLANETARY CIVILIZATION HEW-MAN BREEDING STRUCTURE OF HEW-MAN SPECIES Over the course of 17 malarkians, a team of Galactic xenological researchers visited the Hew-man civilization in 38 separate locations to observe the species' breeding practices. Initial rumors of the primitive practice were grossly understated; not only do the Hew-mans lack rational breeding practices, but they actively engage in behaviors that undermine health, well-being, and social security. This was especially shocking to the researchers as the Hew-mans have demonstrated a mastery of flight, space travel, atomic power, and a basic grasp of quantum mechanics. More importantly, the Hew-mans have imposed rational breeding upon planetary sub-species, but not on themselves. They will, for example, not allow animals with genetic abnormalities breed. This is especially frightful considering the bioloigical structure of the Hew-mans, who have chosen to continue to carry their young inside themselves, despite the great danger this poses to both productivity and health. While species with space flight have typically rationalized breeding to allow a fetus to develop inside an egg or other technological vessel, Hew-mans keep their young inside their females. The most famous of them take photographs of their dangerously swollen bellies for widespread distribution via media and are lauded for bravery. This reinforces a social expectation that females should continue to risk their lives in the pursuit of young children inside them. Production of the young is a deeply irrational process. Cursory transmissions of a breeding aid site, PornHub, indicated a species obsessed with practicing procreation without actually succeeding, allocating vast amounts of resources, time, and personnel to public breeding practice. Initially, this was presumed as a method of social control, with PornHub utilized to distract Hew-mans with fewer resources from those who have more resources. However, it is revealed that PornHub is most popular with those with the most resources, who do not utilize their extra time and resources to find more efficient breeding practices, but instead reinforce the dangerous practices that lead to disease, swollen Hew-man bodies, and irrational emotions. There is some hope for the Hew-mans however: recently production of an egg-laying device (known planetarily as an "Aleyian Egg DIL-do, by which a Hew-man may experience an egg laid inside them, is evidence that the Hew-mans are gropingly moving towards a better form of procreation. Widespread practice with this device may convince the Hew-mans of the superior nature of eggs over swollen bellies. We recommend the dispatch of further teams for education in the use of this device for the Hew-mans, leading up to a full rollout of a permanent egg laying procedure for all Hew-Mans for procreation.

article: As a kid, he haunted my dreams. My worst nightmare was him being in my bed when I woke up, but this wasn't a dream. This was real wasn't it? I back away from the door, but the King kicks it open. It has to be a man in a mask. It has to be, but he is adorned in the entire getup. Not a word is spoken by either of us. He points to the bathroom. What did he want? Maybe this is a prank. Hopefully, it is. I walk into the bathroom and wait for my fate. "What are you going to do to me? Please don't hurt me." The King points to the floor. I sit. He holds his hand in a stop motion. He heads back to the main room. Shotgun blasts rattle my ears. Other gunshots ring out. I peek out the door and see the King blast the Hamburglar in the face. The King turns to look at me, a blank unchanging expression on his face. He leans down and picks up the Hamburglar's handgun and hands it to me. He waves for us to go. "Can't I stay here?" The King shakes his head. He pats me down and finds my car keys. He heads to the parking lot and finds my car without any help. I hop into the passenger seat, and he takes off to an unknown location. I look behind us, and I finally understand what he's running from. Ronald McDonald, Gidget the Taco Bell chihuahua, and Colonel Sanders give chase, and they're catching up to my Prius. The King motions for me to take the wheel. I slide over and start driving. He leans out the window and fires at the mascots who chase us. I watch in the rear view mirror as Gidget has a front tire shot out and crashes. The clown sneaks by the King and drives along side of me. The King pushes my chest back and fires a few rounds into Ronald's van. The clown just laughs. The Colonel holds back, and the clown tries to run us off the road. The King sees a safe haven. He motions for me to pull into the nearest Burger King. I have no reason to doubt him. I veer off of the main road, nearly killing us. My back driver side tire explodes from a gunshot. I keep driving and pull into the BK parking lot and stop near the door. The King pulls out of the car and shields me as he fires more slugs into Ronnie's van. Colonel Sanders pulls in behind us. I grab the handgun from the King's waistband and fire at the Colonel. Two in the chest and one in the head, the Colonel is down. The King gets hit by the clown, who is enjoying the hell out of this. The bullet has gone through his arm. He'll be okay. I grab his shotgun and fire at the clown who has exposed himself. The first slug hits his thigh, the second in his chest. He falls to the ground, a bloody mess. I drop the shotgun on the ground. The King stands and pats me on the back. He motions to go inside. I walk to the door. He opens the first door for me, and I head to the second one. I return the favor. The King returns home triumphant. He takes one step inside when his back explodes with blood. He falls to the ground. I race to catch him. I turn to look at the culprit. It's the one I least expected: Wendy. Yes, that Wendy. She just laughs and walks outside into the parking lot. I walk out behind her and pick up the King's shotgun. She turns to look at me. "You helped to take down the bad guy in all of this. We're going to be heroes. Good job on the Colonel and the clown. Now, it's all mine." She pauses. "Hear those sirens, that's the police coming." I can hear sirens in the distance, but I can't let her get away with it. Even though she's a child, no, she isn't a child. She, like the others, is a mascot, probably twice my age. She is the most manipulative of them all, hiding behind that innocence. She puts her hands up in the air. I grab the shotgun from the ground and point it at her back and squeeze the trigger.
label: human

article: In a town called Yardel, in the 27th year of the Glorious Reign of King Ionil the Second, there was a tower tall and filled with secrets. Carved upon the entryway were the words, written out in the script of the Elder Tongue, the Scholar's Stone. In it dwelled two men, one who was called Ynvarg, though none truly believed that this name, a name from a ancient era now gone when the wild magic that had ruled the world was tamed and conquered and bound to the will of men, was his own from birth. Ynvarg was ancient and oft coughed, great hacking wheezes which shook his body and left him exhausted and in pain, but so very wise. He spoke the Elder tongue as if it were the language of his birth. The other was named Ulthir, a bastard boy of the age of 16. He served as the apprentice of Ynvarg, learning the ways of magic and its command using the Elder Tongue. One day, the youth approached his master, and asked him "Ynvarg, are you my father?" The master turned to his ward, a hint of a smile upon his face. "And what makes you think I am, young one?" "Well, my father disappeared during the Destruction of Morgshold, but I always felt he was alive. I felt drawn to you, as if you were someone I knew, and we share a hint of the same look. But that was not enough to make me suspect. But there is more. You see, my mother never told me my father's name, but I searched through old letters and found his name. Vayar. And what name did the witch of the wilds call you when she bound you with your true name? Vayar. Then there is this." the whelp held out two stones, a deep dark red. He then touched them together and they began to shine with a unnatural light. "Blood stones. Made from our blood. They glow when they touch kinsmen's blood." "I hope you didn't take essence from a old man while he slept. I have need for as much red life as I can muster" "Of course not, I took it when you had me clean the floor after that little mix up with the summoned imp. I know we share blood. And you share my fathers name. So, why don't you just tell me, please? You are my father aren't you?" The boys eyes seemed to shine with tears as he begged for his master to give him trust, a bond. The old man now looked as if someone had told a joke during a solemn occasion, struggling to keep his face straight. "My boy, there is little I can say. I have two pieces of advice. The first is that when you long for a home you shall find one on the banks of the river Eidir. The second," the old man seemed to whisper, forcing the boy to lean in to hear. He listened as if every word was weighted by gold. "The girl by the tavern, Gunwuld? She fancies you." the old man now laughed, unleashing the mirth hidden behind a stony face. The boy's inner fire now raged outwards as if lightning had struck upon straw. "You dare taunt me, old man? I have cleaned your piss pot, helped you up the stone steps, carried your burdens, cleaned your messes, cooked your meals, and in exchange I was promised knowledge. Yet I ask you something so key, so vital, so easily given but so hard to do without, and you refuse me! You will tell me you horrid living carca..." the speech of the quickling was cut short as a great hailstone rained out from the wizards pointed finger, driven by words which carried with them all the power and fury of the cold northern storm. The whelp was struck by four chunks of ice, each of which formed a maniacal that held him fast to the wall of the rock. His lips then frosted over, turning to solid ice. "I must? I must? I must tell you at whose behest, youngling? Do you claim the power to command me, your master, to obedience? Would you have me bowing before your boots young master? You are a fool it seems. You remembered the blood stone recipe, but you seemed to have forced out old knowledge to make room in your little mind. We follow the Old Ways here. It is the sacred path that allows us to command magic in safety. Its tenants guide us. Now, I am going to free your mouth the first thing out of it had best be the 1st of the 8. The boy now felt the ice around his mouth slowly turn warm and melt. "The apprentice is to obey the master, for the knowledge most ancient of the master gives wisdom to the new who will carry it on, and the master must be heeded." the boy stuttered automatically. "Ineed. And yet I must. Still, I suppose the Old Ways do, in some ways command me to do as you ask..... let us say this, we shall decide who deserves the title of master based upon another of the Old Way's. If you ever best me in a duel then you shall gain what you seek." And the master and his apprentice continued in this way for years. With the apprentice following dutifully, but with occasional outbursts like a coal which appears to cool then flares brightly as the wind touches upon it. They dueled many times, but each the master was victorious, using some trick or secret which the boy knew not of. And eventually these duels ended when the master fell ill and began coughing more and more. And so, on the 28th year of the life of the boy Ynvarg died peacefully abed. And the boy, now a man, buried his master in stones carved in the runes of the Elder Tongue, that his body might resist the onslaught of the ages. The boy, now a man, took the tower for himself, and for his bride, the girl Gunwuld. He had been married by his master, insisting than other than the man who brought them together could perform the ceremony. Ulthir had a son in time, named for his master who was perhaps his father in blood, but who was most definitely his father in spirit, as Vayar. And so time marched on and Ulthir continued his masters work, finding secrets old and new and teaching them to those who would serve in the tower that was called the Scholar's Stone, including the young Vayar. Eventually the former boy now master passed away and left the tower and its collected knowledge to his son. Vayar worked tirelessly to instead the passing of time. And one day while he worked, around the home which his father had built far from the village on the shores of the river Eidir, he found himself taken with a flash. He found the river barren of population, and wandered far. He found the village of Yardel, far smaller than he remembered it. He asked about the Scholar's Stone, whose place was barren and received no answer. People spoke about Morgshold as if it yet remained standing to this day. And when he asked the year he was answered that it was the 39th Year of the Glorious Reign of King Ionil the First. So he realised that his effort to understand the passage of time, which carried all men as easily as the river carries a stick, had taken him upstream. And so he realized now his true identity, that of the ancient sage which his father spoke of in his stories. So when he was asked his name he answered that he was Ynvarg, "the Wise One" in the Elder Tongue. And when asked why he had come to the humble dwelling of Yardel he had but one answer. "I wish a peaceful place to construct a tower, a place to work. A place of knowledge. Other than that, well..... who can know the future?"

article: Once my son was old enough, and once my wife consented, nbsp; I left behind the village and left behind my people. nbsp; The unexplained fate of my father who vanished, nbsp; who never returned, from his quest to find his. nbsp; Living my entire life supporting mom nbsp; until supporting my own family until they were so strong. nbsp; So that they would not cry when I left nbsp; in the footsteps of father For a place I've seen in countless dreams, nbsp; The Mountains Yana, steep walled and exalted, nbsp; their base close to home, their peak far, far beyond the clouds. nbsp; Through the range, as weeks passed nbsp; darker became the skies, yet warmer the rock. nbsp; An eternity alone, it felt, but I could not falter nbsp; I held my father's fate entwined with my own. nbsp; My reserves had gone dry many months ago nbsp; and yet with each hand-over-hand I felt my thirst being quenched. nbsp; Without stopping to sleep, somehow each foothold in the stone nbsp; seemed to restore my life seemed to restore my youth. nbsp; Generations of gods must've rose and fallen, nbsp; dynasties of my people must've rose and fallen. nbsp; But I've long since forgotten about them, since finding father nbsp; at the core of the Mountains Yana, surrounded by our ancestors, nbsp; grandfather, and great grandfather nbsp; and hundreds more all with the faces of children nbsp; perfectly preserved in a meadow in the sky, nbsp; in the heart of the Mountains Yana, nbsp; turning their faces to me and asking me nbsp; "won't you play with us?" And the garden grows.

article: As I walked hand-in-hand with my husband and wife team, I spotted the bottle washing ashore. "Hang on," I said to my friends. "That looks like it could be worth something." As I skipped over to the bottle, a creeping sense of unease came over me; the hairs on the back of my neck rose like they were trying to man the lifeboats. Pulling out the cork of the bottle, I noticed the year imprint on the bottom of the bottle: 1914. The letter popped out with no help when I tipped the bottle. Breaking the seal on the letter, I unrolled it, reading the letter. Dear Hanna, If you are reading this, then I have failed. We are cursed, and soon it will pass to you. It is matrilineal, meaning it is passed on through the females of the line. Soon, you will be able to see things no other person will see. You will know when some things will come to pass. I wanted to save you in particular because of the pain this journey will cause. Leave your lovers, Karis and Alberto. Go west, to Waikiki and stay there for three years. If you do not, you will end up in a sanatorium, broken and meandering, when the world needs you. I will do my best to prepare you. In the attic of your mother's home, you will find an old trunk. Once you have left your lovers, you MUST retrive this and go. Supplies will be included, although you will need to go to a pawnbrokers first. May God and Lucifer have mercy on your soul, Angelou Maria de Cervantes, Cursed Contessa On the thirteenth day of the fifth month in the year of our Lord 1914. Heart pounding, I picked the bottle up and walked back to my lovers. I showed them the letter, but I saw..... something. A shadow rising beyond them, in the form of a slim man with greying hair at his temples, glasses and a pinstripe suit.
label: human

article: [ Wrote this awhile back for a collaborative writing forum I work with. Enjoy. ] The defendant stood stoically in the courtroom, seemingly unconcerned with what hung in the balance. Absently, he checked his watch. 12:30 PM. It was time. He nudged his lawyer, whispered something; the man nodded solemnly. This seemed to please him, as he returned to facing the bench. After an interminable pause, a door opened, and the twenty men of the jury entered, seating themselves in the benches provided for them. The judge, an elderly man with a severe look about him, adjusted his wig and cast one last hard glare at the defendant before rapping his gavel, seating the assembled audience. "Anton Malinowski, you will rise to hear verdict," he said, his voice solemn, clear, imperious. Malinowski, the defendant, stood in defiance, his entire being tensed as he glared unflinchingly at the man who had been his tormenter, his adversary, for the past two months. It had all come down to this moment. "Has the jury reached a verdict?," the judge said, turning his attentions away from the Communist before him. "We have, Your Honor," came a voice from the bench, a woman's this time. "Very well," the judge replied. "You may proceed." "In the first count, of Treason against the Government of His Majesty the King, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty," the woman read. "The vote upon this matter was unanimous." Malinowski's glance snapped to the bench, staring daggers at those who shrank beneath the man's gaze. His lawyer placed a hand upon his shoulder, a vain attempt to calm the man. The woman proceeded, her voice cracking now. "In the second matter, of ten counts Murder in the First Degree, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty. Upon these counts, the votes were unanimous." "In the third matter, of eighty-three counts Defamation of the Personage of the King, we do find the defendant Anton Malinowski guilty. Upon these counts, the votes were unanimous." Having finished her labor, the woman sat, heaving a sigh. Malinowski was rendered numb as the judge thanked the jury for its service. He was numb as the judge read out that he was to be executed by hanging. He was deaf and blind to the fury of the crowd assembled outside the courthouse and throughout the country. As he was led away in handcuffs and irons, he was ignorant of the one fact that would make Anton Malinowski, steelworker, a name remembered throughout history. He had started the Revolution. "Fuck, we can't hold'em! Where the fuck is our cavalry?" Officer Fabian Wyrick screamed in desperation into his radio as hordes of enraged protestors converged upon him. The shield wall of the Greater Glodno Police, Special Services Division, had seemed so imposing when the two sides had merely been casting harsh looks and harsh words at one another. Then, the verdict had come, and the words turned to action. Hundreds, perhaps a thousand, rushed toward the courthouse and toward the police barrier, trying to break their man free or at least break a few heads in the process. The police quickly found themselves overwhelmed. Wyrick swung wildly in all directions, making contact at least a few times before his stamina and adrenaline high wore off. Exhausted, and having made no serious dent in the mob before him, he relented. In an instant, the mob set upon him, furiously beating themselves against the riot shield behind which he had crouched, and beating him ferociously with any instrument they could set their hands upon. This was how it would end. Wyrick closed his eyes and began praying for grace, for mercy, for forgiveness of any sins, waiting for the moment to come when it would end. And end it did, though in a most horrible way. Suddenly, a loud revving sound cut through the din, causing police and protestor alike to stop and turn their heads. Advancing down the block, unmistakable in its behemoth size and terrible glory, was a BTR-80. The Royal Army had apparently decided to take matters into its own hands, and proceeded to unleash a torrent of 7.62mm fire and 14.5mm heavy autocannon rounds into the now-fleeing crowd. Most did not have time to scream before they were cut down. Wyrick could only watch, horrified, as the crew of the BTR chased after those who fled, running several down in a splatter of gore. "You fucking monsters!," he shouted, knowing as he did that it was all in vain. "Stop this fucking slaughter! For the love of God stop it!" Not thinking, half-mad with rage, he charged the BTR. It was by sheer luck that he managed to climb atop it, and sheer forgetfulness of the crew that he managed to pop the compartment open. Now, he found himself staring face-first at uniformed crew of one of the Household Guard's armored carriers. It was not a situation most would envy. "What the fuck do you think you're doing? Those are our countrymen out there you goddamn psychopaths! Turn this fucking thing around and go home!" It was futile, he knew, but Wyrick was a man on autopilot, and futility did not register at this point. After a pause, Wyrick received his reply in the form of a solid slug to the jaw. With a sickening crack, he was out cold. Three hours later, the streets were empty, save for the Household Guard patrolling a city that was now under martial law. Untold thousands had been killed or dragged off the streets. And Officer Fabian Wyrick was bound in the back of an armored carrier, on the way to meet an unlikely ally.

I wasn't really listening, but then my ears perked up. "Why?" asked the negotiator. "The counselor told me to do something new, expand my horizons, escape my familiar behavior patterns. I thought for a bit, and then realized I never imagined I could be bad. It sounded like a challenge. I thought I'd give it a try." "But why this? Why not, say, climb a mountain?" asked the negotiator. The criminal looked puzzled for a moment. "Oh. Oh, yeah. I didn't think of that. Yeah, that would be fun. " .

article: Would you have believed that it could happen, if you'd been in my place? I've seen countless heist movies and even experienced a couple of armed robberies firsthand as a teller. But a 4 year old little girl? How would that even be suspect? We like to give back to the community and kids who love their parents bank are likely to stay customers when they grow up. So, any kid whose parent opens a Junior Saver account with us can ask me, the head teller, to be a junior banker for the day. We start the day off with a tour of the place - you know, behind the counter to see the computers, running a stack of hundreds through the counters, and then back to the vault. Then the kid picks a teller to work with all day. The teller is in charge of the kid, and oh, do the parents love a day free of their sweet children! Today was the day that the Smythes brought in little Susie for her junior banker day. We've had it on the books for a couple of weeks, since they opened her Junior Saver account. After I gave her the grand tour, I handed her off to Danielle for the day. Little Susie was just full of all sorts of questions, according to Danielle. Normal kid things, like how high each teller can count, how much can we hold in our vault, and how many silly people came through each day. After awhile, Susie lost interest in all things banking and went to the area we keep toys and entertainment in for when our Junior bankers go back to being kids while they're parents are still away on their day off. I had forgotten Susie was even with us today, until I heard the vault alarm going off and Susie wailing from behind the door. When we got the door open, Susie sniffled and cried out for her mommy, whom we called post haste. We made sure Susie had her things - her dolly, her blanket, and her backpack with her snacks and juice boxes, which she hadn't touched. It was hours later when we realized that the problems with the computer system weren't just software glitches - money was actually being funneled from our account holders' accounts into an off-shore untouchable account belonging to a "Mr. Bear." When we reviewed the security footage, it became obvious. Susie watched Danielle login in to the system and scribbled down the letters Danielle typed. Same thing with Michael, Julia, and even myself. She hid out in the vault and no one noticed, we closed the door after a client was done with his safety deposit box, not realizing she was in there. When she woke up from her nap, she started crying for mommy and daddy. When the Smythes picked up their daughter, I heard her state plainly "I want Mr. Bear!" Her father shushed her and said "Now, now pumpkin, you know we're leaving on a plane this evening to go see your beloved Mr. Bear. Did you have a good day at the bank with the nice bankers?" "Yes daddy, I want to be a banker when I grow up!" "I'm sure you'll be great with money, kiddo."
label: human

article: So this is how it ends for me. 23 years old and living in my "natural habitat." It's been 2 weeks since I was tossed into this pen and all I've been eating is a yogurt like paste that tastes like dirt. My name is Jacob Turner, and I have no idea what planet I'm on, or what galaxy I'm in, for that matter. Earth has been a haven for criminals for the last 200 years. Since the invasion of 2078, humans have been proclaimed the working class among celestial beings. We are used for entertainment, slave work, even scientific experiments. The slaves are the lucky ones. I was an entertainer. More specifically, I handled bets at the race track. These aliens clinched on to human culture, but not without their own modifications. Genetically produced horses make for a good bet. One day I decided I had enough. There are underground dealers who will smuggle humans out for a hefty cost. Human trafficking is very illegal, ironically for the exact opposite reason it was illegal for us back in the day. I hired the best one I could find. It wasn't enough. They had moles throughout the underground network. My agent was unknowingly employing one of them, so he we are. It's the ultimate humiliation, being like a rodent. Children laugh at me and ask why my skin is so smooth. I'm a disgusting being here, and they let me know it. One of the "Human handlers" walked into my habitat, wheeling in a huge box on a trolley. "We got ourselves a grant from the parks department. Your going to have a new friend." Another person? I couldn't believe it. My face lit up with joy. When were they coming? Would it be a woman? What I would give to touch a woman's hair again. I read the side of the crate he was rolling in as he kicked it to roll off the cart. "A.I. UNIT 22342 Lot 334. Female. Blonde." I read further. There was a slogan..... "Your mans best friend is our business." (Will continue later)

article: We're all that's left now. Reddit, the Golden City, The Frontpage of the Universe, The Caterer to all. It floats above the ruined landscape below, a beacon of hope and of sanctuary. Once it was the arbitrator, the crossroads between many nations, the best crop of all these kingdoms would always find it's way to The Top, a huge square at the highest peaks of the city where upvotes would be traded for whatever was on display, be it an animal of advice, a humorous performance from the Youtube or even one of Reddit's own public forums such as rAskReddit. The city was divided up into it's subreddits, every day the citizens would browse and participate in their chosen topic, even the seedier ones. We should have acted. We knew war was coming, even rOutOfTheLoop could tell you that. Our neighbouring nations, 4chan and Tumblr were constantly at each other's necks; their ideological differences were massive and neither side was willing to compromise. As it always did, conflict ensued. It started normally enough, another border skirmish. A Tumblr zealot group attacked which was met by a harsh response by 4chan the escalation continued until full scale war was inevitable. We should have acted, we should have tried to arbitrate and stopped the bloodshed before it stated. But no, we just sat back and watched. After all why would it affect us? But the battles grew and grew, the flame wars would leave nought but ash in their wake. The war looked over, Tumblr had always outnumbered the 4channers by a considerable margin, soon 4chan itself was almost overrun, forcing them to bring in their nuclear option: Youtube. No one knows how they managed to convince The Trolls to enter the fray, all that we know is that it spelled the end. Youtube's trolls were legion, a boundless horde spamming and overwhelming any force standing in their way. Tumblr never stood a chance. Only now did we act, this had gone too far. But as mighty as we may have been, nothing could stand against the Trolls. When Tumblr had fallen they turned their attention to their allies and had soon consumed them as well, their rampage finally stopping after devastating several more of the Social Media States. I remember the day when Pinterest burned. I fought on the front line, they called me a hero then, but what kind of hero waits till it's too late to save anyone. The refugees came to us for help, people all kingdoms and opinions. It was only us and our twin city Imgur that still stood in the end. Even as I speak rarchitecture is planning a refugee camp for them to stay, there's no room in the city anymore. We're putting them to good use though; battlements are being constructed, weapons forged and a wall built around the cities. We must be ready, we must be vigilant. Rumors abound of a Second Troll Host assembled and that they've turned their eyes towards the Last Sanctuary of the Internet. It was only a matter of time after all.

article: Sprawled on the bathroom floor, my body slumped in submission. The crackling of centuries finally catching up, grey hairs sprouting where clumps of brown now disintegrate. My muscles tremble as the skin around them loosen, wrinkles arching and sagging. I become barely bones and the skin that covers. Weakness overwhelms as I struggle to look at them. It was never a dream, they did exist but their influence was beyond what I could have comprehended. I cursed the voices that echoed in my head, that pushed away everyone around me, that ensured I would end up in an asylum. The years spent arguing, rationalizing their presence and pretending everything was fine eventually became too much to bear. They drove off my greatest love, and I finally took my stand. I told them to leave, their occupation was not welcomed, and they agreed. I lie now on this bathroom floor as the spirits of my past evacuate, leaving behind the husk that shunned them. The life rushes from my body as I am left to stand on my own, and all I can utter is "please..... Please, don't go."
label: human

article: I don't know if they did it on purpose, but I couldn't look at them because they angled my chair toward the sun. My father watched confusedly from his sitting chair behind me. Eventually he met what I assumed was my gaze. "Well?" My mother continued pacing across the tile floor in her high heels. Every click was louder than the clack that followed. In my head I pictured the cut-off oval shape on the bottom of her heel as its entire surface area pressed flat against the dirty porcelain, cracking tiny rocks and scattering them apart. "I-I'm sorry." "What are you sorry for? " asked my father more softly than my mother's heels. "I'm..... sorry." Father pulled his hands behind his head, straightening his back before stooping to my level with his palms on his thighs. "What-What do you think you were doing?" click-shatter, clack-shatter "I was playing." click-shatter, clack-shatter "What were you playing, huh?" click-shatter, clack-shatter click-shatter, clack-shatter "I was just playing friends." click-shatter, clack-shatter "Okay. We don't play that, okay? Not with other boys, okay?" "How come?" click-clack, click, clack. Into the kitchen. "We don't play that game, okay? Just My father stood up again and looked at the crucifix on the wall. Not that it wasn't already obvious, but that's where he looked. God bless him, he really did try. "I don't know, son. I don't know. But, we're not supposed to do that, okay? Can you just- Maybe when you're older we can Mother walked out of the kitchen, passed us, and went into my bedroom. Dad put his finger to his lips. " God said that he doesn't want us to do that with boys, okay? So we don't. " "But you Father replaced his finger to his lips. " But mommy kisses you. How come she can, but I Mommy walked out of my room carrying a cardboard box. She strode toward us with her click-clacking the whole way. She stopped in front of dad and dropped the box in my lap. Inside were some of my clothes. She looked at me long enough to take ten drags from ten cigarettes. "What's that for?" asked dad. "There's a car coming in ten minutes. Take anything you might need." Dad didn't even hesitate. "Why?"
label: human

article: Dude, are you serious right now? You're not even trying. You look pathetic. They call you the Third Time's a Charm killer because it takes you two attempts to actually kill somebody properly. And now you come to me. You stupid fuck. We've met twice before. You were in my home economics class way back in middle school. We actually hung out for a bit. You attempted to electrocute me when I was in the shower after I spent the night for a sleepover by throwing a toaster into the shower with me, though you forgot to plug it in. I thought it was just a funny prank, so I laughed it off. Then we met again senior year of high school, biology class. You tried to kill me again by giving me a desk that had a shitty leg. You spent detention whittling down the metal leg of the desk to have it shaped like a shiv. You then weakened the other side of the desk so it would collapse in the direction of the leg shaved like a shiv. You hoped it would collapse and then impale me like some medievil weaponry, but luckily for me the teacher moved my desk that day, and put out a work order for the custodians to take this dangerous desk away. I then realized that you were no longer trying to play a prank, but rather flat out kill me. I never understood why. We were such good friends at one point. Maybe you were jealous of me. Maybe you just got off on the fact that if you killed me, it would give you some sick false sense of power you have over me. But here I still stand, as do you, many years later of unsuccessfully killing me. I don't really understand why you've been trying to kill me all these years. But like I said, they call you the Third Time's a Charm killer for a reason. This being your third time we've met, I would expect that my death is slow, yet painful, having learned from your past mistakes. I thought of another name for you Wiley E. Coyote Killer, because no matter what you do, I've been one step ahead of you. I am the roadrunner to your Wiley E. You are just truly pathetic at this point. If there was a university of serial killers, you would be laughed at and pointed at by the greats: Dahmer, Gein, Ted Bundy. You know you've mastered something when you make it look easy. Dahmer went years without getting caught. Same for Bundy. They also have one thing over you. They've killed, and quite successfully. You however are an embarrassment to serial killers everywhere, and I suggest you just give up now. You are a pathetic fuck.
