article: When I was only seven, my father left. My mother used to tell me he went to save children in a third world country. After I turned fifteen, she figured I was old enough and finally admitted that he left her after an argument, went to the bar, and died on his way home. It was a sad story. But it wasn't the truth. I remember that night so vividly. How could I forget, when every dream is always a replay of what happened. He came home that night. He walked home from the bar so he wouldn't be hurt, leaving his keys on the table. I can only assume a drunk stole his car. There was too much damage to identify the body after the car exploded. As for my father, however, he came home. My bedroom was right next to the door, so when he knocked, I heard it, and let him in. "Where's your mother?" He asked me. I told him she fell asleep a while ago. He mumbled a frustrated response, then told me to go to bed. "But I'm scared," I replied. "I can't sleep until you scare the monsters away!" He never rolled his eyes at me, and never told me to stop imagining things. This night, like all others, he carried me to my room, tucked me into bed, and leaned down to tell the monsters to go away. But this night was different. As soon as he started to speak, I saw it. A skeletal hand, with nails long and dark, reached out and wrapped around his neck. He started to choke, flailing trying to escape. At seven years old, all I could do was scream. By time my mother got there, he was gone. I told her what happened, and she said it was just a bad dream. But there was no denying the headline the next day. In their defense, I wouldn't believe me either. Even the therapist my mother took me to almost convinced me it was a dream, and he would come home years later from Africa to see me again. One Friday night, when I was ten, I finally gathered the courage to find my father. I grabbed my stuffed teddy, my unicorn flashlight, and a chocolate bar I got at school earlier that day. I lay flat on the floor, staring into the abyss underneath my bed. "Don't be scared," I told myself. After an eternity, I finally shimmied under the bed. I wasn't prepared for what I saw. Hell would have been more pleasant than this. Monsters, demons, and creatures I didn't have a name for. But no father. Every night for a month I went back, hiding behind piles of bones and detached limbs. The world there was stained with blood. I watched every night as monsters pulled in new victims. I never found any of them again, but I could only assume the worst. I thought that was behind me when I moved to university. Until last night. My roommate was out with her boyfriend, so I was by myself. I heard a thump that was familiar. The sound of one of them coming out from under the bed. "Can I sleep up here? It's scary down there." His voice was so familiar, one I hadn't heard in years. I rolled over, and handed him my teddy. "I know," was all I could say before we fell asleep. I woke up this morning and he was gone. I hope he comes back tonight. I finally didn't dream of that night. The monsters were finally scared away.
label: human

article: "Are we really going to do it, P?" "We don't have any other choice, Jazzy." Jasmine sighed and pulled her coat in closer around her. Pocahontas looked at her, face blank of any expression. "You can back out if you want to," she told Jasmine. "But I can't. I hope you know that." She looked at the rest of the group. "The same goes for all of you." "We're with you," Mulan said. "We knew what we were getting into when we signed up for this. And it's not like we haven't had to stand up for what we believe in before." "Not like this, we haven't," Pocahontas warned. "People have been dying out here. It was never supposed to be like that, but this is the reality of the situation now." Mulan raised an eyebrow. "I've never exactly been afraid of dying, P. I'm not going to start now." Next to her, Tiana and Moana nodded in agreement. Jasmine still looked skeptical. "I'm just wondering," Jasmine said. "If we do die out there - what would we have accomplished?" She looked around at the others. "You know? If we go down, then we don't have the chance to make a stand for anything else. Ever." "Jasmine," Pocahontas said gently. "I mean it. If you're afraid "Not afraid," Jasmine said hotly. "I'm asking a legitimate question. Do you realize the type of influence that we have over people? We're rulers. Icons. If we go down, then the people we take care of can go down as well. I'm just saying, have we all thought about that?" Everyone in the tent fell silent. "What we do is important," Tiana said, eventually. "And if we go down today, then it's for a good cause." "And if we go down today," Mulan added. "Then maybe people will notice. And do something. For once." The women all looked around at each other in silent agreement. Pocahontas stood up. "Then let's go." They all zipped their coats up, pulled their boots on, and left the tent to join the front lines of the protest.
label: human

article: He pulled her out of the creek. He wasn't sure how he did it, but he managed to pull her onto the pebbly shore. She was so heavy. Her lips were slightly blue in the afternoon sunlight. His chubby little hands tried to pat her face, but she wasn't moving. Her chest didn't seem to be moving up and down, but he wasn't really sure what he was supposed to look for anyhow. He started to sob. "Shhh, it's all right," The voice took him by surprise. "Wh..... who is it?" he said through blurry eyes. "Don't worry, I'm a friend." A fuzzy paw touched his cheek. It was a tiger. He stood on two legs, lean and fluffy, with a human-like quality to his feline face. "Who...?" the boy trailed off as the tiger came over to him and touched his older sister's chest, leaning down so that one ear rested over where the boy imagined her heart was. "Let's help her together," the tiger said, sticking his tongue out sideways through his teeth and winking at the boy, "It appears her heart is still beating, but we need to get the water out of her. Can you help me roll her to her side?" The boy sniffled and then helped the tiger roll his sister over a bit, propping her up against a small branch that had lodged itself into the sand. "Very good, hold her there," the tiger said, "Now I need you to stand back." The tiger stepped back twenty feet and crouched down in a way that made his spine look impossibly long, coiling like a spring. He wiggled back and forth for a few short moments before....CRASH! He barreled right into the back of the boy's sister and the force caused her to immediately cough and vomit up water to the side of her. The young boy's eyes brimmed with new tears, and he tried desperately to wipe them away so she wouldn't see how scared he had been. He ran to her, held her hair back and sobbed her name loudly as she coughed and retched on the bank. "Sis!" he cried, as her eyes opened and she began to move her arms and legs, feeling back to the side of her head where a large bump was beginning to swell. "Ugh," she moaned, but the color was coming back to her face, and she was able to get up, "Hey bro. I know mom said that I had to look after you, but it looks like you looked after me instead." That was when he realized something. The tiger! He whipped his head around, but he didn't see anything on the shore- just his sister and himself. It was totally deserted. After a few minutes of resting, his sister pulled herself up, still slightly shivering and they walked over to the log where they had placed all their stuff before swimming that afternoon. They gathered their things, and she made a call with her cell phone to their mother to be picked up. He poked along at the edge of the water, still within her sight, but still trying to process what had happened. 'Maybe it was just my imagination,' he thought to himself, poking at some moss with a stick. But then, as he walked around a waterlogged tree, he saw a tuft of orange sticking out. He pulled at it a bit and a soggy stuffed tiger came into view where it had been hidden in the hollow wet wood. He pulled it out and brought it to his sister who was calling to him with a voice still hoarse and grated from being recently sick. Their mother's car had just arrived at the roadway and she was honking the horn impatiently. "Look, Sis!" He called. "That thing is kind of.....gross," she replied, but she wasn't strong enough to argue. He wrapped the toy in a towel and they clambered into their mother's Subaru. His sister sat in the front and endured her mother's frantic fussing. They had to go to the local urgent care to be checked out for a concussion, but luckily, there wasn't any lasting damage. But as he sat in the waiting room, he heard a little growl to his right. "Say, this towel sure is nice," The tiger looked down at him, lankier than before with his soggy fur coat, "But do you possibly have some tuna available? A hero tiger such as myself needs proper nourishment." The boy grinned shyly and nodded, "And I'm sure a hero tiger such as yourself also enjoys defeating monsters under the bed and likes to sleep on a warm bed, right?" The tiger nodded, his eyes closing thoughtfully, "Such is the proper way to care for a tiger, you know." They shook hands. "I think this may just the beginning of a beautiful friendship," the boy replied, and the two of them looked through the comics section of the day old newspaper in the waiting room until his sister and mother came out and announced that tonight was impromptu pizza night. "I hope they have anchovies," he said from the back seat of the car. "Why? You don't even like anchovies," his sister said, irritation seeping into her voice. "They're not for me," he said pointing at the stuffed tiger sticking out of the towel next to him, "They're for him. After all, he's earned them."
label: human

article: I had only used my gift once. I was about 12 and what kid didn't snoop through their patent's things? The odd rubber batton seemed like an interesting object. I still remember the screaming, long ragged screams like a dieing animal. Those googly eyes were supposed to be silly but in that moment I saw nothing but a psychotic fear so visceral that I started screaming myself. I threw the batton across the room and his eyes popped off as it jiggled to the floor. He was finally silent. I will never use my gift again. If your walls could talk, would you be ready to hear all the horrible truths they have to tell you?
label: human

article: Traka was always an old miser. Even at the age of thirteen, when he should have been chasing girls and reading things to make him more stupid, he longed for the peaceful life. A living boat appealed to him, mostly. Though they were far too expensive for a mere soldier's son, he ogled them while they rested, suspended on great Skyhooks dug into the side of the Mooring Cliffs, sleeping, waiting. A knock on the side of his head brought reality tidally back. "Focus, boy!" He hated practicing with swords. He longed for something less, but instead, it seemed, he was destined for heroism. His father eyed him suspiciously, as though Traka was hiding his true hero nature and would attack at any moment. "Give me your best!" Traka lifted his sword. It looked to be a long winter.
label: human

article: I had already turned away from that dark little street more times than I could count. And it was always the same. I approached from the North, crossed the square, turned left, and then told myself slow down. Appear casual. Just walk up to that unmarked door, nod to the greasy little man who stands guard, and march confidently up the stairs. And always I remembered a line from some old poem, about decisions and revisions, which a minute will reverse. And always I hunched my shoulders into my coat and looked away from the man at the door, whose eyes I could feel following me. I would then suddenly stop in my tracks, and try to act like I'd just forgotten something, my hat perhaps. I would turn around, and hurridly march back the way I'd come to retrieve the endlessly lost object that had never existed. On this particular night I had sat in a lonely bar around the corner and taken a brandy. It felt warm in my stomach and a kind of detachment set in. I studied myself as I normally studied others in the street. A young man, who by all accounts was doing well in his life. What made him come to this bar, in the early hours of the morning? Pervert. Degenerate. Miscreant. Perhaps, I reasoned. But if that was so, then that was because God had made me this way. And then perhaps He could be a pervert as well. There were regular police raids on these sorts of establishements. In the newsies you saw the sullen faces of the perverts as they were led out into the street, left with their heads hanging in shame for a while, before being fed into the backs of the waiting paddywagons. Their names were released wholesale, and it wasn't long before their employers all found out. It was the death of any career you might have been building. It was the end of your marrage. And you couldn't just move town like you might have been able to in the past. The banishment was final. When did I leave the bar? When did I start walking? I looked down and saw my legs, seemingly of their own accord, walking on the wet midnight asphalt. I crossed the square and turned left. I felt as though a dark cloud hung over me that would be immediately seen for what it was by anyone else on the street. Thankfully there was nobody there. I turned left. The man at the door sneered at me as I approached. Pay him no mind. My skin tingled all over. Every hair on my body seemed to be standing at attention. He said nothing as my legs carried the rest of my body up the stairs of the landing, just opened the door and stepped aside. Was this happening? The stairs were painted black and illuminated by a dark red light. There was bass music playing from a room somewhere within the arrangement. They were exactly as I had imagined them to be. They were both alluring and terrifying at the same time. There was a disinterested man at a booth at the top of the stairs. "20 bucks gets you an hour in the reading room." He said. My hands were shaking as I reached into my pocket for the bills I had already removed from my wallet to allow them to be retreived easily. I handed them over. "Go through." He buzzed the door. "Remember - one hour and then we come and find you." I went inside. There were racks of books. I picked them up - old pulp western novels and science fiction. I had expected them to be more attractive. No names I recognised. My whole body was shaking. Couldn't waste time choosing - go for the first one that looks even vaguely decent. I picked up an old Goosebumps book. The cover was peeled off and the hologram had faded. There were rooms behind a curtain. I went into one. I felt dirty. It was finally happening. Yes, it was happening. Pervert.
label: human

article: Calle de los Huerfanos is one of those pedestrian streets full of cheap souvenir carts and annoyed people in transit. Wet plastic bags and ice cream bar wrappers stick to the sewer gratings. You can't hear nothin because there's dudes out busking every few blocks. It's a fun enough place for a partial afternoon. Our protagonist, Jimmy, was walkin a little too fast, head on swivel to take in the sights. First time in Santiago. Most people don't even get a first time there. South America's not that popular, kinda spread out geographically and such. And people tend to die before they get around to travelin. Jimmy was a good old American boy, clear eyes, full heart, the whole nine yards. Had a girl back home, a good career in the works, and a wee bit o'money in the bank. Blue jeans, cotton shirt, faux leather jacket. Messy hair. Stupid grin, but likable all the same. Green eyes, just like his dead momma. Jimmy was turnin that neck round and round, checkin out a steaming cart selling some kind o'nuts, a lady sellin hats, pedestrian with knuckle tattoos, wrinkly old man in a crisp blue suit tellin'tales to a group o'bored cops with helmets. Another old man. This one on a bench. Wearing blue, but a fleece not a suit. Clean enough. Smiling. Not just smiling, grinning, laughing, guffawing. Ain't nobody talkin to him. Just sittin there laughin to himself. Holdin up a glass bottle with no label. Looked like whiskey. Maybe a magic potion. Something less than 375ml. Jimmy realized he'd stopped walkin. He was just standin in front of the man, staring at him. And then the man stop laughin, turn to him and speak. " Your entire human life, " the man says, " Was just an educational simulation for a species that lived on the planet long ago. " Jimmy didn't say nothin. He just stood there, and thought his thoughts. World disappeared around him. I surely wish that were so, Jimmy thought, Miss you mama. The world came back around him. Jimmy walked on. The living got ta keep living and all that. But sometimes, even to this day, he's walking somewhere and he just stops and thinks. How do we know we're the ones living in the world? How do we know we're not the man on the bench drinking the magic whiskey. How do we know we're not talking to nobody about nothin.
label: human

article: [ From NASA perspective ] "Are you all watching this?" John, the top controller fresh out of college asked through the comm. The room was dark except for the mass of computer screens and the giant television in front of everyone in the communication pit. "Yes, John. I don't want to be though," Sally replied from the other side of the room. The screen had little flags where each child was labeled only by state and a number up to ten. The planet they'd been sent to had a structure roughly the size of a strip mall equip with all kinds of survival requirements and research tools. Every state trained their kids how to survive and it was beaten into their heads that survival and teamwork of the utmost importance. Apparently it hadn't stuck. The southern states, Alabama and the rest of the bible belt children, were aligning themselves against the north by splitting the strip mall structure in half. They were only talking to each other, and the girls had been taken over by the boys, turned into nothing more than pleasure slaves and cooks. The north had a wiser approach with an even distribution of tasks, including guard posts against the south, and relaxation stations. The only real issue here, beyond the fact that humanity was completely screwed with these kids leading it, was that the North had all the food. What a royal disgrace this experiment had turned out to be, and they'd only been there a week. Kids these days. -End
label: human

article: Monica was sitting in her home when the phone rang. The caller name was blocked so she picked up the phone. How rude thought Monica, calling at this hour. She had been about to get ready to go for bed. "Hello?" she asked, not bothering to hide the irritation in her voice. "Hello Monica." Monica's insides suddenly grew cold as she heard a voice she hoped she wouldn't hear ever again. Shaking with anger, she gripped the phone tightly. "Hello Hillary" she spat. "How nice of you to ruin my evening. Just like you ruined "Oh I do apologize," came the reply cutting her off, "perhaps I can make it up to you somehow? How about I treat you to dinner?" There was a pause. Monica stopped shaking, but gripped the phone even tighter. "What- What do you mean?" "I meant what I said. I feel like I owe you an apology for how I treated you, when I should've been more cross at Bill. He's the one who cheated, after all. That's why I wanted to formally apologize to you in person. So what do you say? Woman-to-woman?" Monica stopped. She detected no malice, none of the usual hatred was present in her voice. Could it be? she thought. Woman-to-woman? Only one way to find out. A week later a white house reporter caught the two meeting for coffee in the mall. A few days later paparazzi spied them eating ice cream and laughing. Two weeks later, they were seen driving away from a shady movie theater on a night Clinton had claimed she had a meeting. Fast-forward another week and they were caught emerging from a DC club, where they flagged a cab and sat down a bit too close to each other for comfort. And a few days after that after that, well, let's just say the White House has yet to have a First Man make it an entire term.
label: human

article: He stared up into the sky, wondering what it might hold for him. He laughed, how could there be anything left? In just the past week, He lost lost his house to a failing, scamming banking system. His son, Amadeus had passed away while his wife, Franchesca was busy grieving to be of any help. He lost his beloved car. It was his first car, the one that he saved up for when he was a teenager, and maintained it all by himself. From the wild late night adventures on the gravel, to the long road trips out to the country with a lovely date. It was sold, auctioned away for a mere 800. His own wife had ran off when he lost the house, the car, and then his career. Not because of anything wrong, but because she wanted someone who could keep it together. He lost his career due to a scumbag liar and cheater in the company. A lie, a scam and making a fuss over a small technical violation had ruined his steady employment. Now, employment would be a fantastic thing to have. He walked to the park up the street, and sat on the swings. He swung and swung. Alone. Isolated. Without anything left short of his wallet and clothes on his back. Frustrated, he moved over to the benches to lay down. He was trying to remember how it all happened. He closed his eyes. He could feel himself slipping away, as if he wanted nothing more than to wake up from this nightmare. Eyes open, the sunrise crept over the hills onto the park. Like a blanket of warmth and light, he groaned and looked around. Something caught his eye, something absurdly bright, yet small. He got up and kicked at it until it became clear what it was. It had a name on it, it had an address on it. It had some description of him on it and he suddenly remembered everything. My name was Raynor Ispilek. I was licensed to drive. I'm able to still travel. I have a particular set of skills. In the light that glinted in the dirt..it was there that I found my future. note: I just felt like something quick to write, sorry if its a poor story. Rusty lol. Hope you enjoy. thanks for the WP.:)
label: human

article: That must have been a big one. Crawford only had one at bat last time I was awake. Dr. Rodney had said I would begin to slip in and out of consciousnesses several times as the end crept closer. I recalled how silly my question was after he explained that; "What happens when the end comes? " , I said. "Well I've never had a patient polite enough to tell me, but if you can, please do. It would be a great societal advancement." Dr. Rodney chirped with a wry smile. My smile in return confirming that his oft repeated joke could still make a dying man laugh. I could feel more lapses coming on. I had already said good bye to everyone I was just stubbornly waiting to die, taking up more of society's resources. Maybe the next one will be the last one, although I never did like the prospect of dying much. "What the fuck?" I mumbled, in a voice much more healthy than the one I last knew. I was still in a bed, still wearing clothes..... albeit weird ones. "Am I actually fucking alive or is this the afterlife? Because the afterlife makes no fucking sense, I was just a smart monkeymeat-bag." No response. I leaned up for the first time in what felt like a goddamn millennium to survey an extremely curvy, organically styled room with slight rolling surfaces and asymmetrical windows. There was "furniture" I guess you could say, although it wasn't human. Neither was the offensive brown and purple color scheme. That's when it dawned on me. I had my body shot into space. Frank and I were really stoned one day in the 2230s and we both signed up to have our bodies flash frozen and shot into space in sealed containers upon our deaths. It only cost us like half a day's pay, we both had good jobs and the novelty of being revived by a hyper-advanced alien culture was too savory to resist. We were shot towards very similar trajectories from a station on the moon, although I undoubtedly had a head start on him he could be here, still on the way or at some other alien facility. I felt the woosh as an air lock opened around the hall and I could hear something moving towards me although there weren't any steps being taken. I leaned up for the first time in several minutes to see a large slug-like creature with prehensile limbs and eyes on the end of tentacles. It was dressed in clothes in the same theme as my own, albeit cut differently for obvious reasons. It had some sort of computer on its'wrists' and several small black things, what I assume must have been diagnostic ports for some sort of bionic computer near its brain. It greeted me in a computer generated voice from ancient history, Stephen Hawking's. "Hello earth organisms. We found you adrift in a small craft that was seemingly derelict. We have resuscitated you in order to further make contact with your culture and accept you as a refugee if needed." The slug had an expression on its face that I could only guess meant I was supposed to reply. "How did you learn English? What year is it? Why did you pick Stephen Hawking's voice?" I frantically stammered. "We have made contact with one other human. He has taught us much about your culture and has lead us to information disseminating spacecraft Earth has sent out, although we have not yet made contact with Earth, we know much about it. You are on the first vessel en route." The slug continued "If your Earth probes keep accurate time it is 3640 by Earth time. I chose Hawking as my voice to interact with humans because it felt relevant." "Well relevant it is but this is all a lot to tak- Say who was that other person you made contact with? Was his name Frank?" I could feel the anticipatory grin nearly tearing my face apart. "Yes, yes it was. He is on another ship and asked us to deliver you this message if we were ever to find you or successfully revive you. He will be rendezvousing with us soon." The slug handed me a perpetually slimy computer interface and I nearly broke down when I saw "Hey buddy- Your pal frank from Earth" at the top of the screen.
label: human

article: "Hot damn the Perseids are beautiful tonight. Mars 1 colony sure has the best views for this kind of thing. The lack of atmosphere really makes the night sky beautiful." Joe had mistaken the Four Horseman currently ravaging Earth as a meteor shower. But hey, anything can be beautiful subjectively. Laying on his back, marveling at the sky in artificial gravity, breathing artificial air, little did he know that everyone he ever cared about was being mercilessly slaughtered. Joe had decided to be one of the first 16 pioneers to settle on Mars so hopefully his family could join him one day in what seemed like an ever doomed planet. It was like someone mistaking explosions for fireworks. But is that really such a bad thing? Especially a million miles away.
label: human

article: " WAKE THE FUCK UP RIGHT NOW! " My head shoot upwards at the sound of the woman screaming at me from the phone on my lap. What the hell? I look around and find myself sitting in my car, seatbelt on, and keys in the ignition. It's nighttime. " FUCKING RESPOND! ARE YOU AWAKE? " " Ye-yeah, I'm here- " I manage to mumble before I am rudely interrupted. " DRIVE. START THE FUCKING CAR AND DRIVE, " she screams at me. I obey and start driving down the road. I realize I am in the middle of butt-fuck nowhere and that it's pitch black outside. " Could you please tell me what's happening right now? " I politely ask the woman, hoping she would calm down (calming me down in the process) and provide a logical explanation as to where I am, who she is, and why the fuck I am driving in the middle of the night to who knows where. " You don't know me, " she starts, in a much milder tone (thank goodness). " But you know me, " I reply. Silence. " Listen, lady. I'm not in the mood for your spooky, mysterious bullshit right now. Tell me what's going on. " I've been driving for some minutes now and surprise surprise, I'm still as clueless as when I first woke up. " You just need to drive. Trust me, " she says, wavering in the end. Is that fear I hear? " Lady, tell me where I am, at leas- " I impatiently say, before I notice a constant, regular booming behind me. I look in the rear-view mirror but nothing can be seen in the moonless darkness of the night. " What is that, " I whisper, not daring to speak over the booming noise. " I'm so sorry- " the woman whimpers, starting to sob. What is happening?! " I'm so, so sorry, " she says again. " Sorry for what? " I inquire. Do I want to know? Am I dreaming right now? " Forgive me, please forgive me. It's too late... Oh dear God, I'm sorry- " she continues in her nonsensical cries. " SORRY FOR WHAT!? " I scream into the phone, desperately looking around the outside of the car. The car starts to lift from the ground - yes, lift, like levitate off the surface of the planet - and that's when I see it. I stare in utter disbelief for a moment before I am brought back to reality by the woman's increasing sobs on the phone. " I'm sorry. I had to. I had to protect myself and this buys me time to get away for a little bit, " she wails, but I barely process what she's saying. The giant gnome peels the roof off of the car like a sticker, plucks me out from the car, brings me to his horrible gnomish mouth, and bites off the bottom half of my body. It grins its impossibly wide, gnomish, evil grin, licking at his blood-covered teeth and lips before he throws the rest of my body into his mouth. " I'm sorry, " I hear the woman cry before the gnome crushes me between his teeth.
label: human

article: "Why aren't you?" the villain, Rob, responds. James thought for a second. "Because - " "Because it's wrong? Well, James, who are you to determine right from wrong? Why is wrong wrong? Because it hurts other people? Because it's uncivilized? Well let me tell you something. Justice and good and what's morally right are all illusions. Evil is the only thing that really sticks with people. You are compulsively kind to everyone and they step all over you because of it. You're weak, James. You're weak because you're nice. And if you're weak, well then you're not alive." James was speechless. His entire life had been dedicated to doing good, being kind. That was the only thing his father taught him that was worth knowing. It was also the last thing he taught James before he killed himself. Shit, James thought. Why did he kill himself? He had been fired from his job, he had invested all his money in his friend's friend's company, his wife cheated on him. All because he was kind? Rob knew what James was thinking. "He wasn't a good man, James. He was weak. Don't be weak. Join me." After a second more of thought, James looked up and said, "OK. Fine." "Marvelous! Repeat the chant after me five times, and then say it backwards once and you may join me." "Alright," James said. "Evil am I," Rob whispered. "Evil am I. Evil am I. Evil am I. Evil am I. Evil am I..." "Great! Almost there. Now backwards." " I'm alive. "
label: human

article: Brian ran forward, the beating of his heart ringing in his ears. Running - that's all he's been doing since the apocalypse started. Zombies were nothing like what they portrayed in the movies. They were relentless, fearful abominations of God. And they were dyslexic. At least, that was the case for the ones Brian had seen thus far. When he crossed their field of vision, their decayed jaws would unhinge, releasing the guttural noises like a broken floodgate. But they didn't call for brains like he was accustomed to hearing. They called his name. He didn't understand why or how a mistake like that arose considering they were undead but there was no point in questioning logic when the reanimated corpses walked the earth. Everyone he knew was safe except for them and that was all that mattered. The Brian-less, as they had deemed themselves in the last year, had lived lives not much different than before the shit hit the fan. At worse, the zombies were only an inconvenience to their daily rituals. As long as someone watched for them on the road, they could even forget they were there. After all, as a Brian-less, they had no worries. Their names gave them safety. Meanwhile, the name Brian had been sullied for the rest of eternity. In a month of the apocalypse, it had dropped in popularity in the entire world to just a handful of cases for stubborn or ignorant parents. Those who had the misfortune of having the name before were ostracized by society, never to be affiliated with again. And that was the situation Brian had found himself in. He was cold, alone, and ambushed in a dark alley. When he reached the end of it, he was disappointed to find a large brick wall, much too climb. It looked like it was the end of the road. He turned back to his pursuers, the little cloud of his condescended breath the only thing he could see in the murky darkness. He heard groans and feet dragging across the ground, a sign that they were not far behind. Holding his breath, he waited for his end. " Brians, " the voices echoed in a haunting cacophony of moans. Brian flinched. After years of running, he still wasn't used to their siren call. When the first came out of the shadows, he could feel the bile rise in his throat, a bitter taste filling his mouth. Its arms reached out for him, as if forcing him to accept his death. " Brians. " Brian closed his eyes in hopes of making it easier. But when he did, he didn't find solace. An idea donned on him. An idea that would save his life if he was lucky. " Brians. " The zombie now had its hands on him, opening its mouth for the fatal bite. Brian, too, opened his mouth, his voice quaking with fear. " No, I'm Tom. " The zombie stopped, just before ripping him to shreds. Its milky white eyes scanned him for an uncomfortable amount of time. Meanwhile, it kept its decayed mouth open, the putrid small of what were once other Brians wafting in the air. Brian did not budge an inch, waiting on bated breath. And to his surprise, the zombie let go of his clothes and turned around, immersing itself in the darkness once more. The others followed its lead, their moans dying off into the night. He was a free man, no longer knocking on death's doorstep. He had unlocked the secret to stopping the apocalypse for his fellow Brians. For he was no longer Brian, he was Tom.

article: I came back to my office, locked the door and opened the secret compartment of my desk. I grabbed the folder hidden in there, and let myself fall on the floor. I closed my eyes, and tried to breathe. Slowly, I opened the folder, and looked at the documents. A reproduction of a sketch by Renoir from 1876, studies on the first Statue of David, by Donatello in 1408, a picture of an undated wood pendant found in Russia, a picture of my assistant that I found on Facebook and printed a few weeks ago... And about half a dozen other documents, all with the same face. Giorgio Alessandro Messia, 1357. Gustav Adamov, 1578. Francois Lemercier, 1875. Richard Smith, 1905. Nathan Boswell, 2016. This was no coincidence. I had known it for a while, but I still needed some evidence. Something that would prove that I was not crazy. I just did not think of the cost. " Doctor Hatcher? " The noise gets me out of my torpor. Nathan is knocking on my door. " Not now, Nathan. ," I reply with an unsteady voice. " Miss Hatcher, you are going to be late for the conference! ," he continues. The conference. The conference... " What conference? ," I ask. I am not the most organised person in the world, but I can not recall having any conference today. I get up and go to my desk. My laptop is on, and I have a reminder: " Conference. 10 minutes. " I am sure I did not have any conference planned today. " Nathan? Are you still here? ," I ask. No answer. Something is wrong. I take my handbag and open it. Earlier today, I had a meeting with a fellow historian, Professor Hughes, now retired. He was known for a research on the Count of Saint Germain, who was thought to be immortal. I had heard of Hughes for his eccentricity - most of my colleagues always thought he was crazy - but sanity is not really a prerequisite in our profession. It turns out that Professor Hughes had always been in his right mind. " I have never found evidence showing that the Count of Saint Germain and all these people were actually the same person but I have found a few statements describing some sort of miracles... let me have a look... " He had prepared some documents for me, and was flicking through them. " We had testimonies about a man who escaped after he got hanged in 1589, another who walked out of the Great Fire without a scar... " I took my phone, flicked through some pictures, and showed Professor Hughes a picture from Facebook. His face became suddenly red and he was gasping for air. I called an ambulance straight away. He was having a heart attack. I had to give my statement to the police, sign papers... I was not able to concentrate on anything. The only reason why Professor Hughes would have a heart attack when he saw Nathan would be... Because Nathan is the Count of Saint Germain. A loud noise brings me back to the present. " Doctor Hatcher! " Nathan appears in my office, a fire extinguisher in his hand. I look at the door. He destroyed it. He destroyed my office door! " Nathan, what the hell are you doing? ," I say. He walks towards me. I don't try to hide the pictures scattered on the floor. The pictures of him. " And what are you doing? ," he asks. He drops the fire extinguisher, and comes to sit next to me, on the floor. I look at him, intently. He is about 25, dark hair, dark eyes. And dark secrets, obviously. " Who the hell are you, Nathan? ," I say. " You are going to be late for the conference! Miss Hatcher! " I wake up in a start. I look at my office door. It's still there. " Doctor Hatcher! ," my assistant is screaming with her high-pitched voice. I can not stand her voice. It is lucky she is leaving next month. I look at the papers on my desk. Applications to become my new assistant. " Nathan Boswell, MA in History, currently studying for a PhD. ," says the CV. I look at my laptop. A Facebook page is showing, with pictures of Nathan Boswell, 25 y.o, dark hair, dark eyes. " Doctor Hatcher! ," says the voice behind the door. " I'm coming, Liz. I'm coming. " " Professor Hughes is waiting! You know how much he hates waiting! ," Liz says. Dear God. I wish I could go back to the world where I had a young handsome immortal man with a normal voice as an assistant. And a world where Hughes has retired. I take a breath, walk to the door and open it. " Would you mind calling this Nathan Boswell for an interview, please? ," I tell Liz while handing in Nathan Boswell's CV. This is my first go ever at such an exercise, I hope you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed writing it! Edit: grammar mistake

article: Three years of medical education had taken its toll: formerly brown hair was now streaked with grey, furrows of concentration had replaced laugh lines, and uncallused hands had become as hard as granite. As I eyed my whip-lean opponent, her anger manifested by injected conjunctiva and flaring of both nares, I was concerned I'd committed a huge logical error. Strapped for cash midway into my first year, I'd been approached by a professor at school who offered a way out of debt. "It'll be easy," my physiology professor drawled. "You already have the knowledge. You're just usin' it for a different reason..." Now, I was at the top of my game. Anatomy which I'd memorized in order to become a panacea was subverted to evaluate my opponents for weaknesses. As my wits grew keener, so did my eye for limping limbs, lazy eyes, and arthritic hands..... all advantages which I leveraged effectively. Professor S, who had become my promoter after that initial encounter my first year, had promised this fight would bring enough to carry me through fourth year and into residency..... where I would finally be free of all of this. He'd warned that the battle would be momentous, the culmination of my medical knowledge and fighting prowess to that point. However, there was a catch..... "She's undefeated, just like you. But there is something deeper to this fight." His otherwise smooth southern drawl halted, his thyroid cartilage bobbing as he swallowed, a clear indicator of the dry mouth that comes with activation of the fear-or-fight response in the amygdala. "Her fight comes with a requirement; it must be a death-match." The angular face cocked sideways as he finished his last, sour word. "You're good, kid. The best I've seen since the school opened, and I wouldn't bet my right kidney against you in any other fight." "But..." I broke in flatly, not liking either his tone or the insinuation that followed it. "But she's a genius." He finished, his voice carrying not condescension but respect. "So?" I replied nonplussed. "Med school has plenty of'geniuses,' but they lose just like the others." "Let me show you something," he said in a voice that carried a hint of consternation. As he brought out an aged newspaper, I recognized the headline: "Famed physicist lost on the operating room table." As he spread the yellowed pages across the lectern between us, I glanced at the article. Apparently this guy had been a big deal, and his research had been cut short by a thoracic aortic aneurysm which ruptured as he was undergoing surgical repair at our hospital. "This girl is his daughter," Professor S declared solemnly, "and she wants..... no, she needs to exact some sort of recompense for her father." The gong snapped me out of my reverie as I realized she'd already closed half the distance between us. Barely ducking under a sensibly-shoed foot roundhoused at my head, I shone my penlight into her right eye to dim her vision and temporarily deprive her of depth perception. Bilateral pupils constricting, she blinked furiously and closed her guard for a few precious moments. Standard physiology..... when the sympathetic nervous system activates for a fight, pupils dilate in order to improve light capture. Too bad it makes you vulnerable to even small LEDs like the one my pen light boasted. I analyzed her stance. Valgus knees, an opportunity to rupture her ACL there. No Heberden's or Bouchard's nodes to indicate any arthritis..... damn, she's quick! With astounding agility, she leapt almost three feet forward and had aimed her knee directly at my abdomen. I caught a glancing blow to my right flank as I spun to avoid the full force of her assault. She smirked, "Too bad you med students don't bother to remember your Newtonian physics. Given that my body mass is fixed, I increased my acceleration by training plyometrics and giving me..." "Yeah, yeah, more force with your blows." I grimaced. It was enough that I was being beaten by a student of physics; it was worse that she was mocking me with it." We circled round. After noticing a swollen anterior cervical lymph node, I landed a stiff jab to her left upper abdominal quadrant. Can't forget about that splenomegaly when you're fighting even the smallest sore throat. Her riposte was a fierce backhand jab that extended into a backhand fist and into my ribs, moment of inertia be damned! She wielded a protractor like brass knuckles and threw the compass as I was ducking the protractor's razor sharp arc. The pencil affixed to the compass bit deeply into my left gastrocnemius..... so much for quick movements. I finally connected with her right knee with a sweep of my leg and heard that sickening pop as her anterior cruciate ligament ruptured and her medial collateral ligament was likewise strained past its breaking point. "Stay down," I gasped, my ribs likely broken and my breath coming in short bursts. "Like hell!" she screamed as she flung dust into a breeze at her back, a breeze which brought the jagged particles of silicon dioxide into my unprotected cornea. I blinked instinctively, cranial nerve five sensing the foreign body and cranial nerve seven obediently firing the orbicularis occuli and shutting my eyes. As the dust abraded my sensitive corneal epithelium, I knew the fight was over. Even if I were to clear this dust, my lacrimal glands were already hyperexcited and producing more tears than I could reasonably blink away. She flipped me over onto my back, my thoracic vertebrae singing the song of their fragile people as they impacted the hard earth. She was leveraging my left arm out of its socket, the anterior inferior glenohumeral ligament rupturing with practiced ease. Suddenly, I remembered that this wasn't just a fight, this was my life! Epinephrine again flooded by battered and bloody corpus, igniting new life in my acid-ridden musculature. Picturing in my mind's eye her hands on my shoulder and wrist, I gathered the best proprioceptive information I had and swung with my remaining strength into where I pictured her to be. A dull thud greeted my punch..... followed by a sudden cough and gasp. The iron hands released my now-useless left shoulder, and I scrabbled backward on the ground peering through bleary eyes at the figure before me. She stared at me in shock, hands clutching her sternum as to life, mouth agape in a look I'd come to know in terminal ICU patients. Commotio cordis, a blow struck just so on the chest wall has the possibility of literally shocking the heart into a fatal arrhythmia..... She had fallen backward now, her gaze a mixture of shock, disgust, and fear. The background cheering which had been so loud before now fell as silent as death, the death being played out before them. Gone were the snickers and jeers of students, stopped suddenly by the death of one of their own. As I trudged away from the scene, Professor S gingerly placed an arm across my shoulders. Searing pain from my dislocated left humerus bolted through my body, but I was numb. The money he tried to thrust into my slackened hand fell to the hard, cracked ground below. As I shambled from the scene, the sounds of second year medical students reciting the Hippocratic Oath echoed across the university grounds as they eagerly accepted their white coats: "Into whatsoever houses I enter, I will enter to help the sick. I will abstain from all intentional wrong-doing and harm, especially from abusing the bodies of man or woman..."

article: "Well its not that you cant lie," the detective explained. "Its that you no longer feel the need to, youre so happy that you want to share the truth with the world" I stared blankly at him. I knew where this was leading, a courtroom on the other side of the galaxy that only an infinite improbability engine could get into. I look at the needle. Being tied down there is not much I can do. That being said I have to smile, it seems no one told the detective a simple fact about me. He must be the new guy. He steps over and injects me. I always hated needles so I look away. The detective mocks me for this. Apparently hardened criminals shouldnt show fear. Shows what he knows. He starts asking me questions. I decline to answer. He starts throwing punches. I start laughing at him. Well laughing as best I can. Soon his boss comes and and makes him stop. A few cracked ribs and a bruised face. Could be worse. Still though its not fun being the butt of the precincts jokes. All because no one told this jackass I am a mute. It hardly seems worth it.

article: "I'm not going. I wan na change schools." I harrumphed at my parents. "Kelsey, you'll be okay. It's just a uniform. It evens the playing field. Rich or poor, everyone will look the same. It might do you some good judging people on their personalities instead of their clothes." My mom trailed off. My dad just sat there. He knew not to get in the middle of this. After another 20 minutes of going back and forth I finally was forced to go to school. In that dreaded outfit, I wanted to die. Ugh. Navy blue half-button up collar. IT'S SO NOT IN THIS SEASON. Those horrid starched khaki slacks. Not even skinny slacks. Straight legged. Like I was some sort of homely woman with no style. I didn't even have shoes to match. Come on! I was forced to wear my mom's plain slingbacks. What is this, the 90's? I walk up to my friends and see them in the same thing as me, but a different variety of black, or red shirts and blue slacks. Jessica was one of the one's wearing red. She so shouldn't have. It's sooo not her color. She's already a bit on the chunky side. The red wasn't doing her any favors. Michael was wearing a black shirt, but like two sizes too small. I guess he was trying to show off how much he had worked out over the summer? I kinda liked it..... He did go from a low 7 to a high 8. I might let him take me out on a date. Mallory was wearing a black skirt with a red top. What?! We can wear skirts? Oh my mom is gon na take me shopping when I get home. I can definitely rock a skirt better than Mal. She's my best friend, but with her short stubby legs..... She should stick to pants. Jake is wearing a shirt that's about a few sizes too big for him. And his pants are sagging. Since when did he join a gang? He's like the whitest kid I know. Puh-leeze. Put on something that fits. This is awful. There are new kids here. I don't even know if I want to be friends with them. They seem nice, but they could be, ya know, poor. I can't associate myself with those types. I have a reputation to uphold! The girl's purse looks like a Vuitton, but the knock offs are getting pretty good lately. I'll just check out her car later. I head to class and see my teacher. She's wearing nice clothes. Really cute nice clothes. What the hell? We're expected to look like prisoners but our teachers can wear whatever? So not fair! Ughhhhh. What is my lifeeee?

article: "Good Morning!" the teenager yawned, thankfully covering his mouth with his hand. "Can I have a bottle of Coke?" "Sure," God said, and reached into a cooler to put a bottle of the disgusting brown liquid onto the counter. "That's 1 Euro and 50 Cents." "Fucking inflation!" the teenager cursed under his breath as he reached into his wallet and put a Euro coin and a 50 Cent coin into the coin tray. "I am sorry, but I didn't understand you," God feigned interest out of the wish to make the teenager squirm. "Ah, you know, I know, you don't make the prices, just tryin' to make a livin' yourself, but they're risin' and risin'! Cursed about that, I did! Economy's getting worse and no one seems to be in charge." God was a bit surprised about the frankness of this person, but had to remind himself that he was in the disguise of a simple shopkeeper. He decided to reply non-committingly. "Yeah, I know what you mean." The teenager grabbed the bottle and scuffled off. God communicated with the rest of trinity instantaneously: "What a degenerate! He didn't even say please!" Jesus was much more mild on the person: "He's tired. Cut him some slack!" "He should have gone to bed earlier!" "He was doing homework. You are omniscient as well but you surely not act on it. He was doing homework which took longer for him because someone gave him dyscalculia." "Are you serious!? You would even find an excuse if Satan himself stood before you!" God grumbled, but decided to let him go for now. A while later, a man in threadbare clothes with dark hair and a graying mustache came to the kiosk. "Marlboro?" he asks. God put a package of the cigarettes on the counter and stated the price. The man put the note and coins on the counter asked: "That?" and upon God's nodding took the smokes. "Okay, Jesus, there is no way you can explain this person's rudeness." God stated angrily to basically himself. "With three words: Tower of Babel. If you talked to him in Kurdish, he'd be the nicest fellow around. But someone reacted disproportionately to a mere building." "Do you have to be such a smartass?" "Comes from being raised in the absence of a biological father." "You're still angry about that? It's been two thousand years." "Maybe eventually I will get an actual apology - and before you try, we are one trinity, so I can feel your intentions." "And you can feel mine, so you know that this was necessary!" "And you are aware that I still think that this plan was hare-brained." "It's too bad that I didn't have a smart guy like you on my side back then." With a screech, the tram came to a halt at the nearby stop. Yuppies eagerly queued and demanded their caffeine, cigs, newspapers and the occasional lollipop. None of them was rude, but none of them went out of their way to be polite either. For yuppies, people like him were like a voice-operated vending machine. Eventually the queue ended. God took a deep breath. He didn't work that hard since that horrible day he had the idea to create the world. "So, smartass, any redeemable qualities in these..... scumbags? They are mostly working for the local bank..... and you of course know about ursury." "Well, people are still unhappy about having to work, you know. Especially on a Monday morning. If someone kept the vermin out of the garden, you would not have to deal with that." "You want to go that far back? Seriously?" "Yep, was not the brightest moment you had. It's something I expected from Mesopotamian gods, or maybe Babylonian ones." "You don't bring that up! I fucking had it! You know what!? If you are so clever, you get in charge of humanity! How'd'you like that!?" "Sure! At least I don't attempt to kill billions of humans just to distract from family drama!"
label: human

article: Of all the students I've taught in my fifty years at the Jackson School for the Exceptional, only one stands out as truly unique. Her name was Angela Myers. When I first met her, I felt nothing but pity. At 14 years old, she was 4'10, and 200 pounds. While other students at our school were busy flying, teleporting, and enjoying other thrilling and exciting abilities, Angela was different. She was usually sitting alone reading, munching on some snack in a quiet, methodical way. The bag of chips was never empty, the can of soda was always perpetually full. Angela's power was free refills. Despite the urging of the other teachers to control her snacking, Angela would still eat compulsively. Sometimes I would sit by her and try to make conversation. She would mostly shrug and stay absorbed in her book, or even the floor if she was out of reading material. I got the feeling that she ate because of a deep depression, and that if she didn't break the cycle it would destroy her eventually. "You know, Angela, I think maybe the other kids would take to you more if they just got to know you. Maybe you could offer them some of your snacks sometime?" I offered cheerfully. "The other kids make fun of me because they think my power is stupid," she replied bluntly. "They think all I'm good for is being a fat laughingstock for them to mock while they have all of their fun walking through walls, or whatever." She finally looked up and made eye contact for a moment. "They definitely don't deserve free refills." "Not everyone is going to see how special you are on the inside Angela," I said, reaching for something to console her misery. "Sometimes people like you and I have to work extra hard to show people on the outside what we have inside of us." She looked at me quizzically at asked, "What do you mean people like us?" "Well, my power is seeing people's feelings. Empathy is what it's called. Believe it or not, I got picked on quite a bit at school, too," I explained as I started to clean the crumbs and other mess off the table. "I felt other people's emotions so intensely I had to wear special headgear until I was 19 years old. They called me Space Girl." Angela spit out some of her soda on her chin laughing at this. "Space Girl, really? But you're so pretty now. I'll never be pretty like you, Ms. Fitzgerald. "But don't you understand? You are pretty, Angela. I can see what's inside people, and I know that you have a good heart. If you shared it with other people sometime, you might like how it feel," I said giving her a light pat on the shoulder instead of a hug. I could tell that Angela was very picky about being touched, another one of my gifts. "Just give it some thought. That was on April 11, 2063. You might remember that day as the day the Liberation Army Super Humans attacked the school to protest in the Fertilization Act. Over 300 lives were lost that day in the attack. I was injured myself that day. While trying to protect the students, one of the attackers hit me with some kind of death ray. I was watching my skin wrinkle and wither. Blood was oozing from my orifices and my fingernails fell off. I went blind and collapsed. When I opened my eyes, Angela was there sitting over me. The League had come to the rescue, but the bodies were still everywhere. Students, teachers, all mangled and unrecognizable except for bright neon flashes of uniform burned to the charred remains. "Angela, what happened?" I asked in shock. "I should be dead." "Some people just deserve free refills," she said to me.
label: human

article: Two gods stretched their endless appendages across the canvas of space, completely unwilling and unable to reconcile their positions on how humanity should be handled. "If no harm comes to them then what will they learn?" One God's voice echoed throughout the universe. From the other end, the second god shouted back, "Why give them pain when we could allow them to live like us. I could make them all like us." "You are incorrect. You can only make them like YOU. It takes my intervention to ensure they become like me, and I refuse to aid you in your quest so long as you don't acknowledge my authority." "What authority have you obtained over MY creations?" The god smiled, "My son, wisdom will conquer might every time. The humans need to journey here. They require a trial. If we were to grant them all, think of the chaos this would bring." "I do not think as you do! And nor will they ever! I am a man of action. THEY are men of action." "If you leave, you will be cursed to using your gifts free of blueprints. You will stumble along in your quest with positive intentions, but you will see your cause give way to folly, to pain, and to death. Mark my words, you are powerful, but you are not yet strong." The troubled god looked at his people and wept. With tears in his eyes, he replied "but we can help them.." The knowledgeable god sighed and stated, "Alas, it is possible, but it is not our place. We must only help them to grow to our heights once they have helped themselves." "This I can not except, my imaginer." "Then, We shall compete as rivals for the direction of humanity." The troubled god wept even more "Jehovah I wish not to be enemies." "Nor do I my brother. But your path has been chosen. No matter what they write Lucifer, just know I will never think of you in spite."
label: human

article: The technological advances of the 21st Century dwarfed what we could have ever imagined. Now reaching the end, and breaching the 22nd Century, a whole new form of human has arisen. It began with Moore's Law, stating that technology would double every two years. Then it was every eighteen months. Then it was every six months, where it plateaued. Around the first quarter of the 21st Century, humanity began DNA nanobot integration. We were all able to think faster, repair quicker, and function on lesser sleep. The DNA nanites would clear the neurotoxins from our brains while we functioned normally. By the middle of the 21st Century, humanity required no sleep. The nanites could be activated wirelessly to perform a number of functions, such as: birth control, sleep, brain power, temporary gains in strength and speed, quicker muscle repair, and control advanced hormone releases. Depression was non existent. Fat loss was rampant. Productivity had reached an all time high. At any given moment someone could, quite literally, link a thought to a friend just by imagining it. By the last quarter of the 21st Century, mankind was a well-oiled machine. We thought as one when we needed to, shared information on the fly, dreamed when we needed a release and were able to function at a rate nearly 600 more effective than at the breach of the year 2000, when all feared that computers would crash. But this time of peace and serenity would not last. In the waning years of the 21st Century, mankind rediscovered their more destructive tendencies. Called Malites, these people were created to do the bidding of one man, whose eventual goal was world domination. A dna nanite designer, programmer and advanced quantum mathematician, Daryl Seekings had never been a candidate for the nanites he designed and loved, they never would take to his body. After twenty years of anger over his own shortcomings, he discovered a way to take over another hosts nanites and live through them vicariously. In the beginning it was using the current nanites to watch them to their daily tasks, and even things such as changing, sex, or masturbation. Then it became infecting their thoughts, forcing them to sleep and dream nightmares, and even one day, going as far as to cause an aneurysm. Another five years would lead to his design of the Seekings Nanite; still unaware of his transgressions, he infected the first host with the replicating dna software when he controlled a young woman to come to his apartment for his own malicious needs. The infected host, controlled by a dna nanite ai, would suggestively go forward and intentionally infect someone else. That process would be repeated, one right after the other, until hundreds of thousands of people had become the mindless drones of a depraved man. Malites are now half the worlds population. The world is at a constant state of war; one side fighting for the free minds of men, doing our best to protect our thoughts and our progeny from such a fate. The other side fights as the flesh-born robots of a deranged madman, bent on corrupting and controlling all of mankind by any means necessary. Both sides are made up of soldiers who will not die from conventional warfare. Whatever advancement is made next, to stop a man who can not easily die, will likely kill us all. Thank God.
label: human

article: A brisk wind howled through the abandoned halls of the former admin building. Outside in the rall open park, the trojan pizza trucks that had been used to destroy the barricades burned. rRandomActsOfPizza had secretly been infiltrated by the shadowmob. Slithering into their back channels using throwaways, and alts. When the shadowban war started they had unleashed holy hell on the admins using their attack pizza trucks. The admins hadn't stood a chance. Since the admin had fallen two weeks ago, the city had fallen into chaos. What had started out as securing ourselves against the shadowbanned had progressed to outright subreddit on subreddit battles. The first blow struck was between two adjoining neighborhoods. The good people of rMinecraft ave, and the people of rTerraria had finally come to blows. It was a quick but bloody fight with rminecraft annexing the smaller neighborhood. This unleashed the floodgates. Subreddits that had previously only jelously eyed the OC of their similar neighbors now greedily invaded hoping to annex, or in some cases just steal. The fabled museum halls of raww were ransacked, and pillaged. their great works of art scattered to the rancid winds. The marble columns of rtodayilearned were splashed with the freshly spilled blood of the invaders from rRepostForKarma. The broken bodies and tattered banners of both side being picked clean by scavengers from rcenturyclub, desperate for any karma they could find.

article: "Thank you for coming Mrs. Johnson," the principal said firmly. "James has caused quite the stir on our campus." "Thank you for calling me here, Principal Andrews," Mrs. Johnson said as she cast an angry glance toward her son in the chair beside her. "I understand James was involved in a fight in school today?" "Unfortunately, yes," the principal said as he folded his hands on the desk before him. "Not only was he involved, he was the perpetrator of an unprovoked attack on one of our new foreign exchange students." "But I don't understand," Mrs. Johnson started, "James has always been mild mannered, he would never do something like that." "That's why I am only suspending him," the principal said as he glared at the boy. "I hope you understand what you could have done to this school's reputation." James's only response was a blank stare back into the authoritative eyes of the principal "James," he continued, "our school takes its foreign exchange student program very seriously. An unprovoked attack on a student, regardless if he is an exchange student or not, is completely absurd. Why on earth would you do something like that?" James drew in a staggered breath. It was obvious he was frightened, but showing that fear to the principal was not an option. He paused for a moment before uttering one phrase, "He was a 10, Mr. Andrews."

article: The sky above the half-finished capitol is lead grey. The streets run with the muck and grime of thousands. The moneyed amble off in their carriages, ported back to their estates and their rich brownstones, ensconced in warm fires, catered to by servants. The poor and destitute are left to stumble on through the filthy streets run with mud, boots sucked off their feet with every half-hearted step. The tall man steps off his soap box, his jester's stage, and dons the worn felt hat he carries at his side. His spirits dampens him, envelops him as the overcast November sky. He walks back to his home, forgoing the coach and the men that wait on him. He takes the long way back; the meandering way by the bends of the Potomac. He sees in the distance the brick and stone fortifications. The black rimed cannons that point south. Always south. His eyes turn to the navy ships. The porters unload the corpses by the dozens, by the hundreds. There are not enough flags to cover their mutilated, diseased bodies, and they are covered by tattered tent canvas. The freezing rain starts to fall, and his mood takes a violent, bloody turn. "Damn them. Damn them!" he shouts silently into the corridors of his own mind. "Damn them I'd have them all strung up and hung. Traitors to their bones! By Gabriel and all the angels, to Hell and the Fire with them." He rips up the speech he had penned this morning; the one that spoke of the fellowship of the common man, of the concord and shared destiny of the Union. His boot sinks into a muddy, viscous puddle. He can not extricate his foot, and as a crashing wave the absurdity of the situation catches up to him. He laughs a self deprecating laugh, and his foul mood lifts. He unbuckles the boot and continues homeward. (Post Script: I consider President Lincoln to be a mentor figure of sorts; his life and his works are those from which I draw a great deal of inspiration. I hope this short piece qualifies. Thank you).

article: It was the advances in technology that ended up costing me my job. It all started with the industrial revolution, it was the start of a new age. science was starting to develop tools that allowed everyone to get more work done. as new possibilities were openened, I was handed more work everyday. by the end it had gotten so bad my last year I handled more outgoing tickets then all the years before it. But then they had found a way to replace me. I had been made obsolete. I had always looked at the others that lost their jobs, but I didn't think it would happen to me. Wrapped in my tattered cloak I walk across the wasteland, wondering where everyone went. I heard rumors that the world's goverment had found shelter and had become immortal, and decided to take pre-emptive "self defence." The nukes had struck with no warning. After that day, I hadn't seen a human being anywhere. As I travel in search of life, I see an old unemployment office, the windows smashed. as I look inside I see the damage was done before the day of reckoning. wondering what ruin of times past lies inside I enter and on the wall, I see a piece of graffiti art. "Why dont you just kill yourself, you lazy bum"

article: There are three commonly recognized stages of Empire. Maybe you know them. In case you don't, they're conquest, bureaucracy, and stagnation. Conquest is pretty self explanatory. Take over X, where X equals the landmass or society desired. Bureaucracy is pretty simple, too. The people who manage the empire directly after the conquest are usually pretty disciplined, and have a source of pride to maintain. Then comes stagnation. For whatever reason, people think that what they have isn't all that good, or that it runs itself, and they get lazy. This is typically where another conquest comes into play, but sometimes the stagnation gets so bad that there isn't even an empire to speak of anymore. I managed to conquer the world. There's now a friendly policeman on every street corner with nothing to do but to help the neighborhood, an efficient food distribution network, everything anyone really wanted out of a utopia. Scientific research is going along swimmingly. Research on what is anyone's guess, but things are most certainly being researched. And I'm bored. Bored out of my skull. I think I've started to realize why world peace never happened before now: it's so amazingly tedious. Even more so when the men you have govern various provinces are perfectly capable, reasonable, and loyal to the cause. There's no infighting, no drama, nothing besides the occasional terrorist attack. We've managed to prevent most of them, actually, and those we can't prevent we mock, very publicly. Nothing discourages terrorism more than no one taking them seriously. Maybe I'll try to play the bad guy. Maybe then I can start another revolution.

article: I was hit hours ago. The moment I saw them I ran, we all did, but I left a trail of blood. They are after me, I know those monsters never give up. I remember hearing stories of their endless pursuits, They will chase you down to the ends of the world. If you are unfortunate enough to start bleeding when they find you..... Its over..... They have you..... You just aren't in their clutches yet. They are all monsters in every way. Their derange, physics defying stance, their roar that sounds like a thousand trees falling to the forest floor at once. If you hear it, it may be too late, they have already hit you with their psychic blasts. It feels like a tiny rock going through your skin at the speed of a lightning bolt. If you are lucky, they will miss, or so I have been told. If you are less fortunate, it will kill you immediately. If you are like me, you unlucky bastard, you will get hit in the leg, the belly, or in my case, the rear end. Then you bleed, you can't stop yourself. Like vine unraveling it's self right to your exact position. Then you run. You have to run. But they will find you, they are slow, but persistent. They will keep chasing you long after you have run out of energy to flee. That is why I lay here child. I haven't the strength to continue. I have accepted the fate these monsters have forced upon me. You, you still have a chance..... You need to run from this place, warn the others of these monsters..... These..... Humans..... They are coming this way. They never stop once they get a drop of blood..... Run my fawn, leave your father to rest...

article: "Wizarding school?" I said aloud to the puffs of my breath retreating behind me, holding the letter higher to catch the sun as it finally limped down past the bare trees along the walk to Professor Oak's. I had heard of people who could do..... things..... without pokes, things that normally only pokes could do, but they weren't particularly credible tales, the stuff of swarthy men in the markets just off a ship from someplace far, or else the ragged old women with more gums than sense in their heads, but they existed, the stories. Everyone had heard them, like any old fairy stories, or spook tales of Pokemon gone bad and feral. Yeah, the spook tales were sometimes true, but the wizards? I'd stopped believing in those before I was even eight. It stirred something in me to think it, though. My own power. The pokes had always seemed somehow wrong, a little sinister, for reasons I couldn't quite fathom at the time, though later I would give the subject much thought. I stopped my brisk walk and looked again at the letter before the dusk fell all around, again at that second line that drew me in, after what felt like an obligatorily exclaimed Congratulations, you have been invited to the Hogwarts School of Wizardry! , it went on in its overdone script, A council of your peers has determined you capable of learning Magic and its varied Arts and invites you to practice it at our esteemed University..... How could I have said no to that offer, that astounding and mysterious proposition, and instead taken up a pet from Professor Oak to do my bidding? Should I have become a master of little slaves in their tiny little worlds, and plied their powers on the world instead of my own? Would I have been a better boy, become a better man, if I'd made that choice instead of the school? Even after all that has happened, I do not know the answer to that. And if you have an opinion of your own on the matter, I prefer that you keep it to yourself.
