article: I lay in my bed with tears streaming down the sides of my face, staring at the ceiling. "Oh my god," I groaned. My crow fluttered from its perch on my bedpost and cocked its head to look at me with a shining eye. It hummed a sharp note as if asking me what was wrong. I slowly sat up and wiped my face. "This is a disaster. An absolute disaster," I whispered. "Too many emotions," an unexpected sob broke through my voice. My crow looked inquisitively at me. I threw on a dark robe and rushed out of my chamber and down the tower steps. I tore into the kitchen and stretched my hand out, the freezer door slammed open and ice cream flew to my hand immediately. I summoned a spoon and turned it over, looking at my reflection, stroking it with my fingertips. "I charm thee spoon, behold my command, let that love potion fade with every turn of my hand." I stuck the spoon and rotated it through the ice cream, taking a bite after each turn. After a few times, I looked up at my crow who was now pecking at my potted plants on the table. "I think it worked," I breathed. I pointed my spoon at him. "Remind me not to use my enemy's blood in beauty potions again. I accidentally stirred it counterclockwise at the end and it turned into a love potion!" I laughed, aware that I looked completely insane. "Thought it wouldn't affect me because I hate her so much. In fact, I was going to kill her tonight but nope. There I was, in sitting in my room, crying and composing music instead." I ate a large scoop of ice cream. "Absolute disaster," I said again with my mouthful. I heard a loud rush of paws coming down the hall outside the kitchen. Three of my hounds appeared in the doorway, their tails wagging furiously and their ears laid back. They whined high pitched breaths as their bodies trembled. I stood up. "She's escaped?" I asked. The hounds barked and turned to run back down the hall. I scooped a large spoonful of ice cream into my mouth before rushing out to follow them. They led me out of the castle and into the courtyard.Storm clouds blanketed the night sky, hiding the moon. The hounds barked at a muddy hole beside the stone wall of the dungeon. "She tunneled out," I said aloud. My silver staff appeared in my hand. "Find her!" I commanded, pointing the rod at my hounds. I turned into a black mist to follow them as they ran into the darkness of the woods. They howled to each other, communicating as they split off to search the wide expanse of the woods. In the distance, one of the hounds, Checkers, yelped in pain. The other hounds turned immediately in their tracks to find her. We found Checkers laying in a wet puddle on the ground with pain on her head. She whimpered, telling me that the Hero had clubbed her before running forward into the woods. I summoned a blanket over her and did a healing spell over her body, pressing dirt into her fur where she had been hit as a charm and drawing a sigil in the ground beside her. "You will be okay," I whispered. "When you can walk, come back to me." I turned back into mist and the remaining hounds took off in a run, following the scent. The scent suddenly ended in a clearing. My dogs sniffed the air, pawing at the ground to smell the leaves. Rain began to fall. Then, I spotted her. She was trying to hide in a tree but her leg was wounded from a bite from Checkers and the branch she rested on was wobbling. Twigs and leaves were falling, attracting the attention of the hounds below. They barked loudly, locking their eyes on the Hero. I returned to my human form and raised my staff, "Come here," I said in a low voice. The Hero struggled with all her might as I brought her down. She tossed her wet blonde hair aside as I brought her face to face with me. "Stop kidding yourself," she hissed. "You know your powers are weak against me." She was so furious her white teeth were bared at me in a grimace. Her brown eyes were shining and her cheeks were dewy with rain. I felt my chest begin to feel warm as I looked at her. My makeshift antidote hadn't worked afterall. My rod's power did indeed weaken she was dropped the remaining distance to the ground. She let out a cry of pain as she collapsed on her injured leg. I turned away, my hounds tilted their head in confusion at me as I hid an emotional glance from her. I walked a few steps and stared at the ground. "I have to keep you in prison until I can kill you," I said quietly. "You know this won't stop until one of us is dead." I couldn't look at her. "You could never kill me," I heard her say. "You never have and you never will. Your powers are useless against me and you're nothing without them. You're a pathetic, lonely, hag who will never have the power she wants. The only reason I've never killed you is because you're too much of a coward to fight me without protection." She spit at my dogs. I smiled at her fiery response and looked at her at last. Her hair was now completely soaked and hanging over her face, her clothes were almost see-through and she leaned weakly against a tree. She was the only creature in the world to ever match my beauty. I had been blind to it all this time. "Come willingly," I told her. "I can make it worthwhile." "Never," she said savagely. I walked closer, towering over her. She looked up at me with fierceness. My heart ached, looking at her soft skin. I had a wild thought of erasing all of her memories and holding her in my arms as my companion. I imagined us having a life together, ruling the kingdom as one, never being apart. Hearing her laugh and smile at me with affection rather than disdain. I reached out and held her chin in my hand and she flinched. "I can be different for you," I told her softly. Thunder rumbled overhead. "I would change to make you happy. No more dark magic. No more prisoners." She reached up to shove my arm away. "You are a prison. You could never change that." I reached out to her again. "You would never be alone. I would give you anything you ever wanted." She suddenly cried out in pain and fell in a heap against the tree, clutching her wound with both hands. I stood above her, stroking the silver of my staff. "Having you is all I want," I whispered. "If I can't have that, I don't see the point." "What?" she snarled. She looked up from her wound. Her lips were turning darker as the cold began to affect her skin. "I know that I can't bring your family back. Or bring back the people I murdered. I know that you'll never love me," I said loudly. Her stony glare broke for a moment. Her eyes studied my face. "But I know what would make you happy." I summoned a sword with a golden handle that appeared in the hand of the Hero Then, I pointed down at her leg and soothed it with a pain-easing charm and a clean bandage that's magic would keep it dry even in the rain. Her eyes rose to mine and her thick lashes blinked at me. "What kind of trick is this?" she asked quietly. "I could be everything you ever wanted," I said, my voice breaking. "But I know you'll never give me the chance. You'll never want me." "Why would I?" she yelled. "You're a monster!" "I just healed you and gave you a weapon! Isn't that proof that I have your best interests in mind?" "It's too late for any of that. You will never have my mercy." Her last statement hung in the air as it continued to rain. A chill swept over me. Instead of fighting back, I stood before her resolutely. "You've killed me a thousand times," I said in my softest voice. "Not having you is death itself." She stared at me as tears streamed down my cheeks. "Do what you will." She stood for a moment, then looked down at her sword. She picked it up, shifting her weight from her bandaged foot and adjusted her grip. With our eyes locked, she let out a roar and lunged toward me with a burst of frenzied energy. I watched her body, naked through her clothes, as her arm thrust the sword. I only raised my hands for defense at the last moment. She stabbed the sword deep into the left side of my chest and I fell to the ground beneath her. Pain that had been unfathomable to me before tore through my entire being and I coughed blood, grabbing at the soaking leaves on the ground around me. "I love you," I breathed. "I did this for you." She panted, holding the bloody sword for a moment before passing out on the ground beside me. We both lost consciousness from blood loss. But my hounds only brought one of us back.
label: human

article: My eyes opened to the window with the heavy paint, looking out at the old oak tree. It waved at me in the wind, and the sun brought color out into its bright red and yellow leaves. As the air shifted, many took flight, letting loose a few to the free fall, as branches shifted. Breathing was easy as I lay there, still, loose, and narrow. My back didn't hurt, my legs were tingling in anticipation of movement. Nothing cracked or groaned as I sat up. I just felt "right." Everything was so damn bright, new, amazing. I tried to not lose myself in it as I got up, rolling from my old bed, in my old house. My eyes didn't need glasses, the room was crystal clear. Luna, my old cat looked at me with a casual glance before she settled down again on the covers of it. Her hair was white, fluffy, soft, and she smelled like the flowers set on the counter she always ate when no one was home. I weighed next to nothing, as if my body was just..... just strong- like I was three times as strong as I'd been when I went to sleep the night before. I wanted to cry, to dance, to run, to move- I had to move! The day had just started, and everything was so strange! As I ran down the stairs, I jumped the last few, landing with a thud- but bouncing back up like a rocket towards the kitchen, and out the back door. The air was fresh, the sky blue, the clouds were white and beautiful as the grass and sand beneath my toes. Christ, I wanted to cry. "Come get breakfast! I'll make you eggs." Her voice was just as I remembered it, and I couldn't help but give in. I did cry then. The day went on, and I knew somehow- I just knew, that when I woke up tomorrow I would be back. I would be me as I was, that this was a fluke and a chance. This was a miracle, and if I had any guts at all- I should take it, change what I could, while I could. I didn't do that though. Instead, I spent the day with my mom and I didn't change a thing.

article: My mouth tastes metallic, like blood, and my eyes peel themselves open. I'm in a crowded room and everything is shaking. People are running over to my bedside gripping my arms. I look down and see my body writhing and convulsing uncontrollablly. My arms are twitching, my body shakes and twists. "This is normal everyone. Stand back! Stand back," one of the men gripping my arms is yelling to the crowd. They don't move an inch. The other man holding down my arms shoves a hard bit of plastic between my teeth and my jaw clamps down on it, hard. I'm panicking now, I can't breathe! I gasp in huge gulps of air and the yelling man tells the other to "sip in 7 cc's animorphine, aqueous, no saline." The IV drip next to me whirs and I start to feel calmer now. I get a better look at the men. They're both doctors, and the one on my right is considerably older. He looks about 60, with serious gray eyes and a stiff body type. His hands are sinewy and experienced. The other is much younger, probably in his late 20s. He has intelligence and energy in his movements. The older doctor pulls down his surgical mask and examines me carefully as I lie panting on the hospital bed. The crowd is eerily quiet. "My name is Dr. Fillow. How are you feeling?" My mouth still tastes metallic. Young doctor takes the bit out of my mouth. "What happened? " , I ask. Dr. Fillow glances at young doctor. Then back at me. "You just had a seizure. Your brain is refiring its neurons, doing a systems check, if you will. Can you hear me okay?" I nod. "Alright, good." Young doctor pulls out a small flashlight from his breast pocket and peers into my eyes and mouth as Dr. Fillow continues to speak. "This is going to come as a shock to you, but for the past 67 days, sir, you've been dead." I blink. "It's important that you do exactly what we tell you to do. We used a very dangerous experimental technique to get you back, but the ramifications of it are..... unknown. I need you "I died!" I panic, tears welling in my eyes. "Is this a joke. Is this a joke? Why are you doing this?!" "No, this is real. Everything here is real, and it's going to be alright. This is the first human revival of this kind of all mankind. You are the the first." I feel like I want to cry. Im happy and scared, and confused and my body begins to ache. The crowd in front of me is full of reporters and cameramen, watching closely. They split down the middle and a man in a dark blue suit and red tie hurries into the room. He looks like he's in his 50s and has the smile of a politician. He grips my hand firmly and smiles. "It's good to have you back Mr. President. But we have a situation at the White House, and you're needed as soon as possible."

article: This was the day of my grandmothers funeral. Sitting here after a full day of "mourning." I hadn't shed a tear yet, was I fucked up? I didn't understand the American way, my fathers side had invited all of my grandmothers close friends and family; including the other half of her 2nd husbands family. Drunk by the fire the day was getting late. As always in the Northwest, it was raining. A gentle sort of rain, a distinctly northwest type of rain to accompany a true portlander to her after-life. I felt the warmth of the burning flame seep past my drunken mind to warm me up from the inside; I was lost in the fires dance. Too busy to think the entire day attending all the proper customs that dictate a funeral. Perhaps I hadn't cried yet today, but I today I could not smile. I didn't understand why people had to go around laughing and being happy on the day of her funeral. Later as guests started to leave I collapsed again by the dying fire with my family to enjoy our last night in a house built 44 years ago by the hands of my grand-father. All too tired and too drunk we must not have been thinking clearly. When I declined a DD ride from my family to send me to see my girl-friend currently staying near, I used the phrase "not wanting to use the family card." My dad later says he doesn't recall saying this, but he threatened me, on the day of my grandmothers funeral after I declined leaving to spend ten minutes by the fire with him. It must have been a delayed reaction because only later did I fully realize what he did. As my father was getting scotch I walked up to him and screamed "You Fucking Lil Bitch Dad." An act I don't do and would never do, because although my father is a bitch, he is a sensitive bitch who can't bear the idea of his son calling him a bitch. I knew this, I don't know why I did it. My Uncle was restraining himself from knocking me out on the couch, my father stood stock-still confused, my brother grabbed my suit-case, jacket and threw me out. My brother wanted me to stay in the shed, but he beat me up, I think so my father wouldn't have to do it. I wandered to the neighborhood park with my sky-blue suitcase. Lost with 100 in my account, and not much else. I sat down, lit a cigeratte, than I shed a tear.
label: human

article: "Hey Mick, how you doin'? Same as usual?" "Yeah, thanks man. Doin' alright, yourself? "Business as usual, kid." The dark-haired man at the counter plucked up a Zip-Lock bag from out of sight filled with seven marbles, pink and white, swirling as if filled with smoke and handed them over. I counted the seven. A week's supply. I dropped 30 on the counter. Normally one dream for one night cost five, but buying in bulk gets you a fair discount. "You really got ta stop buyin' that shit, man. It's not good for you." "I don't know what the hell you're complaining about, I'm a loyal customer." The clerk put up both hands in mock surrender. "Alright man, take it easy." A call came from the other side of the shop. "Hey, how come I can't take any of these ones here?" The clerk walked out from behind the counter and followed the voice. A burly looking man was examining a plastic box filled to the top with marbles of black and grey. The box was locked. "Need special permission to get those. Psych eval, court order, something like that." "Psych eval? What the hell for?" "Those ain't sunshine and lollipops over there, ya understand? People don't usually buy them for personal use, if you know what I mean. Got ta make sure people don't abuse this shit." Hovering by the door, the clerk caught my eye. "You alright buddy?" "Yeah," I stammered, and pushed out of the shop. I'd tried one of those black ones before. The clerk wasn't kidding, those dreams will fuck you up. But there's always a market for something that can fuck you up. Always. I clutched the little Zip-Lock tighter in my fist, feeling the marbles rolling over my palm within the plastic membrane. constantly counting them. I got home and instantly ran to the bedroom. There was already a glass of water there. Hastily, I ripped open the bag and dropped one of the pearls in, where it dissolved instantly. Greedily, I drank it, and flopped down onto the bed, fully clothed. I only got my paycheck that morning, and cashed it after lunch. I hadn't had a chance to buy a dream in over a week. I needed my fix. Sleep assaulted me like a wrestler, dragging me into darkness quickly and efficiently. Her face swam into view, pale, blonde, blue-eyed. She smiled at me. I felt the muscles in my face tug at the corners of my lips, and a light burning from behind my eyes and in my throat. I never wanted to go another night without seeing her face.
label: human

article: After ordering her usual, an herbal tea with cream, Abigail chooses a table in the center of the busy coffee shop. She pulls out the latest issue of Vogue, hoping to gain inspiration for tomorrow afternoon's shopping expedition. A woman approaches, and asking if it would be okay to share the table. "I would prefer that you sit elsewhere," she chides without bothering to look up. She asks herself what is wrong with the world, wondering why a total stranger would assume it acceptable to invade what is obviously her personal space. She comes here infrequently, because she hates the smell of coffee. She hates the idea of watching students pack away at laptop keyboards, hurrying to complete assignments that are probably late anyhow. "What is wrong with this world?" She never attended college, despite her parents' pleasing. She was determined to find a husband, one with a lot of money. Her theory was that after years of watching her mother go without..... She needed to break the cycle. She picks up her ringing cell, looks at the caller ID and answers quickly. "Hey Tara! Are we still on for tomorrow? I just saw a pair of boots in vogue that I'll die without. Oh, your sister is coming? You told her that was okay already? Well. Okay then. I'll see you tomorrow at what? Three? Okay. See you then. She immediately begins to search for an excuse. "There's no way I'm going shopping with her sister. That girl spends every second talking about her kids. I hate kids. If I want to share my money, I'll donate some to those starving kids in Africa."
label: human

article: I loved that picture. Truly, I did. Although at this point, I doubt that I'll ever be able to convince him otherwise. What do you even do with something like that? Something entirely sentimental? That's probably the worst part of the break up, knowing that I have no other option. That picture, that incredible, sweet, thoughtful gift, was my favorite possession. I hung it on the wall, next to the mirror I dressed in front of, so that I would see it every day before I left for home. Seeing the goofy joy on his face gave me the strength to handle the day. Life is really unfair sometimes, but knowing that in that moment someone loved me made it all seem ok. He really did love me. But it wasn't enough. Yes, he loved me, but he loved me less than her. Or maybe not. Maybe there was some other hidden reason that he put me second. Maybe it was just that she got there first. She won the race. Or maybe I really am somehow less than her. At this point it's just speculation. Now I have no beacon, no talisman to make me feel strong. Instead I'm left day dreaming about horrible things happening to her. I try to keep them ridiculous and funny so that I don't feel like a horrible person. I picture her getting punched by a monkey, or getting her arrested for racketeering. Like some girl who behaves like a defenseless child would ever be capable of running a mafia. That's the most infuriating part of losing him. Knowing that this was entirely planned by some woman as a power play. I guess that's why the Scooby Doo fantasy is so appealing. Everyone is standing around with her being held in some net when Fred pulls off her obviously cheap Halloween mask. In my mind that's the only explanation for her (obviously less attractive than mine) face. She turns to me and say's "I would have gotten away with it too, if it wasn't for that meddling woman." Of course, I'm seen as the hero, and ride off into the sunset with him. I promise I'm not some insane ex-girlfriend. I would never actually do anything to harm his relationship, because it would kill me to do anything that might make him unhappy. But it's still so hard not to feel jealous, and not to hate someone who is so manipulative. Especially when she takes something you need. That's why I packed up the picture last night. And why I'm driving to his house right now. Because as long as I have that picture, I know I'll hold onto hope that he might eventually choose me. All of the other gifts, the love tokens gathered over a period of building a life together, are fine. They serve a purpose. But the picture is only useful as a reminder of what I've lost. And the only reason I would keep it is if I held onto hope for a future where we're together. I still love him, and I believe that he still loves me, but he's made his choice. So I'm choosing to give the picture back, not because I don't love it or him, but because I love them both too much.
label: human

article: "You're going to lose." "I don't really think that's the case. But I guess we will see won't we?" "How are you so calm?" Click. Woman passes the gun to Man. "I like to think even chance knows which one of us should be the one to go." "Ha! Not very likely." a second click. Man passes the gun back. "Chance is the one thing you can't control. You should know this by now." "Are you quite certain?" Smiles. Click. Passes the gun." Man swallows. "There's no way. You can't control this! You can't!" the gun quivers in his hand. "It's your turn." Man eyes the gun with disdain. "All these years..... All this time, you've been in control of everything. Letting these people rot from the inside out. Ordering me to watch over the countless agonies, the turmoil and war..... Casting me away from your graces, just because I dared question your flawed plan..." Man brings the gun up, pointing at Woman's head. "Well no more!" Woman smiles. "Ah. There it is. You have learned the power of choice. I believe this is all you needed." Woman 1 pulls the gun forward, placing a finger over that of Man, pulling the trigger for him. Click. Click. "Wh-Why?" "It is my time." God closes her eyes. "Enjoy your promotion." Bang.
label: human

article: " Do you really think Earth is dead by now? " I love Jenny, and I'm going to get to see her for the first time tomorrow because it's Mingling Day and we're both 16 now. We're going to have sex, and I'm going to try to get her pregnant. I even hope the baby is a girl so it can stay to live with her rather than coming over to me. However, I've learned this doesn't mean she never annoys me. " I don't know. No one knows, not even the Vorn. " " Yeah, but my grandma says they were wrong. Humans weren't doomed to overpopulation and war. We can control our breeding with contraception or even just by avoiding sex even though when we're all mixed together. If that's true, then they didn't rescue us, they kidnapped us. " " My grandpa says the same thing, " I agreed. I was mostly being diplomatic though. I thought the Vorn had probably been right, and human civilization on Earth had probably been doomed when they had first found us. It was true that humans, unlike the Vorn, didn't have to have sex just because we encountered a fertile female. However, it was also true that our females were always capable of sex, and most people would choose to have sex if they could. The population of Earth had certainly doubled in the four decades before they arrived. That didn't seem sustainable. " Anyway, " I told Jenny, " here and now we live like they do- segregated. We're alive, and we're going to see each other tomorrow. That's all that really matters, right? " Jenny sighed happily and that made any annoyance I still felt melt. " You're right. OK, if we have a baby and it's a girl, what do you want to name it? " " I still think you're nuts to skip the orgies, " Mike called over the noise of the bus. I looked out the window at the approaching Women's City. From the outside it didn't look like much. Just a giant circular wall rising from the lifeless plain of the planet the Vorn had dumped us on. Some people call our world Earth 2 or New Earth. Maybe that's an acceptable name, but the new world certainly isn't an improvement on the old one. Still, when the Vorn are convinced we're responsible about population they'll let us expand. We're doing well with that. Mingling Day is run by humans now, and humans punish anyone trying to city jump. There's talk the Vorn are going to let us have another couple of cities. Maybe they'll let us plant something as well. I looked back to Mike, " If you have a son without a registered partnership then you don't get to keep him. The pop board will assign the child to the best adoptive parent. " " Kids are a lot of work, " Mike countered. " Everyone helps. You're just mad because you broke up with Ann. " Mike folded his arms and turned back toward the front of the bus, suggesting I'd hit closer to the mark than I intended. It was just as well. By that time, our bus had reached the massive gate in the wall of the women's city and we both had better things to worry about. The day passed quickly, a little awkwardly, and pleasantly. In truth, I only remember the first half. On Mingling Day anyone is allowed to drink, and I didn't have the head for it because otherwise the minimum age is 18. Things get fuzzy around noon, and I think I passed out with Jenny in her bed at about 3. Still, before that everything was great. Afterword's, not so much. I woke up, groaned slightly, and rubbed by head. " Ouch. I thought hangovers came the following morning. " Jenny stirred beside me, waking up then sitting up. She looked like an angel. My headache faded somewhat, and I leaned over to kiss her. We'd gotten enough practice during the day that we were getting pretty good. The kissing lasted a few minutes before Jenny pushed me back. " Do we have time? How long will you need to get back to your bus? " I'd memorized that, " Only 10 minutes. " I looked around. It was dark except for the street lights coming through the window and the light that leaked under her bedroom door. " What time is it anyway? " Jenny fumbled a bit in the darkness pulling a piece of clothing off of her alarm clock. She gasped then showed it to me without saying anything. I heard myself gasp as well though I didn't consciously decide to make the sound. The clock read 3:13 a.m. " That can't be right. " " I went around and set all the clocks yesterday. Nothing's more than a second off! " " But what about the sirens? I didn't hear anything! " I fumbled through the darkness finding my pants and in them my phone. The phone agreed with the clock. " Shit! I'm city jumping! The pop board is going to execute me. " The Vorn hadn't done that, but the pop board was serious about getting those extra cities. They'd upped the penalties for illegal mingling. I was starting to freak out. Jenny grabbed me, " Not if you get back to Men's City. " " How? " " Today is the best day for it. Everyone got the day off, everyone got drunk, no one would expect a city jumper three hours after Mingling Day ends. If anyone is watching the wall it's some granny too old to care about Mingling Day, and she'll probably be half blind. " Jenny proved to be more or less correct. She was able to show me where to find a wall maintenance harness, and we were able to move around the city without anyone getting close enough to realize I was male. I texted Mike to hang a rope over the Men's City wall, and miraculously, he wasn't too drunk to get the text, so I had a route back into the Men's City when I got there. When I reached the door to the stairs in the city wall I kissed Jenny and sent her away. She wanted to come with me, but she'd already helped me all she could. She wouldn't get executed for being caught with a man, but she would get in a lot of trouble. I'd let her risk enough just getting us across the city. Alone, things felt even worse. I'd expected the door to the stairs to be locked and I had taken a crowbar to pry my way in, but it wasn't. The stairwell echoed like a tomb as I climbed them. Worse yet, it was completely lit. Anyone who could see me would know in an instant that I was male. Climbing to the top of the wall was the longest 15 minutes of my life. When I finally reached the top without meeting anyone I was physically dizzy with relief. I'd be able to get back out into the darkness. I shouldn't have assumed I was safe. I didn't open the door to peek out. I just threw it wide and stepped out like a moron. There was a woman guarding the walls. Like Jenny had predicted she was old. She was sliver haired and tiny. She moved somewhat uncomfortably as she turned to face me. I didn't think she'd be fast enough to catch me, or strong enough to fight me. Unfortunately, the huge gun she held would see to both of those things though its recoil might knock her over. We were both startled. I raised my hands reflexively, and she trained her gun on me. Then slowly I lowered my hands. I was doomed, I might as well make the best of it. I addressed her, " I'm going to run. Shoot me in the back and make it good. It'll be quick and it'll keep my partner out of trouble. " " You idiot. Come over here and I'll help you get that harness tied off. At least you were smart enough to bring something to get down. " " What? " None of that made sense to me. " You think you're the first person to over sleep on Mingling Day? You're the 5th tonight! Fortunately, we old folks remember how stupid this all is. We can't do much about it, but we watch the walls tonight. I'm going to keep this section of wall clear while you ' escape'and then I'm going to call a man in the other city. Do you have a way up? " I nodded, too stunned to speak. " Good, now hop to. You haven't got much time to get back before dawn. Never speak of this, but remember it when you're old. " I made it. It was close; false dawn was in the sky when I crested the city wall. No one saw me, or if they did they also ignored me. I kept my promise to the old lady and didn't say anything about her help. Actually, I didn't mind having to make up a slightly more impressive lie to give Mike. Almost getting shot by a granny didn't sound so great. I'll keep the second half of my promise as well, and once I'm old I'll watch the walls once a year.
label: human

article: "What the hell is that?" exclaimed Sgt. Hammes, his hand cupped to his mouth in a futile attempt to contain the coming explosion of vomit. There was silence from the rest of us. When we set out to Europa, the pioneers of a new age of humanity, we certainly didn't expect this. "When I set out to Europa, a pioneer of a new age of humanity, I certainly didn't expect this," echoed Captain MacGowan, subconsciously in tune with the narrative - it was quite a tragedy he was gay. "I like it when we all speak one after another," interjected Cpl. Staropoli, who shared my appreciation for the finer things in life, like Nellie Mavis's singing voice and those little vacuum packed candies you can only buy at that one store back at the Mount Olympus Space Center. "Fuck it!" declaimed Pvt. Baronov boldly, causing the rest of Squad To Acclimatize Remote Worlds In other Places (STARWIPE) to take a few steps back as they took all this new information in. "Raul, my boy, you can't do that - look at it, it's literally indescribable! " , noted MacGowan, for Raul was the young private's first name. "There's a reason you contribute to this team but your penis!" But it was already too late. Pvt. Baronov stepped forward to the..... thing and unzipped his spacesuit, forgetting that the subzero temperatures would freeze him solid the moment he did so. At least he made a nice ice sculpture, what with the massive erection and all. In Memory Of Raul Baronov (Oct. 4, 2297 - Apr. 5, 2325), Who Died Doing What He Loved
label: human

article: Jason walked into his apartment after a hard day at the office. He kicked off his dress shoes, and draped his coat on the couch, making a mental note to hang it up before he goes to bed. "Mike? You here buddy?" Jason called out for his new roommate but he had gotten no answer. Shrugging to himself he walked through to the kitchen to poor himself a drink. It had been a long day. He poured himself a glass, but as we went to take a sip, Jason lost grip on the glass. It shattered on the floor, breaking the tile as well. "Fuck, there goes my damage deposit." Jason swept up the broken tile and glass, but noticed something odd underneath the tile, it looked like to be a note. Sitting at the table, the note read: "Jason You're being watched. Constantly. You're an experiment and everything has been part of a game. And the game is almost done. I'm sending this letter from the future to the past. Hopefully it reaches you in time. It worked for me, so it should work for you. You have to get rid of Mike. He's the only other player. Be careful. He might have also gotten a letter." Just then, Jason heard the door creak open, and a hesitant voice ask if Jason was home.
label: human

article: Tonight was my night; my 16th birthday. Finally, after what felt like a lifetime of waiting, it was my time to shine. I had waited almost a year for this day, ever since my best friend Andrew discovered in January that he could fly. I had envied him at first, being the first in the tenth grade with a power. As time passed I was jealous of what it said about him. If powers are a reflection of our character as scientists believed, I came to envy what this said about his life. He was free, he was pure and he was without a care in the world. What did he know about pain? of being beaten by your father every day for imagined sins and infractions? Of having to steal your best friends allowance to wear decent clothes? of being labelled by girls as a'creep' and of your few friends pitying you? But times had changed. New Years eve, my birthday, had arrived and I smiled at my reflection. I wondered what my power would be. Super strength for my strength through the hardships? Mind reading for my ability to empathize? I was entertaining these thoughts when my phone rang. Hello? Hey it's Andrew here, you ready for the party? Sure, pick me up in ten. Hello? I heard static and a click as my phone died. I moved it away from my ear, and then smiled. Tiny cracks ran along the screen and continued to spread from where my hand held the phone. I willed the cracking to stop, and it did.
label: human

article: "Finally, we have discovered the fountain of youth! At long last eternal youth is wait, what does that placard say?" "Whosoever drinks from this fountain shall be as they were from the beginning. So I guess we'll be babies if we drink it." "Well, let's take turns then, every thirty years one of us drinks, and then we raise each other. It's not what we thought, but we'll still live forever!" "Yeah, that's an idea, but first we can bash our heads a bit with these fist sized rocks, because that is what I would rather do than raise a baby every thirty years. We should bottle it, and sell it to rich people who can afford to hire themselves a nanny. Then we'll be rich and can hire nannies for ourselves." "Oh, yeah that's a much better plan. I really don't know where mine came from. I'm glad you have such a strong mind for business." "Besides, we both know I would drink first and then betray you when your turn came about." "You're kind of a bastard, aren't you?"
label: human

article: "We need to talk..." I stood there speechless, mouth agape. 5 long years it had been. And suddenly, there she stood on the doorstep. Her hair was matted. Her skin was a pale blue hue under the moonlight. Her face was worn and tired. She wore a strange necklace. The past half decade must have been rough on her. Silently, I let her into my home. Her clothes were soaking wet. I offered her a sweater and some sweat pants. She declines, preferring to just sit by the fire. The myriad of conflicting emotions overwhelm me. Anger, confusion, and happiness swirl messily in my head. She had seem troubled the days before disappearing, but could always muster a smile. "As long as you're here with me, I could ask for nothing more," she would always say to me. But, one day, she just left. No note. No explanation. How could she leave without telling me? The anger rose within me. I thought that we had always been close! I thought she could tell me everything! There were no secrets between us! Anger quickly gave way to the fonder memories. She always let me have the last cookie. "I'll just get fat. You can have it," she would say. When the neighborhood bully Tara the Terrible I would call her came after me, my sister gave her a good whooping. She was grounded for a month, but Tara never bothered me again. "Why did you leave? Why did you not tell us you were leaving?" I demanded. My sister tugged at her necklace. It appeared heavy and uncomfortable. "I didn't have the strength to tell you, Sis. I knew you would be disappointed in me. You would have called me weak. I couldn't resist giving in. There was nothing for me here. This promised me freedom and salvation." She lifted her necklace as she spoke. "What do you mean you had nothing? You had me! I was here for you!" I could feel the aching pain rising in my chest. "Yes, Sis. You were the only one I had. That's why I couldn't tell you I was leaving. You would have convinced me to stay. Anyways, I realize I had been wrong. The pain I caused you was much more than the pain I ever felt. I came to beg for your forgiveness. I promise to stay here with you. You can talk to me any time. I am here for you." Tears were streaming down my face. For the last 5 years, I was so angry. But, here she was once again. I knew she cared about me. She came back just for me! "Yes, I forgive you. Please don't ever leave me again." My sister continued playing with her necklace. "Would you like a cookie? You look like you haven't eaten for 5 years. You're all skin and bones." "Haha. No thanks, Sis. I'll just get fat. You can have it." "Will you stay the night?" "Sure Sis. I'll sleep right here by the fire. It's nice and warm here." The next morning, my sister was gone. On the floor was her necklace. I picked it up. It was simple and cheap. Only made of rope, with a running bowline knot in the back. I put it in my purse and got into my car. It was a 30-minute drive, but it was a drive I had made numerous times in the last 5 years. I parked on the gravel lot. Across the road was a flower-lined path. I saw my sister at the end of the path. "Here. You forgot your necklace. If you don't mind, I'd like to hold onto it for you. It was only making you uncomfortable. I brought you some cookies. I know what you're going to say, but I really want you to eat them this time." A tear rolled down my cheek. "Thanks for coming back to me. I really missed you." I set the tray down by her grave. I got up and began walking back to my car.
label: human

article: There were more lights in the warehouse and the crowd was larger. The place seemed to have made use of the extra money they were making from the large show ups and improving the place. A larger banner was held high over the arena stating the rules of the fight: Rule 1. No matter the outcome, the fights stay in between these walls Rule 2. Tapout or KO ends the fight. Rule 3. don't kill each other. A bell rang in the background and the fight was on. I paid attention to the way my opponent carried himself. His right leg in front of the other. This meant that he is left hand dominant. He was taking short strides to the left and the right with both hands covering the sides of his face. With each stride he was coming closer. Now, I can see his heart rate from the pulsations of his arteries at the neck, his flight or fight response has already kicked in. I notice two small depressions on the sides of his nose, probably where his glasses would sit on his nose that he isn't currently wearing. A weakness I shall exploit. I let my guard down to test his response, he tests my agility in return with a weak right hand blow that I easily dodged. I send a left kick to his right ribs and he blocks by pushing my leg downward as it continues its path. That was our strategy, he blocks, I dodge. Now the fight has actually begun. He takes a step closer and proceeds to throw a deadly blow with a left swing, I dodge to the left where he now has created a blind spot for himself, without his glasses he probably won't see as a aim for his right ankle with my right foot and send him off balance. As he is falling to the ground the whole world goes into slow motion as a run in my head how I will subdue him. But he doesn't fall predictively. After losing balance and falling half-way to his right side, my opponent, rolls himself into a ball, and as I'm halfway into my move and nearly over his entire body I realize I have made a mistake, he is now rolled on to his back and has a face full of confidence as he proceeds to use both feet to strike my face. I have to cut my losses, I allow myself to lean forward right as his feet were near my torso and he strikes me on my tightly flexed abdominal muscles. sending me a few feet away. we both get up in an instant and realize we're not the typical fighter. He recovered from a fall and nearly struck a winning blow while I suffered a blunt strike to the abdomen instead of one to the face which would have ended the game. This was no ordinary match. It was a bloody game of chess, like playing against a someone who calculated each move and outcome as it the game unraveled. [ please carry on this fight guys ]
label: human

article: I used to be like you. I would have laughed and never believed it to be true, until it was true. Our world was, literally, changed. But I wonder if it was changed or if it was always this way. On April 1st of 2017 I thought it was all a joke. The newspapers read, "Flat Earth Society Conspiracy Proven Right! The Whole Planet Is On Edge!!" and I thought it was all a hoax. Haha, April Fools. Throughout the day they really had me going, too. Even the news broadcast was in a hype about this. I had to hand it to them, dedication to this big of a joke is rare these days. Maybe the joke will make the news tomorrow. I wasn't wrong. The next day the newspapers had even more to say about this! "Earth Not Round. Scientists Fall Flat On Face!!" You'd think they'd come up with a better headline? Even the news kept going on about all the proof that had been found and how this'll change our school systems and was showing diagrams describing seasons and everything. Then it hit me, what if they weren't kidding? I took a second to look around, people were talking about it. EVERYONE was talking about it. As days went on, people were in a mad panic. There were stories of fishermen falling off the edge, countries slowly drifting as the flat surface tilts for the seasons. But it got worse. Did you know the Earth doesn't evolve around the sun, but the sun evolves around the Earth? In The NASA Station Sam chuckled to himself and turned to his partner, Max, in Public Affairs, "How long do you think we can keep them going?" Max shrugged, "Let's see. Bring out more news on the sun evolving the world and connect that to seasons, too. They'll go crazy."
label: human

article: Harold Shaw walked confidently into Dr. Pepper's office. This was his last therapy session at Carbonated Springs Rehabilitation Center, and he was a very different man than the one who had stumbled across the doorstep three months earlier. That Harold had been grossly obese, diabetic, and rambling nonsense about "tanks in the Fulda Gap." The new Harold was fit, trim, possessed a sharp mind, and was actually a bit more handsome. It was all thanks to the good Doctor's "Miracle Fizzy Tonic," a wonderful concoction that started Harold on the road to recovery. Harold sat down on Dr. Pepper's couch. Dr. Pepper was sitting in his usual plush cherry-red armchair, wearing his usual white seersucker suit. He stroked his wispy beard and offered Harold a can of his Fizzy Tonic. "Thanks, Doc!" Harold exclaimed. He quickly downed the delicious drink. Harold felt as if his tongue was celebrating the Fourth of July. "Gee, Doc, it feels as if my tongue is celebrating the Fourth of July! This Fizzy Tonic sure is tasty!" Dr. Pepper smiled and said, "It sure is! I'm very pleased in your progress. You've become a changed man. I remember your first shock therapy sessions with New Coke..." Harold's body gave an involuntary shudder " ..... and your withdrawal therapy to Diet Coke, then to Coke Zero, then finally to my patented Miracle Fizzy Tonic. Here, have another." Harold gratefully took the offered can and chugged it down. Dr. Pepper continued: "There is one last test before you, Harold. One test to prove that you are truly cured. Are you ready?" "I don't know, Doc. I may need another can of Fizzy Tonic. You know, to shore up my courage." Dr. Pepper gave Harold another can and smiled as it was emptied as fast as the others. Harold belched and said, "Okay, I'm ready." Dr. Pepper withdrew a can of Coca Cola from his suit pocket and placed it on the table. Harold stared at it. He could imagine the sweet delight of the soda's sugary goodness, its playful bubbles beckoning him. Harold started to sweat. He could hear the crisp pop of the can opening. He could see the sensual dark caramel color inviting him into Coke's sweet embrace. Harold's hands started shaking. He could see a vision of [ mounted ICBMs rolling past Red Square with thousands of proletarians cheering in the background. ] (https: ) With a titanic effort, Harold gave a cry and swatted the can across the room. Dr. Pepper wore a triumphant grin. His patient was free of the evils of Coca Cola; he was cured. Harold looked at his doctor expectantly. "Well done, Harold." Dr. Pepper rewarded Harold with another can of Fizzy Tonic. "The first stage of your journey is complete." Harold looked at Dr. Pepper with questioning eyes. "The next stage is about to begin. Harold, did you know that there are still some people in the world that don't know about about my patented Miracle Fizzy Tonic?" Harold gasped. "Yes, Harold, it is a shame that those people don't know the healing wonders of my drink. But you can help them, Harold; you must help them." Harold nodded. "You must go out there, Harold, and introduce the people to my patented Miracle Fizzy Tonic. They may resist at first, but you must force them to like it. It will be for their own good." Harold suddenly rose and strode across the room. He picked up the discarded can of Coke. "They will drink it, or they will die!" He crushed the can, sending its vile contents spraying across the room. Dr. Pepper gave a benevolent grin. "Good, good! Now, go forth, my disciple, and spread the good news! [ Always One of a Kind! ] (https: ) "

article: Assuming we have materials that can last quite some time, and can be quickly molded into what we want them to be - I would do it like this: Pick a major class-one city nearby and use a low-yield nuke to flatten a few blocks worth' of buildings in the center so that it's easily noticed from the air by visitors from other worlds should they ever come. article: She used to be my best friend. She was my everything. She was my other half, and now? Now I'm broken without her. I am broken by the memories of harmony. article: Most mornings I wake up a few minutes before my alarm goes off so I doze as I wait for seven am. It was 6:56 that Tuesday morning when I woke up, I had four minutes so I closed my eyes and woke again at 6:59. I waited for 7 for what felt like too long but checking my phone it was still 6:59. I looked at the digital clock on my bed side table and starred at it, waiting for the digital dial to flick to 7:00. It felt like minutes but it didn't change; nor did my phone. I looked at the analog clock on my bedroom wall, the hands were pointing at 6:59 but the second hand had stopped at a second before seven o'clock. Something was not right so I got up and walked around the flat, every read out or clock was frozen at 6:59am. I didn't know why and I didn't know what time it was so I set off to work, skipping breakfast in case I was late. My walk to the station is always quiet at half past seven but that morning was even quieter with only one car passing by on the ten minute walk and the shop which opens at seven thirty am was still shut up so maybe I wasn't late for work after all. At the station I found that the digital clock on the board displaying the trains due read 6:59 and the 7:47 I usually get was displaying. The ticket office was not yet open so I bought a ticket at the automated machine, the receipt read 6:59 as the transaction time. I got a coffee from the vending machine in the waiting room and sat down to wait. My phone continued to read and my watch still refused to tick. It was 6:59 when I finished my coffee and I checked my phone again. A message flicked across the screen "no service" at the same moment the station tanoy boomed into life "This is a customer service announcement. We regret to inform you that all services from this station have been cancelled indefinitely due to current events." Despite the message on my screen, I decided to try and phone work to let them know I could not get in. The phone beeped in my ear and abruptly cancelled the call. What the fuck is going on?

article: Title: Childlike innocence. " MOM! Laurlie already got to play with the racecar. It's my turn! " Eric stuck out his bottom lip as his sympathy inducing eyes watered. Laurie rebutted, " It's not fair. He's been playing with it everyday and I need the car today so I can pick up Samantha from the hair-dresser! " Samantha was the name of Laurie's doll, Laurie was letting Samantha have a spa day. Diplomatically, the maternal figurehead grabbed the sportscar. " If you two can't share, then I'm going to play with the sports car today. " The mother grabbed the car and put it in her crystal glassware cupboard. George despised his suit wearing matriarch. " And I want to keep it in the garage until everybody learns to play nicely together. " Eric's face reddened angrily. When his mother looked away he went into daddie's study, grabbed the book the of matches next to daddies pipe and walked over to his suited matriarch who was now seated at the dining room table. " It's not Laurlie's turn. You have to listen to me! SHE TOOK MY RACECAR. " He swiped the match and brought it to her hair. " ERIC! " Screamed Eric's suit wearing Matriarch..... "Did you hear me Eric?....." Mr. Holder snapped out of his daydream. " Mr. Attorney General, I said I'd like to hear your opinion on this. " The Attorney General cleared his throat. " Ahem. I'm sorry, Secretary Clinton, but at this point I would not support any decision to stop or limit drone strikes against known terrorist dwellings..." He paused with a ponderous look on his face and continued with heightened animation, "What I'm saying is that they took away our freedom and put it in a glass case! Just out of reach Madam Clinton! " He was standing at that point. fervent as he had ever been before. His eyes darted around, looking to the members of the cabinet and he slowly sat back down. " He he he. " Eric snickered to himself. OT: I always like to participate in my own prompts, so I just whipped this one up. It may not be totally accurate haha, I'm not even from the U.S.

article: They don't usually answer back to what I say. Especially at first, they didn't just so you know. But the longer I've been here..... I've gotten to where I can hear them, all the time. They whisper at me, though, they never talk out loud. I don't know why. But they have these little whisper voices, and they do talk to me, just so you know. I mean, I have to be close. But I can hear them. I really can. The other day I sat down on a park bench by one woman and she was whispering about her baby. I couldn't tell exactly what she was saying, but she sounded pretty sad. I did my best to comfort her, just so you know. But she was pretty stiff. Pretty hard to talk to. She wouldn't stop talking about her baby. And yesterday, yesterday there was this old man. He was standing on the curb like he was about to cross the street, and if there had been cars coming I would have asked if he needed help. Not that it would do any good now, even if there were any cars -none of these people ever drive, for some reason. And I can't ever get a straight answer out of them when I ask them questions. It's almost like they can't hear me, except I know they can because they're people. They really are people, just so you know. But anyway. This old man. He was standing on the curb and when I walked by him I could hear him talking, too. He was whispering about his mother. I got real close, just to see if I could help him or something, and he just kept talking about how his mother would be worried if he didn't get home soon. Which is weird, because this guy was at least in his 80s; no way he'd have a mother still alive. He wouldn't respond to me, but I did try to help him, just so you know. It's hard, though, living where no one will talk to you. You actually start to feel invisible after a while, like you're a ghost or something. Recently, I've been wondering a lot whether or not I'm actually in some dream. I've gotten hurt several times, which you'd think would wake me up if I was dreaming, but I don't know what else this could be. The only place no one will talk to you is in your dreams. But I'll tell you what, I've gotten some advice from these people. They won't answer me or carry on a conversation, but I guess some of them have been able to tell what I've been thinking. I've been thinking that maybe to wake up, I need to actually die in this world. And I guess they heard me talking to myself about it or something, because lately every time I walk past somebody, they're telling me that I should go down to the river and jump in. At first I didn't see what good that would do, but then I realized that I could get one of those huge rocks down there and tie it to myself before I jumped. Tie the knot real tight, so it's hard to get loose. And once rope gets wet, it's about impossible to untie -just so you know. At first, I didn't take the suggestions seriously, but now it's to where all these people will whisper about is me jumping in. It's starting to drive me kind of crazy, actually. And I need to get them to shut up. I need to be able to wake up, to get back to where people will talk to me and not just whisper instructions about how to kill myself. Lately it's gotten to where I can hear them even when I'm not very close. All these different voices, telling me how to end this thing. I'm going down to the river tomorrow. Just so you know.
label: human

article: They must've got the wrong one. It's okay. I have that kind of face. Or had, I guess. I can't say I have much of a face at this point. The same sentiment rings true for the face I used to have, now scattered on the floor before the body it used to define, inside-out and painted crimson with pulp of what was my frontal lobe. It looks painful. I don't know if it was. I think it was. I think it must've been. It's clearly painful for the remaining corporeal beings in the room. I'm not sure what else to expect when you put a loaded high caliber weapon to the back of another man's head and pull the trigger, but this was definitely not the result they anticipated. The only one with any semblance of composure is the dog, who just whimpers, licks the speckles of my blood from his chops, and settles on his haunches. The man holding the dog is not nearly as calm. That's understandable, considering he was the only one facing me as the bullet entered-and violently exited-my head. The handler stood at a 45 degree angle to me, holding back the dog on a considerably short chain. Prior to my execution, the two had put on a great show, each trying to out-bark the other. It might well have terrified me, in its own right, but at the time my attention was rather focused on the barrel of a gun pressed unnecessarily forcefully against the peak of my skull. In the end, the show I put on for him was significantly more effective. Though they he positioned himself what should have been a safe distance away, a good portion of me had sprayed across the handler and his dog, a bright contrast against his all black attire. Now shot, now ethereal and now somehow fixed above and throughout this scene, I watch as his eyes expand beyond the size allowed beneath the holes of his knit ski mask. His body starts convulsing, rattling rhythmically as if one reversed the resonance of a banged gong, exponentially building to his explosive "Fuck." As if waiting for this audible cue, the one in the corner vomits. It's a full-body, doubled-over-on-your-knees vomit. Whatever weapon he was holding hangs loosely on his neck as he partially spews on it with his yellow stink. Tucked away in the dark corner behind the scene, clutching an automatic rifle the size of his torso, he must have been trying so hard to look so stern. Yet I hadn't even noticed he existed until I no longer did. His stream is fully expunged before the "Fuck" even finishes bouncing off the walls. The lone woman in the room (I'm pretty sure she's a woman) is now in front of the gun-wielder, between him and the chair in which I was seated, where the body I had worn had been sitting. She pleads with gunman, beats him with her fists, screams her fucking head off at him. "What did you do?" "Were is the reset?" "Who the fuck was that?" The gunman only stands, his arm still erect, holding the gun in the same spot my head had been. A yellow pool beneath his left foot adds to the abundance of bodily fluids filling the room. Then the feed cuts off. I can't say why it was on for so long. My brain wasn't intact, and yet my thoughts were-are-intact. They're strong and unstoppable, completely unquenchable, adrift without stimulation in this soft dark nothing. For those final moments, what living tissue was left of my mind to carry me through that scene? I didn't just watch or hear or see; for the dwindling instance of my life, I became that room. And now, in this total deconstruction of time and matter, what's left of me to be abandoned in this eternal circle of thought? I wish I knew a bit more. Though, I suppose that's the great wish of the dead. For all the closure and resolution found in the films and the books and the ballads of the living, nothing prepares you for the questions never answered in the absence of your life. without even a hand to count to track the time or an eye to see it, I can't measure how long I've been left to thinking. I'll just call it an eternity. I turn these impossible observations over and over, playing them forwards and backwards as well as I can, buy all I'll ever know, for certain, never changes. I was killed by a bunch of kids who thought you could reset life.
label: human

article: Freddie and Helen Kissinger had lived on 15 Elm Street in the small town of Nottingdale, Indiana, for the last forty-five or so years of their lives. Freddie was a school principal at the local elementary school, Helen taught music at the same school. Freddie had advanced cirrhosis of the liver that was expected to be untreatable at his age, and Helen had been coughing up blood from the tears in her stomach lining that had come up as a result of some parasitic infection or another. They were ready. Sort of. Helen squawked from the bed, " Did you leave the letter for the kids? " Freddie quavered, " Yes, dear, it's behind the screen door. " " What about the dog? " " The dog died two years ago. " " Leave some cookies out on the porch for the kids when they stop by. " " I did at noon. " " What-what about the garden? " " Helen, who gives a shit? We're going to die. " It was a beautiful day outside. The petunias swayed in perfect formation, the sun beat down through the windows of the little isolated house on the lonely road coming out of town. Freddie kicked the dog on the way upstairs, with his sleeping pills in hand. Four of them would kill an adult human, and Freddie wasn't exactly sure if either of them still qualified as either of those things. He wore his dress blues, while Helen wore her Sunday best. He had to coerce her into taking off the plumed hat before she settled down. He gave eight pills to her, and eight to himself. Little nuggets of death lying in the dusty bowl of his time-worn palm. He was ready, and looking at Helen, his wife of sixty-three years, he knew she was ready too. They mouthed the words together. One. Two. Three. Freddie palmed the pills. They lay clutched in his hand, and he sighed and leaned back as if he had done something momentous. He stuffed them under the covers. He lay down and waited for his wife to die. Fifteen minutes later, he heard his wife's breathing slow. It was time. He carefully got out of bed. He didn't have cirrhosis. He just drank a lot and hated his wife. He looked outside. He was ready. He stepped out of the room with a boundless energy he hadn't felt since he graduated high school. He clattered down the stairs and clicked his heels. Suddenly, " YOU DICKLESS BITCH, I KNEW YOU DIDN'T TAKE THOSE PILLS. " Fuck. He grabbed the shovel and went upstairs.

article: Every day without fail, a prompt about the divine is posted to WritingPrompts. With so many in need, how can the gods answer the call? The answer is simple: They team up. One group exists to help meet the needs of a prompt-hungry populace: the Pan-Eternal Godhood Bureau Overseeing All Relevant Dieties. The men and women of PEGBOARD strive to keep the replies coming. These are their stories. "Is this the control room?" Satan asked as he walked into the control room. He wasn't what you'd expect from a devil - he was human, for one. Looked pretty unsure of himself, but [ it was his third day ] (https: ) so that wasn't too surprising. "That it is," I said. I leaned forward to shake his hand. "Welcome to PEGBOARD command, I take it your indoctrination went well?" Satan nodded. "Uh, yeah. I've already started a few projects. That's why I'm here, I was hoping you could help me with something." "Of course," I said, "that's what we're here for." I motioned for Gabrielle - my second in command - to follow us. She wasn't as new to her job as Satan was, but she still had a lot to learn. The rest of the technicians in the room knew their job well, they could handle anything short of a dire emergency. Satan lead us down the hallway and to one of the many celestial elevators. We piled in and he pressed the button for the basement. "Can you give us a briefing while we wait?" I asked casually. All the other deities knew by now not to waste our time by waiting to give us the details. Not that it actually mattered to us, usually they were the ones with no time to waste. "Right," Satan said. "Okay, so you know the whole'get out of Hell on a bet' sort of thing?" I nodded. "Right, classic fiddle contest or game-playing. The latter's usually Death's domain but he doesn't mind sharing." "Okay, so I did that. I figured these games are all rigged, right?" "Absolutely," I said. "If you're the one doing them, that is. Death plays a fair game but he's been around longer than anyone so he's simply better at them than anyone else. You, though, you're the prince of lies. You can cheat." I caught Gabrielle trying not to smirk at this. It wasn't the first time we'd had to remind new Satans that they were evil. "That's the problem," Satan said. "I thought this would already be done. The guy agreed to a driver's test, and I stipulated that it had to happen on the Highway to Hell, because I figure what kind of shape is that highway going to be in? He'll hit a pothole a mile in and we'll be done." I nodded. "I see the problem," I said. Gabrielle made a face that said she didn't, but didn't want to look uninformed in the presence of one of our bosses. That was fine, she'd see in just a second. The elevator doors opened to the blasted volcano fields that surrounded the Highway. They were bleak, full of ash and skeletons, buzzards in the air, the works. The Highway itself, on the other hand...... "The Highway's perfect?" Gabrielle asked, apparently shocked into saying something. I nodded. "Twelve lanes, perfectly graded, optimal traffic patterns. Not a pothole or even an overly-sharp curve. It's how souls get to Hell, Gabrielle, it has to be able to handle a lot of traffic." "What really gets me," Satan said, "is that the asshole who came up with this challenge had to already know that! He saw it on the way in!" "And you want a way to cheat," I said. Satan nodded. "Can I just damn him anyway?" "Actually," I said, "you can. There's a lot of lore about you sticking to deals that you made, but those were all Satans that came before you, their rules don't apply. On the other hand, if you throw that away, neither do their powers. If you want to gain the benefits of those thousands of years, you have to also take on the drawbacks." "So I have to do the typical Satan thing where I obey the letter of the rule. I could build another highway," he was thinking out loud at this point. "That wouldn't be the highway to hell. It'd probably still work, granted, but I don't think it's what you're looking for," I said. "You have an idea," he said. I frowned. Technically, it was against the rules for me to tell the bosses how to do their jobs. Of course, we'd gone against those rules just a few days ago with the "Hell Is Other People, Specifically You: How To Do Your Job As Satan" briefing we'd put together. We got a lot of leeway. "Okay," I said finally. "The highway here, it goes all the way to Dis and into the Seventh Circle, right?" Satan nodded enthusiastically. "And it's one-way, right?" Satan snorted. "I know I'm new but I've got a little sense." "Well that's your answer then, isn't it?" Satan grinned. "I never said which direction they'd be driving, did I?" He started laughing. That's exactly where I'd been trying to lead him. I saw Gabrielle nod appreciatively. Satan wasn't done. "And I never said what kind of car they'd get. I'm thinking a'78 Grenada, no power steering, prone to overheating - it is Hell after all." "Are we done here?" Gabrielle murmured to me. Satan was obviously talking to himself at this point. "And the radio only gets Nickelback!" I nodded. "Yep. I think he'll do fine."
label: human

article: Another day was over. My laptop shut with a snap that echoed through the empty room and I sat in silence, staring out the window of my sixth floor apartment. The hazy yellow street light threw lonely shadows upon the abandoned playground structures I was so familiar with. I shrugged out of my jacket, placed it on the chair, and bent down to unlace my shoes. Tomorrow would be yet another day solitude keeps me company. I would get little done and speak with absolutely no one. This was not how I pictured my life to be while growing up..... As I stood, I noticed a movement in the mirror beside me that didn't match my own. The figure within straightened just before I did. It was subtle, almost undetectable, yet I was almost certain it happened. My reflection blinked when I blinked, leaned forward when I did, and when I raised my hand to run it through the hair in front of my face, so did she. But as I watched her cautiously, one loose strand of hair fell before her eyes and they glimmered anxiously as though hoping I hadn't noticed. A lump rose in my throat and I was frozen in place, unable to look away. My heart pounded ferociously in anticipation. After what felt like an eternity, I shuffled forward and hesitantly reached for the shiny surface, fingertips hovering inches away. My vision blurred with tears and I saw my reflection in the mirror begin to cry as well. I gripped the edge of the mirror in despair. "Please..." I begged, choking as a sob surfaced. "I know you're there. Please..... I'm so alone out here..." The girl within the metal frame shook her head, tears falling freely, and slowly raised her hand from the edge of the mirror as if to touch my face, but she could not reach beyond the surface of the glass. When my fingertips fell upon cool, smooth glass, realization set in; I felt my hope shatter and sank to the ground. I was completely alone.
label: human

article: The children's faces lit up when they finally saw it. The sun danced off its crimson-brown scales, slowly revealing its full frame as it emerged from the darkness. The cave opening was etched into the side of a towering man-made granite wall, which reached all the way to the electrified wire-roof, sealing the pen. A thick layer of enforced glass separated the spectators from the creature. The children in the group pressed their faces up against the glass to try get closer view. Their excitement used to delight Ben, but not anymore. Now he couldn't help but feel for the Attraction. "Her name is Sherin," Ben announced to the spectators. "She's 133 years old." Ben knew Sherin for eleven of her years. However, she had been in the park for more than double that. He remembered the day he was hired as a dragon-keeper. He had no experience, and the education was limited, at best. But even if the education was more thorough, he wouldn't have listened. He was a different person back then: he was just a boy. He was just like these wide-eyed kids who he observed with unfair disdain every day, their sticky candy-coated fingers staining the thick enclosure glass. Just like them, he wasn't aware of this noble creature's realty. It's not their fault. They're only kids - they don't know any better. How could they? He recalled one piece of advice given in training by a senior supervisor: distance yourself. It's the one piece of advice he should've taken seriously. ' Treat this like your regular 9 to 5 '. That's what that bastard said. How could I treat this like a regular job? It's not. These creatures aren't wild turkeys. They're more human than most of my friends for god sake. And they're captives. Plain and simple. They're captives and I'm their gaoler. I try be a friendly and caring gaoler, sure. But my presence exists to control them. " Why isn't it flying mister? " one of the children shouted. " She may be tired, " Ben lied. That answer was always different. I hate lying, but I have to. Not just to save others from the truth, but because deceit in ingrained in this job. I'm not permitted to tell outsiders how she has gradually lost her ability to fly since she's been cooped up in this pen. Not that I would want to explain that. It breaks my heart. And why do I stay? Because she likes me. Don't ask me why. I'm a cog in this damn machine. But I sense her relief when I'm around, and I like being around her. If I leave, who knows who will be put in charge. I no longer trust people, not after what I've seen here. Ben walked closer to the enclosure. He took out rag cloth and glass cleaner and scrubbed the candy residue from the glass. The children were now talking amongst themselves, losing interest in the dragon who was lying still with her face almost covered by her wing. " OK, kids, " Ben said, trying to sound enthusiastic. " It's time to see Barone. The male dragon. " " Is it even bigger? " asked one of the shortest children of the bunch. " A lot bigger, " Ben replied. " And does this one like to fly? " Ben swallowed deeply. " Not today. "

article: " Should we give up? " My brother's usually brash voice felt distant, broken. I stood hunched over the metallic control board, my fingers twitching from button to button, somehow causing the static on the screen to amplify. The screen displayed a shuddering image of NASA's logo, which failed to do more than dance back and forth across the screen. I was beginning to think my brother had a point. " Geoff...We can't, " I mumbled as my right hand shot up towards a green button in the middle of the board, pressing on it gently. No change. " Sooner you're gon na find the self-destruct switch. " I heard clanking as my brother stood up, his heavy boots hitting loudly against the metal floor as he crossed over to where I stood. He set his hand gently on my shoulder and breathed heavily. " Look, sis, you haven't moved in an hour. It's broken. " He reached down with his free hand and picked up one of the buttons- one of many that I'd found to be dislodged while trying to get the machine to work. I stepped away and stretched wearily, feeling my back crack as I did. Straightening up did actually hurt, and I wasn't sure if I'd taken a full breath the entire time I'd set my mind to the control board. Maybe it was time for a break. From the computer at least. I looked around the domed room: our new home, really. We'd been here for just over a week now, and we scarcely left the room. There wasn't much that felt safe here, but this was where we awoke, so this was where we claimed. It was maybe fifty feet in diameter, and the roof was well more than twice my height at the tallest point. The space itself was split off into several sections, separated by crisp curtains, something like you would see in a hospital. There was a space dedicated to bunks, a storage space, two labs, both appearing to specialize in different research, a kitchen area, a bathroom, a door which led outside, and two entrances to passageways that we had not dared to venture to. The center of all of it was the control board, a monster of a computer which must have been capable of anything when it still worked. Oh, and there were windows. Windows which beheld the exterior of our prison. At first we thought we'd been stranded in some strange lab in the middle of the desert. All that we can see outside is sand, though the red coloring probably should have clued us off. The sky was the real giveaway. The Sun is so small here, leaving our days hazy and dim. We have two moons, one of which is so close that we're pretty sure it'll fall onto of us one of these days. And it whips around three times a day. " Maybe we'll get used to Mars. " I tried to insert hopefulness into my voice. " I mean, if NASA ever comes to get us, that'd be nice, but we should try and make the most of it. " " We're not dead... " Geoff ran his hand through his thick, black hair, scratching absently at the back of his neck. " See, positives already! " I gazed out the window, trying to look for something I hadn't seen before in my previous seven days of searching. " We're just crazed amnesiacs living on Mars. " I spun around and glared at him, biting at my lip as I tried to come up with a response. He wasn't exactly wrong... We couldn't remember anything from before. Our days were going just as normal, and suddenly, here we are! I sighed. He reclined against the control board, pressing several buttons on the tower as he did so. I swung to the side just in time to see the display not give any response. As always. He was looking at me expectantly. " So... " I started, looking around our dome, until my eyes locked on one of the two passageways. " We find out why. " He frowned, his blue eyes flashing over to the passageway nearest him. A grin spread across his face as a strange glint entered his eyes. " You know what, Leslie? Be my guest. Why the heck not. I'd much rather get killed by the vacuum of space than by being bored to death in a weird lab-thing. " " You're hilarious. " I strode over to the passageway on the right side of the dome, bordering the bathroom and the storage space. " It's a walkway. Not outside. No vacuum! " I grabbed the circular lock on the door and began to tug. It was a like a ship's wheel, screwed into place tightly on the door. " No telling if it's just as broken as that control tower, you know. " " At this point, I just want to find something out. It's a risk, okay? " He rest his hand on the prong that I was trying to pull down to unlock the door. " Well, let's find out then... " He shoved downward with all his weight, and I did as well. A moment or two passed as the lock stayed firmly in place, and then it gave with a loud click. We unscrewed until the lock came loose, hissing as it slid backward from its frame, revealing a dark tunnel beyond...and breathable air. I took a cautious step forward, my hand reaching out for the guard rail which lined the tunnel from its start to as far as I could see. It was a wide tunnel, probably large enough to fit five people walking side by side, so we entered easily. Slowly, we began our progress down the passage. We were only a few steps in when Geoff froze suddenly, his eyes laser focused on something deep in the tunnel. " Huh? " I prodded him, my voice echoing off the walls. " Shh, " he whispered, still motionless. " Listen. " I closed my eyes and focused, clearing my mind to process the silence. I waited for several long seconds, straining to hear whatever it- and there it was. A gurgling noise, like a gentle stream flowing ceaselessly down a slope. " Is that...water? " Thanks for the prompt! This was a lot of fun to write 3
