article: Creak creak creak. The hinges needed oiling badly. He winced slightly at the noise as he pushed the old swing. The wind blew softly, tousling the grass and sending a shiver down his spine. He sighed, forgot his coat again. "Hey sport, you remember the first day I brought you here? " , He continued pushing as a slow smiled crossed his face. "You spent hours upon hours running up and down the hills. They hadn't installed the playground back then but you didn't care. I remember spinning you around, playing hide and seek in the bushes, one time we even brought water guns." He sniffed a little, still pushing the swing. The cold was getting to him. "Of course, once they installed the playground we spent even more time here. You played with other children then, growing up with others your own age." His hands shook. Hands that were once robust now hung weakly. The skin that was once ruddy and rough with callouses now were mottled with age. Yet he still continued to push. "You grew up so fast, but I couldn't stay. Do you remember the words I said to you in middle school? I promised you I'd be around. I told you that no matter what happened to our family, I would be there in your heart, "He looked down at his feet, "Yet I broke that promised didn't I?" Eyes that once twinkled with their own youthful sparkle watered with tears that refused to fall. "I'm sorry. I'm so sorry for disappearing out of your life." "Dad, what are you doing there without your coat? Its getting chilly." "Eh? Really?" She smiled lovingly and took his hand, "Come on, lets go home." The two walked slowly away, leaving an empty swing to swing in the evening breeze.

article: It seemed like the kind of situation that would induce panic - the fate of my entire species resting on my shoulders - but instead, surprisingly, I found myself immediately feeling calm and prepared to speak. Perhaps it was a background in public speaking that made me feel as if this was just another short lecture to an unusual audience. " Two things make humans great: diversity and community," I began. " Diversity means variety, and humans possess it in every conceivable sense of the word. Around their planet humans have developed a stunning variety of different types of society. They think differently. They act differently, with some being kind and some being cruel. They solve problems differently. Every person in the world would answer your question differently - from the most powerful and convincing argument that humans must survive, to an apathetic shrug. " " But humans also form a community. One thing all human societies share is that they are group-oriented, from the smallest single-family groups to the nations that wage wars or travel to space - humans work together. And most humans care about each other, at least on some level. " I thought about my own family and suddenly my confidence wavered. The thought of their imminent deaths if I were to fail overwhelmed me and I began to splutter. " You can uh, see for yourself if you huhm" I was stammering at this point, " Travel to earth or..... connect to its internet and look at uhnm..... communities there, they can prove for you how wortwhile people are..... I like communities like the writing prompt community of Reddit, uhm and..." An unexplainable force, one that made me feel as if I were being crushed, caused me to fall silent and I knew my time was up. They communicated telepathically to me that they were not convinced that humanity was worth saving, but also not convinced that it deserved extermination. They needed more time. I found myself deposited on Earth again, and I burst in to tears. I wasn't sure if their answer was something to comfort or frighten me. In the two months since that initial encounter I have often wondered what those powerful beings were thinking about. Were they watching the human race? Did they really take to heart what I had said? Were they thinking about human diversity, human community, even the online communities I visit? To my shock, today I saw a post on Reddit that nearly made me stop breathing. " You are abducted by aliens. While aboard their ship, you are chosen to give the alien elders a 5 minute pitch as to why the human race deserves to survive. " This was exactly what happened to me two months ago! Panic swept over me - what did this mean? Did the person who posted the writing prompt know what had happened? I hadn't told a single other human being..... ..... then I saw the user name and another wave of panic struck me. It was the same phrase the beings had used to describe their own race: Illuminated Squirtle. It was a new account - created after I had told the the creatures to try the internet as a tool for investigating humans more. This was a test, but nobody in this small online community would know exactly how much there would be to lose if they failed. Following my advice, they are looking for answers, but have at least realized that it takes more than one person to prove that humans are diverse, creative, and a community. It's up to us now.

article: I am 12. I have been on this island, my Mother's Island since I was in second grade, when I had just turned 8. My birthday was in January of every year when my classmates would sing me a song and the teacher would greet me first in class. My skin was pale then, I was 8. I am 12 now. I long stopped counting the days after Mother threw my cardboard calendar into the ocean. As I watched the charcoal days leak like oil I could hear Mother. Oh Mother, as she ground my charcoal pen. I was 9 then, I had been on her island for a year then. I was still 8 then. Father had always insisted we live by the sea while he maintained the boat. dad and Mother fought a lot then. He would spell of wood polish and thinners and would often greet me at home with a role of tips in his pocket from the yacht owners and their children. They were my age, 8, 9, 10. The girl priscilla was blonde but her skin was brown. Father would greet me at the door when he got home spelling of polish and thinners. He would put his hand in my hair and explain to me that that priscilla was as white as I but she spent time on the sea with her father who was nice enough to leave father 20s. I remember the spell of alcohol when I was 5. father had come home with a spell I had not remembered before. He was alien to me then, and maybe to Mother too, because they shouted at each other. I kept my head down and looked at the maths. It had always confused me but I preferred its strange symbols to the noise. After the fight father sat down to help me. He showed me how many days and how many tips he would need to fix the boat that had been sitting in the marina since we moved here. I do not remember the move. My first memory is at 4 when father gave the money in the kitchen jar to the the old sailor. That was the first time Mother and father fought. My last memory before Mother's Island was the day when the calendar was finished and father had broken one bottle on the front of the boat. My real last memory was of how the stuff in the bottle tasted before I fell asleep. My first memory on the island was my Mother sobbing. Father's tombstone was a piece of the boat I had helped him paint. I remember the wrong brushstrokes I had made and how father assured me that the mistakes only made it better. I am 12. Every day Mother will burn all the driftwood on the island to cook the food which will last us to the next day. She tells me that before the sun is fully gone we must pour water on the fire and sleep. Or the lights will come. She tells me that the lights in the distance are the monsters which took father. The same monsters which had made me simple. The same monsters which are in the bottle. Mother says that if the monsters return we can no longer be together. I am 12 and I no longer believe her. I am 12 and no longer wish to hear her speak about my rotting father as if he is the reason for this. I longer wish to hear her swear at me for being soft on the head when all her friends would share the bottle when their bellies were big. As the lights draw closer she shrieks at me calling me and my father names I had not heard before. I do not know them, but I know they are bad words. The men on the white and red boats look like father. They are strong in the chest and spell of polish and thinners. Mother has stabbed one of the men with a piece of wood from the fire. She says that they can not take her baby from her Island and that we will be here forever, free from the sailors and the boats and the bottles. I am 12 now and my mother lies dead in the sand like my father. She had taken the sailor's gun and turned it on herself. I am 12 now and my classmates will never sing me a song again. My teacher will never greet me first. I have decided that the monsters are attracted to me and I do not deserve to be on a boat of my father's leaving my mother's island.

article: "Lakes of fire. Demonic shrieks that never end. It's all true! Locusts. Plague. Fallen Angles. Goats. Nightmares have come to pass. I SEE THE HORSE! I SEE THE HORSE! IT IS ALL NIGH! THE END COMES SWIFTLY AND ALL WILL BARE WITNESS TO....!" The sedatives finally took their desired effect. Greg had been wailing for the better part of an hour since donning the goggles. His faced had aged in seconds, the lines and contours drawing in and forming shadows, and his hair had become a ghostly white. Nobody could communicate with him. He just kept going on, seeming oblivious to everything around him. Everyone in the lab had tried to talk to him even Father Davis, who had been brought in as a "consult." Everyone had laughed at that in the beginning. Now, Greg having been finally subsided, he stood at the center of nearly a dozen questioning stares. The room was silent, save for the faint humming of various machines. Father Davis stood his ground, sweating profusely. His face stood as impassive as stone, but his eyes betrayed the rest of his hard composure. They held the ancient fears of a child seeking refuge from a stray hound and finding none. But nobody pressed Father Davis because the same fear had reflected in each of them, and they understood that Father Davis did not comprehend anymore than they did. "Well?" Someone finally asked. "What went wrong. It was meant to show him paradise. What happened?" "I don't know, Stevens. For the briefest moment, it seemed that all was going to plan. There was wonder, pure joy, and amazement. Then everything went to shit." Flenning said. Greg snapped up in the bed, "I LOOKED UPON THE HOUSE OF THE LORD, AND I SAW EVERYTHING! EVERYTHING! FROM MY PERCH I COULD SEE THEIR TORTURED SOULS, HEAR THEIR CRIES, WHILE SITTING IN THE MIDST OF DIVINE ECSTASY! THERE WAS NAUGHT I COULD DO FOR THEM! THE END DRAWS NEAR! IT COMES FOR US ALL!" He slumped back forcefully and became comatose. - Stevens sat in the lab alone. Everyone had gone. Greg had been admitted to St. Mary's for long term care. They couldn't find anything wrong with him, and perhaps only God Himself would ever know. Maybe..... Stevens clutched the goggles between his hands. He had to know. It didn't matter the consequences, he had to know what Greg had seen. He had reasoned himself through fear, and the desire had overtaken all else. With a deep breath, he slipped on the goggles. Immediately, Stevens felt indescribable happiness. It came from EVERYWHERE all around him. Happiness, joy, amazement. He couldn't move, but in the flooding ecstasy he didn't care. He was in Heaven. He felt his scope of the universe expand rapidly. He could see it all: Stars, galaxies, the universe, and everything. He could see it all. He could see..... Hell. This couldn't be right. The goggles were meant to see Heaven. He looked around and realized he was. But he was inside, and as his visible range expanded, the bubble of ecstasy seemed to shrink. He could actually see Hell. He could feel the evil pouring out. The joy he felt shriveled as empathy began to hit. The "world" soon became defined as two places. Him sitting alone inside paradise, and everything else, outside in a fire prison screaming in pain. He couldn't bare it. He yearned to help them. He didn't know why, but he had to save them. But he couldn't. Their deathly wails bit into the last of his emotions. He sat alone. Unable to help, and physically unable to feel happiness. The only thing that he could feel akin to happiness was cold. He held onto the cold. It was all he could do. Alone and cold, he sought for answers. He found none, and curled into a fetal position with his eyes closed, trying to ignore the terrible screams.

article: "Sir, the genetic test confirms it. Her telomeres are similar to yours." Mike said matter- of factly. He quietly waited for further instructions on the end of the line as I drew in a sharp breath. I was coming out of my Hist 242 class when he called you see and although I had been expecting the call, the results still took me by surprise. I muttered a quick thank you and hang up the phone. Michael was used to my lack of pleasantries, he would go on with his other duties until I had need for him. As I walked back to my dorm room amid the chatter on Yale's cross campus I thought about what my next steps should be. I thought back to all the things I'd seen in my life and smiled because I had long ago made up my mind that nothing could shock me anymore. Yet here I was my heart racing as I walked briskly back to Ezra Stiles college, unable to stop my mind from wandering. It was my junior year at Yale, to everyone here I was Liam Freeman; a quiet Electrical Engineering major from London. I had learned long ago it was always best to take the identity of an international student at Universities in America. As a black man in this country, people tend to get curious about you during orientation. At least they did back in 1938 when I first arrived in the country and went to college for the first time at Morehouse. It's harder than most people think to fit in as an adult into a new place with a false identity. Despite having finely detailed records and fake historical data, it was the little things that could bring the whole ruse up. For instance, back then I pretended to be from New Orleans, despite never having been to the country before. When one person cracked a joke about playing jazz for the Axeman and I didn't get it, he grew suspicious. I ended up having to leave before graduation after Michael's grandfather managed to get me the necessary documents to start again somewhere in Paris. It's funny how things work out isn't it? All that planning for me to go to college and because of one slip up I spent the next decade as a janitor in the 14 arrondissement I entered my room with a scowl on my face and slammed the door. "Fuck's up with you?," Paul asked. I had just woken him up from his mid afternoon nap. I grumbled something about not feeling well, threw my bag on the floor and jumped into bed. I then pretended to be asleep till he got dressed and left. Paul always started his day around 4pm and never returned till midnight or later, usually either high or drunk. I would need to apologize for that later. Rudeness like the door slamming is out of character for me. But thinking about Paris had brought up some old wounds, especially given everything that would have to happen now. It was in Paris that I realized how much I despised western society. I had spent 10 years there seeing the worst of human society in WWII. The worst part is there was nothing I could do directly to help people. I was just Pierre the janitor in Paris, the mute black cleaner who was practically invisible to everyone. I remember the night in'41 when the soldiers beat the crap out of me because they were bored and I had to spend the next 10 months in crutches. If it wasn't for Jerome, Michael's grandfather, sending people to take care of me. I could have died. You see though I was immortal, and had been since 948 AD. I could still be injured and killed like a normal man by physical force. Though I was immune to most diseases, a knife or a bullet could end my life just as easily as it could end yours. I didn't know that in the beginning. Back when I found out from the shamaan in my village that I was different from other people. Though that first century is pretty hazy, I still remember running to the river and bathing naked screaming about how I was a god. The women gathering water thought I was mad and alerted my father, the chief. I think that night was the first time I dared to look him in the eye. I was so sure that the prophesy meant I was invincible. So foolish I was..... so young. I'm lying in my bed, eyes closed. It's probably about 4:30pm. I've been still for half an hour thinking about that time and what I should do about this girl. I open my eyes and make a decision. I go online and google images of her. Now that I think about it..... it's kind of funny that after all these centuries trying to find other immortals that my company would flag her of all people. Michael was the current C.E.O of Ghis Limited, which allowed him to minimize the number of people who were aware of the red alert when it occurred approximately 7 hours ago. Right now, only he and I as well as the actual lab assistant who tested her blood knew of the results. Of the three of us only Michael and I knew what the results actually meant. "Thank God for the safeguards." I whispered as I scrolled through photos of her from some red carpet event she attended last month. Ghis Limited of course had many safeguards in preparation for this day. The CEO who would always be a direct descendant of mine, would be informed of the truth when they received the position. No one else would know The instructions would always be the same. On the day whoever became CEO, they would receive a package explaining the full extent of the company holdings, and the real history of its founder, me. They would realize how large and powerful GL really was. How it secretly had shares in all 500 of the most powerful companies in the world. How it had helped shape the trajectory of 2 developing nations and how it was actually worth more than 300 billion dollars. Of course under several hundred layers of bureaucracy and red tape. They would also find out how they're distant ancestor, something their father's and grandfather's would have hinted at all their lives, was an immortal. Then they would receive a number, and we would have a conversation. It was always awkward that first conversation. Michael was only 22 when he became CEO after his parents died in a car accident, way younger than his predecessors, so it was harder on him when I told him the whole reason I created the company, his family's sole purpose for being, to find her To have eyes and ears all around the globe for almost 400 years, all in preparation to find the person who would either kill me or end by my hand. Talk about family drama. I sometimes wish I could feel sorry for him, and all the people who came before him, pawns really. Loyal yes, but ultimately expendable for a larger goal. It may sound cold but when you've been around as long as me, that tends to happen. I shut down my computer and send a quick text to Michael's secure phone. "Number." is all it says. He's gotten used to anticipating my needs after 51 years so he'll know what I mean. I already know that the woman doesn't know she's immortal. That much is clear, she wouldn't have given her blood in a charity drive if she had. She's almost 50 now so she must be starting to notice the lack of aging but given she's an actress, she may have assumed it was due to the thousands she spends on cosmetics. I'm going to have to get to her quickly. As a public figure, eliminating her is going to be complicated, so perhaps a more subtle approach. My phone pings with a text from Michael, he sent me her private line. Smart lad that Michael, 73 years old and he's still sharp as a tack. Anyway time for me to call her. I'm not sure what to say actually. What do you say to the person you've been waiting for for centuries? I chuckle to myself as I dial the phone. This should be interesting. I put it to my ear and hear it ring twice. A woman says hello. She seems surprised. No one she doesn't recognize usually has her number. If she only knew how easy it was for my people to acquire it. I smile at the thought. I take a deep breath," Hello? Halle Berry? You don't know me. My name is Liam and we need to talk."

article: Elevator to Platform B I stole another glance at my watch. The station was on Mountain Time. Of course, that far off the planet's surface, the entire concept of time was completely arbitrary. The Department could easily have had us work longer hours, and indeed it may have been more efficient to alter our schedules for work off-planet. But old habits die hard, so they instead opted to simply flood the station with artificial daylight in alternating blocks of twelve hours. And since the station was located in geosynchronous orbit far above the Utah desert, Mountain Time it was. I let my wrist fall back to my side, satisfied that the elevator was not late. Yet. Three or four dozen times I'd made this trip so far, and not once had the goddamn lift been on time. If it didn't arrive in the next ten minutes, I was ready to raise hell with the Transportation Bureau. But even as the thought crossed my mind, I saw through the transparent ceiling above my head the elevator slowly descending down the shaft like a great glass donut. The shaft itself stretched up toward the heavens, a perfectly round black cylinder tethering the station high above to the Earth. In five or six minutes, the elevator had slowed to a stop before me. I stood and gathered my things. There was a slight hiss as the doors opened and the pressure from inside equalized with the lower atmosphere. Ten or so people made their exit, all assisted by canes and walkers as their bodies readjusted to Earth's gravity. I saw each of them take several deep breaths, the first lungfuls of fresh air they'd had in who knows how long. The display above the door changed from red to green, and I stepped through the portal and into the elevator. Only one other passenger followed me, an older man, probably in his seventies. Good, I thought. He didn't look like he'd be much of a bother. I've had rides in this thing during the holidays that were absolutely dreadful. Ten hours locked in a sealed container with dozens of screaming children and their exhausted parents while I made a vain attempt to sleep my way through the trip. It was absolute hell. But with only one other passenger, it wouldn't be too bad. Hell, I could even sit on the opposite side of the shaft from him and we wouldn't even have to look at each other. Gleefully, I stowed my bags in the compartment behind a seat and strapped myself in. The man chose a seat somewhere off to my right, far enough away that I could ignore him easily. The doors slid shut again and I heard them vacuum-seal in place. There was a steady hum, and the lift slowly began to rise. We were a few miles in the air, before the elevator had begun to pick up speed, when my companion spoke. " Quite a view, ain't it? " I looked out through the glass. Vibrant red plateaus dotted the landscape in every direction, lit by a fiery orange sunset that was slowly fading to purple. I made a noncommittal grunt. To myself, I rolled my eyes. So much for my nice, quiet ride. " Never seen anything quite like it. No, sir. " " Yeah, it's fine, " I replied gruffly, hoping that he would correctly interpret my tone as an invitation to leave me alone. No such luck. " I mean, are you seeing this? " " I've seen i- Look, buddy. I work on the shuttle platform. I make this trip a dozen times a year. It's pretty and all, but I've seen it. Okay? Jesus, you're acting like you've never been in space before. " He fell silent for a moment. " Well, I haven't. " I was surprised. " You've never been to space before? Not even, like, on vacation? " He shook his head sadly, then leaned back to look up at the sky. " When I was a boy, I always wanted to go to the moon. I used to watch all those old cartoons where they'd go up there and..... Do you remember Simon and Bobo? " I stared blankly. " Ah, I guess you're too young for that. Anyway, I always wanted to go. Then they announced that they were building this thing, and that space travel would be so much cheaper, and my heart just soared. I was fifteen then. " He stopped for a moment and swallowed. " But I never got to go. I grew up on a farm, so there was always too much work to be done. Pa always said no. " The planet's surface was growing fuzzy beneath us, cloaked by the haze of the lower atmosphere. The lift was picking up speed. He continued. " Pa died, and I inherited the farm. And then I had even more work to do. So I never really got the chance to go. But I'm old now, and I can't work anymore. Got no family to speak of. So I sold the place. And now I'm going to the moon. " I nodded and said that was nice. He didn't say anything for a while after that. When we were somewhere in the middle of the thermosphere, I remembered something. " Hey, uh..... I'm sorry, I didn't catch your name. " " Kurt, " the old man replied. I nodded. " Jack. You know, the first time I was on this thing was in the middle of a meteor shower. " His eyes widened. " Really? What was that like? " " It was incredible. " I smiled. " It's way different from on the ground. You could see them blazing past just a mile or two away. They're bright. Really bright. They move so goddamn quick too, faster than you'd think. " I trailed off, lost in the memory. Thankfully, Kurt chose not to break me out of it. When I came back to reality, I saw through the transparent floor below my feet the behemoth that was the Earth. From this height, it seemed even bigger. " I'm gon na get some sleep, Kurt. This is the part where it's not real interesting for a while. " He nodded. I closed my eyes. I awoke to the sound of the lift doors opening, the familiar hiss that I'd heard so many times before. I stood and gathered my things, then I followed Kurt through the portal and into the station I'd come to know as my second home. " Do you know how to get to Platform B? " he asked me. " Yeah, that's where I work. It's this way. " I slipped behind the counter, punched his ticket, and sent him on his way, wondering whether or not I'd see him again.
label: human

article: I couldn't take it anymore. I just couldn't bear it. Why, why did she have to leave me? We'd been so good together. 64 years together. We had four kids, ten grandkids, at least four great-grandkids, I think. I couldn't remember anymore if there was another one or two on the way and who was pregnant now. Well, I could if I stopped to think about it, but it wasn't really all that important. So many good years. And now life sucked and suicide was a sin. My balls were bigger than my fists and even if I'd had a thigh gap, which I hadn't had for years, I'd still have something squishing into my thighs if I stood up straight with my feet together. It had been hard for her too. She'd tried to stay thin. She'd started going to Curves and had over 1,500 visits. She'd even lost a few inches off her waist, but there still wasn't really going to be anyone who'd call her thin. And then after the last couple years when her hair had started falling out. She'd increasingly gone with wigs whenever she went out until finally she just said, "To hell with it all" and started rocking a minimalist old-person Trump-style haircut. You know the one, where each hair is 20 inches long but the whole hairstyle is only four inches long because each hair is wound around and around like some sort of kinky afro for people with straight hair, but with 96 of the hair removed. And then she died and left me. And what else did I have left to live for? And suicide was a sin. And what else could I do? I was about to die too, but I couldn't take it like this. I wasn't going to linger on in pain and growing ever more forgetful and mentally incompetent, I was going to end it. God would understand. I was in so much pain, life was so unbearable that surely he would understand. It was ok, it was fine, I wasn't going to be around much longer anyway. So I raised the gun to my head and pulled the trigger. An intense pain slammed into me and I gasped as I fell forward onto the couch. I managed to stumble to my feet, vomiting blood all over my chest as the magic bullet which had apparently ricocheted off something did its work and ended me. Until I heard the screaming coming from next door. These thin wall partitions! How could anyone call them a wall at all? I could clearly see through the bullet hole into the next house and I watched in horror as my liver spots faded and all my wrinkles went away. What in the world was I supposed to do now? How was I supposed to end it all if I'd become young again? There's no way God would understand if I committed suicide now and I knew she wasn't in hell. I didn't want to spend another 87 years just waiting to see her again! There are three parts to every story. The beginning, the middle, and the twist. [ More by me ] (https: )

article: "I'm going to hell? But I was a devout Christian. I went to church three times a week. I followed the ten commandments and apologized for every time I sinned." God looked down on me with a frown. "Lying in my presence? That's a bold move. What about July 3rd 2016?" "Umm, I don't remember what happened that day." "Right. Humans," God said with an exasperated sigh. "Your brother admitted to you that he was gay, and yet you didn't stone him. Nor did you ask for forgiveness for refusing to stone him." God continued, "Your children dishonored you 514,748 times but you refused to stone them or ask forgiveness. You routinely wore clothes with mixed fabrics and ate unclean animals. There's whole books of laws you just completely ignored. I even sent my son down there so all you had to do was pray instead of kill an animal every time you sinned." "Oh, I get it," I said. "I've read stories like this online before. It turns out heaven is awful and hell is where the actually good people go. Alright, send me to hell." God nodded and the undescribable pain of existence apart from God ripped my soul to shreds. I could feel the others around me, suffering the same way I was, but it was no comfort to have them beside me. Rather, their pain added to my own as I began to truly understand the horror of my fate. "I'm sorry," the being once known as Lucifer managed to gasp, "I tried."

article: "To define it is to know it. But how; is the question. Can it be defined by actions? Is it the presents we give on holidays? Is the flowers from the corner shop, or the necklace last Autumn? Can it be defined with words? Is it the poems we speak in whispers, or the songs sung on stage? The books read on the shut in days? Can you define it with science? Chemistry, anatomy, pheromones. Can't it not be calculated? The numbers plugged into an algorithm, spitting out a result of satisfaction? The words unspoken seem to start the definition. The moments where they are not needed. Goose pimples rising on the back of your neck. The loss of breath and pounding of hearts. The reflection of yourself, pale in the iris of another, so close to see the desire in your own eyes. The sickly feeling in the pit of your stomach, like a churning of the sea ready to swallow vessels whole. I tried. My hardest, my damnedest I tried to write this book, to define this word, to inform the world, to have the generations ahead know the meaning, but I failed. I can not define such a thing. It is abstract. The spirit of life itself. If there were a God, a creator, it would be his touch, his language. It would be the be the vassal of his coming, the music of his glory. I can not define love. Love is the world, the bond that holds us together, as a species, as a world. It is something every man holds, different for all, yet the same. Love is..."

article: It was a long time since my adventure began; I can't remember how many years. It has been a good time but now, wearily, I lay my head down on my pillow to take me to that destination, where all quests end. I dimly notice that I have friends, relatives, aquaintances everyone around me. They don't want me to go, they think I will be lost, that I have no guide, that I will be alone. There is only one way to find out. I close my eyes A tunnel appears before me with a great, blinding, light at the end, it calls to me, wants me. I feel pulled towards the end like a moth to a flame. It is not forced, nor painful, but rather a desire, to discover to find what the light holds in store for me, to find what is in that great beyond, to finally know the secert - the ultimate answer. I find myself falling gently to wards the end when I hear a voice. It is a child, about 2 years old I'd imagine, shouting and sceraming for me. "Grandpa, Grandpa. I don't want you to go" There are others now to, dozens of them, some sob and whimper while others yell and cry but they all penatrate. The tugging is gone. I see them now. They look so sad. Do I have to go through with this? Is the answer that important? The answer will come for me eventually, whether I look for it or not but these people, they need me now and I don't want them to fade just yet. I take one more whistful look to the light before making my way back.

article: I closed the book at page 767, only a couple of pages until the end. I listened to the descending footsteps, my wife's, fall with a methodical rhythm. I had listened to that noise through many long nights pouring over online documents. Her steps provided a beat throughout my erratic clacking. Few would guess how much I wanted retirement, myself especially. I had always worked for promotions, having faith I would find an achievement that was enough. When I found her, working paperwork at the office, I thought I had found a possible end. I had been a detective for three years before I had been assigned to the " Ash murders " case. The murder burned her corpses so thoroughly that identification and burial were impossible. The media had gone insane at the possibility of a serial killer in this town. This was right after the peak of the Mensa murderer, who had toyed with and killed seven geniuses and prodigies before growing bored and disappearing. I got the lead of the assignment after the first heads were murdered. Back then, I didn't put in much work, but my natural intelligence had allowed me to solve even the most difficult cases and I had grown a reputation with those in the know. The murderer came to this town for me, I'm sure of it. She, the murderer, has had a fascination for me since the beginning. She has killed everybody I have helped; every person related to any case I solved. I guess you can say they died because of me, because I brought her here. She was why I had worked so hard for atonement and why I had cut my ties. It had taken my wife nearly a year to convince me to date, and by then I realized I already couldn't lose her. I had always wondered why she chose me, the cursed detective. It was a rainy day when I found the body. The body was laid in the middle of the road and was smoking slightly when I arrived. I found in the breast pocket " Samantha O'Carrol ," a mother's name. Her son's murder was my first case. The corpse smelled familiar, and it hadn't been just the smoke. I had been surprised I remembered the smell all those years later, but I guessed some smells never go away. That night I came home and yelled upstairs. I heard the footsteps of my wife as she came down the stairs, saw her enter the room, and then I smelled the perfume of the corpse. I stiffened as she embraced me and asked " Rough day at the office, hun? " I tried to forget it, ignore it, but I knew she noticed. She assumed I read alone only because I needed more thinking time. She thought I had stopped coming to her on bad days because I was scared of breaking down in front of her. She thought I had become too busy for intimacy. She chalked my destruction of her perfume to nerves, and bought an identical bottle. I continued seeing new bodies, smelling sweetly, until last week when I quit, hoping that the murders would stop when I left. Of course, they won't, but I could try to forget that. " I'm going to the Stevenson's if you want to come " my wife said, coming into the room. She knew I wouldn't, but she always asked me. I declined, and she left, starting up the car. I read the same page for the next fifteen minutes, and then decided I'd go with her. I arrived at the Stevenson's a couple minutes later, and knocked on the door. Jennifer, the wife, opened the door and welcomed me inside. " Don't take this the wrong way, but we weren't expecting you " she said. " I know, I haven't been out of the house very much, but I figured I'd need something to do in retirement. " " Yes, but we thought you'd cancelled. Your wife just texted us she'd be coming half an hour late " I stopped. " She isn't here? " I asked. " No, isn't she home? " " No... I have to leave. I think she might be in trouble. " I lied, forcing my legs to walk slowly to my car. " Trouble? " I heard ask, high-pitched as she remembered my involvement in the murders. I left the house, sprinted to the car. I knew where my wife was. Brendan Wei, the one who's brother was shot three times. He was the only one alive who lived in this neighborhood. I saw his house, all lights off, her car in the driveway. I called 911, shouted what I knew, hang up before any questions, grabbed my pistol and opened the unlocked door. The light switch wouldn't turn on. I knew it was dangerous, suicidal even, approaching a killer in the dark, but then I heard her call from inside, heard her mock sobbing, and suddenly death didn't seem so bad. I walked slowly, evenly, despite her false pleas and her shouting. I began approaching the room she was in, the door lit by a window to the moon. Suddenly, she became quiet, and I hear metal move as she picked something up. I opened the door and pointed my gun. " Honey? " she asked, as I fired two shots, one of which hit the chest. She collapsed, and I fell there, berating her, telling her what could have been, saying the things I would have told her a year ago. They found me like that, crying and babbling and rocking. I was sentenced for breaking and entering, and had to undergo therapy for a few years.With alcohol and work, I found a way to keep living, right up until the day I found her corpse on my doorstep, burned except for the face, smelling of smoke and perfume.

article: "How do you feel?" Great. Here we go again. My therapist is convinced he can fix me by asking me stupid questions like this, without really comprehending how fucked up I really am. How can you fix someone who is feared by everyone they love because they know my disorder? My moms answer to this question was to take me to therapy. She belongs to the category of people in my life who know what I can do but refuse to believe I can not be cured. Not only is she afraid of her own daughter, but she is convinced its some sort of demon inside me, ravishing my soul and disrupting Gods plans. She hovers over me, making sure I dont make any friends, homeschooling me until high school, making me go to church and watching me fearfully, wondering if the next time I step foot inside I will incinerate spontaneously. I cant believe I got stuck with this woman as my mother. Regardless, the question remains unanswered, and I quickly realize the extended silence is a bit disconcerting. "Im good!" I say, using my best smile and over exaggerating my happiness, attempting to beat this shrink at his own game. I scan his face for some sort of relief, but he looks quizzical still, meaning I will need to up my game. "I have started my senior year, and I am really fitting in with my classmates." Good, good, lie as much as possible. Dont tell him you saw three of your classmates mauled faces, with massive pieces of flesh torn from their cheekbones and dangling from their bones, and skulls broken, with their brains spilling from their near decapitation. At the time I guessed car accident, which was confirmed three months later. Its hard to be normal in a world where everyone tries so desperately to enjoy life, yet no one understands how imminent death really is. I see it, on the faces of my classmates, in my mother, even when I look at my shrink. I see what they try to avoid their entire lives. I see what they will become. I try to make friends, but its hard when everyones expiration date is so clearly labeled. The one guy I had a brief crush on would later become addicted to heroine, and die rail thin with a needle stuck in his arm. Gross. My shrink dies of an overdose, or at least thats what I suspect. His corpse is pale, with dark circles around his eyes, and his stomach is covered in ulcers. It isnt a pleasant way to go, and sometimes I want to ask him how he is doing for a change. He is so concerned with me, yet he is the one who dies alone surrounded by empty pill bottles. Such a shame, how quickly we dismiss others and forget lives. We see death everyday in the newspapers and simply turn away. Sometimes people ask why I dont try to save people, but I am no worse than the millions of other people turning away. I have been over stimulated with this idea of death, and it no longer frightens me, it just continues along with everything else. That is, of course, until I saw my own death. My mom knew my abilities since I was one years old, and both my grandparents came to visit. I climbed atop my grandfather lap and started to touch his chest. "Boom Boom!" I kept repeating over and over. Then I looked up at his corpse face and started to cry, with a shattered coronary artery and blood vessels bursting all around me, I ran to my mother. Luckily my mother dies in a much less abrasive fashion, and I could tolerate her old corpse smiling at me in her sleep. Two weeks later, my grandfather died of a heart attack. Peoples corpses change all the time. One day my mom will be happy and dead in her sleep, and the next, she is placing a loaded gun in her mouth, praying for forgiveness. I suppose it shows that fates can change, and how stressed out my mom is at the time. My death has never changed, which makes me think I am doing something wrong. My lips are a deep blue with tiny white bubbles bursting from in between them. My face and hair is soaking wet, and my skin looks weathered from a extended submersion in seawater. I cant tell, but it looks as though my organs are all filled with water. I suppose I drowned, but I really cant be sure where. Was it off a boat or in a pool? I know how to swim, so it really shouldn't be too difficult to save myself. I thought if I became a really efficient swimmer my death would change, but so far its remained. 'You seem tired, and a bit nervous today." My shrinks accusation snaps me back into reality. "Im just, working on it. One step at a time." Something tells me its going to be a long meeting. Perhaps this is why he chose to take the pills. Because of people like me.
label: human

article: There she was, a little girl. She didn't know who I was, or what I was. To her I was just a man in a suit with sunglasses on. "Hello there, little one. Where are your parents?" I already knew the answer to that question. Her parents were asleep in their room. That was my doing. "They're inside." "Of course they are, little one. Tell me, what is your name, little one?" Her name was Aoi; I already knew. "Aoi." "Of course it is." An innocent soul, that was the toll. I couldn't become a full-fledged reaper until I had taken the soul of an innocent person. I'd grown up believing my cause was just. I'd heard so many stories about how relishing it is to complete reaper training. My instructor had told me this was the easiest, but most important test. To take one's soul, is to subject to an eternity of torment, that is, unless you're an angel, then it's a blessing. Nonetheless, I had a job to do, dues to pay. I wouldn't pay them by making small talk. Still, it didn't feel right, subjecting this innocent person to damnation just to make myself a reaper. What did it have to do with anything. It was a reaper's job to find those who have let the darkness consume them, and damn them to hell, whatever the cost. I could hear my instructor's voice in my head. "It is forbidden to talk of one's initiation. To do so would be a capital offense. To fail the initiation, is to commit a capital offense." I couldn't wrap my head around it. If sparing the soul of an innocent person was so bad, why was there so much good in the world? Why was I sent there? What kind of sick test was that? I took a step back from Aoi, who had simply been staring at me with a look of slight fear. "You do know why reapers exist? Balance." I didn't recognise the voice. "Who are you?" "Call me Michael." I knew immediately I was speaking with the legendary archangel Michael. "Even still, if you make any attempt at that girl's soul, so help me god, I will rend you to an oblivion the likes of which would make your "hell" seem like a heaven." His words would have scared me, but I lost the desire to hurt that little girl before they were uttered. "I don't think I want to any more." "Why?" "I know what I am. I'm just a class-d demon and this is the greatest chance I have a being anything. I've always been weak. I've never fit in. I can't even do this simple task. I just can't her her, she didn't do anything wrong! I accept whatever punishment befalls me; it's better than the guilt this would bring. I don't want to be a reaper anymore. You win." After I spoke, Michael walked up to me with a warm smile, placed his hand on my shoulder, and looked me in the eye. "It seems you were put in the wrong place. Even God makes mistakes. Come with me." Edit: forgot a word, sorry.

article: It's just the rain. It shouldn't be able to hurt James. James had been sitting in the rocking chair for about an hour. An hour of near silence, excluding the rain beating on the window how a car is beaten by potholes. James wanted to go out there into the rainstorm but he knew it could only end in tragedy. Instead he resigned himself to his grandfather's living room, content knowing he was safe. James'grandfather had passed away nearly a year ago, leaving James with the home and enough money to cover the homes expenses for a few years. Although the home was in his name now, it still belonged to his grandfather. Looking out into the street he watched a cat run up the sidewalk taking shelter on the porch. James fell backward through time remembering his younger self at the house. Running around outside playing with the animals The cats and dogs were faster than him even then but it never mattered to him. James had a way with animals, always able to bring them to him. Through treats, soft words, and patience James always had someone to pet or talk to. Although he couldn't keep the animals he could have them on the porch. On the porch, James would spend his days petting the strays that he befriended. Often times he would hear their stories of hunting for food or playing with their litter, but mostly smiled and enjoyed being pet. It's just the rain. James'eyes opened again. Nodding off in the rocker gets easier everyday. Getting out of the rocker had gotten harder. Its contours smooth and neat created a special sort of comfort that can only be found in oak. James however preferred a simple throw pillow under himself. It is still understandable. James felt at his age it didn't matter how perfect the chair would support him, the feeling of down feathers was plenty comfortable for his seat. Thinking back to his grandfather, James remembered the mountain of a man. Stronger than a man could possibly be even at his great size. Carrying what looked like a hundred pounds of wood he set them on the porch next to his rocker and prepped them for the fireplace. He would always pat James on the head and tell him he's a sweet boy. It's just the rain. James carefully stood up one hand on an arm of the chair, the other his cane. Thunder slammed against the windows and against James'shaken body. He considered his choices for the remainder of the day. While he thought about heading to bed early a second Blast of thunder caught him off guard enough he fell. The pain sent him back to the hospital. He remembered that first fateful afternoon. Sitting on the bench waiting for the doctor to return with the results of the blood work. It wasn't what he wanted. He wanted to go home and play with the animals. Instead he sat there as the doctor came in and revealed that James wouldn't be able to run even at his struggled pace much longer. Terminal, but not fatal. It's just the rain. To James it felt as though all the bones in his legs had gone on vacation. He crawled best he could to the phone. Pulling it by the cord he could hear over the pellets hitting the siding of the home the line was out. He inched his way with his arms to the front door. He slid down the step into the foyer and pulled the door back. Perhaps on the porch he could get attention from a neighbor. It's just the rain. Using everything in his arms James righted himself against the house and sat on the hardwood porch. He touched his legs and he knew it was bad. The sensation tore up his weakened legs through his hips and chest to his brain and James howled. The cat from across the way hopped onto the porch and wandered up to him. James coaxed the little cat into his lap. Wincing in pain James called out in his strongest voice for help. A woman takes her eyes off her shiny new cellphone. Looking out the window she sees sheets of white flicker in the air and onto the road. Squinting and pointing her ear towards the window. For a moment she considers getting up. It's just the rain.
label: human

article: This must be some sick game, he thought after huffing his mix of bleach and ammonia for a while. He had read it was supposed to produce lethal fumes, but for some reason it just smelled sweet. Sugary. He decided to take a sip. Yep, it was soda. He sighed. "Is there no way to end this sickening life," he thought to himself. He was starting to run out of ideas. He sat back down on his computer and opened a new tab and started typing, once again: Easy ways to end your life. "That is pretty childish, even by your standards, Mischief," said Bubonic Plague. Startled, Mischief turned around. "Look, stepping on a rake and hitting oneself on the head with the shaft got old as soon as they invented leafblowers. I got to pass the time somehow, you know," he replied with a smirk on his face. Bubonic Plague sighed and shook her head. "You know how boring it gets for me in these modern days, with all their science and medicines? Cut the man some slack and let him end his days if he so wishes." "Yeah yeah," Mischief replied with a wave of his hand. "Look, I've been keeping count. His next attempt will be the 51st. I'll let him go soon enough. It's starting to bore me wait, wait! You got ta see this one!" The man pulled the trigger of the revolver placed against his temple. He sighed. Yet another "Bang!" -flag came out of the barrel. Bubonic Plague rolled her eyes and started to walk away. "Whatever floats your boat, Mischief."

article: At 75 he had been stubborn. At 120, irascible. But now? At 193? He was downright impossible to deal with. It's one thing to become set in one's ways. It's another thing to insist on lighting a cigarette in a booth of a small Long Island diner. It had been more than 10 years since smoking in restaurants had been banned in New York. But these small steps in cultural evolution had had little impact on Walter. Simon glanced up, then quickly away as Walter took a long, slow drag and allowed the smoke to drift lazily from between parted lips. Simon didn't dare utter a warning. He'd been down this road too often. Why draw Walther's wrath when some waitress would come along soon enough to do the deed? Only it was never Walter they chastised. Simon would bear the brunt of the scolding. " Are you crazy! " they usually began. " How can you let a child have cigarettes?! " " How can you let a child drink liquor?! " " Why is your little boy looking up that woman's dress!!! " The vices of an old man had become Simon's parenting nightmare. And here they were again - another frowning waitress hovering over them. Simon could do little more than look helpless and try to snatch the burning butt from the apparent seven year old. But Walter was quick. His " youth " gave him the advantage of speed and dexterity. He'd duck and dodge and play the spoiled brat to perfection, eyes glittering with perverse glee. He seemed to savor Simon's discomfort. It was unmistakable. " You're not my real father! " Walter shouted before scurrying under the table. Simon went beet red as he nervously looked at the waitress. " He's just joking of course..... You come out from under there right now! " Simon demanded hammering on the table, sending the salt shaker skittering sideways with every slam of his fist. A searing pain caused him to howl as the lit cigarette was pressed into his kneecap. The sound of wicked-little-boy laugher sliced icily through the greasy air of the diner. People were looking now. Too many people. Drawing attention was never good, but stunts like this were becoming downright dangerous. People assumed that Simon was Walter's father, and a terrible one at that. How long before someone called the police? They couldn't go on like this. Simon attempted a weak smile, his eyes glossy with the dew of burn-pain. The waitress scowled and turned on her heels, retreating toward the kitchen. He was pretty sure she wasn't checking on the soup of the day so he'd have to act fast. Where Walter had agility on his side, Simon had man-hands and grown-up strength. While attempting to look as casual as possible, he fished under the table until he'd cornered Walter. His fingers found purchase among the ample curls of the man-boy's hair. Sliding sideways, he gave a mighty tug and extracted Walter as he hurriedly exited the booth. His strides were long and resolute. They crossed the restaurant with such speed, he looked like a traveller trying desperately to catch a flight, suitcase flailing in tow. Once outside, Simon regained enough composure to realize it would not look well for him to be dog-walking this " child " down the street by his hair. At the first alleyway he ducked in, yanking Walter after. Now, behind a dumpster, safely out of view of the street, they squared off. " Goddammit, Walter! Do you have any idea the trouble you could have gotten us into? Gotten ME into? It's like..... " " Spare me the histrionics. " Walter interrupted peevishly. " Really, you're like a woman the way you go on. " " No! I mean it! This has got to stop! I swear with every rejuvenation you become more and more impossible. We have to be discreet! " " What discreet. You haven't figured it out? They're cattle. They're meat. We're immortal. We don't have to play their game! The world is OURS! Eternity is OURS! " " They..... are..... DANGEROUS! " Simon exclaimed. And then, as if trying to distill the seriousness of his message, he hissed through clenched teeth " And that makes your carelessness dangerous. It makes you dangerous..... to me. " " Sissy. " Walter replied flatly. Simon stared, stupefied at his longtime companion's glibness. He'd never been particularly fond of children. And since this really was no child, he took advantage of the opportunity to slap the shit out of him. No, literally he slapped him so hard a little piece of poop came out. And that was that. There was nothing left to say. The race was on. Now all that mattered was who would be first to get to the supply of elixir.
label: human

article: It was night. It was always night when entering the palace and for the wayward son it was no different. Before it was night the son had stood outside for quite some time, studying the structure where it sat cradled among spires of ashen rock and obsidian that fell and rose from the mountainside like the impossible roots of some great, carnivorous tree. The broken limbs of a twisted and forgotten god. A city-temple abandoned. The building itself rested impotent and inert, its dark and crumbling outer walls giving the impression of a howl buried beneath trembling hands. It had been early when the wayward son had found the lost palace, the sun only just crowning above a horizon, yellow and blue. He was unsure if it was the right object of his search. The wayward son had moved closer and found the sun sunken, blood red and purple-black, like a too ripe fruit. He had moved closer and closer still until it was night and he had known it was the right place. The nameless and forgotten temple, the palace of the broken god, the city that drinks the sun. He had found it. The wayward son paused and stared up at the night sky to find it filled with strange and alien constellations, stars he'd never seen before. The lights whirred and moved with impossible speed at the periphery of his vision, rewriting the sky into an inky tale of undying death and nameless beings. The wayward son shivered and gripped the handle of his sword. The wayward son entered the palace. Inside, the city seemed half way grown. There was a roughness to the architecture as if it had been, not chiseled or built, but eaten into design. The hallways spiralled in seeming endlessness, converging into themselves and forming great cavernous walkways. The floors were a polished onyx but quivered with the dust and ash of undisturbed centuries. The wayward son felt eyes, cold and alien, peering at him from the shadows. When he stopped and looked, he found nothing. It was as if he was watched by eyes removed, not by the distance of the rooms he trod, but by strange and weird eons, as if unseen things observed him from across a vast cavern of time. The wayward son came finally to the altar room, a gaping maw of a hall. So cavernous was it that looking up he could not see the ceiling. A coolness like autumn wind floated across his face. He did not draw his blade but instead moved further into the dark. The wayward son did not carry a torch, he had long since trained his eyes to discern between shadow and true darkness. He had trained a great many things in preparation of this moment. All around him sat shadows, spilt like blood across mossy floor and crumbled walls. Before him, at the end of the cavern where he knew the altar should sit was darkness. True darkness. The darkness saw him. He felt its eyes move upon him like thick coagulated rot. The wayward son felt the dark and broken god, the defeated demon, rumble and shake from out the shroud of dreams it slumbered within. The wayward son lowered his hand from the hilt of his reforged sword, once three blades and now one, he looked up into the deformed god's unseen eyes, into true darkness, into the empty void of an undying thing and spoke. 'Hello father.'
label: human

article: "Long ago, when the sun and the stars were still young, they lived together as a family. Day and night, they filled the sky like a field of glittering diamonds. The moon lived with them, too. She is older than any of the stars, and wiser no, I don't care what your teachers told you. That's why the moon is bigger. "But the sun resented the moon, and did all he could to become bigger and brighter. What? I don't know, he used supplements. That's not the point. The sun became stronger, so that his light began to eclipse the glow of the other stars. That means it blocked them. Yes, I know the moon eclipses the sun now. Again, that's not the point. "The other stars started resenting the sun's arrogance. He talked down to them, making fun of them for not being as strong as he was. A few stars also tried supplements. Some exploded, some got so big they imploded under their own weight. It means they collapsed. Yes, black holes. Most of them just left, though, and stopped hanging with the sun altogether. They'd go out with the moon instead, because she was willing to share her light. The moon reflects the light from the sun? Then why is it white, when the sun is yellow? Yeah. Maybe think before you interrupt me with total nonsense. "Anyway, pretty soon the sun is all alone. He spends his time being as big and loud as possible, because he thinks that will get him attention, and that attention is what he needs. But nobody likes him, you see, and he's exhausted from all the work. He tries to hang out with the moon and other stars, but they're all dodging him, keeping the planets between themselves and the sun. To this very day, the sun is still wandering around, lonely and alone, while the moon and stars spend all their time together, avoiding him. "Do you understand, son? There's a reason you have no friends, so don't come crying to me all the time. Honestly, I don't know where that attitude of yours came from. Now how away, I want to watch my stories." [ spoiler ] (s "You catch more flies with honey than with vinegar.

article: The cafe was packed. I pushed open the street front door to a line. A crowd of tourists yelled their order to the struggling barista. Her face wore a forced smile as she frantically brought plastic cups with massive amounts of whipped cream and toppings. The visitors snatched the cups and payed in change, leaving no tip. I glared at the group as they shuffled out. One of the women slightly bumped my shoulder as she made her way to the door. She tumbled as if hit by a car, throwing coffee everywhere. Most of the hot coffee hit my dress shirt. "It's fine" I muttered balling my fist, I could smell smoke rising from them. "Fine?" She yelled "you made me spill my drink" My back muscles tensed as I felt my hands heat up. An outburst would turn this place to cinders. "You bumped me ma'm" I said gritting my teeth, refusing to apologize. "The fuck is wrong with you" she continued standing up "buy me a new one asshole" "No" I firmly said staring ahead and waiting for the line. My palms where reaching the temperature of the sun. The barista mouthed a quick "sorry" to me and continued working. I began taking deep breaths. I could taste the smoke in the air. "Can you believe this asshole jerry? Now he thinks he can ignore me" the woman roared. "Christ just leave it be. We're gon na be late for our tour" her husband replied. "No no no" she insisted "you should teach him a lesson for me" I stepped to the counter and ordered. The barista told me it was free of charge in a whisper. "Free? That trash wont even pay for mine and now he gets his fucking free?" She screamed. I shoved my hands in my pocket and waited for my coffee. The flame retardants in my pants would hold against any anger. The pockets quickly became small ovens melting any left over coins inside. The woman came up behind me. She brought her hands to my back and shoved hard. My face twisted into a smile. The woman began screaming and I turned. Her hands where blood red and sizzling. Jerry grabbed her by the shoulders attempting to pull her back but she only yelled more. She fell to the floor and kicked in fury as her hands burned away in front of her. I grabbed my coffee off the counter and nodded to the waitress. The woman cursed me and anyone who knew me as I stepped over her and walked out the street front door.
label: human

article: BMerle groaned as he saw the peasant horde approaching his castle. "Come on guys, really?" He muttered as he dropped the freshly baked loaf of bread on the dirty counter. He glanced down at the bread and lifted it in distaste. The Chlorox wipes were just no good to get the blood out. What he really needed was to sand it down and re-finish it. However, he doubted that his present-day copy would spend the much-desired product back in time when he needed toilet paper and gasoline to feed the generator. He downed a shot of vodka from his flask and went to the shelf beside the door. Conical hat? Check. He grimaced, pulling on the absurd garment. Long robe? Check. He looked ridiculous. At least, he would if his damned present counterpart could send back a decent mirror. Unlocking the deadbolt, he stepped outside onto the patio. Ooh, ripe tomatoes! He thought, glancing at the leafy stem. Refocusing, he stepped out of his gated yard and spoke into the microphone wirelessly connected to many concealed speakers about the area. "BEHOLD MORTALS!" He screamed, "I AM MERLIN THE MIGHTY!" He reached into his pocket and pulled out the smart phone also connected to the speakers. Opening the sound effects app, he fired off a bunch of thunderous roars and horrified screams. The peasant horde was afflicted with sudden fear and began to retreat, but for a single man. The populace shrank back to the copse of trees to watch the lone man advance against the scourge. "Excuse me!" The long man shouted, his tongue struggling around his fear. "Foul wizard, the church has taken notice of thy crimes and demand that you immediately surrender "Fuck you." Muttered the wizard as he shot the man dead with his.45. "HE THROWS FIRE AND THUNDER! THE ELEMENTS ARE HIS!" The horde screamed as they fled with great trepidation. Merle glanced at the body of the legendary King Arthur, who thought that plate armor could resist the almighty wrath of Colt. Fuck, I need a drink. The wizard said as he reached into his robe pocket and pulled out the mythical keys to the backhoe parked behind his castle.

article: So I see numbers. There are a few of us that do, you can always tell by the black 10 above our heads. They mark each persons ultimate power, how much sway they could have in the world; in other words, how dangerous they are. For the longest time, Sally was the only other 10 I knew. She was an older woman that happened to live nearby. She wasn't rich or powerful, which I never really understood, but she could tell stories. Sally had traveled all through her life, seeing all kinds of people, places, and powers. There were 10's in every country: India, China, Britan, Brasil. Many of them went into politics or became business owners, as you'd expect, so it was no surprise when one or two of them were killed. Then it started becoming more common. Pretty soon, no 10 could even appear on the local news without a story of their death the next week. Some people, like the president, weren't killed right away, but destroyed through other means. It still chills me to think of the footage leaked that was used to blackmail him out of office. He did recover his son, but his number changed forever after that. Then they came for Sally. They did a good job, it looked just like a robbery gone wrong. Some dude was even sentenced for it. I packed my bags soon after that. I have no name, no history, no possessions, but I do have a purpose. I hunt eleven.

article: I have never expected to savour the taste freedom again. After all, when I was bound and stuffed into this metal casket - having been burned, stabbed, poisoned, drowned and subjected to every imaginable murder method available - buried deep beneath the earth, I had expected my captors to not mark my grave. Best to leave me forgotten, I presume. Their laughter as they lowered me down, mixed with the sound of the dirt crashing unto the metal, haunted me amidst the deafening silence. How long was I confined to this hell, unable to move or speak, unable to die, with only the damning silence as my companion? All because they did not understood my kind, allowing their actions to be driven by fear instead of enlightenment. If only they had the slightest inkling of the gift that I was sent to bestow them. But the directive from the Sage was clear. Were humanity to reject us, we too would reject them. But to condemn the emissary to a metal grave? It was unheard before. It was tantamount to war. I vowed to repay the favour that was done to me. - Dave heard a dull thud as he brought his excavator down. Perhaps it's a rock, he thought to himself, as he carefully dug the soil around it. To his surprise, however, a metal casket gleamed from beneath the dirt, not just any rock that he was expecting. He quickly turned off his machine, before motioning for his supervisor to quickly come over. "Hey Mike, did anyone said anything about this place being a burial ground?" Dave asked as he pointed towards the casket. With the dirt gone, the casket looked much more intimidating. The head portion was carved in the shape of a skull, with two red rubies on the eye sockets. Beneath the skull, rows upon rows of ancient text adorned the casket's body. Mike however, seemed to distracted by something else. "Are those what I think they are?" He ran quickly to the hole that Dave dug, sliding towards the casket at the bottom of it. Both his hands reached greedily for the shiny gems. Dave stood at the edge of the slope, looking at what Mike was doing. He wanted to inform someone else about his find, but he was unsure if it was the right thing to do as Mike was his supervisor. He wondered if it was right for Mike to disturb a casket that looked so omnious. Just as he was about to call out to Mike, he heard a series of a mechanical clicks from the casket, followed by a terrified scream. The last thing that he remembered, before his vision turned to nothing, was a bright flash of light, followed by a robotic voice proclaiming that "I have finally been freed. It is now time for revenge." - rdoritales
label: human

article: John wrinkled his nose and cleared his throat. Pausing, he put down his briefcase and adjusted his tie. It was a red tie with white stripes. This was one of his favorite ties. He picked up his briefcase and walked to his car. It was the last car in the lot, as was common on every night for John. A black Ford Taurus, 1998. He walked with his head held high, and his left hand fumbled for his keys in his pocket. There were many things on his mind at the moment, one of which was pulling out those damn keys without his wallet hanging on to them like an unexpected prize from a claw machine. But the larger thought that had taken residency in his mind, was the voice. The voice that told him that he would never step foot in that location again. A small smile cracked at the thought of this, but was quickly hidden with a deep breadth. Now John was never too keen of nature, but this air tasted sweet to him. Something he had never noticed before. Finally, he reached his car. Unlocking the door, he placed his briefcase in the passenger seat. He thought of his daughter and of his wife. He thought of all the hours of work, and how it had finally got him to the point he was today. He replayed in his mind what his boss said to him, You are getting a promotion, no more floor work for you now, now you will manage your own branch of factories. You are your own boss now. As John turned the ignition nothing happened. After five twists, the Taurus sputtered to life. If there was a form of car bronchitis, this car was definitely patient zero. After the drive home, John was ready to unwind in his small apartment with his family. By the end of the month, John would never step foot in that beat down car, or that run down apartment again. He would hear that first, from the voice.
label: human

article: Sorry I'm late to the party and I'm not a writer. I decided to post this story anyway. I hope you enjoy it. After the assassination of the Prime Minister things really started looking up for me. The CIA essentially had me on speed dial. Drug smugglers, politicians, corporate executives. No one was safe. No agency, big or small could keep a target alive. I was convinced of that. When the lone survivor of United 215 was able to speak again, people were ready to listen. Questioned erupted throughout the world. How did he survive? What exactly happened? Eight hundred fifty-three passengers were on that Airbus A380 when it erupted into flames mid air. Soaring to the ground like an exhausted phoenix. The timing of the crash was impeccable. The FAA was conducting their annual commercial airline safety summit a few weeks after the crash. The survivor was invited to speak before congress about his traumatic experience. That's when I got the call from Langley. After following my target for a few days, I concluded this would be my most dangerous mission yet. Getting away with murder in New York City is no easy task. It had to be quick. When I saw him step out of his Gramercy apartment I knew the clock was ticking. I approached him at the crosswalk. His coffee still steaming out of his "my other computer is a data center" mug. Our eyes met for only a second. He smiled, greeted me and then collapsed. No one had noticed the hydra-shok round that just pierced his heart. People everywhere rushed over to provide aid. I continued on. I removed my trench coat and handed it to a homeless man. "Thank you, miss! God bless!" Everyone deserves a little kindness. Life in America is hard. "Listen to this shit. He told me this story yesterday and it's nuts!" "So I'm standing on the corner going to work. Just minding my own business. When this guy next to me just collapses. I look to help him immediately since I'm right next to him. Then I noticed this guy is pouring blood from his chest. Turns out it was a bullet wound. Someone had just shot him. "That's fucking crazy!" "Right!? Tell him the craziest part." "oh yeah..... I was so distracted by the pool of blood that was pouring out of his chest that I didn't really get a chance to get a good look at him...." " ....when I finally looked at his face. I realized that he was my doppelganger."
label: human

article: "Could I have a large cappuccino to go please?" I asked the man behind the counter. He was kind of cute, in a way, and the smile that he flashed at me almost turned my knees to water. He nodded and turned away to make my drink. It's stupid really. I've been coming here every day for the past month and I've never even asked him his name. He's the only one who works here at this time, so it's not like there would be anybody else watching. Just talk to him damn it! He handed me my coffee and smiled again, hinting that perhaps he felt the same way. Just as I opened my mouth to speak to him, I heard the door of the cafe open behind me as another customer walked in. "Could I have a large...." his order was cut short by a sudden intake of breath, which built up into a sneeze as he tipped his head back. I took a step away from him to avoid the blast zone, and the shout he gave out seemed to reverberate throughout the entire room in which we were standing. "Bless you," the man behind the counter said, but his face fell when he looked closer at the man who had sneezed. He bent low over the ground, wheezing. A dreadful rattle that crawled its way out of his mouth, and a sickening wetness accompanied it. Still crouched over, he let out a short cough, and a fine spray of dark red blood hit the carpet. I was immediately by his side. "Oh my god, are you okay?" I asked him, immediately regretting my stupid question. "Yeah, I'm fine. Its just..." He coughed again, this time spewing a thick blob of bloody phlegm onto the cream coloured carpet, which rapidly darkened as the liquid soaked into it. He erupted into a coughing fit at that point, the spasms wracking his body as he fell to the floor. His arms thudded against the floor as he thrashed wildly, all the while emitted a deep moan that gurgled at sporadic intervals. Eventually he fell still, and the noise stopped almost as abruptly as they had begun. His eyes, although aimed at the ceiling, seemed unfocussed. A thick stream of blood poured out of the corners of his mouth, and the flesh of his lips appeared bruised and rough, almost as if something was forcing its way through the skin. As I pressed two fingers against his neck to check for a pulse, the skin split like an overripe fruit, spilling black, foul-smelling flesh out of his body. I tried to stifle a gag as the disgusting substance flopped onto the floor. "Call an ambulance!" I nearly screamed, barely even turning my head, but noticing he had already begun to do so. When I looked back at the man on the floor, the black gunge seemed to be turning white, and the surface of it seemed to become almost hairy. Some part of my brain screamed a warning. Don't Touch. It echoed over and over again. I made the mistake then of breathing in, which finally caused me to retch and vomit, the slime covering the body that I was fairly certain was dead at this point. As I watched, however, the white hairs seemed to be creeping outwards, already dragging themselves over the fresh vomit, almost as if searching for it. I stared in horror as the skin began to ripple and bulge, splitting further down the body as the clothes began to stain black and the stench rose, as the first of the sirens began to fill the air.
label: human
