article: She was quite a distance away, but I heard her anyway. "Bear" she exclaimed. Standing and brushing the flint knappings from my hides, I grabbed my spear and rushed into action. She was shreaking and running into the village. The bear would endanger the entire tribe if it followed her here. As the protector it was my duty to the tribe. Other younger men had also armed themselves with clubs and whatever was handy; but they stood near the wooden wall ready as I rushed to the path. I strode out to face the beast. It was best to not rush into the danger without knowing how many or how large the beast was. I could see her coming, flailing as the largest bear I have seen followed. It had been a long winter and clearly it assumed that human was on the menu. It looked like three cubs followed some distance behind. Rushing quickly tword the cubs I roared to get the mother's attention. I could easily take out the cubs, but we would need them later. Better to take out the hungry bear. The cubs squeaked in panic, and the mother stopped it's run, and reversed to protect it young. It was quick, but I am swifter that a charging bear. As it rose up to intimidate I stabbed it through with my spear. it's claws hit with a massive swipe that would have rendered most men dead, but only left the faintest scratch on me. Again I stab the beast as the cubs scattered. Another mighty hit, but this time I left my spear in place and grabbed its forearm; and jumped behind with a mighty leap. there was a snap, and the beast howled in pain. still holding the arm I kicked its back and heard another snap. it howled horridly as it slumped to the ground. Letting go of it; it then approached its head, and twisted it with a quick snap. I am Kal, Protector. and no beast shall harm my tribe.
label: human

article: Cursed is not the word. I am the last human and I am adrift in the void. It's been so long since I left the solar system. I have died billions of times; some I recall the major events that led me here. I was the last human long after humanity evolved to something I can't quite comprehend. I am static and it saddens me that I'll never join them. A recurring thought background noise. I was standing on Earth, briefly dead, then alive before quickly dying again. I watched the scene unfold slowly as the Earth was consumed by the Sun, as I was consumed by the sun. I would reform, ever so briefly inside the outermost layers of the Sun only to die nearly instantly. It was this way for so long. Over time, the ferocity of my deaths abated. The sun became transparent, punctuated by a small, brilliant white orb; and I drifted away. My life, as it is, has become a slow movie a few minutes alive and a few minutes dead. It's always suffocation and freezing. I have seen the stars die, and the lights fade from a rainbow hue to yellow and red; finally to blackness. I feel the tug of unseen giants lurking in the darkness and have felt their crushing strength. But eventually they too die and I am reborn from their absence. I am the last. I am lonely. I feel nothing. I remember; my last refuge. I remember my loved ones. I remember my childhood and my parents. I remember pleasure, pain. Unfathomable sadness and absolute joy; and I feel them. I remember light, and there is light.
label: human

article: Alex's supervisor looked at him with disappointed eyes. " ...I'm not sure what's going on with you, Alex. Lately your behavior has been erratic and well, it's frightening our customers and the other employees. " Alex ceased his eye contact and began looking at a tile on the floor. He could just make out something scurrying across from the side of his vision, but worked hard to keep himself from following it. " I know this might be uncomfortable, but have you thought about...you know? Seeing someone about this? Maybe going to a doctor? " Alex continued his silence. This wasn't the first time he was being fired from a job, and it will probably not be the last. The recommendation to see a doctor always stung though. He felt broken. He knew something inside was not right. " Look, I feel horrible about doing this. You're clearly going through something right now and I think you need to get some help. But I can't have you working here if you can't perform the normal job duties. I really want you to go see someone. If you are able to, uh...get better...you know that you can always come back and we can find a position for you. " Alex stood outside of his former workplace, waiting for the bus to take him home. He tried to shut down his senses. But they were too overwhelming and frightening at times, he just had to respond to them. He remembered the horror he caused his family when it all started happening in his 20s. How they desperately pleaded with him to get help, then how they slowly sank away when he got worse and worse. He looked down at the pamphlet that his supervisor gave him. It's the county's mental health center. He looked at the address and phone number. Suddenly Alex felt a presence behind him. The man's sent was strong and unmistakable. He always appeared at just the right times. Alex always felt more at ease around him. The air surrounding him just felt warmer and the sent was intoxicating. He was Alex's only comfort in a life of isolation and loneliness. Alex has never seen his face and has never learned his name. Even though his presence and aroma was overwhelming, there was something in his mind that never allowed him to turn around. He knew he couldn't trust himself - his conversations with his supervisor confirmed that. Alex wanted so desperately for this man to be real - to not be a hallucination. So he never turned around and just allowed his presence to envelop him. The man whispered gently to him. He could feel the air that passed by his ear as each word was pronounced. He was whispering the closest thing that Alex could classify as sweet-nothings. He always knew the right thing to say when Alex desperately needed reassurance. Alex closed his eyes and enclosed himself totally in the man's presence. He felt the man reach an arm down his shoulder and onto his chest. He held him so tightly in his embrace. The man continued to whisper reassuring words. Alex allowed all the humiliation and frustration of his termination flow out from him, it seeped from his heart and onto the pavement below. The rough and mechanical sound of the bus stopping in front of him jolted Alex from comfort. The whispers ceased and the warm feeling and sent was gone. He didn't even know that there was a small downpour of rain that had started while he sat at the bus stop. He shivered through his wet clothes. He calmed his body and told himself to wait patiently for the man to return - he would always know the right time to show up. As the bus drove away, Alex had forgotten his pamphlet. He dropped it in the midst of it all. It was wrinkled and fading from the downpour. The splash-back from the bus caused a large amount of water to flow underneath it. The water carried it gently down the sidewalk and into a storm drain.
label: human

article: At last, it was complete. The painstaking work, the attention to detail..... While not a lifetime, way way too much time had been spent on this project of mine. The city of New York, in glorious detail. Thousands of tiny little trees, gallons of latex paint, millions of toothpicks, buckets of glue and newspaper for the papier-mache. And the lights! I lost count a long time ago. The streetlights, the building lights, and all timed for the correct time of day and everything. It was a beautiful sight to see it at night. Businesses would go on and off, home windows would illuminate and then be turned off as the imaginary residents went about their daynight cycle. I even put in a few lines of magnetic track to allow the buses, cars, carriages, and even those courier bikes to run about. It was a little much to ask that people move around, so I just put them about in static positions. There's a Waldo in there somewhere, and a Santa, and of course, the entertainer denizens who populated times square, all littered about the place as needed. There was even working water. Oh, not for plumbing or sewers, but any fountains? Yep. Ponds, running water? Yep, everything worked. The water surrounding Mahnattan did flow, to keep it fresh, a nice slow pace. And the ferries all worked too! Heck, I even had the tunnels. Everything I could think of. Everything I could make or acquire (or both!) It was all there, and current to today. I had at last put the final touch on the model. The spire of the Chrysler building. One would have thought the Empire State or the new WTC would have been the most challenging, but no, the Chrysler building's art deco top was indeed a long time in creating, but even it too was at last finished, and in place. I sighed. Contented. It was Done. But alas, it was nearing time. Not yet, but soon. I took a few flying shots with my gyro stabilized drone camera, to simulate flying through the city. Different angles, different approaches, different times of day. I took static pictures with my camera. Same thing. Different angles. I had, of course, documented the build itself, but this is different. It's one thing to see it being built, the magic behind the finished product..... but it's quite another to just stand there and take in the beauty of it all. When I'd done all I could to preserve the moment, the perfection that was my scale model..... I stared at it. A long time. So pretty. I really didn't..... "Now?" I turned to my sister, sadness in my eyes, but exasperated that she'd ruin the moment. "God, Jenny, will you hang on a moment?! This took forever to.." "Yeah, yeah, whatever, Jake. Dan's coming over, and I'm not waiting for you." I rolled my teenage eyes. "Fine." I set up the few video cameras in their positions. I didn't want to do this. But I had to. For Art knows no sympathy. And Jenny has her date with the loser. And Sparky, the reason for all this. I turned the cameras on. "Ok, let Sparky loose." The Massacre of New York took only seconds. Sparky, our Dachshund, tore into my masterpiece with the rabidness of a deranged lunatic, bent on destruction. The little smoke bombs, harmless and noiseless, went off in each building as the dog proceeded to dig and find the little morsels I'd hidden in them. Of course, he didn't need much direction, as he was trained, since I started this vision, to destroy Papier-mache things, and this was just his moment. After a minute, sated, he stood in the middle of what was once New York..... then sauntered off, satisfied that he'd done his job. "Wow. He tore that up pretty quick," remarked Jenny. "Seems like a waste of time, Jake, you ask me." I turned to her, smug in my overall satisfaction. "It's Art, Jenny. You wouldn't understand," I said with derision dripping from my words. She looked at me with daggers. "Whatever, Jake. For a 13 year old, you sure are a snot. Grow up." She turned away, going, I assumed, to swap spit with her newest boyfriend of the year. I didn't really care. I got what I needed. Now to the editing for my short. I thought to myself, I'm going to be the next Spielberg, or Abrams.....
label: human

article: Was it still maturbation all those years, or was it more like fucking a robot? These and other deep questions were all I could think about today. A few minutes ago I sliced myself open with a kitchen knife. I expected to be gushing blood all over the tomatoes I was chopping, but instead I saw a destroyed mess of wires. I hadn't confronted my parents yet. I was trying to think of what to say. Did I have a prosthetic I didn't know about? If I was a robot, that means someone programmed a whole bunch of weird sex shit in my head..... and they were kind of perverted in what they chose. My girlfriend. How would I break the news to her? Jesus, I needed to get sober quick. Is there a way to sober up off of LSD? I stared at the clouds and waited for the drugs to run their course. ..... this was going to be a long 8 hours.
label: human

article: Eight years ago I was visiting a day spa on holiday, in the mountains when a massive earthquake destroyed everything. Or at least I assume that it did there's no way for me to tell, really. At the moment of the earthquake, I was getting myself a towel from an exceptionally large closet. I've been trapped in here ever since. Something's blocking the door, I don't know what. I've stopped thinking about it. I've made the best of it, though. There's definitely enough room in the closet to make a life in, and enough towels to make it with. My towel bed is comfortable and spacious, my towel couch is well-stuffed and folds out if I have guests. There's even a towel lamp, which I use to read towel books in the evening. The lamp's shade is a particularly thin hand-towel, kind of like the napkins they give you at fancier restaurants, and for kindling I use old rags that have served their purpose. I've even got art there's a towel by Macy's that I'm particularly fond of, framed on the wall. It's a luxuriant blue, with the kind of texture that dazzles if you look at it too long, and often I do. I was thinking of getting another one, but I don't want the wall to look too cluttered. There's a fine aesthetic balance, there. I even started my own family Junior was just a washcloth only a few years ago, and already he's the kind of hand towel that I always believed he would be. His mother and I are so very proud. It's a blissful scene in the morning I'm reading the paper when he comes down around eight, just in time for school. My wife is in the kitchen, making breakfast the hearty smell of towels cooking hits me all at once, and I'm content. I won't lie to you, though even though I've just described to you this perfect idyll of domestic life, sometimes I wonder what happened to the rest of the world. That's why I'm not worried right now, even though something is making noises against the door I mentioned. I'm perfectly calm. I have towels wrapped tightly around me, and I feel safe. The door finally opens. A man walks in. He looks around, then turns to shout to someone, "Hey, I found all the towels!" Then he turns back, and sees me. At first he is only confused, but I give him a sincere smile and it seems to reassure him. He says to me, "We've been looking for towels for a very long time we knew they were around here somewhere, we just didn't know where." He inspects me carefully. I'm wearing my towel suit, as I was just about to go to work, so I don't mind the intense sartorial scrutiny. But I don't say anything. "How long have you been in here?" "Eight years," I finally say. For a moment, he contemplates in silence what such a long time must mean. Its weight is surely felt. Then he says, "Listen, there's a spa out there, and a bunch of teams from the FIFA Women's World Cup just showed up. They're all just running around naked, since we ran out of towels. I'm not telling you that you have to, but if you could grab a handful of towels and bring them out, it would be really helpful." I look back at my life my furniture, my kid, my wife. Everything I've lived for, for eight years. It's a lot to think about. It's a hard decision. I ask him, "How many do you think you'll need?"
label: human

article: Tom awoke uncomfortable in his chair. He had fallen asleep in his living room for the third time that week. Groggily he pulled himself up, but groaned and quickly hunched back down to avoid the morning sun. Three weeks since he moved out of that basement studio apartment and he still wasn't used to the sun. Another groan as Tom's neighbor revved up their lawn mower. Tom still hadn't introduced himself. He hadn't warmed up to the suburban idea of friendly neighbors yet, but he knew he would have to eventually. "It won't be so bad," he thought to himself. "Maybe I'll actually need a cup of sugar one of these days." Tom worked nights, another idea he hadn't fully warmed up to. It certainly paid well, and he still made it into the city on weekends to maintain a social life, but the backwards schedule was still an adjustment. And he needed better blinds if he was going to sleep during the day. "Just a year or two," he told his friends, "to pay off my student loans and get some good experience." They called him boring, but he didn't mind. He didn't have parents who could help him pay for school, and he knew what he had to do. "Maybe I am boring," he thought, "at least I won't be in debt." Tom was halfway to his bedroom when his doorbell rang. He hesitated, thinking he might just ignore it so he could get some more sleep. "I guess it's as good a time as ever to meet the neighbors," he grumbled to himself. He opened the door to an overly bright day, and before his eyes could adjust, he was greeted by one of the two large shapes standing in his doorway. "Hello-rrrrr vrrrrr-eet-rrrvvrrrrvrrr-present the-vrrrrrrrrrrrrvrrr..... " Tom couldn't really hear anything over his neighbor's mowing, but at least the shapes had settled into two well dressed men with name tags, carrying backpacks and aggressive smiles. " I'm sorry, what? " Shouted Tom. He knew the polite thing would be to invite them in, but he really was tired, and decided men with name tags and backpacks were not likely to leave quickly. " vrrrrrrrrr-om the chu-rrrrrrvrrrrrrr vrrrr-onder-rvrvrrr rr-epted Jesus into yo-rrrrvrrrrrrrr? " Tom could tell by their expressions that this was a question, and pretended he understood. " OK, what can I do to help? " Tom yelled over the mower. " Rrrrrvrrrvvvrr-looking for Jesu-rrrrrrvrvrrr vrr-urch of Jesus Ch-rrrvvv-o help us tr-vvrrvrrr..." At this point the man who hadn't been speaking handed Tom a pamphlet. It had a picture of a sunset with a halo, and Tom was more confused than ever. " Alright, so you're looking for Jesus..... because he's on the run? Am I in trouble here? " " No, no, no," shouted the first man, still smiling aggressively, " we're just here t-rrrrvrrrrrrr-ould like to a-rrvvvrvrrrvv vrrrvvrvvr rrvvv..." At this point Tom had given up, and just wanted to get some sleep. " Thanks, I'll keep a look out. Neighborhood watch and all..." he shouted as he closed the door. He felt a little bad, but they weren't exactly neighbors anyway. Tom dumped the pamphlet into the trash, and headed back through the living room to his bedroom. The house was much more cozy and comfortable without the direct sunlight, and the mower was just a soothing hum through the windows and walls. "Still five hours until work," he thought, and climbed into bed.
label: human

article: Her breath smelled like strawberry bubblegum. That's what went through his mind as handed her a pencil. " Thanks ," she whispered, flashing her stunning teeth. She sat in front of him in Ms. Burke's business class. He had noticed her on the first day of school; he couldn't keep his eyes off of her. To him, she was a stunning flower in an otherwise dull garden. When Homecoming came he finally worked up the courage to ask her to the dance. She blushingly agreed. Teenage love, what can be more beautiful and what can be crueler? Many summer nights ended with them in each other's arms, wrapped in blankets in the bed of a rusty pickup. Where they said their " I love you " s and promised each other eternity underneath the stars. Baby names were decided, rings chosen, a lifetime planned. College applications were sent, jobs were found and new people were met. Where once was a solid stone, a crack appeared. Eyes wandered, shoes were thrown, tears were cried. Many nights were sleepless, yet on one night he came a realization. He no longer cries and with time he came to see that she was not the only flower in the garden (how did he never see the thorns!) nor was she the most beautiful. Today, he can chuckle and appreciate his strawberry bubblegum.
label: human

article: Hey guys, did you hear about the government shut down? It sounds terrible! All those people being furloughed, it's just not fair. Also, I think that our Congress should pass as many bills as possible regardless of their quality or constitutionality. If you question our government, you don't deserve to live in America. Let's not forget about Iran, either. They're still trying to build nukes and threaten our ally Israel. And China is taking away our jobs and just look at what happened to Detroit. All I know is that they better not come for my social security and universal health care sounds like a good idea. I guarantee you I'll vote out this do-nothing Congress next election! I learned my lesson but God forbid whoever the other party nominates for President in 2016! It will be the death of America if my candidate doesn't win. Will they care about our veterans and teachers and small business entrepreneurs and climate change scientists and our children? Won't somebody please think of the children? Speaking of children, abortion is a pretty hot topic upon which I'll base my entire political philosophy. 911 Never Forget. Why haven't they imprisoned the bankers who brought this nation to its knees? Wall Street should not interfere with our democracy, only corporate news stations should do that. Last night I heard on NPR that greenhouse gas emissions are up 5 percent from this time last year, isn't that a tragedy?
label: human

article: "One of us has to go in there?" said the Satanist. "Has..... to?" Asked St. Peter confusedly, while below on Earth a jet full of terrified people slammed into the ocean in part of god's confounding master plan. The atheist and satanist locked eyes and cried "Not it!" in unison before racing past Saint Peter's post and the gates of heaven to the stairway that led to hell. Saint Peter watched their forms disappear down the long flight into obscurity below, and shrugged. He tried not to think about it, and tried not to let it bother him, but there was work to do as the capacity of a 747 began lining up for processing. The light at his booth turned from red to green, indicating there was room again in heaven, and he processed the load of new souls as per usual. He didn't know why heaven was full sometimes and sometimes not, but that was something else he tried not to think about. It wasn't like god was in there eating the souls or anything, right? He'd never really been inside to check, and it was awful quiet, but he tried not to think about it. From the stairway to hell the sounds of music, drunken shenanigans, fornicating and fighting drifted up, as they always did. It almost sounded like fun, but he tried not to think about that.
label: human

article: Shoving the pinestraw and faded woodchips out of the way, I begin digging. The ground on top was soft, easy to get through. Like a slightly undercooked cupcake. As I delve further into the dirt, rocks and other tough obstacles stand in my way. I decide it's time for my shovel. Jamming the tool into the earth, I lift soil away faster than I ever would have with my hands. Knowing I was reaching my prize, I returned to digging by hand. As my fingers pry away the remaining rocks, the prize at the bottom begins to reveal itself. I dust off the top of the box, and raise it above me. Through the translucent purple plastic, I see it. My childhood bird.
label: human

article: I'll ask her today. Just keep it short and sweet, try not to mumble, in and out before my voice has time to betray me or my heart beats its way out of my chest. I'd been building up to it for a while now, a brief smile after making my order, even a small bit of awkward conversation on the days I was feeling particularly bold. ZEEW, ZEEW, PING - bullets flew past my face. Bit closer than they usually got, but still nothing to worry about. Not so safe for the machine behind me though, as it smashed to the ground, the lights on its front dimming. As I walked up to the cafe, the words of confidence I kept repeating to myself felt like they were actually beginning to work. Opening the door, this all changed in an instant, the doubt kicked in. Three years now I'd been walking in for my daily cappuccino, funnily enough, almost exactly the same amount of time the battle had been raging on. Less funnily, the end to this personal battle each morning seemed just as far off as the actual battle reaching its climax. I don't even really like coffee all that much, caffeine held no sway over me like this angelic barista. CLANG, CLANG, BASH - two metallic bots battled it out just infront of the window, each focused on metalic destruction, but evidently only as a secondary focus to keeping a safe distance from passers by. A dog walker strolled on absent mindedly as the machines parted like the Red Sea to make way. No, not today, today was the big day. Today was my day! I'm just going to walk up and ask, before I even order, get it done, get my answer one way or the other. Walking up to the counter the confidence began to grow again, rising from the ruin that was my state of mind just moments previously. And before I knew it I was there, once again face to face with her, the chance to make or break me, do or die time, he who dares, and all that. "Morning, hello, ermm, so I was thinking about if, would you like to perhaps" - BANG, SPLAT! - THUMP - her body slumped to the ground, blood splattered on the wall behind where her perfect head had been so beautifully positioned. The first person to have been killed in this war, and the first person to have been killed by the machines. But not the last. It turns out that it wasn't my big day after all, it was actually a big day for everyone - the day something went very wrong, the day the battle went from being fought machine on machine, to machine on human.
label: human

article: I left the lawn tractor outside the garage before I went on vacation. It was a less than stellar idea, but at least I covered up the seat so it didn't get wet during the rainstorm. I checked to make sure the chip didn't get washed off or something. No water got under the hood, that's fine. No rust on the metal bumpers, good. Most importantly, a nice, soft, straw padding on my wait a second those eggs are not supposed to be there. The mother and father are nowhere to be found. The eggs felt warm. I decided to leave my lawn tractor out for another day. - The parents did come back so those eggs were probably fertilized. I decided to leave my lawn tractor out for another week. - Another rainstorm. I checked to make sure the nest wasn't damaged. It wasn't. - The eggs hatched, and out came these bald little monsters, their beaks cartoonishly large for their tiny little heads. Their eyes are closed with so many folds, it felt kind of nauseating to look at. They were like tiny, wriggling little worms. But they were warm, so warm, so I decided to leave the lawn tractor out until they flew away. - I know I shouldn't, but I keep finding myself poking and prodding the little things. There are little spikes coming out of them now, and soon those little spikes will turn into feathers. Maybe then they'll get a little less ugly, but somehow, I felt they would be the cutest in their monster little selves now. - It was amazing. With the bare minimal of feathers grown in, they started resembling those yellow baby chickens I had. I reminisced about those little guys briefly, remembering how some fairly..... unkind..... neighbours reported them to the city bylaw enforcement..... I am getting angry, I will stop being angry. I will focus on these little guys in front of me. - They began being more active. Before, they would only respond to their parents. Now, they would look at me when I get close. It rained last night, so I picked up a worm on a whim. I dangled it in front of their eyes, and they followed my hand almost magically. But they did not eat the worm. I was disappointed. - Today, I had a lot of free time, so I spent it watching the baby birds squiggle around in their nest. I saw an unhatched egg. It was disheartening, but it made the three little beaks in front of me all the more precious, knowing there was a chance they could have stayed in their shells. I tried petting one of it, mainly to comfort myself, and they seemed to enjoy my touch. I scratched under the beak as a followup, and it opened its mouth. I wonder..... - I have a collection of worms, slugs and snail eggs from my garden today. I scratched Fatty, who I named so because I will probably make it fat to satisfy my selfish whims, under its beak. It opened, and I slowly lowered a worm into its mouth. Fatty then snapped its beak rapidly, downing the worm in the blink of an eye. It looked at me. I scratched under its beak. Fatty opened its mouth. I put in some snail eggs, and it snapped its beak enthusiastically. One more time. This time, I gave it the slug, but it turned away. At this point, the other two birds began chirping. I dangled a worm in front of one of the other two birds, and they too began eating. I'll need two other names. - They are now Fatty, Chubby and Cheeky. Today, I found a HUUUUUUGE slug, as big as a section of my finger! I scratched Fatty under its beak, and it opened its mouth. I fed it a worm, and as if on cue, the other two joined in, chirping for food. I found that Cheeky is a gourmet, she'd only eat snail eggs. I hope it was a she, she just feels like a special little princess who doesn't even like worms, the most cliche of bird food. Chubby would eat everything. He is kind of fat. I still can't decide on a gender for Fatty though, even though Fatty is the first one I bonded with, how peculiar. But the most important thing is, I have recorded the entirety of the battle between Chubby and the huge slug on my phone. As I dropped the slug into Chubby's mouth, it balled up, and Chubby's snapping beak slid off the smooth, lubricated skin of the slug, sending the slug-ball into the air. Then, with almost perfect accuracy, Chubby caught the falling slug once more, and snapped its beak. Again, the slug-ball slid right out, flying high into the air. Unfortunately for Chubby, the third time, he only managed to knock the slug into the ground as it came back down. Unfortunately at this time, the parent birds came back and I had to bail. - I scratched Fatty under its beak, and it opened its beak. I waited. Fatty waited for a while, then closed its beak and looked around, as if confused. I scratched under its beak again. Fatty opened its beak, and extended its neck out so far it almost seemed like his neck grew a few inches. For a tiny bird, that's almost frightening. I had to reward that effort, so I gave Fatty a worm. Fatty snapped it down, and opened its beak again. These little things are growing fast, their appetites increase at an alarming rate every day. But I am prepared today. I had made a small worm pit, and picked from it a handful of fat, juicy worms. I placed a plate of flat beer in the grass, and now I have a plate full of slugs. Finally, with some rather extreme effort, I dug up a small cup of snail eggs from rotting tree branches I never bothered to clean up. One worm goes to Fatty, a pinch of snail eggs to Cheeky, and Chubby just scarfs down everything in my left hand whatever is in there. Suddenly, as if in unison, they all turned their backs to me. Three little squinty eyes looked at me through their still-growing tail feathers. As if doing a dance, the three little squinty eyes wriggled left and right. Then, a giant marble of liquid white with bits of blackish green oozed out of each of those eyes, beautiful in a most gross fashion. They had just pooped in my general direction, and probably expected me to clean it up like their parents do. I, uh, ignored it and kept feeding them. They pooped twice more, each time bigger than the last. Those tiny little wriggling butts became almost hypnotic to watch, at least until I realized how wrong that sounded. - Every day when I see those little sparrows, there would be no trace of poop. How do the parents clean their babies? I'd rather not think about that. Fatty, Chubby and Cheeky have grown out their feathers now, and they look like full fledged birds. They might be flying away at any time, and in a way, it made me feel sad. Obviously. So I decided to pick them up today, and see if they were really my friends, or if they were just after my food. Fatty was obviously reluctant. When I placed him in my hands, it would desperately try and jump back into the nest. That ungrateful little prick, to think it was my first. Chubby almost didn't care, and oh god, I hope I'm not ruining this little guy's chances to fly because I could actually feel its weight, bird-boned as he is. That is..... not a good sign. I am a terrible person. I picked up Cheeky, and she felt almost at home. She actually stood up, and tried to climb up my sleeves. It was a wonderfully productive day, I had three little cuties in my hands and my friends are going to be hearing all about it. I lead a sad and lonely life. Just as I was about to facepalm myself for even thinking of something so cheesy, I realized those little birds were full of freaking parasites and bugs are crawling all over my hands. I screamed a little inside. - I couldn't go see those birds for three days. Apparently one of the parent birds got injured by something, and didn't leave the nest to hunt for food for a while. It was fiercely protective of its children. Every time I got close, it screeched and flapped its wings. But it's finally healed, and went back to hunting. Goodbye parent bird 2! As always, I fed the little guys, and I picked Cheeky up. At this point, I realized I had gone off the deep end - I could actually differentiate between three baby sparrows. Whatever the case, I placed Cheeky on my picnic table, sat down and let my chin rest on the table as well. Playing with Cheeky at eye level was simply different from looking down at her. But I played with someone far more addicting last night, and it's called PS4, and we played all the way until 3AM, so I yawned. When I finished, and opened my eyes, I noticed Cheeky noticeably closer to my face. I slowly opened my mouth voluntarily. Cheeky tried to stick its head in my mouth. Partly because she is a filthy bug ridden fleabag, and partly because I don't want bugs in my mouth, so really, wholly because of the bug thing, I closed my mouth shut. Cheeky stepped away backwards. I slowly opened my mouth again, and Cheeky quickly stepped forward, trying to stick her head in again. The cycle repeated a few times, because I found it funny. Until Cheeky got fed up, and snapped her beak on my lip, refusing to let go even as I lifted my head off of the table. Thankfully Cheeky is a super light sparrow, or else her dangling from my lip swinging back and forth would've required plastic surgery to fix. While the pain was one thing, nothing hurt more than what my little sister, who had conveniently saw the whole thing when she came over, said to me over the dinner table. "I know you don't have a girlfriend right now, but..... are you really that desperate?" I thought to myself, you know what, if Cheeky is a real girl and..... I lead a sad and lonely life and I should probably just kill myself. Or not, no, birds are the cutest things ever and I don't feel sorry for the kind of stupidity going through my head at times. My love for Cheeky is for her pure, innocent, playful mannerisms, sort of like how you would feel affection for a little girl like, a younger sister, or a niece, or..... Tomorrow I'm going to the police station and calling a psychiatrist.
label: human

article: His crimes were too ghastly to comprehend. His reign of terror was the stuff of nightmares. Those who survived recounted the atrocities he inflicted, while he sat at the defendant's table impassive. The verdict was a forgone conclusion. The only suspense was the punishment. He too took that with the impassive demeanor he displayed throughout his trial. He was then led away for the sentence to be carried out. Ten years afters the lawyers had their turn, the day of punishment had arrived. He had his final meal and was strapped to the gurney. The warden then read the warrant. 'Prisoner number G22355 having been found guilty in a court of law, you will receive the punishment required by the law. Therefore you will receive an immortality injection followed by immolation in an asteroid for an indeterminate period but no less than 10 billion standard years. May God have mercy on your body
label: human

article: My love, I write to you in haste for I have not much time. I have finally found it. The perfect avocado. As I type this message, it sits upon my counter, beholden to nothing but its own magnificence. It was in the market down by the pier. Remember where Toby fell into the puddle? Right there. There wasn't a cloud in the sky, the wind was soft and alluring, and I was thinking about you when my gaze drifted to the little market tucked away down there. Dozens of avocados spilled from their wooden container, perfectly shadowed from the morning sun by the taunt linen cover of the stall. My fingers slid across their knobbly skin feeling each rough protective knot and gnarl. I knew there would be one here that was perfect. I didn't see it so much as feel it. Its rind was marred with imperfect roughness, but smooth enough to entice me to slide my fingers deeper and grasp it in my palm. It sat lightly as I took it from the pile. Its dark form was that perfect shade of purple-black, black in the sun, but purple in the shade. I rolled it back and forth and it glided across my hand. It was balanced like a sphere and every proportion aligned with the other. Glancing at the seller, I casually flipped off the stem. Beneath it was the most verdant green. Harsh like the green of a jungle fern, but soft and inviting like summer grass. I squeeze it - ever so softly - and it squishes slightly as my fingers press against its flesh. A tingle travels up my arm and my shoulders quiver. Fresh, ripe, and ready. The seller stared at me. "How much?" I asked. She pointed to the sign. 50 cents! "For any of them?" She shrugged. What a fool. I slipped her a dollar and winked with the avocado in my hand. She rolled her eyes and I turned back towards my apartment. I had no desire to share perfection, and if she thought that every avocado was worth 50 cents, then all the better. A REAL merchant knows that every price is what the buyer will pay. I would have paid a thousand times that for the little fruit. I know I will never find an avocado more perfect than this. How many years had I seen the avocado shadow on the wall, knowing that somewhere lay its maker in the vast avocado sea? I had found it. It was mine and mine alone. I don't know yet what I will do with it. Perhaps I will make our favourite guacamole, remember it? With the cayenne and cilantro and a touch of sriracha? I will tell you in my next letter. Every moment I spend typing is another moment of wasted time. As always, I can not wait to see you again, to eat with you again, to share with you again. Every bite of avocado will be one I wish was with you. Every moment is but a shadow without you here, my love. I will miss you always, Jaime
label: human

article: (Oh, this dovetails so nicely into my world. I am so jumping in.) Now that we were no longer dodging mortars and the intermittent - and wildly off-target - missiles, I could actually get a breather. Check the camera's still there - it is. Erase the footage of me screaming like a little girl, definitely. Start over again. "Ahem. As ma stop, clear my throat again, take a drink of water from the canteen. "As many of you already know by now, the fighting out here is fast, frequent, and furious. For the past two weeks, I've been embedded with the BDM 42nd'Red Vipers', a premiere special forces team, and for the past two days we've also been joined by the BDA 2957th'Volunteers. I shoved the camera, turning it toward the bloodied and mud coated humans covering in the trench next to the Bovi. They were at most, half the size of their counterparts, and even that was a stretch. "It wasn't so long ago - just 2 years in fact - that we would be shooting at each other. But that's all changed. Now we're fighting side by side, for the same worlds." Switching the camera to autofollow, I rose and approached the two nearest humans. "Excuse me, you mind if I ask a few questions?" "Not gon na make us sound like idiots or monkeys?" Racism and prejudices against the humans were still pretty rampant. There was a preceding war, they had lost, and we had brought them under our government when their atrocities had been revealed. It was..... painful. But that wasn't my job or my concern. I wanted to tell the story of soldiers, and race didn't matter. "No. None of that horseshit. You as people. I'll be gentle too. Fair enough?" They nodded in agreement. "So," flipping the camera back on, "can you tell me why you joined up with the volunteers to start with?" The woman actually smiled a bit, pushing the worst of the mud off her body armor. "That's easy. They said'the bad guys are coming for your world, we need help.' Went straight to a recruiting station and signed up. This world's my home, figure I owe it at least that much." Nodding, I turned toward the man, who shrugged and tried to look sheepish. "She says it better than me. I was military before, though, so I knew they needed bodies. Signed up that day, haven't been home since." "I see - so how did you end up with the legendary Red Vipers, a special forces regiment." Scratching his chin and ignoring the blood, he shrugged again. "Honestly, I don't know. I told them, I'm military, I want to be near the front lines, where can I do the most help? They looked up my records and said'we want you to help with the Vipers.' I used to fight the Vipers, so I knew who he meant." "I just said put me up front," the woman offered, "put me up front and let me protect my neighbors. I won't complain about anything, just give me a shot. Next thing I know, I'm meeting this tall drink of water who tells me I better ask for help when I need it, and I better get it when I ask." Nodding, I flipped the camera to face me. "The Red Vipers have been at the front of many battles, despite being on the flanks and behind enemy lines. They were the first to respond to this new incursion just last month, even though they've been fighting for 7 years straight. Tell me, how do the Vipers you work with look?" "Scary," the woman offered calmly, "they see a target, they go for it, they make it dead, and they get everyone out. Sure, we get a few wounds, but we live." "Yeah," the man agreed, "best of the best of the best, definitely. They're tired as hell, you can see it, but they're still fighting top form. We haven't lost anyone since I got here." Inadvertently answering the question as to why he'd been embedded here. Of course, my thoughts get interrupted as a MAC90D set opens up full rate on an enemy something. Even in the trench, I can feel the wind from the launching shells and reloads. That's when it occurs to me; they said social interest. I turned toward one of the Bovi - looks like a Major. "Sir, can I ask you a few quick questions?" He grunted and nodded, using a soaked handkerchief to try and clear some of the mud from his muzzle. "You've had the volunteers here a few days now. How would you describe the relationship?" That actually made him pause, thinking about it, not necessarily in diplomatic terms. "A week ago, would've refused. Sat'em down as aides. But frankly, having seen them fight? Maybe they can't haul an AMR, maybe they can't carry a hundred kilos at a go, but damned if they don't have it where it counts." Rising to his hooves, he turned and actually saluted the two humans. "I'd take these two into hell with me - done themselves more than proud." Predictably, they both saluted back, clearly stunned. That setup always worked for the propaganda stuff. Besides, folks like that never shirked their duties. They'd fight twice as hard just to prove they were every bit as good as the other species. "Then can I ask you all.... how do you think the battle is going here?" Looks were quickly exchanged, and the Major took over again. "Official canned answer, we expect to rout the enemy any hour and completely destroy their assets. Unofficially, we've taking a pounding but they're getting it worse. Soon as we get some air support, it's mopping up time. We're in a good position, we have the best people, we'll be home for breakfast at least." "So we're winning?" "Yep. We're winning," he agreed, "just as soon as the air support gets here." There was a scream of engines approaching, and he looked up while also pointing. There was no mistaking that it was a Hog II ground attack aircraft. There was an unusual whirring as the main gun fired, the camera tracking as it moved off into the distance. And didn't turn around. "Well shit. Bingo ammo. So we wait a little longer." All I could do was turn toward the humans, who looked elated and dejected at the same time. "So what are you thinking?" The woman shrugged helplessly, but the man shook his head confidently. "Bad call, should have sent fresh planes. Gotten some of ours out of mothballs faster, maybe. But, if the Major says we can take them out? I wouldn't doubt it for a minute. We'll win. Then we'll go find another fight and win that too. Biggest mistake these idiots ever made was invading our homes. Every inch they want to take, we'll make them fight and bleed for." I couldn't have asked for a more perfect close. Flipping the camera to face me again, I put on my best smile. "And there you have it. This is Larry Sun for DFIC, signing off."
label: human

article: The flood of perfect white raging outside forced my windowpane-like eyes shut every time I tried to open them. The bleaching luminance however did have a warm embrace; it settled over my shaking cold face like graceful feathers poured from a sun-baked pillow. My breathing floated and settled like dew within my deathly lit bowl. All of the scratching, tapping, creaking and thumping objects from before the countdown seemed to have been wrapped in soundproof wool. The only discernible sound from the overwhelming white noise was the scratch of the atmosphere stabbing at any thing resembling a crack. I guess it was trying to be the first to execute my unforgiving sentence. The usually lively ecosystem of species spread through my limbs seemed to suffer some slight dismay with my penalty. I felt scattered tingles as most of them burrowed, scuffled or shook back into the small retreats and cracks. My body was giving up already..... and I've barely left orbit. As things quieted down I started to smell the blood on the dirt of Mars - oh the irony of the starry dream I had in my time with toy trains, cotton candy, dirt and drunkenly formed fatherly discipline.
label: human

article: I hold the phone to my ear in disbelief. "Bullshit." The voice in my ear keeps talking. "In Times fucking Square?" Let me give you a bit of backstory. I'm John Kilburn, and I work for the Bureau of Paranormal Activity. And today there's an honest-to-fucking-god dragon flying around Times Square, and I'll bet you any sum of money that people are standing around taking cellphone videos of it. My phone rings one more time. "What is it now?" The desk agent responds, "You can't use your usual equipment. This is too public." "What, you want me to kill a dragon with my bare hands?" I have a multitude of other options: Grenades, plasma rifles, stun guns, a railgun, and a dart gun. Lots of goddamned sci-fi guns to not use. With a slight chuckle, he replies, "No. With a sword." "How in the fuck..." I put my face in my hands in disbelief, "How in the fuck is killing it with a sword any better?" "It'll look like you're putting on a show. Tourist attraction or some shit. We'll get you the sword on your way there." I'm only a few blocks away, so I start running towards Times Square. A block out, an agent stops me and hands me my weapons- a sword and shield. "Press the button on the sword to energize these." I don't even respond- I'm already too pissed off that it's the twenty-first century and I've got to go fight this thing like King fucking Arthur. I just pick up the weapons and go, sprinting until the dragon is in my field of vision. And this is one ugly son of a bitch- brown scaly skin, frail wings, black teeth the size of my hand. I prime my sword and shield- they both hum with blue energy, probably some kind of plasma tech. I hear a voice in my earpiece- "John. The sword is broadcasting an infrasonic signal to attract the dragon." "Why in God's name would that be a good idea?" I glance at the dragon as it starts lumbering towards me. There's no response, so I start charging at the dragon, swinging my sword at its chest and making a gash two inches deep. The crowd around us cheers, probably thinking this is some kind of show. The dragon charges again, this time raising a claw against me. I hold my sword straight up, stabbing the dragon through the foot and eliciting a roar of pain, accompanied with a breath of fire. Of course this asshole can breathe fire, I thought. The dragon decides to try a new tactic, breathing a bolt of fire at me. I barely raise the shield in time and the flames disperse around me, just barely deflected. The dragon starts to flap its wings, slowly but surely rising up into the sky. I jump off an information stand to try and stab it, but it's out of reach- I fall and skid to the ground, my sword scraping the concrete. I look around, wondering how to attack the dragon. I decide there's only one way to win this fight before anyone gets hurt- I reach into the inside of my leather jacket, pulling out a small, collapsible gun that extends into a longer rifle. I get on one knee and aim upwards, my eye aligning with the sights. Taking a deep breath, I hold down the trigger, a sustained bolt of plasma burning into the creature's skin. It starts falling slowly at first, then dropping like a rock, crashing to the ground. "Sword and shield, my ass. It's the twenty-first fucking century." A helicopter comes in to retrieve my quarry, and I disappear into the crowd. A voice comes on in my earpiece, and I can't believe what I'm hearing. "A fucking werewolf? It's the middle of the day!"
label: human

article: "Houston we have a problem.." " Houston to Michaelanlo 1, we acknowledge you have in issue and your 10-2 on the reception. Report your issue. " David who had wanted to be a astronaut since he was a young boy, had always dreamt he would get to make some famous line that would go down in history." Hearing Neil Armstrong say "One small step for man, one big leap for mankind," gave him goosebumps he'd listen to the transmission and he knew he'd go down in history.... He could feel it in his bones, the thoughts made him warm, even while he was in the vacuum of space. The crackle of the built in headset came back to life. " Michaelangelo 1, this is Houston do you have a copy? What's your 20? " "Uhhhhhm you guys won't believe this.." " Michaelangelo 1 please report your issue" When David first stepped off of thithe ship he marveled at the vast beauty of the red planet, he reported his touchdown and began to dig approximately 100 yards from where Michaelanglo landed. After digging for what seemed like forever he managed to notice that the dirt he was collecting almost seemed like it cut through like butter. After filling the sample jar he made his way back to the ship to do some testing on the samples. Micaelanglo 1, we get it. Its April Fools Day. Haha you've been up there working hard and you need to blow off some steam. We'll have a nice and big Mars candy bar waiting for you when you break the atmosphere" "I am absolutely serious right now" " Haha yeah right David, you're always such the jokester" "FINE! YOU DONT BELIEVE ME? SWITCH TO THE LIVE CAMERA FEED AND I'LL GET MORE SAMPLES." David puts his gear back on and steps out into the giant red desert and begins to dig. After digging about 5 feet he holds up a piece of chocolate to the camera and claims he's going to eat it when he gets back into the ship. As he is making his way back to the ship he hears once again that familiar sound of the radio kicking on. " "The Martians are to far away but it sounds like they are chanting something." Oompa loompa dippidy dooo thaaat chocolate waaaaas not for you "Hard to make out what they're saying" " Michaelangelo 1 what is happening? Video feed has fallen" "OOMPA LOOMPA DIPPIDY DOOO" " DAVID DO YOU HAVE A COPY!? " ...... " I think we lost him" EDIT: Typed this on a phone please excuse grammar and other things.

article: It was a Sunday, the day the bombs fell. I don't quite recall the date, but I do know that. I know that because she was wearing the pale blue dress, the one that made her eyes shine like diamonds and her hair look like burnished copper. I liked that dress. We were in church, quietly praying, breathing in the censer smoke and watching the sunlight glint on the dust motes in the air. It was cool in the church, a welcome reprieve from the heat and the dust. It must have been summer, heat and dust always mean summer right? I opened my eyes just a fraction and looked at her. She was peeking too. I smiled and she smiled with me, my heart leapt to see that smile. I liked that smile. I would have given anything for that moment to never end, the two of us frozen in time. Sharing that secret smile until the end of the universe. It was then we heard the wailing, quiet at first but soon it was deafening, a choir of screaming devils invading our sacred place. Panic started, the air-raid siren was never used. Not for drills. This was real. So people ran, back to their houses and their shelters, desperate to pack their things and hide away from whatever death was about to be rained upon us, to hide from the war that we all knew would eventually find it's way to our secluded corner of the world. I didn't run. Neither did she. We walked outside and sat on the step, I had my hand on her waist and we gazed into the street. Slowly we turned to face each other and kissed, it was the sweetest, saddest kiss I ever had and I could feel her tears trickling slowly down her face. Her lips, her hair, her skin as soft as down, her scent..... a scent I could drown in. I liked that kiss. As we pulled away I smiled and gently wiped the tears from her face and whispered "No tears now honey. We've had a hell of a run"
label: human

article: Old age caught up on Jimmy Santry like an Olympic runner. He always felt he was unstoppable. His health, he thought would give him immortality. He strode towards his well lit bathroom mirror. The rumble in his lungs was forming. It never amazed Jimmy that spiders, long legged daddy's, and ants would creep around his sanctuary of cleanliness. Often enough, he would flick them off his face, shoulder or naked chest. Jimmy loved company. On closer inspection of his wrinkling face, he spotted pussy spots. A man of his age reimagining puberty, 60 years on. Popping puss never felt so gratifying. The yellow, infused with red wine blood struck the reflective mirror. A wipe of his finger always did the trick. Tasty too. The rumble was raging more viciously now. He erupted a fit of phlegm and blood into the sink. Old Jimmy never let his bodily fluids go to waste. It was feeding time.
label: human

article: Surely I was not losing my mind. No..... Those was definitely her eyes. Big and round and a soft brown in eventide light, and a ghost of the golden star that shone on them during the day. I shook my head, trying to push the memories out from the forefront. Instead, I decided to focus on getting through the next crowd of people. The sidewalks here are like the tide, rushing groups that came in waves. There it was again. A young woman walked past me, earpods lodged in their place. She was pretty, I suppose, in the way that strangers sometimes were. But the hair of the stranger was the rolling gold curls that I knew some years ago. Another person laughed nearby, and it was also hers. I smiled to myself and glanced around, half-hoping, half-fearing that I'd find her. I found the laughing girl, feeling both relieved and disappointed that it was not the lover I once knew. I sighed and stepped to the precipice of the sidewalk. Inhale deeply for eight counts. Hold for four counts. Exhale for eight counts. It was a lesson in breath control I had learned in the ancient past, in my days of marching band. It was also a suitable meditation for clearing the head. It had worked when my business threatened for several weeks. I managed to keep my head calm, and revive it, but now. Now all I could think about was her. How she made my heart pound. How she turned a miserable time into a memorable one. How she- I needed sit down. The street had cars racing down both sides, so jaywalking was out. I pushed rudely through a gaggle of pedestrians into the shaded marketplace inside. In a pretentiously half-restored coffee corner. I slid a ten on the counter. "Mocha Bianca, mate. I'm in a bit of a rush." The barista's snort of derision was almost non-existent with the potential bribe laid out so garishly. He moved with practiced speed, giving me a piping hot coffee in a couple minutes. "Four fif "Keep it." I snatched the coffee and strutted away as quickly as I could, the aroma wafting out of the cup, and sending me back to her dormitory suite. I pushed open some doors on the other side of the market and caught a gust of salty air. It should have blown some sense into my head, but all it did was remind me of her stories of surfing, of wandering the hills around Los Angeles. I sat down on top of a sea wall, cup of coffee in one hand, and looked out into the sunset. She was the golden woman, eyes, hair, laugh, and soul. As bright and joyful as the western sunset, with promise of singing and dancing long after the light dissipates. God damn it all.
label: human

article: Everyone has a voice inside their head. Usually the voice is there to bring up embarrassing things you did in high school and remind you of important deadlines after they've passed. Jared had two voices in his head. No more, no less. One voice was his own, but the other voice was different. For starters, it wasn't his own voice. It was the voice of a middle aged British man. This is somewhat peculiar since Jared was a twenty-five year old from Connecticut who had never been abroad. Jared never bothered to discuss this with anyone. He just accepted it as the norm since it had been with him for as long as he could remember. To make matters worse, the voice's sole function in his head was to narrate his life. Jared couldn't converse with this voice no matter how much he tried. It simply narrated his actions and feelings. Much to Jared's frustration, it was often wrong about what it was saying. There was always a modicum of truth to what it said, but it twisted the truth in bizarre ways. It used to drive him crazy. Nowadays, he had mostly learned to ignore it. Having a British man in your head narrating your life makes it difficult to socialize at times. Jared realized he couldn't trust the voice early on, when he was in elementary school. He was eating lunch with one of the few friends he had when the voice claimed that his friend had stolen some grapes out of his lunch bag. After accusations declared and a friendship soured, Jared found out that the voice had fingered the wrong kid. Someone else had stolen his grapes. Jared blamed his lack of social skills on the British voice. He was shy around most people, and seeing any halfway attractive female left his palms sweaty and his mind blank. Tired of the relentless loneliness and lack of intimacy, Jared tried his hand at online dating. He enjoyed using Tinder. It allowed him time to craft thoughtful responses and to hide from the inevitable gauntlet of face to face interaction. Eventually, he matched with a girl named Vanessa. For some reason she decided that Jared tickled her fancy and agreed to meet up for a date. The plan was to meet at a nearby cafe one evening. When the night came, Jared was a nervous wreck. He showered and was in the process of shaving when the voice chimed in. Jared had waited for this night all his life. He couldn't contain his bloodlust any longer. " Ow! " Jared shrieked. He cut himself with his razor at that last line. Bloodlust? What narrative was the voice spinning tonight? He finished shaving, and started dressing himself He chose dark clothing, for stealth. He donned his favorite leather boots in case he needed to take her into the woods. " What the hell are you talking about? " Jared demanded with incredulity. This voice was making him sound like a serial killer. He did not need this on his first date. " Whatever, fuck it " he said, to his empty room. Jared had been stalking Vanessa's social media profiles for weeks. He pored over every detail he could learn about her. He was obsessed with her. He loved her. He wanted her dead. Jared seriously considered cancelling the date as he walked towards the cafe. This voice was pissing him off, and he didn't want to make a bad first impression. He continued on. He had already cancelled twice because of nerves, and he knew he couldn't again. Jared walked at a slow and deliberate pace. As each boot step squashes the grass beneath him, he imagines himself crushing Vanessa's windpipe under his foot. " No I don't " he growled to himself through clenched teeth as he fought to keep the proposed image out of his head. He walked up to the cafe and saw Vanessa through the window. She looked even better than he had imagined. He wanted to take her behind the cafe and choke the life out of her immediately. Jared made a mental note to see a psychiatrist the next day. The date went better than he expected despite the horror story unfolding in his head. Vanessa was incredibly easy to talk to, and she seemed not to notice, or at least ignore his preoccupation. Every second passed with agony, Jared just wanted to get her out of the cafe so he could make her heart stop beating. After the fifth grisly murder scenario proposed by the narrator, Jared had to excuse himself to the bathroom. He splashed water on his face and stared at himself in the mirror. " Stop what you're doing! " He ordered the voice with ferocity. A man using the urinal quickly finished peeing and scurried out of the bathroom. The anger was building in Jared. He knew it was time for someone to die. He could see it. Blood everywhere. He longed for it. It was inevitable. It always had been. Jared stopped talking to himself in the bathroom, so as not to appear completely insane, and returned to his date. " Are you okay? " Vanessa asked, " You seem upset. " " I'm fine, I just have a lot on my mind from work " he lied. " How about we go back to my place then? I'll make you a drink " she said. Jared couldn't believe she was inviting him back. He thought for sure that she wasn't into him. " Sure, I'm down with that " Jared started to feel more at ease. They exited the cafe and began walking to Vanessa's which was only a few minutes away. Soon. Soon, Jared would be alone with her. He walked with purpose to her apartment. The end is nigh. " I usually don't take people back to my place this soon. I just feel like I know you since we've been talking on Tinder for so long. You're not going to murder me are you? " Vanessa asked playfully. Yes, without a doubt " No! I promise " he said, feeling somewhat uneasy. They entered Vanessa's apartment. She poured him a drink, and after they clinked glasses, she excused herself to the kitchen. The time is now. Jared knew death was approaching. Jared simply rolled his eyes, he wasn't going to let this old Brit ruin his evening. Vanessa came back into the room. He turned around as she plunged a butcher's knife into his stomach. He looked up at Vanessa in shock. Her face lit up with delight and she let out a sickly cackle. Jared, still in shock, shoved Vanessa to the ground and pulled the knife out of his stomach. He ran out of her apartment doubled over, clutching his wound. He made it to the stairwell when she caught up with him. She swung at him wildly with another, more serrated knife. Thanks to the adrenaline pumping through his veins, he felt nothing as she cut into his forearm. The knife became lodged in his arm; Jared saw his opening. He grabbed Vanessa and, with all the strength he could muster, threw her down the stairs. Vanessa tumbled down the stairs and landed on her head with a satisfying crack against the cement. Blood oozed out of her skull, but she was still moving. Jared hobbled down the stairs. He felt alive. He looked at her in disgust and crushed her windpipe with his boot. The first kill is always messy.
label: human

article: I woke to the cheerful chirp of my cell phone's morning alarm. I rolled over on my side to dismiss it, and the sleepy murmur of my waking thoughts were abruptly overtaken by searing pain. "Agh!" I cried, rolling off my right arm and cradling it. "What the hell?!" I looked at it, almost afraid of what I would find. And then confusion rolled in like a storm, complete and befuddling. Carved into my right forearm was a single word, two letters long. GO I winced, touching the broken skin tenderly with my other hand. The cut was shallow, more of a severe scrape than a true incision, and the wound had already scabbed over. I looked around the room, trying to gather my thoughts. What was going on? How had this happened while I slept? I stopped, realizing that I couldn't remember what had happened last night after coming back to my room after showering in the hall baths. I had been planning on studying for Thursday's exam..... My eyes fell on the calendar. November 23rd. Of course. A series of realizations broke over me like chilly little waves. My family isn't very..... occult. They don't go in for things like ghost stories and whatnot. But my mom loves to tell this one about when I was a newborn, not even a week old. "She was just crying and screaming her head off," Mom would say. "Nothing we did worked. I rocked, I sang, I fed her, I bathed her. I even," she would always look a little embarrassed at this part, "I even shouted at her." And then Dad made her put me down before she lost it and they went and sat in the next room for a bit to calm down before trying again. "At first her crying got worse. So much worse! The kind of screams that make your blood run cold. I thought she would make herself sick from crying so hard. But then, just as I couldn't take it any more, and was going to go back to the nursery, it just..... stopped." She had dashed into the room, certain that I had somehow cried myself to grievous injury, only to find that I was fast asleep, with my face nuzzled up next to the sleeve of an old yellow cardigan. "I hadn't worn that cardigan since college," Mom would whisper, her eyes getting wide. "I had completely forgotten about it, though it was stored in the nursery closet, which held a lot of old clothes at the time." Dad had been with her the whole time, and no one else was in the house, so if they hadn't pulled the cardigan out for the baby, "Then who was it?" Of course, she freaked out a little at the time because, 1) ghost cardigan, and 2) you're not supposed to put anything in the crib with the baby because it increases the risk of SIDS. But it stopped me from crying, so she left it in there with me but kept a sharp eye and ear out. For the longest time, I thought it was just a creepy story that Mom liked to tell to mess with me. Don't be bad or your ghostie godmother will be mad! But as I got a little older, I suspected that maybe she had just been too tired and forgot about doing it herself. Then, on the night of my tenth birthday, I was on a sugar high and trying in vain to fall asleep in bed when suddenly, a crying baby was in the room with me. It didn't take too long to figure out after that. On my twentieth birthday, four days ago, I went back and visited my ten year-old self. She wanted to know if I was in college (yes), if I had a boyfriend (yes), and if things were cooler after you turned 18 (kind of). She still seemed a little frazzled about the baby episode, and we figured out together that this seemed to be something that happened every 10 years. But then I confessed that I didn't remember seeing 20 year-old me when I was ten, but she seemed to remember her recent interaction with the baby, and that's when we realized that the younger self wouldn't remember, but the older self would. She asked me if I had seen 30 year-old me yet, and I told her that I hadn't. "Well, it's four days after my birthday today," she said. "It's November 23rd." "I wonder how long we've got?" I said. "Until we can't speak any more." The ten year-old seemed to panic at the notion that our conversation was a limited commodity and seemed to jump up with the urgency of her next question. "Mom and Dad," she said. "Do Mom and Dad..... are they..." She swallowed. "Are they proud of me?" Before I could formulate an answer, I was back in my dorm room. I tried to think back and recall the visit from my 10 year-old perspective. There had been nothing. And now, I had had my visitation with the future. At least I knew that I would live to be 30. It was an odd assurance to have, but some days were just so difficult. The classes, the responsibilities, the people..... Some days, I just wanted to stop. GO burned on my arm, stinging, warm. I washed it with soap and water, setting my jaw at the renewed tingles of pain, and trying to hide what I was doing from the other girls who came through the bathroom. I had Organic Chemistry that morning, and a lab in the afternoon. As I set up my ink chromatography experiment, my phone vibrated on the lab bench where I had left it with the rest of my things. I checked it. It was a text from my boyfriend. U comin over 2nite? Miss U I gnawed on my lip. Arch and I had been on and off for over a year now. Really, ever since we had started dating. Somewhere in the back of my head, I had an inkling that it wasn't going to work out, and it was never going to work out. But I was so used to being in a relationship with him; that's why I kept going back. And Arch didn't seem to mind. He just kind of went with it. If I wanted a break, we took a break. But then he'd invite me over to hang out or whatever, and then we'd be back on again. It was exhausting, but it was just part of the routine. I scratched at my arm and winced. GO A couple of other people were at Arch's place when I showed up. "I told'em you'd make them your specialty," he said. "Chicken fried rice!" I wish I could say this was the first time he's sprung a dinner party on me. I made dinner, and then I tried in vain to study in Arch's bedroom while he and his friends played their tabletop game all night. At one point, I found myself lying on the dirty carpet of his bedroom, staring at the patchy ceiling and wondering what I was doing with my life. It's not like anyone else out there wants me, I thought. Besides, Arch can't possibly take care of himself. He needs me to stay. I flexed my right hand. GO A month later, I ran into the girl who runs my chemistry lab at the cafe. "Hey!" she said. "You're the one who draws the little cats on test papers when you don't know the answer." "Yeah," I admitted, a little embarrassed. "I do it for the grader, because I feel bad." "Well," she said, "that would be me. So thanks for the doodles. I look forward to them!" Then she cleared her throat and said, "Not that you should take that as encouragement to do better on your tests." Sue and I got along surprisingly well, and we met regularly for coffee. "What's up with this new wardrobe?" she asked me once. "And you definitely got a hair cut. Is there a new guy?" "Nope," I allowed myself a smile. "Just got rid of the old one, that's all." On one of our long rambling talks, I divulged that I had never seen Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire because I had loved the book so much that I was afraid that the movie would murder it. So she invited me over to her place that weekend. "We're celebrating a friend's birthday," she said. "He's kind of a nerd, so it's Harry Potter-themed. We'll be marathoning the movies in the background." She poked my elbow across the table. "You wan na come?" "Wouldn't it be weird since I don't know the guy?" I protested. article: Imitation learning has traditionally been applied to learn a single task from demonstrations thereof. This approach can be effective for simple tasks with clear demonstrations, but it can also result in a lack of flexibility in handling novel situations. In contrast, inverse reinforcement learning involves trying to deduce the underlying reward function of the demonstrator given their behavior. This approach can lead to more generalizable policies that can handle novel situations. Furthermore, developments in multi-task and meta learning have allowed imitation learning to be applied more effectively to tasks with complex and diverse sets of skills. These approaches allow the agent to learn to learn, or to learn to transfer skills learned from one task to another. article: Insider trading, for those of you who aren't familiar with the term, is the practice of trading (i.e. buying or selling) a public company's stock by individuals with non-public knowledge about the company. Inside trading is considered a felony. For example, in 2001 Martha Stewart had a significant amount of stock in a drug company called ImClone. When a new drug by ImClone failed to get FDA approval, Stewart's broker tipped her off that the stock prices were about to fall dramatically. Stewart sold 230,000 in ImClone shares the day before the failure to get FDA approval became public knowledge. Ultimately, Stewart was found guilty of insider trading, which lead to five months in prison, five months of home confinement, and two years probation. Stewart is now a convicted felon. This all brings me to my point of this CMV. I can think of no reason why insider trading should be considered illegal, and especially why it should be considered a felony. Typically the designation of felony is reserved for only the most heinous of crimes- such as murder, rape, assault, etc. It is absurd to believe that insider trading is anywhere near these crimes. Some may say that insider trading should be illegal as it gives some people an unfair advantage when it comes to buying and selling stocks. But is that really a good enough reasoning to make it illegal? There are numerous legal ways that people can gain an unfair advantage in the stock world- certainly nobody is going to arrest Warren Buffett's daughter if Buffett gives her stock advice. Furthermore, who exactly gets harmed by insider trading? Insider trading may be the ultimate example of a victimless crime. Insider trading results when a willing buyer and a willing seller agree to trade property that the seller rightfully owns, with no prior contract being made between the parties to refrain from trading if there is asymmetric information. Even Milton Friedman, a Nobel laureate in economics said- "You want more insider trading, not less. You want to give the people most likely to have knowledge about deficiencies of the company an incentive to make the public aware of that." So there you go, CMV. article: We develop a well-balanced central-upwind scheme for rotating shallow water model with horizontal temperature andor density gradients - the thermal rotating shallow water (TRSW). The scheme is designed using the flux-vector splitting (FVS) approach, which separates the numerical flux into two components: a wave-propagation flux and a hydrostatic flux. The wave-propagation flux handles the advection of fluid properties such as temperature, density, and momentum, while the hydrostatic flux represents the vertical variation of pressure due to gravity. To ensure stability and accuracy of the scheme, we derive a set of thermodynamic consistency conditions that satisfy the conservation laws of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as the second law of thermodynamics. These conditions enforce a balance between the wave-propagation and hydrostatic fluxes, and ensure that the numerical solution does not violate any physical laws. The scheme is implemented using a second-order Godunov method with piecewise parabolic reconstruction (PPM) in space and a third-order TVD Runge-Kutta method in time. We test the scheme on a number of benchmark problems, including the rotating shallow water equations with and without temperaturedensity gradients, the geostrophic adjustment problem, and the baroclinic instability problem. Our results show that the TRSW scheme is highly accurate and robust, with excellent conservation properties and good scalability to large-scale simulations. The scheme also effectively captures the dynamics of thermal and density-driven flows, making it an excellent tool for studying a wide range of geophysical phenomena.

article: A pharmacist is basically a specialist in medication, meaning they probably know more about medicines than some medical practitioners.
